project_name: Anti-epidemic team dispatched to Anagola
description: On October 7, 2020, a 10-member anti-epidemic medical team dispatched from China arrived in Luanda, Angola. They planned to stay in Angola for 15 days to exchange experience with local professionals and aid in Angola's fight against the COVID-19 pandemic. The medical team's experience included working on the front lines during the COVID-19 pandemic in Wuhan, China. The team had experts trained in surgery, pulmonology, intensive care, nursing, the prevention of infectious diseases, and Chinese traditional medicine.  Chinese Ambassador Gong Tao, State Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Angola Lopez, and State Secretary of Public Health of the Ministry of Health Mufinda greeted the team at their arrival. Secretary Mufinda noted that Angola was in an opportune time for China's assistance. Chinese ambassador to Angola Gong Tao emphasized that the solidarity between China and Angola was strong a reason to share medical information with Angola.  The medical team completed the mission and departed from Angola on October 21, 2020.

project_name: 4 Malaria experts sent to Angola

The experts then traveled to Mozambique to work on similar work (see Project #68605).  The team spent 45 days in each country.  After the establishment of the anti-malaria center at the Luanda General Hospital (Hospital Geral de Luanda), it was envisaged that Chinese experts would set up and test the facilities, exchange ideas with local specialists, and provide technical training to medical staff (see Project #32853). This promise was most likely fulfilled via this technical assistance captured in this project.

The team was stationed at Luanda General Hospital (Hospital Geral de Luanda) in the Kilamba Kiaxi municipality of Luanda and was comprised of 18 doctors who specialized in fields such as urology, acupuncture and cardiology as well as 1 translator and 1 chef.   Since 2009, Sichuan Province has been sending medical teams to Angola every 2 years.

The medical team, dispatched by Sichuan Provincial Health Bureau, consists of 12-members and among the members there are experts in various fields such as internal medicine, surgery, orthopedics, pediatrics, laboratory, and pharmacy. The team will provide medical service in Angola for two years. project_name: 25th team donated medical supplies
description: On May 17, 2021, the 25th Chinese medical team to Benin donated medical supplies to Roxar Central Hospital in the Mono Province of Benin. The shipment consisted of 89 varieties of prescription and over-the-counter medicines, including anti-malarial and hypertension medicines totaling 5.8 million CFA francs; and medical equipment such as masks, medical caps, thermometers, gloves, infusion sets, sterile needles, cotton balls, drainage bags, and more totaling 1.96 million CFA francs.  After the handover of these materials, the medical team hosted a medical clinic and distributed health leaflets on hypertension and common tropical diseases.

project_name: 23rd team dispatched to provide consultation in clinic.
description: From January 19 to January 20, 2019, the 23rd Dispatch China-Benin Medical team provided a two-day clinic and consultation service in Lokossa City, Benin. During the two-day clinic, the 23rd medical team provided free medical consultation and medicines, as well as raised health awareness, and taught hygiene techniques. They also taught attendees about traditional Chinese medicine, Tai Chi, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, first aid bandaging, and 7-step hand-washing. At the clinic, more than 100 patients were diagnosed and treated, of which 21 received acupuncture and cupping treatments, more than 100 boxes of medicines were distributed free of charge, and more than 300 health promotion materials were distributed. Financial details are not certain, including the exact funding agency.  The 23rd medical team is serving one year in Benin, and is one of many medical teams sent to Benin since 1978 by the Ningxia Health and Welfare Commission (see project #59446)  The medical consultation coincided with a donation ceremony for school supplies to 20 Benin students (see project #60130), and a donation of office supplies to the Lokossa City Municipal Government (see project #68810).

project_name: 23rd team dispatched to Lokossa
description: On November 27, 2018, China's 23rd medical team, comprised of 15 doctors, arrived to work in Benin for one year. A farewell ceremony for the medical team was held on December 20th, 2019. During the 23rd medical team's service, they had 12,108 outpatient visits, 1,484 surgeries, and 2,146 ward rounds. Additionally, the medical team donated over 1,500 boxes of medicine.  The 23rd medical team was involved in an "Internet + Online consultation and inter-operative video consultation" initiative. To this end, the Zhongbei Remote Consultation Center was founded, offering free consultations to more than 2,000 people. On March 21st, 2019, a "Internet + medical health" remote guidance surgery was completed for the first time in the Monono and Kouffo Provincial Central Hospital. On May 6th, 2019, the 23rd medical team set up a medical treatment tent at the Benin-China recruitment fair.  The 23rd medical team was stated to have gone to Lokossa to operate on Beninese patients. The team was comprised of experts in both traditional medicine like surgery, orthopedics, gynecology, etc., as well as Chinese medicine like acupuncture, cupping, etc.   China has been sending medical teams to Benin every 2 years since January 1978. China originally signed the agreement to send medical teams to Benin in 1976. The Health and Welfare Commission of Ningxia Hui autonomous region (请宁夏卫健委与) is responsible for sending the teams. Over the 41 total years of Chinese medical teams in Benin, there have been over 600 Chinese medical workers, more than 3 million patient visits, 130,000 inpatients, and over 57,000 operations. project_name: 25th team sent to Benin in January 2021
description: On January 21, 2021, the Chinese Government sent their 25th medical team to Benin. A welcome ceremony was held for the arrival of the medical team. Chinese Ambassador to Benin Peng Jintao attended the ceremony. Team members consisted of specialists in the fields of general medicine, cardiology, gynecology, radiology, pharmacology, otorhinolaryngology, and traditional Chinese medicine. Following their services in Benin, the team departed on August 11, 2022.

project_name: 16th team donated PPE to Princess Marina Hospital
description: On March 31, 2021 the 16th Chinese Medical Team donated a batch of personal protective equipment valued at BWP430,000 to Princess Marina Hospital to fight against the COVID-19 pandemic.   The 82 cartons of donated PPE include disposable face masks, protective clothing, isolation clothes, disposable inspection gloves and isolation shoe covers, which are commonly used in the isolation ward.

project_name: Fujian province provided 16th team to Botswana
description: On September 19, 2020, China's Fujian Province dispatched the 16th medical team to Botswana. The team consisted of 46 members and will be in Botswana for two years. The team was dispatched to Botswana to assist in COVID-19 treatment, prevention efforts, and general medical aid. According to the Fujian Government, by August 31, 2021, the team had received 26,971 outpatients, 14,015 inpatients, and performed 2,926 surgeries in Botswana.   On September 18, 2020, the Fujian Provincial Health Commission held a departure ceremony for the medical team. Ambassador Wang Xuefeng, Counselor Wang Bangfu, Counselor Yang Xunlei, all the staff of the Chinese Embassy in Botswana, Fang Shaoxiong , members of the Party Group of Fujian Provincial Health and Health Commission, and the members of the 16th medical aid team participated in the event.

project_name: Gov't sent 2nd team
description: On December 26, 2018, China's second medical mission to Burkina Faso arrived and were treated to a celebratory arrival/farewell to the first medical team dinner. The second medical team was comprised of 10 doctors who were expected to stay in Burkina Faso for a year. Near the end of their stay, the doctors carried out the second phase of the "Light Action" cataract surgery project (see linked ProjectID#86706).  The dispatch of the first Chinese medical team is captured in ProjectID#60122.

project_name: 1st team provided drugs, surgical equipment, & training in Saponé
description: Sometime between July 7, 2018 and December 26, 2018, China's first medical mission to Burkina Faso provided donations of drugs and surgical equipment to health structures in the rural town of Saponé. The team also organized an activity to popularize knowledge in the area of ​​disease prevention.   The first Chinese medical team arrived in Burkina Faso on July 7, 2018 and departed on December 26, 2018 (see linked ProjectID#60122 ).

project_name: 3rd team sent to Burkina Faso
description: On January 6, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Burkina Faso welcomed the third Chinese medical team to Burkina Faso. The team was sent to Burkina Faso on 12-month tour. It provided medical services to overseas Chinese citizens and local Burkinabè people. An additional 12 person team was sent to Burkina Faso for two weeks in April 2020 for pandemic prevention and treatment (see project ID#93397). The first Chinese medical team came in 2018 (see project ID#88756) and the second came in 2019 (see project ID#60122). The team members on the third team included an orthopedist, a gastroenterologist, a practitioner of traditional Chinese medicine, an anesthesiologist, and a pulmonologist. The team mostly worked out of University Hospital Center of Tengandogo (CHU-T), but traveled to rural locations for short-term clinics.   In June 2020, the team made a donation to Regional Central Hospital Koudougou (see project ID#94575). In October 2020, the team made a donation the Health and Social Promotion Center in Moaga (see project ID#93768). They made similar donations to Moaga and Saatenga in November 2020 (see project ID#94574).

project_name: Gov't sent 1st team
description: On July 7, 2018, China sent its first-ever medical team to assist in improving Burkina Faso's public health. The team was comprised of over a dozen Chinese doctors. More than 500 consultations were carried out at the Tengandogo University Hospital and 200 at the Koudougou CHR. Surgical operations were also carried out, part of which with equipment made in China.  On December 26, 2018, after fulfilling their final duties at the Tengandogo University Hospital Center and at the Koudougou Regional Hospital Center, the team members were treated to a goodbye drink offered by the Embassy, ​​in the presence of the Secretary General of the Ministry of health, Robert Karama. There, they also welcomed the second Chinese medical team to continue the mission of improving public health in Burkina Faso (see ProjectID#88756).  In addition to this care, cooperation between the two countries has materialized through a donation of medical equipment including an ECG machine, a multi-parameter monitor, surgical devices and equipment, medical consumables and personal protective equipment. The value of the donation, made on October 30, 2018, to the Ministry of Health amounted to more than one million RMB, or approximately 82 million CFA francs (see linked ProjectID#88583).  In addition to this, donations of drugs and surgical equipment were given to health structures in the rural town of Saponé where the medical mission organized an activity to popularize knowledge in the area of ​​disease prevention (see linked ProjectID#88741).  It was also announced that 200 patients would benefit from Chinese Government-funded cataract surgery via the first phase of the "Light Action" (Action de la lumière) project (see ProjectID#60124).

project_name: team donated supplies to Regional Hospital Center in Koudougou
description: On June 17, 2020, the Chinese medical team in Burkina Faso (see project ID#94573) donated medical supplies worth XOF 1 million to Regional Hospital Center (French: Centre hospitalier régional, CHR) in Koudougou. The donation included traditional Chinese products, blood pressure monitors, ibuprofen, and supplies to combat Covid-19.

project_name: Supplies donated to the Health & Social Promotion Centers in Moaga
description: On October 19, 2020, the Chinese medical team operating out of the Tengandogo University Hospital Center (see project ID#94573) donated XOF 5 million worth of medical products to the Health and Social Promotion Center (French: Centre de santé et de promotion sociale, CSPS) of Moaga, Burkina Faso. The donation consisted of supplies such as antibiotics, hypertension medications, surgical masks, and disinfectants.

project_name: 1st team performed cataract surgeries for patients
description: From December 23-31, 2018, Chinese doctors performed cataract surgeries in Burkina Faso as part of an operation called "Action de la lumière" (Light Action).  More than 200 Burkinabé patients aged between 50 and 80 have recovered their sight. The operation was carried out by 10 Chinese medical experts part of the first Chinese medical team to Burkina Faso (see linked ProjectID#60122).

project_name: National Health Commission sent 12 medical experts
description: On April 16, 2020, 12 Chinese medical experts left Tianjin and arrived in Burkina Faso. The group was to exchange experience, technical guidance, and education on the prevention and control of COVID-19 with Burkina Faso health authorities and medical personnel during a two-week period. The team met with members of the Burkina Faso Ministry of Health, World Health Organization (WHO) representatives, and Chinese Embassy personnel. The National Health Commission of the People's Republic of China sponsored the team. Also on April 16, 2020, the Chinese government made a donation of medical supplies to Burkina Faso (see project ID#93398). These supplies were to support this medical team in its work.

project_name: 2nd team performs cataract surgeries as part of 'light action'
description: From December 7, 2019 to December 21, 2019, the National Health Commission of China dispatched 10 members of the second Chinese medical team to Burkina Faso to its capital, Ouagadougou, to carry out free cataract surgeries for the local people at Tangadogo Hospital as part of Phase II of the “Light Action” Project. The team composed of experts and nurses from he Eye Hospital of WMU, China.  The clinic lasted 15 days and more than 300 patients was screened. A total of 250 eligible patients completed the operation. The success rate of the operation was 100%. On December 21, the closing ceremony of the "Light Walk" event was held at Tanggadogo Hospital.  Linked ProjectID#88756 captures the year-long term for China's second medical mission to Burkina Faso.

project_name: 5 medical experts sent for Malaria treatment
description: On February 9, 2008, a group of 5 Chinese medical experts has arrived in Bujumbura, Burundi. The group will be helping Burundi with Malaria treatment, while the government of Burundi has already prepared laboratories, equipment, and offices for the group. International Affairs Department at the National Health Commission ("卫生部国际交流中心" or "卫生部国际合作司") is in charge.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 1st team to perform cataract surgeries
description: In December 2016, the Chinese Embassy in Burundi implemented the "Walking towards Light" ("光明行") Project, which involved operating a temporarily free clinic at Prince Regent Charles Hospital. During the nine-day period, Chinese ophthalmologists performed cataract surgery free of charge for 182 patients in Burundi. The Chinese expert group also trained local medical staff and donated surgical equipment and related medicines to Prince Regent Charles Hospital.   The project was led by National Health Commission of PRC (国家卫生计生委) and implemented by a medical team coming from Chinese hospitals including Peking Union Medical College Hospital (北京协和医院、青海省人民医院、江西大学眼科医院). See Project ID#57410 for a second team deployed in 2018.

project_name: 2nd team sent for surgeries & equipment donated for 'Guang Ming Xing'
description: On June 13, 2018, a Chinese medical team was deployed in Burundi to perform free cataract surgeries for two weeks as part of the "Bright Tour" (Chinese project name is 光明行 "Guang Ming Xing"). The team worked at the Prince's Hospital of Burundi. By the time the project ended on June 20, 2018, 220 patients had undergone surgeries under the project. China donated $500,000 worth of medical equipment and medications related to the surgeries as part of this project.   This is the second batch of ophthalmologists sent as a short-term mission Burundi, see Project ID#52928 for the first team of Guang Ming Xing (“光明行”) project, which is led by National Health Commission of PRC (国家卫生计生委) and implemented by Chinese hospitals including Peking Union Medical College Hospital (北京协和医院、青海省人民医院).

project_name: 9th team dispatched to hospitals
description: China has been sending medical teams to Burundi every two years since 1987. Qinghai Province has been responsible for sending the teams. The 9th medical team included 29 members who were stationed at Prince Regent Charles Hospital, Gitega Provincial Hospital, and Muramvya Provincial Hospital. They completed their term of service between 2000 to 2002. The task of the Chinese medical team is to work closely with Burundian medical staff to carry out medical work (excluding forensic work), provide technical guidance, and exchange experience in medical practice.  Burundi was responsible for providing medical equipment and medicines, covering the international travel expenses for the Chinese medical team, and providing living expenses. Burundi also exempt medical devices shipped from China from taxation and duties, and exempt team members from paying taxes during deployment period. The living expenses mentioned are as follows: 80,000 BFA/month for the team leader and deputy chief physician (unclear if this is one or more person); 70,000 BFA/month for the attending physician, physician, and translator; and 70,000 BFA/month for other personnel.

In 2019, China sent professional and technical guidance on Ebola prevention and control materials and equipment to assist Burundi in the fight against Ebola virus. During the 5 days of staying, the Chinese expert team visited the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Burundi, Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Lutte contre le (SIDA), and exchanged work with the World Health Organization Office in Burundi, and the 19th batch of China-aided Burundi medical teams; visited Burundi and Congo ( Gold) Katoomba Border, Katoomba Border Hospital, La Centrale d'Achat des Medicaments Essentiels du Burundi (CAMEBU), Capital Grand Prince Hospital, Burundi National Institute of Public Health (INSP), etc.

project_name: Teams provided tons of medical equipment to hospitals in Bujumbura
description: On June 7, 2021, three Chinese medical teams in Burundi donated almost 15 tons of medicine and medical equipment to be distributed to residents and hospitals of Bujumbura, Burundi. The three teams were Bujumbura Medical Point, Mubanda Medical Point, and Gitega Medical Point. The materials included clinical drugs, protective masks, and surgical medical devices. The supplies were then distributed within a week of their delivery on June 7, 2021. The purpose of this donation is to support Burundi’s COVID-19 response efforts. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.   A handover ceremony was held for this donation. The captains of the three medical teams and directors of the recipient hospitals attended the ceremony.

China has been sending medical teams to Burundi every two years since 1987. Qinghai Provincial Aid medical teams had previously come to Burundi to offer medical services that lasted two years at a time; however, in 2018 the groups began to come for just one year. The 19th medical team's mission was supposed to last a year as well. However, due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the medical team ended their mission in March, 2021.

project_name: 18th team sent to Cabo Verde
description: On November 14, 2018, the Chargé d’affaires of the Chinese Embassy in Cape Verde and Cape Verde’s Minister of State signed a Protocol Agreement for China to Send Medical Teams to Work in Cape Verde (in Chinese: "中国派遣医疗队赴佛得角工作的议定书"). The agreement stipulated that from 2018-2020, a medical team from China -- the eighteenth sent to Cape Verde -- would provide services to Cape Verde.  On December 17, 2018, Ambassador Du Xiaocong hosted a dinner at the Chinese Embassy in Cape Verde to welcome the medical team. Cape Verde’s Minister of Health Dorosario and the dean of Praia Central Hospital also attended this event. The medical team is comprised of eight members, including one anesthesiologist, three gynecologists and obstetricians, two surgeons, one orthopedic surgeon, and one interpreter. According to SAPO Noticias, the eighteenth medical team will compensate for the deficit of surgeons at Hospital Agostinho Neto in Praia, Cape Verde. This eighteenth medical team relieved the seventeenth Chinese medical team, whose arrival in Cape Verde is captured in the linked project #52961.    This project was completed on February 17, 2021, when the 19th medical team arrived to Cabo Verde.   China has been sending medical teams to Cape Verde every two years since 1984. Heilongjiang Province was originally responsible for sending the teams, but Sichuan became the dispatching province changed in February 1988.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for team housing project
description: On December 20, 2001 an exchange of letters was signed between China and Cabo Verde for the Chinese Medical Team Housing Project. In 2002, the China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) provided a grant to the Government of Cabo Verde for this project. The monetary value of this financial commitment is unknown. However, it is known that the Chinese Government committed EUR 1.9 million for this project and the Praia Central Hospital Surgical Ward Construction Project (captured in Project ID#53192). Therefore, for the time being, AidData estimates that MOFCOM evenly divided the funds across the two projects (committing EUR 950,000 to each project).   The Chinese Medical Team Housing Project involved the construction of housing units for Chinese medical teams stationed at Agostinho Neto Hospital (HAN or Praia Central Hospital or 普拉亚中心医院) in the capital city of Praia. The construction area occupied about 750 square meters.   On June 25, 2003, five Chinese engineers arrived in Praia to make preparations for the implementation of the project. Construction began on December 2, 2003. Then, from August 18-26, 2004, five Chinese experts carried out a mid-term project inspection on behalf of MOFCOM and found its implementation to be excellent. On August 30, 2005, the project was officially completed handed over to the Government of Cabo Verde. The Chinese Ambassador to Cabo Verde Sun Rongmao and Director General of International Cooperation of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Anthony Alves Lopez signed the project handover certificate on behalf of the governments of China and Cabo Verde.

project_name: Gov't sent medical expert group
description: On May 23, 2020, a medical group sent by the Chinese government arrived in Brazzaville, Congo. The group was established by the National Health Commission and selected by the Hebei Provincial Health Commission. It included 12 experts in clinical medicine, epidemic prevention, and laboratory testing. The medical expert team worked in Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire, shared experiences, and trained professionals with the Congolese epidemic prevention department and medical staff in the fight against Covid-19.   On May 24, 2020, the medical expert team in Congo (Brazzaville) held lectures on epidemic prevention knowledge for the embassy and the Chinese-funded enterprise association. On May 25, the expert group held a working meeting with the National Anti-epidemic Technical Committee of Congo to exchange and share China's effective experience in epidemic prevention and control mechanisms, epidemiological investigations, and identification and isolation of close contacts. On May 26-27, the medical expert team trained more than 150 medical staff from 6 hospitals in Brazzaville, the capital of Congo. On May 27, the medical expert team held a lecture on epidemic prevention knowledge for overseas Chinese in Brazzaville. On May 28, the medical expert team took a chartered flight to Pointe Noire, the second-largest city in Congo. On May 29, the Governor of Pointe-Noire Province, Paka, met with the expert team. The expert team conducted training for local medical staff at the Luanwang Kiri Hospital. On May 30, the medical expert team held a lecture on epidemic prevention knowledge for overseas Chinese in Pointe-Noire and surrounding areas. On June 9, the medical expert team concluded their mission in Africa and left Brazzaville, Congo to return back to China.

project_name: Hubei Province provided team for Covid-19 aid
description: On May 4, 2020, the Chinese medical expert team arrived in Côte d’Ivoire. The team consists of 12 medical experts from the Hubei Province of China. While in Côte d’Ivoire, the medical team will share their experiences they have accumulated during China’s fight against COVID-19 and provide support to the Côte d’Ivoire government and medical institutions for COVID-19 prevention and response efforts. The team will also conduct inspections of COVID-19 designated hospitals and testing centers. According to Liu Yun, the Vice President of Tianjin People’s Hospital, the medical expert team came at the invitation of the Cote d’Ivoire government.  The medical team arrived on April 30, 2020. project_name: Eye experts sent for the bright journey project
description: In September 2014, Beijing University People's Hospital and Beijing No.3 Hospital sent three cataract experts to Djibouti to carry out the Guangmingxing (光明行) or "Bright Journey" Project. During their one month stay in Djibouti, they performed around 520 free cataract surgeries and 1086 eye exams. They also helped to train the only two eye doctors in Djibouti. They returned to Beijing in 19 October 2014. The value of this project is unknown.

project_name: Epidemic expert team sent
description: On April 30, 2020, the Chinese government sent an epidemic expert team to Djibouti to provide COVID-19 response and prevention assistance. This epidemic expert team consisted of 12 members. The National Health Commission formed the team and members were personally selected by the Sichuan Provincial and Tianjin Municipal Health Commissions. The team arrived at Djibouti’s Ambouli International Airport on April 30, 2020. Zhuo Ruisheng, China’s Ambassador to Djibouti, the representative of the Djibouti government, the Secretary of State for Youth and Sports, the Secretary-General of the Ministry of Health, the General Counsel of the Ministry of Health, and the relevant leaders of the National Anti-Epidemic Emergency Leadership Committee received the team at the airport.  On May 3, 2020, Prime Minister Kamil of Djibouti met with the epidemic expert team at the People's Palace in Djibouti. Zhuo Ruisheng, the Ambassador to Djibouti, the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Djibouti, the Minister of Health, and the Presidential Health Advisor attended the meeting.   On May 10, 2020, Prime Minister Kamil of Djibouti awarded the Independence Day National Medal to all 12 members of the epidemic expert team at the Djibouti People's Palace. This medal was awarded in recognition of the expert team's contribution to Djibouti's fight against the epidemic. Djibouti’s Foreign Minister, the Minister of Health, and China’s Ambassador to Djibouti, Zhuo Ruisheng, attended the ceremony.  The expert team departed Djibouti and returned to China on May 11, 2020. Djibouti Foreign Minister Yusuf and the Minister of Health held a ceremony at the airport to see the expert group off on behalf of the Djibouti government. Zhuo Ruisheng, China’s Ambassador to Djibouti, was also present at the send-off.

This mission was the first time that the Chinese medical team had provided medical services to people outside of Djibouti's capital. The team received medals for their service during the pandemic from Prime Minister Abdoulkader Kamil Mohamed. description: On 8 March, 2011, the Chinese Government and the Government of Djibouti signed an agreement to dispatch the 16th medical team to work in Djibouti. The 14-member team arrived in Djibouti on 1 April 2012. They served at General Peltier Hospital (l’Hôpital Général Peltier) until the end of 2013.  Since 1981, the Chinese Government has sent 19 medical teams to Djibouti.

project_name: 29th team offered medical clinic at Bariobe, Bioko Norte
description: On May 24, 2018, the 29th Chinese medical team traveled to the Village of Bariobe in Bioko Norte to conduct free medical consultations for its people. In addition to the medical assistance, the medical team also donated 4200 RMB worth of medical supplies for the village (project ID#88588).  The village of Bariobe is located 21 km outside of the city of Malabo. This medical clinic is aimed to make it easier for the villagers to get professional medical assistance. The 29th medical team helped more than 200 people and provided 185 prescriptions in such departments as internal medicine, surgery, orthopedics, gynecology, pediatrics, ophthalmology, etc. These free clinics are aimed to help Equatorial Guinea's development in its health department and find a deeper connection between China and Equatorial Guinea.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 23rd team to hospitals
description: Since 1971, Guangzhou Health Department has been sending medical teams to Equatorial Guinea. On August 29, 2006, the Chinese Government and the Government of Equatorial Guinea signed an agreement dispatching the 23rd Chinese medical team to Equatorial Guinea. The team was stationed at the Bata General Hospital in the city of Bata and Malabo Regional Hospital in the city of Malabo. It completed its term of service between 2006 and 2008.   On July 7, 2008, all members of the 23rd medical team were presented with awards in recognition of their work.

project_name: Sent 30th team
description: On July 6, 2019, the 30th Chinese medical team to Equatorial Guinea arrived in the country. A handover ceremony from the 29th to the 30th medical team was held on July 9, 2019 at the embassy. Counselor Su Jianguo visited the 30th medical team on August 2, 2019. This project is complete with the arrival of the 31st Chinese medical team to Equatorial Guinea in January 2021. China has been sending medical teams to Equatorial Guinea since 1971.  According to the Dongguan Time Network, a total of 19,839 outpatient visits were completed, 2,438 operations were performed, 22,965 ward rounds were conducted, and 93 clinical training sessions were conducted for 420 people during the team's time in Equatorial Guinea.

project_name: Sent 29th team
description: On January 5, 2018, the 29th Chinese medical team to Equatorial Guinea arrived in Malabo. The medical team is consisted of 27 medical staff from Guangdong Province. According to the Guangdong Provincial People's Government, while in the country, the Guangdong medical team received 7,689 outpatients and 9,147 inpatients. They performed 116 emergency treatments, 1,349 operations, 635 anesthesia procedures, 1,420 acupuncture treatments, and 11,039 assays and examinations.  On February 6, 2018, Chinese Ambassador Chen Guoyou visited the 29th medical team to send them Spring Festival blessings and greetings. The Ambassador also visited the team on February 10-11 to mark the eve of the Chinese New Year. The 29th Medical team conducted free clinics in the 8 villages, which is recorded in projects ID#86713, 88591, 86721 (第29批援赤道几内亚医疗队的故事：上班要面对艾滋病，下班要开荒种菜).  A handover ceremony from the 29th to the 30th Chinese medical team was held on July 9, 2019, and the 29th team arrived back in China on July 22, 2019. China has been sending medical teams to Equatorial Guinea since 1971.

project_name: 29th team donated to Ehoko Village
description: The Chinese 29th medical team also donated 3000 RMB worth of medical supplies, equal to 250,000 CFA francs, while conducting a medical clinic in the Ehoko village in the Bioko Sur Province (project ID#86713). The donation was used for medicine for the villagers.  Due to the lack of transportation and financial resources, the Ehoko village has always lacked the proper medical resources to support the medical demand of its people. In order to alleviate this stress, the 29th medical team drove 3 hours to Ehoco to conduct free clinic to treat 110 patients and handed out 51 prescriptions. This event would help Equatorial Guinea promote its health developments, aid the Equatorial Guinea society, and promote the friendship between the two countries.   More information on the 29th Medical team can be found in project ID#62283.

project_name: 27th team donated medicine & medical equipment
description: On February 29, 2016, the 27th Chinese medical team in Equatorial Guinea handed over a donation of medicine and medical equipment in Malabo. Team leader of the 27th Chinese medical team in Equatorial Guinea, Lin Ming, and Equatorial Guinea Ministry of Health official, Gao Li, signed the handover certificate on behalf of both parties. The Equatorial Guinean Minister of Health, the president of the Malabo Regional General Hospital, and all members of the 27th Chinese medical team attended the donation ceremony. It is unclear how much this donation cost.  Linked ProjectID#35432 captures the free-standing technical assistance provided by the 27th Chinese medical team.

project_name: Gov't sent anti-epidemic medical expert team in response to Covid-19
description: On May 25, 2020, an anti-epidemic expert team of 12 members arrived in Malabo in response to the COVID-19 epidemic. The team was formed by the National Health Commission and selected by the Hunan Provincial Health Commission. The team included experts in respiratory care, infectious disease, intensive care, Infection control, public health, laboratory testing and nursing.  Zhao Lijian, the spokesman for the Foreign Ministry Information Department of the People's Republic of China, announced their arrival on May 25. The team remained in Equatorial Guinea for 10 days and left on June 8, 2020, after providing medical assistance.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 22nd team to hospitals

The team arrived in Equatorial Guinea in June 24, 2004 and competed its term of service in mid-2006. It was presented with various awards by the Equatorial Guinean government on July 6, 2006. project_name: Gov't dispatched 24th team to hospitals
description: Since 1971, Guangzhou Health Department has been sending medical teams to Equatorial Guinea. The team met with the Chinese Ambassador to Equatorial Guinea on June 26, 2008, shortly after arriving in the country. Then, on July 3, 2010, President Obiang presented awards and honors to the members of the 24th Chinese medical team prior to their departure from Equatorial Guinea.

project_name: 29th team held a medical clinic for the residents of Corisco Isl&
description: On May 25th, 2018, the 29th medical team to Equatorial Guinea from China held a free medical clinic for Corisco Island residents. At the clinic, the medical team also donated 3000 RMB for medicine to the residents (project ID# 88590). The donation amount is equivalent to 250,000 Central African Francs.  The departments receiving medical treatment include internal medicine, surgery, gynecology, pediatrics, etc. 47 patients were received during the clinic.

On July 2, 2014, the Equatorial Guinean President Obiang granted each member of the 26th medical team with a medal and certificate of honor for their work.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 3rd team to hospitals & centers
description: Since 1997, Henan Province has been sending medical teams to Eritrea every 2 years.   On November 28, 2002, the Chinese Government and the Government of Eritrea signed a protocol agreement, dispatching the 3rd Chinese medical team to Eritrea. The team was stationed at Orotta Referral Hospital, Halibet National Referral Hospital, Berhan Aini National Referral Hospital, and Asmara Physiotherapy Center, all of which are all located in the capital city of Asmara. The team completed its term of service between 2003 and 2004.

project_name: Sent 13th & 14th teams to Orotta Hospital as technical aid
description: On June 21st, 2019, Ambassador Yang Zigang and Minister of Health Amna Nurhusein signed an exchange of letters detailing the provision of technical assistance to Eritrea's Orotta hospital. This is the eighth phase of assistance that China has sent to Orotta Hospital. This assured that the 13th (project #87284) and 14th Chinese medical teams would be dispatched to Orotta Hospital. The assistance was said to commence directly after the signing of the exchange of letters. This phase of cooperation will last for two years.   Orotta Hospital was built with Chinese aid in 2000 (project #493 and project #30533). Orotta Hospital is one of the four main hospitals the Chinese medical teams in Eritrea are sent to. China has provided seven phases of technical assistance since 2004, "dispatch[ing] technicians to carry out medical equipment repair, maintenance and technical personnel training to ensure the normal operation and use of the hospital".

project_name: Gov't dispatched 10th team to hospitals & centers
description: Since 1997, Henan Province has been sending medical teams to Eritrea every 2 years.   In 2016, the Chinese Government dispatched the 10th Chinese medical team to Eritrea. The team was stationed at Orotta Referral Hospital, Halibet National Referral Hospital, Berhan Aini National Referral Hospital, and Asmara Physiotherapy Center, all of which are all located in the capital city of Asmara. It completed its term of service between August 16, 2016 and August 21, 2016.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 2nd team to hospitals & centers
description: Since 1997, Henan Province has been sending medical teams to Eritrea every 2 years.   On December 29, 2000, the Chinese Government and the Government of Eritrea signed a protocol agreement, dispatching the 2nd Chinese medical team to Eritrea. The 18-member team was stationed at Halibet National Referral Hospital, Berhan Aini National Referral Hospital, and Asmara Physiotherapy Center, all of which are all located in the capital city of Asmara. The team completed its term of service between 2001 and 2002.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 11th team to hospitals & centers
description: Since 1997, Henan Province has been sending medical teams to Eritrea every 2 years.   In 2017, the Chinese Government dispatched the 11th Chinese medical team to Eritrea. The team was stationed at Orotta Referral Hospital, Halibet National Referral Hospital, Berhan Aini National Referral Hospital, and Asmara Physiotherapy Center, all of which are all located in the capital city of Asmara. It completed its term of service between August 30, 2017 and September 11, 2018.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 9th team to hospitals & centers
description: Since 1997, Henan Province has been sending medical teams to Eritrea every 2 years.   In 2015, the Chinese Government dispatched the 9th Chinese medical team to Eritrea. The 18-member team was stationed at Orotta Referral Hospital, Halibet National Referral Hospital, Berhan Aini National Referral Hospital, and Asmara Physiotherapy Center, all of which are all located in the capital city of Asmara. The 18-member team   completed its term of service between June 26, 2015 and August 21, 2016. As of the end of April 2016, the ninth medical team had treated 36,176 outpatients, treated 7,765 inpatients, completed 2,781 surgeries, rescued 2,023 critically ill patients, anesthetized 2,006 patients, and treated patients with acupuncture and moxibustion.

project_name: Sent 'bright journey' team for ophthalmic surgeries
description: Between December 16th, 2019 and January 6th, 2020, China sent a team of 7 ophthalmologists and 3 assistants to "perform cataract surgery and diagnose and treat other eye diseases" in Eritrea, as a part of "Bright Journey" (“光明行”), one of the eight initiatives established during the 2018 FOCAC (Forum on China-Africa Cooperation) meeting. Over the course of the 21 days, the team performed 508 cataract surgeries and diagnosed and treated 1,250 patients with eye diseases.

project_name: Sent the 12th team
description: On September 13th, 2018, the 12th medical team sent by China to Eritrea arrived at Asmara, Eritrea (第12批中国援厄医疗队). On this date, a ceremony for the arrival of the 12th medical team was held, and the 11th medical team sent to Eritrea was recognized and thanked (project #56080). This project was completed with an award ceremony on August 23, 2019, and 18 members of the 13th batch of medical aid teams were sent to replace them (project #87284).  China has successfully sent 12 medical teams to Eritrea of 222 members since sending the first medical team to Eritrea in September 1997. Sending medical experts to Eritrea is an important measure for China to implement the China-Africa Cooperation Forum Action Plan, as was outlined on September 3-4 at the Beijing Summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 4th team to hospitals & centers
description: Since 1997, Henan Province has been sending medical teams to Eritrea every 2 years.
