The team was stationed at Orotta Referral Hospital, Halibet National Referral Hospital, Berhan Aini National Referral Hospital, and Asmara Physiotherapy Center, all of which are all located in the capital city of Asmara. The team completed its term of service between 2005 and 2006.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 8th team to hospitals & centers
description: Since 1997, Henan Province has been sending medical teams to Eritrea every 2 years.   In 2013, the Chinese Government dispatched the 8th Chinese medical team to Eritrea. The 18-member team was stationed at Orotta Referral Hospital, Halibet National Referral Hospital, Berhan Aini National Referral Hospital, and Asmara Physiotherapy Center, all of which are all located in the capital city of Asmara.   The 18-member team included experts in cardiology, intensive care, Chinese medicine acupuncture, general surgery, nerve surgery, urology, maxillofacial surgery, orthopedics, ophthalmology, anesthesiology and radiology. It completed its term of service between May 31, 2013 and July 3, 2015

project_name: Gov't dispatched 5th team to hospitals & centers
description: Since 1997, Henan Province has been sending medical teams to Eritrea every 2 years.   On October 12, 2006, the Chinese Government and the Government of Eritrea signed a protocol agreement, dispatching the 5th Chinese medical team to Eritrea. The team was stationed at Orotta Referral Hospital, Halibet National Referral Hospital, Berhan Aini National Referral Hospital, and Asmara Physiotherapy Center, all of which are all located in the capital city of Asmara. The team, which consisted of 15 doctors, completed its term of service between January 14, 2007 and 2009. In February 2008, 5th medical team donated medical devices worth RMB 60,000.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for team dormitory construction project
description: In 2017, the Chinese Government provided an RMB 35.41 million grant to the Government of Eritrea for the Chinese Medical Team Dormitory Construction Project. The purpose of the project was to construct a dormitory for the Chinese medical team stationed at Orotta Hospital in the capital city of Asmara. More specifically, it involved the construction of 21 sets of dormitories with bedrooms, living rooms, bathrooms, and kitchens. It also involved the construction of a consultation room, treatment room, observation room, two storerooms, a reception room, a public kitchen, a dining room, an entrance, corridor, stairwell, an athletic court, and parking spaces. Jiangxi Changnan Construction Group Co. Ltd. was the contractor responsible for project implementation. A groundbreaking ceremony was held on June 1, 2017. The project was officially completed on May 21, 2019. China’s Ambassador to Eritrea Yang Zigang and Eritrea’s Minister of Health Amna Nurhusein signed the project handover certificate.

project_name: Gov't provided funds to dispatch team to conduct cataract surgeries
description: On July 7, 2015, Chinese Ambassador to Eritrea Qiu Xuejun and Eritrean Minister of Health Amna Nurhusein signed a protocol for the National Health and Family Planning Commission of the People’s Republic of China and the Ministry of Health of the Eritrean State in Asmara on the dispatch of a Chinese ophthalmologist medical team to Eritrea for cataract surgeries. The project's name is ""Guangming xing"" (“光明行"").   For this project, Chinese medical experts were expected to conduct over 300 cataract surgeries, and then donate surgical equipment, medicines and other materials to the Eritrean government. On August 19, 2015, the medical team arrived from China to Eritrea. The medical team was made of 11 people, including 4 ophthalmologists and 3 nurses, who were responsible for carrying out at least 300 cataract operations in Eritrea, and carrying out activities such as ophthalmology clinics and lectures in accordance with Eritrea's needs. On August 20, 2015, Wang Liya, the leader of the ""Guangming xing"" Chinese medical team of China's assistance to Eritrea, and the vice president of Henan Provincial People's Hospital, visited the Eritrean Minister of Health Amna Nurhusein in a courtesy visit. The Chinese aid medical team's captain Sun Laiguang also attended this meeting.   The medical team was dispatched from the Chinese National Health and Family Planning Commission. The team worked in Eritrea for 10 days and completed over 300 cataract surgeries. September 5, 2015 was the last day for the group to complete surgeries. On that day, the Chinese ambassador to Eritrea and the Eritrean Minister of Health signed the ""bright"" activities goods delivery certificate. The Chinese medical team also donated the surgical equipment and medicine brought by the medical team to the Eritrean government. In total, the Chinese Government provided RMB 6 million to support this implementation of this project.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 6th team to hospitals & centers
description: Since 1997, Henan Province has been sending medical teams to Eritrea every 2 years.   In 2009, the Chinese Government dispatched the 6th Chinese medical team to Eritrea. The 18-member team was stationed at Orotta Referral Hospital, Halibet National Referral Hospital, Berhan Aini National Referral Hospital, and Asmara Physiotherapy Center, all of which are all located in the capital city of Asmara. The team, which consisted of 15 doctors, completed its term of service between January 16, 2009 and January 12, 2011.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 7th team tto hospitals & centers
description: Since 1997, Henan Province has been sending medical teams to Eritrea every 2 years.   On March 4, 2010, the Chinese Government and the Government of Eritrea signed a protocol agreement, dispatching the 7th Chinese medical team to Eritrea. The 18-member team was stationed at Orotta Referral Hospital, Halibet National Referral Hospital, Berhan Aini National Referral Hospital, and Asmara Physiotherapy Center, all of which are all located in the capital city of Asmara. The team completed its term of service between January 12, 2011 and 2013 (中国第七批援厄医疗队).

project_name: Sent the 13th team
description: On August 23rd, 2019 Eritrea welcomed the 13th medical team sent by China to provide free medical care. There were 18 members on the team with an average age of 39. This occurred with the departure of the 12th batch of medical aid teams that China sent to Eritrea (project #56089). In their 17 month term of service, the medical team received more than 13,400 patients, conducted 4,864 Chinese acupuncture and physiotherapy, wrote 2,398 image reports, and completed 1,554 various operations, including 260 major operations.Traditionally, the teams provide medical services at Orotta Hospital (Captured in #87276), Halibet National Referral Hospital, Berhan Aini National Referral Hospital, and Asmara Physiotherapy Center, all of which are all located in the capital city of Asmara. The team arrived in Eritrea a few days earlier on August 17th, and served until January 29, 2021. Given the time-frame, the medical team played a large role in the prevention and control of the COVID-19 pandemic.  China has successfully sent 12 medical teams to Eritrea of 222 members since sending the first medical team to Eritrea in September 1997. Sending medical experts to Eritrea is an important measure for China to implement the China-Africa Cooperation Forum Action Plan, as was outlined on September 3-4 at the Beijing Summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation.

project_name: 16th team sent
description: On December 18, 2011, China’s new ambassador to Ethiopia, Xie Xiaoyan, visited the 16th batch of Chinese medical teams sent to Ethiopia. It is unclear when the 16th team arrived in Ethiopia and when they were scheduled to return to China.

project_name: 20th team sent
description: In August 2017, the Chinese government sent their 20th medical team to Ethiopia. The 20th team was a continuation of medical cooperation between Ethiopia and China since 1974. Comprising 15 medical professionals and 1 translator, the 20th team was headed by cardiologist Zhao Cheng. The team was based at the Tirunesh-Beijing Ethio-China Friendship Hospital on the outskirts of Addis Ababa. Along with work at the Tirunesh-Beijing Hospital, the team has done medical treatments in more than 73 clinics and two Chinese companies.  In November 2017, 10 medical team members provided services including mouth and respiratory organ treatments, eyes protection support and heart condition checkups to school children in Addis Ababa.

project_name: 19th team donated medical supplies to Bishoftu General Hospital
description: In 2017, the 19th Chinese medical team to Ethiopia (#59973) donated 500 thousand birr worth of medical supplies to the Bishoftu General Hospital in Bishoftu, Ethiopia. According to All Africa, the donation comprised of 23 pieces of medical equipment. The donation was given while the medical team was providing medical services at Bishoftu General Hospital for a five-day period in early June 2017.

project_name: 14th team sent
description: On February 21, 2009, the Ethiopian Ministry of Health held a farewell party for the 14th Chinese medical team to Ethiopia. According to the Economic and Commercial Counsellor's Office of the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in Ethiopia, Dr. Kebede, Minister of State of the Ministry of Health, Mr. Abebe, Director of the Human Resources Development Department, and Mr. Ahmed, Director of the Public Relations Department, as well as our Ambassador to Ethiopia, Gu Xiaojie, and our Counselor Qian Zhaogang attended the banquet.

project_name: 2nd military team deployed
description: On January 9, 2016, a Chinese military medical expert team was sent to Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, to complete a one-year medical assistance mission. This is the 2nd Chinese military medical team deployed to Ethiopia. The team consisted of nine members from nine departments of the Xinqiao Hospital, one of the three teaching hospitals affiliated to the Third Military Medical University. During their year-long mission, the Chinese medical team completed more than 1,400 cases of clinic treatment and more than 150 highly difficult surgeries. The team also held lectures regularly for Ethiopian military medical personnel and provided medical imaging examinations and health care services for Ethiopian military and government officials. The medical team returned to China on January 17, 2017.

project_name: 1st military team deployed
description: On January 12, 2015, a Chinese military medical expert team was sent to Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, to provide a one-year medical assistance to the General Hospital of the Ethiopian National Defense Force (ENDF). This marked the first Chinese military medical expert team to Ethiopia. The team consisted of eight experts dispatched from the People's Liberation Army (PLA) Third Military Medical University. During their time in Ethiopia, the team undertook the tasks including outpatient service, group consultation, surgical operations, emergency treatment as well as professional training for medical workers in seven departments of the General Hospital of ENDF including the internal medicine-cardiovascular department, the neurosurgery department and the otolaryngology department. According to China Military News, the Chinese military medical experts received and treated outpatients for 4,000 persons/times, saved lives of 63 critically ill patients and performed surgery operations or provided surgery operation guidance 220 times without any cases of death or malpractice. The Chinese military medical team returned to China on January 12, 2016.

project_name: 3rd military team deployed
description:
On January 10, 2017, a Chinese military medical expert team was sent to Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, to complete a medical assistance mission. The nine members of the medical team are all clinical doctors from the departments of nephrology, cardiovascular internal medicine, urinary surgery, ear-nose-throat, oral and maxillofacial surgery, operation anesthesia and radiology of the Southwest Hospital affiliated to the Third Military Medical University. The team will carry out clinical treatment, personnel training and technical assistance at the General Hospital of the Ethiopian National Defense Forces (ENDF) in Addis Ababa. 
 
 The current status of the project and the team is unclear.

project_name: 18th team sent
description: A handover ceremony from the 17th to the 18th Chinese medical team to Ethiopia was held in July 2015. The 18th Chinese medical team to Ethiopia worked out of Tirunesh-Beijing Hospital in Addis Ababa. During their time in Ethiopia, the 18th batch of the Chinese medical teams to Ethiopia provided free clinic services to the villagers in Jimma, Ethiopia, after a commemoration ceremony for Mei Gengnian, the leading doctor for the first Chinese medical mission to Ethiopia in 1974. The 18th medical team handed over work to the 19th medical team sometime in September 2016.

project_name: 13th team sent
description: In January 2005, the Chinese government sent their 13th medical team to Ethiopia. The team consisted of 15 medical experts, 11 of whom were slotted to work in Addis Ababa, and 4 in Naz. The team was scheduled to be in Ethiopia for two years. It is unclear exactly when the team returned to China.

project_name: 19th team sent
description: In September 2016, the Chinese government sent their 19th medical team to Ethiopia. The 19th team was a continuation of medical cooperation between Ethiopia and China since 1974. Comprising 16 medical professionals, the 19th team was headed by Zhang Xiaoyang. Members of the medical team were from China's Henan province. The team was based at the Tirunesh-Beijing Ethio-China Friendship Hospital on the outskirts of Addis Ababa. The medical team was scheduled to stay in Ethiopia for 385 days, providing free consultation and operations at Tirunesh-Beijing and other hospitals.

project_name: 4 medical experts sent to help with Malaria prevention
description: According to the Ministry of Commerce of the People's Republic of China, from June 27 to August 10, 2009, 4 Chinese medical experts trained 20 doctors and government officials on malaria prevention in Ethiopia. They also helped install and adjust the anti-malaria equipment that China donated to the anti-malaria center in Nazrēt, Oromo.

project_name: Sent team to support the fight against Covid-19
description: On April 16, 2020, a twelve-person medical team arrived in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia from China to help the country contain the spread of Covid-19. During the team's fifteen-day visit, they visited treatment facilities and shared their experiences fighting the virus with their Ethiopian counterparts. The members of the team were selected from fields such as nosocomial sense, public health, nursing, traditional Chinese medicine, etc.  On the same flight that brought the medical team, there were also supplies donated by the Chinese government to the Ethiopian government (see Project ID#94525).

project_name: 17th team sent
description: In August 2013, the Chinese government deployed their 17th medical team to Ethiopia to Tirunesh-Beijing Hospital, also known as the Ethio-China Friendship Hospital, in Addis Ababa. Chinese medical teams working in Ethiopia have been sent to work at Tirunesh-Beijing hospital since its completion in 2012. A handover ceremony from the 17th to the 18th Chinese medical team to Ethiopia was held in July 2015.

project_name: 21st team donated orthopedic equipment & pharmaceuticals to Hospital
description: On July 18, 2019, the 21st Chinese medical team to Ethiopia donated orthopedic equipment and pharmaceuticals worth RMB 507,524 (close to $73,000) to the Tirunesh-Beijing Hospital (Ethio-China Friendship Hospital) on the outskirts of Addis Ababa. The donation was in line with an exchange of letters agreement signed by the Chinese Government on January 28, 2019.  The equipment was provided at a handover ceremony, which was held alongside a voluntary medical activity and a free consultation event hosted by the 21st medical team. In attendance at the handover ceremony were the entirety of the 21st batch of China's aid to Ethiopia medical team (16 members), as well as representatives from the Tirunesh-Beijing Hospital.

project_name: Ophthalmologist team offered services & donated medical equipments
description: On Apr. 28, 2014, a Chinese ophthalmologist team dispatched by the National Health and Family Planning Commission of China started providing ophthalmological services for free at Alert Hospital in Ethiopia's capital Addis Ababa. The team under the campaign, "Bright Journey" was composed of six specialists. Its service and technical exchanges and experience sharing with Ethiopian medical staffs ended on May 15, according to a statement from the Ethiopian side. The six specialists from Pecking Union Medical College hospital (PUMCH) of china arrived last Monday. They were expected to carry out site restoring operations for about 300 Ethiopian patients. They were deployed at Alert Hospital with medicines and medical equipment of advanced technology and consumables donated by China, which will stay permanently after the mission. Chinese Premier Li Keqiang visited the patients and doctors on May 5, 2014 during his visit to Ethiopia.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 17th team to hospitals
description:
Since 1977, Tianjin Province has been sending medical teams to Gabon. On July 28, 2011, the Chinese Government and the Government of Gabon signed a protocol agreement, dispatching the 17th Chinese medical team to Gabon. The team was stationed at the Sino-Gabonese Cooperation Hospital (Hôpital de la Coopération Sino-Gabonaise de Libreville) in the city of Libreville and the Sino-Gabonese Friendship Hospital (Hopital de L'amitie Sino Gabonaise) in the town of Franceville. The team completed its term of service between 2011 and 2013.
 
 The mission includes a team of 15 professionals in all medical specialties that will carry out diagnostic and therapeutic activities  and train staff in the Sino-Gabonese hospitals of Bellevis in Libreville and of the Sino-Gabonese Friendship Hospital in Franceville. As part of the agreement, the Chinese government will annually donate drugs and medical supplies to the two hospitals.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 19th team to hospitals
description: Since 1977, Tianjin Province has been sending medical teams to Gabon. In 2016, the Chinese Government and the Government of Gabon signed a memorandum of understanding, dispatching the 19th Chinese medical team to Gabon. The team consisted of 18 medical specialists, 3 health technicians, 1 block nurse, 2 interpreters and 2 cooks. It was stationed at the Sino-Gabonese Cooperation Hospital (Hôpital de la Coopération Sino-Gabonaise de Libreville) in the city of Libreville and the Sino-Gabonese Friendship Hospital (Hopital de L'amitie Sino Gabonaise) in the town of Franceville. The team completed its term of service between November 2, 2016 and August 13, 2018.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 15th team to hospitals
description: Since 1977, Tianjin Province has been sending medical teams to Gabon. On June 21, 2005, the Chinese Government and the Government of Gabon signed a protocol agreement, dispatching the 15th Chinese medical team to Gabon. The 27-member team was stationed at the Sino-Gabonese Cooperation Hospital (Hôpital de la Coopération Sino-Gabonaise de Libreville) in the city of Libreville and the Sino-Gabonese Friendship Hospital (Hopital de L'amitie Sino Gabonaise) in the town of Franceville. The team completed its term of service between December 4, 2006 and November 26, 2008.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 16th team hospitals
description: Since 1977, Tianjin Province has been sending medical teams to Gabon. In 2008, the Chinese Government dispatched the 15th Chinese medical team to Gabon. The team was stationed at the Sino-Gabonese Cooperation Hospital (Hôpital de la Coopération Sino-Gabonaise de Libreville) in the city of Libreville and the Sino-Gabonese Friendship Hospital (Hopital de L'amitie Sino Gabonaise) in the town of Franceville. The team completed its term of service between November 2008 and December 2010.

project_name: Sent peace ark medical mission
description: On October 9th, 2017, China's Peace Ark Hospital Ship was anchored in Gabon to provide free health care to locals. Hundreds of residents of Gabon received aid on the 178 meter long ship. The ship has 300 beds, 8 operation rooms, and 7 health care offices.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 13th team to hospitals
description: Since 1977, Tianjin Province has been sending medical teams to Gabon. On June 11, 2000, the Chinese Government and the Government of Gabon signed an exchange of letters, dispatching the 13th Chinese medical team to Gabon. The team was stationed at the Sino-Gabonese Cooperation Hospital (Hôpital de la Coopération Sino-Gabonaise de Libreville) in the city of Libreville and the Sino-Gabonese Friendship Hospital (Hopital de L'amitie Sino Gabonaise) in the town of Franceville. The team completed its term of service between 2001 and 2003.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 20th team to hospitals
description: The 20th Medical Team arrived in Gabon in July 27, 2018. The team was dispatched to Sino-Gabonese Cooperation Hospital in Libreville and Sino-Gabonese Friendship Hospital in Franceville.   On December 27, 2018, Ambassador Hu Changchun Met with President of the Gabonese embassy and the 20th batch of medical teams to aid the Franceville unit leader Sun Junjie and his party. Ambassador Hu listened to the report on the daily work of the Franceville Medical Team and the recent free clinics. He fully affirmed the hard work and boundless spirit of the medical team members, and together with Captain Sun, he promoted the improvement and enhancement of the medical assistance work in Gabon.   On August 2, 2019, the team was given awards by the Gabonese government for their service. Their term ended in late August as the 21st team arrived on August 21, 2019.

project_name: Sent medical assistance team for treatment & training
description: On April 28, 2011, the 9 members of the Wuhan General Hospital of Guangzhou Military Area Command of the Chinese People's Liberation Army returned to Hubei Province after serving for a year in Gabon. The medical assistance mission provided medical personnel and training to medical centers in Gabon. The doctors treated over 6,000 patients and trained over 300 medical workers in the Gabonese Army. The medical team also helped train the Gabonese doctors on new technology and new business. The amount of money this project entails and specific contact information is yet unknown.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 18th team to hospitals
description: Since 1977, Tianjin Province has been sending medical teams to Gabon. On February 21, 2014, the Chinese Government and the Government of Gabon signed a protocol agreement, dispatching the 18th Chinese medical team to Gabon. The team was stationed at the Sino-Gabonese Cooperation Hospital (Hôpital de la Coopération Sino-Gabonaise de Libreville) in the city of Libreville and the Sino-Gabonese Friendship Hospital (Hopital de L'amitie Sino Gabonaise) in the town of Franceville. The team completed its term of service between August 2014 and October 2016.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 14th team to hospitals
description: Since 1977, Tianjin Province has been sending medical teams to Gabon. On August 7, 2003, the Chinese Government and the Government of Gabon signed a protocol agreement, dispatching the 14th Chinese medical team to Gabon. The 27-member team was stationed at the Sino-Gabonese Cooperation Hospital (Hôpital de la Coopération Sino-Gabonaise de Libreville) in the city of Libreville and the Sino-Gabonese Friendship Hospital (Hopital de L'amitie Sino Gabonaise) in the town of Franceville. The team completed its term of service between September 2003 to September 2005.

project_name: Gov't provided loan for hospital rehabilitation & construction project
description: In 2005, China’s Ministry of Commerce provided a $3 million interest-free loan to the Government of Gabon for the Hospital Rehabilitation and Libreville Medical Team Housing Construction Project. This project involved the rehabilitation of the Sino-Gabonese Cooperation Hospital (Hôpital de la Coopération Sino-Gabonaise de Libreville) in the city of Libreville and the Sino-Gabonese Friendship Hospital (Hopital de L'amitie Sino Gabonaise) in the town of Franceville. It also involved the construction of housing for the Chinese medical team stationed in Libreville. Shanghai Construction Group (SCG) was the contractor responsible for implementation. The project started on February 12, 2006 and it ended on November 30, 2006. It was officially handed over to the local authorities on March 9, 2007.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 1st team to Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital
description: On March 14, 2017, China’s Ambassador to The Gambia Zhang Jiming and the Gambian Health and Social Welfare Minister Ceesay signed a protocol agreement on the dispatching of Chinese medical teams to work in The Gambia.   Then, on June 2, 2017, the Chinese Government dispatched the first Chinese medical team to the Gambia for a one-year mission. The team consisted of 9 members from Liaoning Province and it was stationed at Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital. Liu Guipeng and Xu Yongqing treated 605 patients, 159 patients with diagnosis and treatment of difficult diseases, 119 cases of surgery (8 cases of malignant tumors and complex operations), and more than 100 health services and medical services (Shengjing Hospital of China Medical University). The team's work was finished on June 22, 2018.  This was the first Chinese medical team sent since diplomatic ties were reinstated between China and Gambia in 2016, and the 16th Chinese medical team ever sent to Gambia. The second Chinese medical team and the third Chinese medical team that were dispatched to The Gambia (following the resumption of diplomatic ties in 2016) are captured in #60550, and #57444, respectively.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 2nd team to Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital
description: On December 13, 2017, the Chinese Government dispatched the second Chinese medical team to the Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital in Banjul. The medical team, which included 9 members, arrived with a donation of surgical instruments, baby health equipment and tablet medicines urgently needed by the hospital (as recorded in #56755). The team completed its term of service on June 30, 2019.

project_name: 4th team sent
description: On November 8, 2020, a team of 10 medical experts left Shenyang, Liaoning province for Banjul, Gambia. The team consisted of ten medical experts that specialize in gynecology, general surgery, orthopedics, anesthesia, and pediatrics. This team was to be in Gambia for one year, and work at Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital like the teams before them.   The team arrived on the same day as another group of Chinese medical workers dispatched to the Gambia on a special 3-month Covid prevention assignment. See project #92882 for more information.   China has been sending medical teams yearly to the Gambia since March 2017, when a protocol agreement on the dispatching of Chinese medical teams to work in The Gambia was signed. The agreement came after the restoration of diplomatic relations between China and the Gambia in 2016. The second Chinese medical team and the third Chinese medical team that were dispatched to the Gambia are captured in #60550, and #57444, respectively.

project_name: Dispatched medical expert team for Covid-19 aid
description: On November 8, 2020, China dispatched a special medical team to the Gambia to aid in COVID-19 response and prevention. The team consisted of nine experts from Shenyang, Liaoning, that specialized in critical care, infectious disease response, and respiratory medicine. This team was to be in the Gambia for three months.  The team was established by the Chinese National Health Commission and members were selected by the Liaoning Provincial Health Commission. During their stay in Gambia, they were to inspect local medical institutions, conduct training for Gambian medical staff, exchange and share China's pandemic experience, put forward prevention and control suggestions suitable for Gambia's situation, and carry out front-line clinical treatment when necessary.   A ceremony was held to celebrate the team's arrival in Banjul, the capital of Gambia, on November 9, 2020. The ceremony also celebrated the arrival of the fourth medical team dispatched to the Gambia, which arrived on the same day. See project # 94675 for more on the fourth team. Ma Jianchun, the Chinese Ambassador to Gambia, and the Gambian Minister of Health greeted the team at the airport.

project_name: Sent a 10-person team as part of the 'brightness action' campaign
description: On December 11, 2018, Ambassador Ma Jianchun and Minister Touray signed an agreement between the health departments of the China and Gambia to send a team of Chinese ophthalmologists to the Gambia to carry out cataract surgery in the next two months (Embassy of the People's Republic of China in the Republic of Gambia).  From January 19, 2019, to January 29, 2019, a team of Chinese medical experts went to the Sheikh Zayed Regional Eye Care Center in Kanifing, the Gambia. The "Bright Travel" medical team consisted of 10 experts from the Fourth Affiliated Hospital of China Medical University. These experts were to conduct a 10-day free cataract surgery at the eye center as part of the "Brightness Action" campaign. The head of the Chinese Medical Team, Dr. Leeyanhun Gung, said the medical experts form part of the fourth badge of doctors who successfully treated 206 patients during their 10-day visit. The Chinese Ambassador to The Gambia, Ma Jianchun, said that this eye-care project was initiated by the people’s Republic of China in 2004 to prevent and treat blindness in developing countries.  According to the medical team leader Liang Hongjun, the medical team also donated some medical equipment and medical consumables for the construction of the local eye hospital while carrying out cataract surgery in the Gambia. The medical equipment donation is recorded in project #56912. The value of these surgeries is unknown. This project is completed.

project_name: 3rd team sent to Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital
description: On June 21, 2019, a third group of medical teams arrived in Banjul at Gambia for one-year mission. On June 24th, a welcoming ceremony was held at the Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital, where the medical team will provide technical consultancy and carry out surgeries such as laparoscopic surgeries. According to the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in the Republic of Gambia source, this third medical team established working ties with the Ministry of Health and Edwards Francis Small Teaching Hospital. The amount of members involved in this medical team is unknown. This project is completed. This project is linked to the two previous medical teams sent to the Gambia in 2017 and 2018, recorded in projects #57017 and #60550.  On June 12, 2019, Ambassador Ma Jianchun met with the Chinese working group of the Zhonggang counterpart hospital cooperation project at the embassy. Ambassador Ma listened to the report of Yang Qing, the deputy dean of the Shengjing Hospital affiliated to China Medical University, the head of the Chinese working group on the cooperation between the hospital and the Gambia Edward Hospital in the field of obstetrics and gynecology to help build the gynecological endoscopy center.   On June 24, 2019, Ambassador Ma Jianchun met at the embassy with Director Fu Weili of the Liaoning Health Commission and the head of the third batch of Chinese medical aid teams. Ambassador Ma listened to reports on the handover of the second and third batches of medical teams, and the third batch of medical teams established working contacts with the Ministry of Health and Edward Teaching Hospital.   On July 11, 2019, Counselor Luo Wenjun, Attaché Bo Chuanjie, and Deng Hong of the West African Representative Office of the Economic Cooperation Zone of the Ministry of Commerce in the Gambia Embassy in the Gambia formed an inspection team to conduct a special safety inspection on the medical team. The inspection team visited the Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital and the camp where they were stationed. They focused on inspections of medical safety, camp safety and security.   Due to the pandemic, the doctors worked for over 18 months before they finished their mission and went back to China on January 10, 2021.

project_name: 1st medical assistance team
description:
In 2006, the Chinese Government and the Ghanaian Government signed a MoU on China sending medical teams to Ghana. The official documents were signed in 2007.
  The first medical team consist of 11 doctors from hospitals in Guangzhou. They arrived in Accra on Dec.30, 2009, and additional members arrived on Mar.9, 2010. The medical team would be working at the Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital in Accra.
 
 On June 22, 2011, the 1st medical team donated 870,000 RMB to the Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital (captured in #32345).

project_name: Gov't sent 9th team to China-Ghana Friendship Hospital
description: On December 28, 2019, the 9th Chinese medical team departed from the Guangdong province for Ghana. The team had 11 members, and was led by Shi Yongyong, the Director of the Anesthesiology Department of the Dade Road General Hospital of Guangdong Provincial Hospital  of Traditional Chinese Medicine. The team had a particular focus on disseminating Chinese traditional medical culture, treatments, and techniques.   During the 390 day mission, the team reportedly treated approximately 4,000 local patients, carried out 193 operations, rescued 24 critically ill patients, and conducted 21 trainings for local medical personnel. Notably, the team also worked closely with the Chinese embassy to create and promote a Covid-19 prevention and control plan, and diagnosed and treated approximately 300 people with Covid-19 during their time in Ghana.  The team returned to Guangdong on February 9, 2021. A welcome ceremony was held on the same day at the Health Plaza of Dade Road General Hospital, which was attended by Chen Zhusheng, deputy director of the Guangdong Provincial Health Commission, Zhang Jianhua, secretary of the party committee of Guangzhou University of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Lu Yubo, honorary president of Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Chen Dacan, president, and Zhai Lixiang, secretary of the party committee.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 3rd team to Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital
description: The 3rd Chinese medical team included 11 members from Guangdong Province who were stationed at Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital in Accra. They began their term of service on December 13, 2013, and during the summer of 2014, the team was involved in Ebola response efforts.  On September 12, 2013, the third medical team donated 400,000 RMB of medical supplies to Korle-Bu Hospital (captured in project #58088).

project_name: Gov't dispatched 5th team to Lekma Hospital
description: The 5th Chinese medical team included 10 members from Guangdong Province who were stationed at Lekma Hospital (or Teshie General Hospital or China-Ghana Friendship Hospital, located in the west of Teshie city.). They began their term of service between on December 12, 2015.  In November 2015, they carried out 209 free cataract surgeries. On May 26, 2016, the team granted 475,000 GHS to Lekma Hospital (captured in #57981).

project_name: Gov't dispatched 2nd team to Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital
description: The 2nd Chinese medical team included 11 members from Guangdong Province who were stationed at Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital in Accra. They completed their term of service between December 21, 2011 and December 13, 2013.  On August 1, 2012, the second medical team donated medical supplies worth $300,000 to Korle-Bu Hospital (captured in project #35241).

project_name: Deploed cardiovascular surgery team to Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital
description:
On November 30, 2015, China deployed a team of 10 cardiovascular surgery specialists to Ghana's Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital. There, they conducted surgeries and offered training to native surgeons. The team met with Business Counselor Li Jiang and Chinese Ambassador Sun Baohong upon arrival.
 
 The team spent two weeks in Ghana and was the first group of cardiovascular experts deployed by China to Africa. The team successfully completed 10 cases of miscellaneous cardiac surgery, 4 cases of pacemaker surgery, and 6 cases of mitral valve replacement.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 6th team to Lekma Hospital
description: The 6th Chinese medical team included members from Guangdong Province who were stationed at Lekma Hospital (or Teshie General Hospital or China-Ghana Friendship Hospital), which is located in the west of Teshie city.  They began their term of service between in 2016 and completed their term of service on December 13, 2017.

project_name: 10th team provided medicine supplies to traditional hospital
description: On July 20, 2021, the 10th Chinese medical team to Ghana donated 70 boxes of acupuncture needles, moxibustion tools, acupuncture charts, and other medical supplies to the China Traditional Herbal Hospital. This donation was made in order to encourage the practice of Traditional Chinese Medicine, or TCM.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 7th team to Lekma Hospital
description: The 7th Chinese medical team included members from Guangdong Province who were stationed at Lekma Hospital (or Teshie General Hospital or China-Ghana Friendship Hospital), located to the west of Teshie City. They completed their term of service between December 13, 2017 and December 10, 2018.

project_name: Dispatched 8th team to the China-Ghana Friendship Hospital
description: On December 10th, 2018 the Chinese Embassy in Ghana and Ghanaian Ministry of Health hosted a simultaneous farewell ceremony and welcome ceremony for the Seventh and Eighth batches of Chinese medical teams in Ghana. The arrival of the medical team is in accordance with an agreement signed by China and Ghana in 2007 (linked to project #32346). The transition ceremony was attended by Chinese Ambassador to Ghana H.E. Shi Ting Wang, Ghana's Minister of Health, Kwaku Agyeman-Manu, Deputy Party Secretary of the First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou University of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Guo Wenhai, Superintendent of the China-Ghana Friendship Hospital, Dr. Juliana Ameh, representatives of the Guangdong Provincial Health Department, representatives of the seventh and eighth batch of China medical teams, officials from the Ministry of Health, and some diplomats from the Embassy, according to the Chinese Embassy in Ghana the total attendance was at more than 90 people.  According to a Xinhua news release, the eighth medical team works alongside local doctors in the China-Ghana Friendship Hospital (LEKMA Hospital), and they offer free services to locals in the country's remote areas. The team was stationed in Ghana until the arrival of the ninth medical team whom arrived in Ghana on December 28, 2019.   China also donated 901,000 Chinese Yuan to the same hospital (see project #85701).

project_name: Gov't dispatched 1st team to Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital
description: On June 18, 2006, the Chinese Government and the Government of Ghana signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU), dispatching the first Chinese medical team to Ghana. Then, the two governments signed a protocol agreement on July 26, 2007. The 1st Chinese medical team included 11 doctors from hospitals in Guangzhou who were stationed at Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital in Accra. They completed their term of service between December 30, 2009 and December 28, 2011.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 4th team to Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital
description: The 4th Chinese medical team included 10 members from Guangdong Province who were stationed at Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital in Accra. They completed their term of service between December 13, 2014 and December 19, 2015. The team was sent by the Guangzhou Municipal Health System.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 17th team to Ignace Deen Hospital & other
description: The Chinese Government has sent the Republic of Guinea 26 medical teams since 1968. On March 3, 2000, the Chinese Government and the Republic of Guinea signed a protocol agreement dispatching the 17th medical team to Guinea. The 17th medical team consisted of 16 experts from the Beijing Municipal Bureau of Health who were stationed at Ignace Deen Hospital (科纳克里伊涅斯丁医院 or Hôpital Ignace Deen), Labé Regional Hospital (拉贝医 or Hôpital Régional de Labé), and the National Institute for Drug Quality Inspection (科纳克里药检所). The team completed its term of service between July 22, 2000 and September 2002.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 28th team to Sino-Guinean friendship hospital
description: On September 15th, 2020, the Chinese government sent the 28th medical team to Guinea for 18 months to work at China-Guinea Friendship Hospital, in the capital Conakry. The medical team consists of 21 members, who are experts in a variety of health areas such as rehabilitation, neurosurgery, neurology, cardiovascular disease, and radiology. 19 members of the team are from Xuanwu Hospital of Capital Medical University and 2 are from Beijing Municipal Center for Disease Control and Prevention and Beijing Municipal Health.  The medical team will work to develop the hospital into a top medical center for nerve diseases in Guinea and West Africa so that local patients with such diseases can receive high-quality diagnoses and treatments. Efforts will also be made by the team to intensify bilateral cooperation in health policy, health reform, and hospital management. During their stay, the team the had provided outpatient services to 1,834 patients, admitted 2,276 patients to the hospital, conducted 218 operations, provided diagnoses and examinations for 1,518 patients, and conducted emergency treatment in 674 cases. The Sino-Guinean Friendship Hospital is a major hospital built with assistance from the Chinese government (Project ID# 13330, 64425).

project_name: Gov't dispatched 21st team to Ignace Deen Hospital & other
description: The Chinese Government has sent the Republic of Guinea 26 medical teams since 1968. The 21st medical team consisted of 15 experts from Beijing Municipal Bureau of Health who were stationed at Ignace Deen Hospital (科纳克里伊涅斯丁医院 or Hôpital Ignace Deen), Labé Regional Hospital (拉贝医 or Hôpital Régional de Labé), and the National Institute for Drug Quality Inspection (科纳克里药检所). The team completed its term of service between August 16, 2008, to August 29, 2010.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 19th team to Ignace Deen Hospital & other
description: The Chinese Government has sent the Republic of Guinea 26 medical teams since 1968. On March 5, 2004, the Chinese Government and the Republic of Guinea signed a protocol agreement dispatching the 19th medical team to Guinea.  The 19th medical team consisted of 15 experts (including 13 medical experts and 2 auxiliary personnel) from the Beijing Municipal Bureau of Health who were stationed at Ignace Deen Hospital (科纳克里伊涅斯丁医院 or Hôpital Ignace Deen), Labé Regional Hospital (拉贝医 or Hôpital Régional de Labé), and the National Institute for Drug Quality Inspection (科纳克里药检所). The team completed its term of service between August 19, 2004 and June 30, 2006.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 4th batch of public health experts for Ebola response
description: On November 21, 2014, the fourth batch of Chinese public health experts were dispatched to Guinea to help combat Ebola. They were dispatched by China's National Health and Family Planning Commission. The three experts came from the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention, Beijing You An Hospital, and Peking University People's Hospital. The fourth batch was expected to return to China after a month of serving in Guinea. The Chinese Government dispatched four other batches of public health experts to Guinea over the course of 2014 (projects #36343, #64657, #85288, #64668)  The fourth batch of Chinese public health expert were responsible for monitoring the Ebola epidemic situation, assisting the Chinese medical team in the prevention and control of epidemic conditions, and diagnosing and treating major diseases in Chinese-funded institutions and Chinese and overseas Chinese in Guinea. The team also carried out educational activities to prevent and control the epidemic.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 1st batch of public health experts for Ebola response
description: On August 11, 2014, the first batch of Chinese public health experts were dispatched to Guinea to help combat Ebola. They were dispatched by China's National Health and Family Planning Commission. The three-person team returned to China on August 15, 2014. The Chinese Government dispatched four more batches of public health experts to Guinea over the course of 2014 (projects #85288, #64657, #64659, #64668)

project_name: Gov't dispatched 5th batch of public health experts for Ebola response
description: On December 22, 2014, the fifth batch of Chinese public health experts were dispatched to Guinea to help combat Ebola. They were dispatched by China's National Health and Family Planning Commission. The two out of three experts came from the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention and Beijing You An Hospital. They were expected to serve in Guinea for one month before returning to China. The Chinese Government dispatched four other batches of public health experts to Guinea over the course of 2014 (projects #36343, #64657, #64659, #85288)  While in Guinea, the three-person team trained over 1,000 local medical staff, government officials, and other community workers in Conakry, Guinea. They also cooperated with the 24th Chinese Medical team. Furthermore, the expert group will also provide training on Ebola virus prevention and control for Chinese-funded institutions in China and overseas Chinese.

project_name: 27th team sent for 18 months
description: On December 24, 2018, the Chinese Embassy in Guinea held a reception for the 27th medical team sent by Beijing Jishuitan Hospital to Guinea. The 19-member team arrived in Conakry on December 20, 2018. This medical team was expected to stay in Guinea for 18 months, during which time the doctors will provide various healthcare services. Due to Covid-19, the team stayed for 3 extra months. The team developed a number of new medical technologies and actively participated in the construction of China-Africa Friendship Hospitals and other key national tasks, laying a good foundation for future health cooperation between China and Guinea.  On September 18, 2020, the 27th medical team finished its service in Guinea. On the 22nd, the President of Guinea Alpha Conte awarded the Officer of the Guinea National Order of Honor to Captain Zhao Xingshan, and the Ministry of Health of Guinea awarded the medals to all the medical team members.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 26th team to Sino-Guinean friendship hospital
description: The Chinese Government has sent the Republic of Guinea 26 medical teams since 1968. The 26th medical team consisted of 19 members (17 medical experts, a translator, and a chef) from a hospital in Beijing. They were stationed at the Sino-Guinean Friendship Hospital (Hôpital De L'amitié Sino-Guinéen), which is located in Kipé district and the municipality of Ratoma. The team completed its term of service between July 12, 2017 and December 24, 2018.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 20th team to Ignace Deen Hospital & other
description: The Chinese Government has sent the Republic of Guinea 26 medical teams since 1968. The 20th medical team consisted of 15 healthcare professionals from Beijing's Xuanwu Hospital who were stationed at Ignace Deen Hospital (科纳克里伊涅斯丁医院 or Hôpital Ignace Deen), Labé Regional Hospital (拉贝医 or Hôpital Régional de Labé), and the National Institute for Drug Quality Inspection (科纳克里药检所) in Guinea. The team completed its term of service between August 16, 2006 and August 2008. The 15 members helped treat 31,000 patients, conduct 19,777 outpatient operations and 1,555 surgeries, and train 178 local medics in advanced healthcare management procedures.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 25th team to Sino-Guinean friendship hospital
description: The Chinese Government has sent 26 medical teams to the Republic of Guinea since 1968. The 25th medical team consisted of 19 members from Beijing Tongren Hospital. They were stationed at the Sino-Guinean Friendship Hospital (Hôpital De L'amitié Sino-Guinéen), which is located in Kipé district and the municipality of Ratoma. The team completed its term of service between January 18, 2016, and July 22, 2017. It formulated a comprehensive Ebola prevention and control training plan and trained nearly 1,700 Guinean staff.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 24th team to Sino-Guinean friendship hospital
description: The Chinese Government has sent the Republic of Guinea 26 medical teams since 1968. The 24th medical team consisted of 19 members from a hospital in Beijing. They were stationed at the Sino-Guinean Friendship Hospital (Hôpital De L'amitié Sino-Guinéen), which is located in the Kipé district and the municipality of Ratoma. The team completed its term of service between August 16, 2014 and January 13, 2016. It formulated a comprehensive Ebola prevention and control training plan and trained nearly 1,700 Guinean staff.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 22nd team to Ignace Deen Hospital & other
description: The Chinese Government has sent the Republic of Guinea 26 medical teams since 1968. On December 30, 2009, the Chinese Government and the Republic of Guinea signed a protocol agreement dispatching the 22nd medical team to Guinea. The 22nd medical team consisted of 16 members (with expertise in neurosurgery, neurology, internal medicine, general surgery, orthopedics, anesthesiology, radiology, ultrasound, pharmacy, laboratory, operating room, acupuncture, and cooking) from the Beijing’s Tiantan Hospital who were stationed at Ignace Deen Hospital (科纳克里伊涅斯丁医院 or Hôpital Ignace Deen), Labé Regional Hospital (拉贝医 or Hôpital Régional de Labé), and the National Institute for Drug Quality Inspection (科纳克里药检所). The team completed its term of service between August 25, 2010 and September 2012.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 2nd batch of public health experts for Ebola response
description: On August 16, 2014, the second batch of Chinese public health experts were dispatched to Guinea to help combat Ebola. They were dispatched by China's National Health and Family Planning Commission. The three experts came from the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention, Ditan Hospital, and Peking Union Medical College Hospital. It is unclear when this team returned to China. The Chinese Government dispatched four other batches of public health experts to Guinea over the course of 2014 (projects #36343, #64657, #64659, #64668)

project_name: Gov't dispatched 18th team to Ignace Deen Hospital & other
description: The Chinese Government has sent the Republic of Guinea 26 medical teams since 1968. On April 24, 2002, the Chinese Government and the Republic of Guinea signed a protocol agreement dispatching the 18th medical team to Guinea. The 18th medical team consisted of 14 experts (including 12 medical experts and two auxiliary personnel) from the Beijing Municipal Bureau of Health who were stationed at Ignace Deen Hospital (科纳克里伊涅斯丁医院 or Hôpital Ignace Deen), Labé Regional Hospital (拉贝医 or Hôpital Régional de Labé), and the National Institute for Drug Quality Inspection (科纳克里药检所). The team completed its term of service between August 2002 and September 2004.  According to the protocol agreement, the Government of Guinea was responsible for covering international plane tickets, housing, basic medical equipment, sales taxes, and duty fees. The Chinese Government paid the salaries of the 14-member team.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 23rd team to Sino-Guinean friendship hospital
description: The Chinese Government has sent the Republic of Guinea 26 medical teams since 1968. The 23rd medical team consisted of 19 members from Beijing Anzhen Hospital. They were stationed at the Sino-Guinean Friendship Hospital (Hôpital De L'amitié Sino-Guinéen), which is located in Kipé district and the municipality of Ratoma. The team completed its term of service between August 16, 2012 and August 18, 2014.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 3rd batch of public health experts for Ebola response
description: On October 17, 2014, the third batch of Chinese public health experts were dispatched to Guinea to help combat Ebola. They were dispatched by China's National Health and Family Planning Commission. The three experts came from the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention, Beijing Youan Hospital, and Peking University People's Hospital. The third batch returned to China on November 13, 2014. The Chinese Government dispatched four other batches of public health experts to Guinea over the course of 2014 (projects #36343, #85288, #64659, #64668)  While in Guinea, the expert group visited the WHO offices in Guinea several times to understand the epidemic situation, analyzed the latest epidemic data in a timely manner, summarized the control experience, and wrote a work report for domestic and embassies and business offices for reference. They also held lectures for the Chinese in Guinea and Chinese-funded institutions to popularize knowledge about epidemic prevention and control of common tropical diseases. The experts guided the China Embassy and Chinese-funded organizations in disinfection and insecticide work, helped local Chinese-funded organizations to investigate and control loopholes, and developed targeted and practical prevention and control plans based on local conditions. They also assisted Chinese medical teams, the Sino-Guinea Hospital, and other local hospitals diagnose and treat patients.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 8th team to Hospital Nacional Simão Mendes
description: Since the Government of Guinea-Bissau resumed diplomatic relations with the PRC in 1998, Sichuan Province has been sending medical teams to Guinea-Bissau every two years. On June 16, 2000, the Chinese Government and the Government of Guinea-Bissau signed a protocol agreement, dispatching the 8th Chinese medical team to Guinea-Bissau. The 18-member team was stationed at Hospital Nacional Simão Mendes in Bissau. The team completed its term of service between 2000 and 2002.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 14th team to China-Guinea-Bissau friendship hospital
description: Since the Government of Guinea-Bissau resumed diplomatic relations with the PRC in 1998, Sichuan Province has been sending medical teams to Guinea-Bissau every two years. In 2012, the Chinese Government dispatched the 14th Chinese medical team to Guinea-Bissau. The team included experts in internal medicine, surgery, pediatrics, obstetrics and gynecology, imaging, ultrasound, nursing, anesthesia, and acupuncture. It was stationed at China-Guinea-Bissau Friendship Hospital (Hospital de Amizade Sino-Guineense) in the Brá neighborhood within the city of Bissau. The 17-member team completed its term of service between September 17, 2012 and October 15, 2014. It reportedly completed 60,000 outpatient visits and 20 free consultations.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 16th team to China-Guinea-Bissau friendship hospital
description: Since the Government of Guinea-Bissau resumed diplomatic relations with the PRC in 1998, Sichuan Province has been sending medical teams to Guinea-Bissau every two years. In 2016, the Chinese Government dispatched the 16th Chinese medical team to Guinea-Bissau. The team was stationed at China-Guinea-Bissau Friendship Hospital (Hospital de Amizade Sino-Guineense) in the Brá neighborhood within the city of Bissau. It completed its term of service between December 27, 2016 and December 2018. On December 19, 2018, an award ceremony for the 16th Chinese medical team was held in Bissau. The Chinese Ambassador to Guinea-Bissau Jin Hongjun attended the ceremony, and certificates of honor were awarded to all members of the 16th medical team. On the same day, the 17th Chinese medical team was welcomed to Guinea-Bissau, and the 16th medical team project was completed.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 12th team to Canchungo Regional Hospital
description: Since the Government of Guinea-Bissau resumed diplomatic relations with the PRC in 1998, Sichuan Province has been sending medical teams to Guinea-Bissau every two years. In 2008, the Chinese Government dispatched the 12th Chinese medical team to Guinea-Bissau. The team was stationed at Canchungo Regional Hospital in the town of Cacheu. The team completed its term of service between 2008 and 2010.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for team housing construction project
description: In 2011, China’s Ministry of Commerce provided a grant to the Government of Guinea-Bissau for the Chinese Medical Team Housing Construction Project. According to email correspondence between AidData’s Executive Director and the Director General of the Office of the Secretary of State for Planning and Regional Integration in Guinea-Bissau, the monetary value of this grant commitment was CFA 328,276,800. The purpose of this project was to build housing for Chinese medical teams stationed at the China-Guinea-Bissau Friendship Hospital (Hospital de Amizade Sino-Guineense) in the Brá neighborhood within the city of Bissau. It involved the construction housing units with kitchens, bathrooms, and central air conditioning. Table tennis, volleyball, and badminton courts were also built for team recreation. The project also involved the construction of water tower and a 90kW generator to provide utilities. Jiangsu Jangdu Construction Co., Ltd. was the contractor responsible for implementation. Construction began on June 26, 2011 and the project was completed on March 28, 2012.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 13th team to Canchungo Regional Hospital
description: Since the Government of Guinea-Bissau resumed diplomatic relations with the PRC in 1998, Sichuan Province has been sending medical teams to Guinea-Bissau every two years. In 2010, the Chinese Government dispatched the 13th Chinese medical team to Guinea-Bissau. The team was stationed at Canchungo Regional Hospital in the town of Cacheu. The 8-member team completed its term of service between September 2010 and September 22, 2012.

project_name: Experts sent to hold Ebola prevention training course
description:
On December 23, 2014, the opening ceremony of the Ebola fever prevention and control training conducted by Chinese public health experts in Guinea-Bissau was held in Guinea-Bissau's China-Guinea Friendship Hospital. This trip by Chinese experts was set to last for 32 days.This project was conducted with the assistance of the China (Sichuan) Medical Team for Africa. This aid project is for the training of 500 of Guinea-Bissau's medical staff, community workers and volunteers, and other related personnel. The training content was mainly on the prevention and control of Ebola virus disease. On January 8, 2015, the public health physician training group of experts from Sichuan trained 43 medical personnel. 
 
 China funded 1 million CNY for the Ebola emergency in 2014, the cost of this training project may be included in that transaction amount (see project #52352).

project_name: 17th team sent
description: In 2018, the Chinese Government dispatched the 17th Chinese medical team from Sichuan to Guinea-Bissau. The team was stationed at the Kasongo Hospital in the Cacheu District and the China-Guinea-Bissau Friendship Hospital within the capital city of Guinea-Bissau. It completed its term of service between December 19, 2018 and April 20, 2021. On February 25, 2021, an award ceremony for the 17th Chinese medical team was held in Bissau. Guinea-Bissau Public Health Minister Deuna, Chinese ambassador to Guinea-Bissau, Guo Ce, other officials, and all members of China’s 17th batch of Guinea-Bissau medical team attended the ceremony. On April 20, 2021, the 18th Chinese medical team was welcomed to Guinea-Bissau, and the 17th medical team completed its service.

project_name: Team donated medical supplies to hospital in Canchungo
description: On October 7, 2014, a handover ceremony was held for the Chinese medical team's donations of medical supplies to the city hospital in Canchungo City, Cacheu District. Wang Hau, the Chinese Ambassador at the time, was present at the ceremony.

project_name: 12 medical experts sent for ophthalmic cataract restoration surgery
description: On July 28, 2018, China sent a team of 12 medical experts to assist Guinea-Bissau with an ophthalmic cataract restoration surgery project. On July 31, a launching ceremony was held for the project at the Hospital Nacional Simão Mendes. Through this project, which is generally known in African countries as the 'Bright Action' project, these Chinese medical experts provided assistance in Guinea-Bissau. The expert team included 6 ophthalmologists from the Sichuan Provincial People's Hospital, 3 ophthalmologists from the Hospital Centre S. Januario of Macao Special Administrative Region, etc..  As part of this project, the Chinese experts provided free cataract surgeries for those in need, donated medical equipment, and provided technical training to local medical officials The team screened more than 400 patients and completed 216 cataract operations during their stay in Guinea-Bissau. On August 10, the President of Guinea-Bissau gathered the medical team and thanked them for their aid to Guinea-Bissau. The project ended on August 11, 2018.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 15th team to China-Guinea-Bissau friendship hospital
description: Since the Government of Guinea-Bissau resumed diplomatic relations with the PRC in 1998, Sichuan Province has been sending medical teams to Guinea-Bissau every two years. In 2014, the Chinese Government dispatched the 15th Chinese medical team to Guinea-Bissau. The team was stationed at China-Guinea-Bissau Friendship Hospital (Hospital de Amizade Sino-Guineense) in the Brá neighborhood within the city of Bissau. It completed its term of service between 2014 and December 27, 2016. In December 2015, as part of this medical mission, 13 doctors provided free medications and consultations, treated cases of malaria and influenza, provided advice to about 200 residents of King's Island near Bissau. In addition, they gave free consultations in the regions of Bafatá, Gabú and Cacheu, where some villages lack health centers.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 10th team to Hospital Nacional Simão Mendes

project_name: Gov't dispatched 11th team to Hospital Nacional Simão Mendes

project_name: Gov't dispatched 8th team to Motebang Hospital
description: Since 1997, Hubei Province has been sending medical teams to Lesotho every 2 years. On June 21, 2011, the Chinese Government and the Government of Lesotho signed a protocol agreement, dispatching the 8th Chinese medical team (第八批医疗队) to Lesotho. The team was stationed at Motebang Hospital, which is located on Mandela Road in the town of Hlotse within Leribe District. The 8-member team completed its term of service between September 2011 and September 2013. The team treated 45,000 patients, conducted 1,133 operations, donated equipment, and trained more than 100 local medical personnel.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 7th team to Queen Elizabeth II Hospital
description: Since 1997, Hubei Province has been sending medical teams to Lesotho every 2 years. On March 31, 2009, the Chinese Government and the Government of Lesotho signed a protocol agreement, dispatching the 7th Chinese medical team (第七批医疗队) to Lesotho. The team was stationed at Queen Elizabeth II Hospital, located in the capital city of Maseru. The 15-member team completed its term of service between late June 2009 and June 28, 2011.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 9th team to Motebang Hospital
description: Since 1997, Hubei Province has been sending medical teams to Lesotho every 2 years. In March 2013, the Chinese Government and the Government of Lesotho signed a protocol agreement, dispatching the 9th Chinese medical team (第九批医疗队) to Lesotho.
