However, it began sending teams again in 2002. On August 10, 2007, the Chinese Government and the Government of Sierra Leone signed a protocol agreement, dispatching the 13th Chinese medical team to Sierra Leone. The 10-member team was stationed at King Harman Road Hospital in the capital city of Freetown.   It completed its term of service between July 2007 and July 2009. The members of the team had expertise in internal medicine, surgery, pediatrics, gynecology, ear-nose-throat, ophthalmology, anesthesia, and radiology.

project_name: Implemented phase 1 of maternal & child health project
description: On August 12, 2016, Chinese Ambassador to Sierra Leone Zhao Yanbo and Sierra Leone's Minister of Health Fofana signed an agreement on China's "Bright Walk" activity for cataract surgery in Sierra Leone and a maternal and child health project. According to the embassy website, China will provide training on children's first aid, disease screening, growth and nutrition monitoring. In November 2016, the project was officially launched as the doctors from Hunan Children's Hospital arrived in Sierra Leone to perform medical inspection and treatment for Sierra Leonean children, as well as to arrange academic exchange between pediatricians.   The second phase of this project began in 2018 (#63046).

project_name: Gov't agreed to dispatch teams to King Harman Road Hospital
description: On October 17, 2002, the Government of the People's Republic of China signed an agreement with the Government of the Republic of Sierra Leone agreeing to send a medical team to provide training to local doctors and assist in public health work. The team was to take up residency at the King Harman Road Hospital in Freetown and eventually extend their services to other provinces.  The first dispatch of medical teams occurred in December 2002, and Chinese medical activities have been ongoing as of October 2006.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 21st medical expert team friendship hospital
description: On June 22, 2019, the Chinese Government dispatched a 21st medical expert team to the Sierra Leone-China Friendship Hospital (中塞友好医院) at Jui. On June 27, 2019, the Chinese Embassy in Sierra Leone commemorated the arrival of the team with a China-Sierra Leone Public Health Cooperation Reception.  The team, led by Dr. Jiang Haibo of Central South University's Xiangya Hospital, was comprised of 20 members, 19 of these being medical professionals. The team treated patients for infectious diseases and cataracts. The team also supported Sierra Leone's COVID-19 response following the outbreak of the virus. The medical mission lasted 15 months, with the team returning to China on October 11, 2020, marking the project's completion.  During the team's 15-month mission, they carried out a large number of operations, and have diagnosed and treated a total of 21,740 patients. Nearly 300 surgeries were performed, 34,781 various tests were carried out, and 374 members of medical and nursing staff were taught by clinical training. As part of the mission, on November 30, 2019, 19 medical experts from the 21st China Medical Team partnered with the Confucius Institute of the University of Sierra Leone to provide free medical services to Sierra Leoneans at an event held at the University of Sierra Leone in Freetown. The team included specialists in internal medicine, surgery, traditional Chinese medicine, infectious diseases, and ophthalmology. At the event, the specialists provided first aid and infectious disease prevention education, carried out physical exams, and offered treatment.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 14th team to King Harman Road Hospital
description: China has been sending medical teams to Sierra Leone from Hunan Province since 1973. China stopped sending medical teams in 1993 due to civil conflict and political instability. However, it began sending teams again in 2002. On January 14, 2009, the Chinese Government and the Government of Sierra Leone signed an agreement, dispatching the 14th Chinese medical team to Sierra Leone. (中国向塞拉利昂派遣医疗队议定书在弗里敦签订).The 10-member team was stationed at King Harman Road Hospital in the capital city of Freetown. It completed its term of service between July 16, 2009 and April 20, 2011. The members of the team had expertise in internal medicine, surgery, pediatrics, ear-nose-throat, ophthalmology, anesthesia, and traditional Chinese medicine.

project_name: Team trained medical workers in combating Covid-19
description: In spring 2020, a Chinese medical team sent by the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention (an institute under the National Health Commission) trained Sierra Leonean medical workers to help the latter combat COVID-19, as Sierra Leone registered its first case on March 31, 2020. As of April 6, 2020, the medical team trained around 100 medical workers in Sierra Leone. The medical team has helped medical workers with specific training, including the proper way to wear masks.   This medical team is one of fourteen sent to Africa by the National Health Commission of China to help combat the COVID-19 pandemic.  The medical team's visit included a two day training session held on March 27th-28th, 2020. The training course consisted of two parts, theory and practice, presided over by Doris, Director of the Laboratory Management Division of the Ministry of Health of Sierra Leone. Fifteen technical officers and managers from Sierra Leone's Southern and Western Provinces participated in the training.  The theoretical training consisted of laboratory management strategy in times of crisis, classification of COVID infection symptoms, transmission, global epidemic situation, and China's prevention and control strategies and experience, how to improve the quality of collection of suspected case samples, and COVID-19 clinical laboratory preparation and response guidance plan. On the second day, practical training was conducted in the clinical laboratory of Bo City Government Hospital, including how the sampling personnel should do a good job in personal protection, as well as the collection, packaging, transfer and receiving process of samples from suspected cases of COVID.

project_name: 1st military medical experts team sent
description:
In July 2016, Chinese military sent a team of 10 medical experts from the People's Liberation Army 302 Hospital and Chinese Military Medical Institution to Sierra Leone to work with the medical staffs of 34 military hospital of Sierra Leone's Armed Forces (中国首批援塞军事医学专家). Their duty included establishing the Mobile Electronic Surveillance System for Infectious Diseases (MESSID) which was the first Modern infectious disease prevention and control system in Sierra Lone. The medical team also treated many local patients, trained local nurses and doctors, and sent 15 excellent medical personnel to China for further studying. At the same time, they carried out a number of medical research in malaria, typhoid fever, hepatitis, HIV, Ebola and unknown-origins fevers.
 
 On June 2, 2017, a farewell ceremony was held by the Chinese embassy to see the team off to China. Approximately 120 guests attended the event, including the Honorable Acting Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Ms. Isata Kabia, Honorable Deputy Minister II of Health & Sanitation Mrs. Zulainatu Cooper, as well as the 60 Chinese doctors, nurses and health experts.

project_name: 3 public health experts sent
description: On August 17, 2014, a team of three Chinese medical experts (Xu Daomiao, Sha Xinping, and Zhang Heng) landed at the Lungi International Airport in Freetown. The experts worked with the 16th medical assistance team at King Harman Road Hospital, helped monitor the China-Sierra Leone Friendship Hospital, and trained local medical staff on disease control. They returned to China on 17 September 2014, after the arrival of a 59-person CDC medical team and a mobile laboratory in Sierra Leone.

project_name: 3rd medical & laboratory team sent to fight Ebola
description: On January 17, 2015,  medical and laboratory personnel from Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention and the 302 Military Hospital of China arrived in Freetown, Sierra Leone to exchange the second team. This team has a special expert group and includes more experienced nurses compared to the previous two teams. The team will work in the China-Sierra Leone Friendship Hospital for 2 months.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 17th team friendship hospital
description: China has been sending medical teams to Sierra Leone from Hunan Province since 1973. China stopped sending medical teams in 1993 due to civil conflict and political instability. However, it began sending teams again in 2002. On November 4th and 6th, 2015, the Chinese Government and the Government of Sierra Leone signed an exchange of letters, dispatching the 17th Chinese medical team to Sierra Leone. The 10-member team was stationed at the Sierra Leone-China Friendship Hospital in the town of Jui. It completed its term of service between late 2015 and 2016.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 16th team to King Harman Road Hospital
description: China has been sending medical teams to Sierra Leone from Hunan Province since 1973. China stopped sending medical teams in 1993 due to civil conflict and political instability. However, it began sending teams again in 2002. On April 10, 2013, the Chinese Government and the Government of Sierra Leone signed an agreement, dispatching the 16th Chinese medical team to Sierra Leone.   The 10-member team was stationed at King Harman Road Hospital in the capital city of Freetown. It was supposed to complete its term of service between 2013 and 2015. However, after 5 months of the Ebola outbreak, the King Harman Road Hospital was shut down in October 2014.

project_name: 2nd team donated medicine & equipment to Juba Teaching Hospital
description: On August 15, 2014, China's second medical team in South Sudan donated medicine and medical equipment worth 400,000 RMB to Juba Teaching Hospital. The materials donated were used to treat patients at the hospital.

project_name: 2nd team held clinic in Torit
description:
From November 28-30, 2014, the second Chinese medical team in South Sudan held a clinic at the Eastern Equatoria State Hospital in Torit. The team treated over 1,000 patients and performed three operations. Chinese institutions such as Huawei, China Hydropower, Shandong Expressway, Fanhua, and AVIC International were reported to have assisted in organizing the clinic, but the exact nature of their assistance is unknown.
 
 The second Chinese medical team arrived in South Sudan in February 2014 (#60732).

project_name: 7th team held clinic & distributed medicine at University in Malakal
description: On August 10, 2019, the seventh Chinese medical team to South Sudan (project #59020) visited Upper Nile University in Malakal and held a free clinic. During this visit, they treated more than one thousand patients and distributed over CNY 50,000 of medicines.  See project #59020 for details about the team's general mission.

project_name: 2nd team sent
description:
On October 21, 2013, the Chinese Ambassador to South Sudan and the South Sudanese Minister of Health signed a memorandum of understanding for China to send its second medical team to South Sudan. The team arrived in South Sudan on February 26, 2014 and the South Sudanese Ministry of Health held a welcome ceremony for them on March 3, 2014. The team consisted of 12 members from Anhui province.
 
 In August 2014, the team donated a set of medical equipment worth CNY 400,000 to Juba Hospital (#31211). From November 28-30, the team held a clinic in Torit, South Sudan (captured in #60806). From January 26-31, 2015, the team held a clinic in Rumbek, South Sudan (captured in #53333). The second medical team departed from South Sudan on March 19, 2015, when the third medical team arrived (#59012).

project_name: 5th medical offers free consultations & donated medicine in Rumbek
description: From March 26th to March 29th, 2018, the fifth Chinese medical team deployed to South Sudan (see: project ID #59017) conducted free medical consultations in the city of Rumbek, South Sudan. The team diagnosed and treated more than 2,000 patients and performed 13 surgeries. They also donated more than 300 kinds of medicine.

project_name: 4th team sent
description: On December 15, 2015, Chinese Ambassador to South Sudan Ma Qiang signed a memorandum of understanding pledging to send China's fourth medical team to South Sudan. The team arrived in South Sudan on March 28, 2016. From January 23 to 26, 2017, they went to see patients in Yei, Yapa, Rumbek, Torit, and Yirol. From March 14 to March 23, 2017 the team traveled to the cities of Kaujok and Wau to attend over 5,000 patients. The 4th medical team consists of 15 people from Anhui Province. On May 3, 2017, the Chinese Embassy in South Sudan held a ceremony to send off the 4th medical team and welcome the 5th team. This project is completed.

project_name: 6th team sent
description:
On May 3, 2018, the 6th Chinese medical team consisting of 15 doctors from Anhui Province arrived in South Sudan. As of the end of March 2019, the team had treated 5,784 patients with outpatient procedures and 1,159 with inpatient procedures, including saving the lives of 538 critically ill patients. On May 4, 2019, the Chinese Embassy in South Sudan held a ceremony officially sending off the sixth medical team and welcoming the seventh.
 
 See projects #71433 and #71422 for specific acts performed by this team.

project_name: 7th team sent
description: On May 3, 2019, the Chinese Embassy in South Sudan held a ceremony to send off the sixth medical team and welcome the seventh medical team to South Sudan. On August 10, 2019, this team visited Upper Nile University in Malakal and held a clinic (project #60776). On December 22, 2019, the team donated milk, biscuits and provided medical consultations to minors at Confident Children out of Conflict (CCC), a Juba-based orphanage for vulnerable children lacking parental care (project #71188). The seventh medical team included 13 medical specialists in fields such as obstetrics and gynecology, general surgery, internal medicine and pediatrics, as well as 2 support staff.   The seventh medical team's mission lasted 17 months and ended in September 2020. During their mission they provided about 8,000 free medical consultations across South Sudan.

project_name: 5th team donated medical equipments
description: On January 20, 2018, the fifth Chinese Medical Team granted medical equipment and medicine to Juba Teaching Hospital in South Sudan. The Chinese National Health and Family Planning Commission and the People's Government of Anhui Province and Hefei City funded the donations to the hospital including more than 350 kinds of medicine, medical equipment and medical consumables.

project_name: Anti-epidemic team sent
description: On August 19, 2020, an arrival ceremony was held to celebrate the arrival of a Chinese anti-epidemic medical team in South Sudan. The team consists of 8 medical and nursing experts and they will work in South Sudan for nine days. The team specializes in the fields of laboratory technology, infection, insensitive care, public health, and nursing. During their nine-day residency, the medical team will work with senior South Sudanese government officials, local health experts, medical institutions, and medical staff on COVID-19 prevention and response.   During the ceremony, the Chinese government also donated anti-epidemic supplies to South Sudan (Project ID#94236).   On August 27, 2020, the medical team finished their mission and held a work summary report meeting.

project_name: 1st team sent
description: In January 2012, China agreed to send a medical team to South Sudan to provide health services after the establishment of the country in 2011. China dispatched the first medical team in December 2012. The Department of Health of Anhui province is responsible for sending the 12-member team to Juba Hospital in South Sudan. On July 3, 2013, it was reported by the South Sudan’s Health Minister Dr. Micheal Milly Hussein that Chinese doctors working at Juba Teaching Hospital had their stay extended by one year.  They delayed their return again due to turmoil in December 2013. On January 10, 2014, they received a certificate of honor from the South Sudanese Minister of Health, and on January 13, 2014, the team returned to China, marking the completion of their mission.

project_name: 6th team donated food & medical assistance to Juba Orphanage
description: On June 1, 2018, China's sixth medical team donated foodstuffs and treated children with eye and skin infections at Juba Orphanage in South Sudan. The total value of this donation is unknown.  See project #59019 for details about the team's general mission.

project_name: Embassy dispatched 7th medical aid team
description: On January 14, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in South Sudan sent the seventh batch of medical aid teams to the Upper Nile State in South Sudan to set up free health clinics. The medical team was at the clinics until January 17, 2020, and during those three days, the team diagnosed and treated about 1,000 local patients, performed 4 surgical operations, trained 9 local medical staff, helped solve more than 70 difficult cases, and held 1 medical knowledge lecture.  On January 17, 2020, China’s Ambassador to South Sudan, Hua Ning, made a trip to visit the medical team members at the free clinics. The Governor of the Northbound Nile State of South Sudan met with Ambassador Hua and his delegation at the Farouji Airport. Zhou Zuokun, the Deputy General Manager of CNPC International Nile Company, and Bol Luath Deng, the Mayor of Melut County, joined the Ambassador on his visit to the clinics. Ambassador Hua went to the Faroji Friendship Hospital, which was built with the aid of PetroChina, to visit the seventh medical team in South Africa at their free clinics in the hospital.   PetroChina, PetroChina Engineering and Construction Corporation, and other Chinese-funded enterprises in South Africa have provided strong logistical support and local coordination support for the free clinic activities. This is the seventh batch of medical aid teams provided by the Chinese Embassy to run free clinics in South Sudan. Previous teams have run clinics in Bor, Yei, Yapa, Rumbek, Torit, Irol, Wau, Kovachok and other areas.

project_name: CDC expert team inspected the work of prevention & control of Ebola
description: From September 2, 2019 to September 14, 2019,  an expert team of three from the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention went to South Sudan to inspect the work of  prevention and control of Ebola. The expert team visited the South Sudan Ministry of Health, the Health Emergency Command Center, the Central Public Health Laboratory, the Juba Ebola Isolation Treatment Center, the Juba Teaching Hospital, and the Juba International Airport monitoring point. Ambassador Hua Ning also rushed to South Yei State on the border with the Congo (Kinshasa) to inspect the local preparations for Ebola prevention and control, visited primary medical departments, and inspected local medical facilities. The expert group listened to reports on the prevention and control of Ebola from the national and local health departments in South Africa, discussed with the South Ministry of Health, WHO, and Ebola prevention and control experts in Yei State, and discussed the high incidence of malaria, tuberculosis, hepatitis B and HIV in South Africa. The disease prevention and control work was exchanged.   In addition, the expert team conducted lectures and trainings on basic knowledge of the prevention and control of infectious diseases such as Ebola and malaria for Chinese-funded enterprises and overseas Chinese in South Africa, conducted professional exchanges with the Chinese medical team for South Africa, and went to relevant Chinese-funded enterprises to learn about infections. He also participated in the diagnosis and treatment of malaria patients in many Chinese-funded enterprises.

project_name: 9th team sent
description: On September 6, 2021, the Chinese government sent their ninth medical team to South Sudan. This team will replace the eighth team sent by the Chinese government. The team will be stationed at Juba Teaching Hospital to train South Sudanese doctors and carry out treatment on patients at the hospital. The team is composed of doctors from the Anhui Province in East China.  On October 10, 2021, the medical team went to a children's home to provide psychosocial support and free medical care services. On September 8, 2022, a send-off and award ceremony was held to thank the medical team for their services and to celebrate the completion of their visit.

project_name: 3rd team sent
description:
On March 19, 2015, the Chinese Ambassador to South Sudan and South Sudanese Minister of Health signed an MOU about China's medical teams to South Sudan. At this meeting, the Minister of Health warmly welcomed the arrival of the third Chinese medical team consisting of 12 people from Anhui province. On March 2, 2016, the team received a certificate of honor from the South Sudanese Ministry of Health.
 
 The fourth medical team arrived on March 28, 2016, ending the term for the third medical team.

project_name: 6th team provided over 1400 free consultations
description: From February 12th to February 15th, 2019, the sixth Chinese medical team (see: #59019) sent to South Sudan gave out free consultations to patients at the Paloch Friendship Hospital in the Upper Nile State of South Sudan. The doctors attended over 1400 patients, performed 9 surgical operations (including one case of AIDS), gave out 2 lectures, discussed cases with local doctors 2 times, and guided 15 surgical operations. The total monetary value of these activities is unknown.

project_name: 6th team provided free consultations in Bor
description: From March 11th to March 15th, 2019, China's sixth medical team sent to South Sudan (see: project ID #59019) gave out free consultations in the Bor, the capital of Jonglei state in South Sudan. The team attended over 2000 patients, performed 6 routine surgeries, carried out 20 cases of special diagnosis and treatment operations, instructed local medical staff to perform 26 operations and various diagnosis and treatment operations, and trained operating room management and related nursing operations. The team also held 1 academic exchange, held case consultations and discussions with local doctors 4 times, and  distributed hundreds of materials on disease prevention and health education.

project_name: 5th team offered free consultations at Palogue Oilfield
description: From February 9th to 14th, 2019, the Chinese Embassy in South Sudan organized the fifth batch of Chinese-assisted medical teams (see project #59017) to South Sudan to go to the Palogue Oilfield in the Upper Nile State to carry out free consultation activities. The medical team diagnosed and treated more than 2,000 local patients, carried out 9 surgical operations, B-ultrasound examinations in obstetrics and gynecology, Chinese medicine acupuncture, cupping physiotherapy and other special projects.

project_name: Team carried out a clinic in Rumbek
description:
From January 26 to 31, 2015, the second Chinese medical team in South Sudan went to Rumbek to carry out a “care for health and friendship” clinic to send medicines and disseminate health knowledge to the local people. The clinic was mainly held at the Kiir Mayardit Women's Hospital and the Lake State State Hospital, which were funded by China. More than 1,600 patients were treated in this clinic, with 6 surgeries performed and 9 anesthesias performed.
 
 The second Chinese medical team arrived in South Sudan on February 26, 2014 and departed on March 19, 2015 (#60732).

project_name: 5th team sent
description: On May 3, 2017, the 5th Chinese medical team consisting of 13 doctors from Anhui Province arrived in South Sudan to complete a one-year medical mission. On May 4, 2018, the Chinese Embassy in South Sudan held a ceremony officially sending off the fifth medical team and welcoming the sixth. Specific actions performed by this team are recorded in projects #58595, #71302, and #71453. This project is completed.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 33rd team to hospitals
description: The Chinese Government has been sending medical teams to Sudan every two years since April 1971. Shaanxi Province has been responsible for sending the teams.  In 2017, the Chinese Government and the Government of Sudan signed a protocol agreement dispatching the 33rd medical team to Sudan. The team was stationed at the Abu Ushar Friendship Hospital, Omdurman Friendship Hospital, and Ad-Damazin Friendship Hospital, all of which were previously built with funding from the Chinese Government. The team completed its term of service between 21 October 2017 and 18 October 2018.

project_name: Team sent to conduct 'brightness action 2018' project
description: On November 28, 2018, a group of 8 Chinese medical experts was sent to the Eye Hospital of Al-Nilain University in Khartoum, Sudan to conduct free surgeries on Sudanese cataract patients. This program is a part of the Chinese aid program to Sudan, known as "Brightness Action 2018" (“光明行”). The program is implemented by China Xi'an 1st Hospital and is co-launched by Khartoum State's Health Ministry and the Economic and Commercial Counselor's Office of the Chinese Embassy in Sudan. The medical team dispatched had previously conducted surgeries in Sierra Leone, Senegal, and Chad. The program lasted for 20 days and was completed on December 18, 2018. A total of 241 surgeries were conducted.

project_name: Ministry provided grant for housing project at friendship hospital
description: On 28 October 2004, construction began on a Chinese Medical Team Housing Project at Abu Ushar Friendship Hospital (中国援苏医疗队员住房工程) in Gezira (or Al Jazirah) State, approximately 110 km southeast of Khartoum. This project was financed through a grant from China’s Ministry of Health, but the monetary value of this grant commitment is unknown.  The project involved the construction of a 380 square meter housing unit for Chinese medical teams at the Abu Ushar Friendship Hospital. Qilu Group was the contractor responsible for implementation. Construction was completed in April 2006.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 26th team to hospitals
description: The Chinese Government has been sending medical teams to Sudan every two years since April 1971. Shaanxi Province has been responsible for sending the teams.  On 29 March 2003, the Chinese Government and the Government of Sudan signed a protocol agreement dispatching the 26th medical team to Sudan. According to this agreement, the Government of Sudan would provide housing, transportation, living expenses, office and medical expenses, tax exemptions, visa assistance, and the return plane tickets from Khartoum to China. The Chinese Government would finance the tickets from China to Sudan, any travel expenses of family members, and shipping costs of medical equipment to Sudan.  The 36-member team was stationed at the Abu Ushar Friendship Hospital and Omdurman Friendship Hospital, both of which were previously built with funding from the Chinese Government. The team completed its term of service between 2003 and 2005.

description: The Chinese Government has been sending medical teams to Sudan every two years since April 1971.  Shaanxi Province has been responsible for sending the teams. project_name: 34th team provided surgery as part of Cataract Rejuvenation Project
description: On September 15, 2019, a launching ceremony was held for the Cataract Rejuvenation Project in Sudan, where a new ophthalmology clinic within the Omdurman Friendship Hospital was unveiled. The project will see the Chinese medical team in Sudan helping provide cataract surgery for patients. The team provided free surgeries to at least 159 patients and helped them regain eyesight.  The project is implemented by the 34th Chinese medical team (captured in Project ID#86799).

project_name: Gov't dispatched 35th
description: In October 2019, the 35th medical team from China arrived in Sudan to carry out free medical services. The 35th team conducted operations at the Abu Ushar Friendship Hospital and the Omdurman Friendship Hospital, both of which were previously built with funding from the Chinese Government. The team consisted of 42 members. It was led by the Affiliated Hospital of Yan'an University, and the members are from 20 tertiary medical institutions in 7 cities, including Xi'an, Baoji, Xianyang, Tongchuan, Weinan, Yan'an and Yulin. The departments that the team assisted include 16 majors such as internal medicine, surgery, gynecology and pediatrics.   During their 1-year service, the team treated a total of 28,451 outpatients, completed 1,831 surgeries, and rescued 50 critically ill patients. 6,056 people were treated with acupuncture and moxibustion. The team also provided 7 training for Sudanese health administrative officials at all levels and front-line medical staff.   After 1-year service in Sudan, the team left on November 2, 2020, as marked by a commendation and a send-off video conference. The Sudan Ministry of Health awarded the team a certificate of honor.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 36th team to hospitals
description: The Chinese Government has been sending medical teams to Sudan every year or so since April 1971.  On January 16th, 2021, the 36th medical team arrived in Sudan, as agreed to by the Chinese and Sudanese governments. The team was stationed at the Abu Ushar Friendship Hospital and the Omdurman Friendship Hospital, both of which were previously built with funding from the Chinese Government. The team consisted of 42 members, covering 14 medical professions. They will be in the country for a year, and the departments assisted include 14 specialties such as internal medicine, surgery, ophthalmology, obstetrics and gynecology, and dentistry.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 30th team to hospitals

The 37-member team was stationed at the Abu Ushar Friendship Hospital and Omdurman Friendship Hospital, both of which were previously built with funding from the Chinese Government. project_name: Gov't dispatched 31st team to hospitals
description: The Chinese Government has been sending medical teams to Sudan every two years since April 1971. Shaanxi Province has been responsible for sending the teams.  On 7 February 2013, Chinese Ambassador to Sudan, Luo Xiaoguang, and Sudan’s Minister of Health, Issam Ding, signed a protocol agreement dispatching the 31st medical team to Sudan. The 42-member team was stationed at the Abu Ushar Friendship Hospital, Omdurman Friendship Hospital, and Ad-Damazin Friendship Hospital, all of which were previously built with funding from the Chinese Government.  The team completed its term of service between August 2013 and 2015.  During a 2013 interview, the captain of the 31st medical team stated that the cumulative number of patients seen by all 31 Chinese medical teams in Sudan was 7.78 million.  250,000 of these patients were hospitalized and 160,000 patients received surgery.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 34th team
description: In October 2018, the Chinese Government dispatched the 34th medical team to Sudan for a one-year medical aid mission. The team consists of 42 members, all from Shaanxi, China, covering 14 majors including internal medicine, surgery, ophthalmology, obstetrics and gynecology. The team was stationed at the Abu Ushar Friendship Hospital, Omdurman Friendship Hospital, and Ad-Damazin Friendship Hospital, all of which were previously built with funding from the Chinese Government.   On September 15, 2019, the medical team launched the Cataract Rejuvenation Project ("白内障复明工程"), which was a new ophthalmology clinic within the Omdurman Friendship Hospital (captured by Project ID#86894).  On October 16, 2019, a farewell reception for the 34th medical team was held by Ambassador Ma Xinmin at the Chinese Embassy in Sudan. The Sudanese Minister of Health issued a certificate of honor to Chinese medical staff. Throughout the one-year mission, the team has treated a total of 71,051 patients and 1,879 inpatients and completed 4,235 surgeries.  The Chinese Government has been sending medical teams to Sudan every year or so since April 1971.

project_name: Gov't sent anti-epidemic medical expert team
description: On May 28, 2020, the Chinese Government announced it would be sending a team of anti-epidemic medical experts to Sudan to fight the COVID-19 epidemic. The team arrived on the 28th. On June 6th, 2020, the medical experts met with officials in Sudan and discussed the prevention and control of COVID-19 with members of the 35th Chinese medical team in the country. On June 9th the team held consultations with Sudan's health officials on the necessary measures needed to be taken to prevent the COVID-19 spread.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 29th team to hospitals
description: The Chinese Government has been sending medical teams to Sudan every two years since April 1971. Shaanxi Province has been responsible for sending the teams.  On 25 March 2009, China’s Ambassador to Sudan Li Chengwen and Sudan’s Minister of Health, Tabita Shukayi, signed a protocol agreement dispatching the 29th medical team to Sudan. project_name: 24th team sent for the provision of free medical services

It completed its term of service on November 3, 2018.

project_name: Gov't sent the 17th team
description: On August 12th 2015, the 17th medical team sent by China arrived at Uganda.  The 17th team finished its mission in Uganda in September 2017, when the 18th medical team arrived to replace them (#60063).  China has sent medical teams to work in Uganda since 1983.

project_name: Gov't sent 20th batch of medical aid teams
description: On October 9, 2019, China's 20th medical team to Uganda left China for the country. On October 14, 2019, the Chinese Embassy welcomed the new team and held a farewell ceremony for the 19th team in the China-Uganda Friendship Hospital in Naguru. The team began working on the next day.  The 9 team members are from Third Affiliated Hospital of Kunming Medical University, Yunnan Traditional Chinese Medicine Hospital, and Yunnan Province Infectious Disease Hospital. The doctors specialize in Head and Neck Surgeries, anesthesiology, abdominal Surgeries, Urology, colorectal surgeries, infectious diseases, and acupuncture.  During their tenure, the team taught local doctors the techniques of Laparoscopic appendectomy and held lectures on acupuncture. Originally, they planned to stay for one year, but they stayed longer because of the pandemic. The team finished their tenure on January 24, 2021.

project_name: Gov't sent the 21st team
description: On January 28, 2021, the 21st Chinese medical team was dispatched to Uganda. The 21st team originated from the Third Yunnan Provincial Hospital and the Yunnan Provincial Hospital of Infectious Diseases. The medical team has at least seven doctors of various specialties, nurses, a translator, and a chef. During its tour, the team would provide support on general surgery, acupuncture/massage, respiratory medicine, anesthesiology, otolaryngology, head and neck surgery, urology, and gastroenterology. The medical team will also share these experiences and knowledge with the Ugandan health care providers in its host hospital, China-Uganda Friendship Hospital in Kampala.  The 21st team also provided a donation of medical equipment to the hospital, including respirators, oxygenators, oxygen saturation monitors, sputum excretion machines, and electrocardiographs.

project_name: Gov't sent the 18th team to Uganda
description: On September 13th 2017, the 18th medical team sent by China arrived at Uganda.  The team departed on September 30th, 2018 after they attended a farewell ceremony at the Chinese Embassy in Uganda.  China has sent medical teams to Uganda for the past 35 years.

project_name: 19th team sent
description: On September 18, 2018, China sent the 19th medical team to Uganda to take over from the 18th medical team. There were nine members on this medical team selected from The First People's Hospital of Qujing (曲靖市第一人民医院), the Second People's Hospital of Qujing, Qujing Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine (曲靖市中医医院), and Qujing Medical College (曲靖医学高等专科学校) in Qujing, Yunnan Province. Outpatient visits reached 9,410 and 240 surgeries were performed. They began on September 30, 2018 and ended on October 14, 2019. During their tenure, they not only performed many surgeries, but also provided traditional Chinese medicine training to Ugandan doctors in China-Uganda Friendship Hospital.  China has sent 19 batches of medical teams, totaling up to about 200 doctors, to Uganda since 1983. By 2018, the doctors had treated thousands of Ugandan patients and trained interns, as well as staff, at local hospitals.

project_name: 14th team sent
description: On August 2009, the 14th medical team of 8 members arrived at the Jinja Hospital in Uganda. The team trained local medical personnel and sent 8 doctors from Jinja Hospital for training in China. They completed their mission in August 2011. China has been sending medical teams to Uganda since 1983. Yunnan Province has been responsible for sending the teams.

project_name: Medical aid team in Uganda held free clinic in Hoima
description: In July 2014, the Chinese National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC) has completed a free clinic in Hoima that served 1400 people. After the completion, CNOOC had promised to offer similar services at Buhuka Health Centre III and it delivered as promised in 2015.

project_name: 17th team conducted a free clinic for local people in Karuma
description: On May 21, 2016, the 17th batch of medical teams from China to Uganda went to the Karuma Hydropower Project in Kiryandongo to conduct a free clinic for the local people. The event was organized by the China Hydropower Uganda Karuma Project Department. The medical team members worked continuously from the morning to the evening, and received a total of more than 700 consultations.   This was the 17th medical team's third free clinic since August 2015.

project_name: Gov't sent 16th team to China-Uganda friendship hospital
description: In August 2013, the 16th medical team of 8 members arrived in Uganda. The team works at the China-Uganda Friendship Hospital in Kampala. China has been sending medical teams to Uganda since 1983. Yunnan Province has been responsible for sending the teams. On August 12, 2015, a reception was held to celebrate the departure of the 16th batch of medical teams. This batch of teams had completed their two year term in Uganda and were preparing to return back to China.

project_name: Gov't sent 15th team to the Jinja Hospital
description: China has been sending medical teams to Uganda since 1983. Yunnan Province has been responsible for sending the teams. On August 2011, the 15th medical team of 8 members arrived at the Jinja Hospital in Uganda. They team moved to the China-Uganda Friendship Hospital in June 2012 and completed their two-year mission in August 2013.

project_name: Team conducted a free clinic for local people in Kamuli
description:
On November 21, the 17th batch of medical teams from China to Uganda went to the location of the Isinba hydropower project in Kamuli province to conduct a free clinic for local people. The event was hosted by the Ugandan Chinese Enterprise Association and implemented by China Water Resources and Hydro Power Corporation. The medical team arrived at the Isinba Hydropower Project Camp on the afternoon of the 20th and took the ferry boat to the other side to start the clinic. Seven doctors worked continuously from the morning to the evening, and received a total of nearly 700 consultations. 
 
  So far, the medical team has provided five free clinics for the Ugandan people. The clinic was the first time that the 17th batch of medical teams visit Uganda this year.

project_name: Gov't sent 13th team to Uganda
description: China has been sending medical teams to Uganda since 1983. Yunnan Province has been responsible for sending the teams. The 13th medical team of 8 members worked in Uganda from August 2007 to August 2009. As part of this medical team project, China donated 300,000 RMB worth of medical equipment to Ghana for the Jinja Hospital (金贾医院).

project_name: Gov't sent its 11th team
description: China has been sending medical teams to Uganda since 1983. Yunnan Province has been responsible for sending the teams. In August 2003.. the 11th medical team of 8 members arrived at the Jinja Hospital in Uganda. They completed the mission and returned to China in August 2005.

project_name: 14th team in Uganda donated medicine & equipment

project_name: 10th team sent

project_name: Gov't sent 12th team
description: China has been sending medical teams to Uganda since 1983. Yunnan Province has been responsible for sending the teams. project_name: 18th military team dispatched
description: China has been sending military medical teams to Zambia since 1984. On January 20, 2015, China’s 18th military medical team arrived in Zambia. The 11-person team was stationed at Maina Soko Hospital in Lusaka and completed its term of service on January 18, 2016. The members of the team undertook outpatient service, consultation, operation, guidance and teaching activities at Maina Soko military hospital. They also provided medical care for the President and the First Lady, and treated hundreds of senior officials and officers from both Zambian government and military.

project_name: Metal mining group sponsored a team of doctors to perform operations
description: April 13 to April 16, 2011, A team of Chinese doctors from Beijing Tongren Hospital performed cataract operations on 109 Zambian patients. China Nonferrous Metal Mining Group contributed 1.09 million RMB towards this mission. The humanitarian mission is a part of China's "Bright Light Tour"/"Bringing Light Tour" around the world.

project_name: Gov't provided medical equipment & team for Covid-19 prevention
description: On January 7, 2021, the Government of China donated oxygen ventilators and other medical equipment to Zambia, in order to aid Zambia in COVID-19 prevention efforts. The supplies will be distributed to four main hospitals in Zambia. During the donation handover, the Chinese Ambassador to Zambia Li Jie stated that the government of China will send a medical team of 28 Chinese professionals to aid in Zambia's medical response to the COVID-19 pandemic. 20 of these professionals will be sent to Zambia's main hospital in Lusaka, 4 will be sent to Livingstone Hospital, and 4 will be sent to Ndola Hospital.  The monetary value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: 15th team dispatched to hospitals
description: China has been sending medical teams to Zambia since 1978. Henan Province is responsible for sending the teams. The 15th medical team included 28 members who were stationed at University of Zambia Teaching Hospital (also known as University Teaching Hospital), Ndola General Hospital, Livingstone Central Hospital, Kitwe Central Hospital, Thomson Hospital, and Kabwe General Hospital. The team completed its term of service between August 2009 and July 29, 2011.

project_name: 18th team dispatched to hospitals
description: China has been sending medical teams to Zambia since 1978. Henan Province is responsible for sending the teams. The 18th medical team had a total of 28 members distributed across Levy Mwanawasa Hospital, University of Zambia Teaching Hospital (also known as University Teaching Hospital), Ndola General Hospital, and Livingstone Central Hospital. The team began its term of service between April 29, 2016 and was scheduled to depart in May 2017. On May 18, 2017 a welcome-home reception was held for the team.  It primarily focused on the provision of general services, expertise, and training to Zambian hospital staff. The team also offered free clinics in rural areas and on the grounds of Chinese-funded enterprises. At a final awards ceremony, the head of the 18th medical team said that "the medical team anesthetized over 1,800 patients, worked on call more than 300 times, rescued 200 dangerous and serious cases, and gave over 20,000 reports of examinations and tests.” Overall, the team reportedly treated over 12,000 patients and conducted 1,500 surgeries. The 18th medical team also helped to develop Zambia's telemedicine capabilities (project #59257).

project_name: 17th team dispatched to hospitals
description: China has been sending medical teams to Zambia since 1978. Henan Province is responsible for sending the teams. project_name: 18th team donated telemedicine equipment to hospitals
description:
In 2017, the 18th Chinese medical team donated three sets of telemedicine equipment to Zambia's Ministry of Health. The equipment will be installed in Zambia University Teaching Hospital, and Livingstone Hospital, and Ndola Hospital as part of their overall medical mission (project #57339). Telemedicine services help patients remotely access doctors, which is useful for rural residents without easy access to urban-based hospitals. These tools also allow doctors in China and Zambia conduct consultations and strengthen communication among Zambian doctors.
 
 According to a MOFCOM announcement, the handover ceremony took place on March 21, 2017. 
 
 Before this project, China already donated one set of telemedicine equipment to Levy Mwanawasa Hospital.

project_name: 19th military team dispatched

project_name: 17th military team dispatched

project_name: 19th team donated medical equipment to 4 hospitals
description: On January 17, 2018, the 19th Chinese medical team donated an assortment of medical instruments valued at $120,000 USD to the four hospitals they served in (Levy Mwanawasa Hospital, University of Zambia Teaching Hospital, Ndola General Hospital, and Livingstone Central Hospital). project_name: 21st team dispatched

project_name: 14th military team dispatched

project_name: 15th military team dispatched

project_name: 13th team dispatched to hospitals

project_name: 14th team dispatched to University of Zambia Teaching Hospital & other

project_name: Gov't dispatched 9th team to hospitals
description: On 19 December, 2002, the 9th medical team arrived in Zimbabwe.  The 9th medical team consisted of 12 members, and they were stationed at Harare Central Hospital and Mpilo Central Hospital.  They completed their term of service between 19 December, 2002 and early 2005. The Chinese Government has been sending medical teams to Zimbabwe every two years since 1985.  Hunan Province has been responsible for sending the teams.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 12th team to hospitals
description: On 8 January, 2011, the 12th medical team arrived in Zimbabwe.  The 10-member team included a urologist, orthopedic surgeon, anesthetists, and others working in orthopedics, urology, and radiology.  They were stationed at Harare Central Hospital and Parirenyatwa Hospital.  They completed their term of service between 8 January, 2011 and 2 May, 2013.  The Chinese Government has been sending medical teams to Zimbabwe every two years since 1985.  Hunan Province has been responsible for sending the teams. In 2012, the 12th medical team donated ureteroscope equipment to Parirenyatwa Hospital and the University of Zimbabwe, which is captured in the linked project #35659.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 11th team to hospitals
description: On March 6, 2008, the Chinese Government and the Government of Zimbabwe signed letters of exchange, officially dispatching the 11th medical team to Zimbabwe. The 11th medical team consisted of 10 members. They were stationed at Harare Central Hospital and Mpilo Central Hospital.  They completed their term of service between May 2008 and 2010.  The Chinese Government has been sending medical teams to Zimbabwe every two years since 1985.  Hunan Province has been responsible for sending the teams.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 8th team to hospitals
description: On December 12, 2000, the Chinese Government and the Government of Zimbabwe signed letters of exchange officially dispatching the 8th medical team to Zimbabwe. The 8th medical team consisted of 5 members (one orthopedic expert, three anesthesiologists, and a translator) who were stationed at Harare Central Hospital and Mpilo Central Hospital. The team completed its term of service between December 12, 2000 and January 6, 2002  The Chinese Government has been sending medical teams to Zimbabwe every two years since 1985.  Hunan Province has been responsible for sending the teams.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 14th team to hospitals
description: From 2015 to 2017, China's 14th medical team completed its term of service in Zimbabwe. The team arrived to Zimbabwe in April 2015, and consisted of 10 members who were stationed at Harare Central Hospital and Parirenyatwa Hospital. The Chinese Government has been sending medical teams to Zimbabwe every two years since 1985.  Hunan Province has been responsible for sending the teams. This project is completed.

project_name: team donated 18th batch of supplies Parirenyatwa hospital group
description: On December 15, 2020, a Chinese medical team in Zimbabwe handed over a donation of medical equipment to Zimbabwe's largest referral hospital, the Parirenyatwa Group of Hospitals (PGH). The medical equipment was donated by the National Health Commission of China to promote the global fight against the COVID-19 epidemic.   The donated materials included ventilators, blood oxygen saturation monitors, electrocardiographs, and oxygen machines. The handover ceremony took place at PGH in Harare, Zimbabwe. Lue Weiqiang, the captain of the Chinese medical team, spoke at the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 10th team to hospitals
description: In July 2005, the 10th Chinese medical team, which consisted of 4 physicians, arrived in Zimbabwe.  They were stationed at Harare Central Hospital and Mpilo Central Hospital.  They completed their term of service in August 2007. The Chinese Government has been sending medical teams to Zimbabwe every two years since 1985.  Hunan Province has been responsible for sending the teams.

project_name: Team donated 17th batch of medical supplies
description: On June 11, 2020, a handover ceremony was held for the donation of medical supplies from a Chinese medical expert team to Zimbabwe. The ceremony was held at Parirenyatwa Hospital, the designated hospital for COVID-19 in Zimbabwe. This is the 17th batch of medical supplies donated by the Chinese government to Zimbabwe. Counselor Zou Xiaoming attended the event and delivered a speech. Jiang Zhichao, a member of the medical team in Tianjin, signed the certificate for the handover of donated materials on behalf of the Chinese side. This signing was witnessed by Counselor Zou Xiaoming and representatives of Parirenyatwa Hospital.

project_name: 16th team dispatched
description: In July 2018, China sent the 16th medical team to Zimbabwe.  During their year-long term, the medical team completed more than 300 operations and treated more than 7000 patients.  Among these operations, the medical team visited Kariba, Kuiru, Mutare, and Harare orphanages in remote areas of Zimbabwe to provide free medical treatment for the local people. In 2018, the team also responded in a variety of ways to provide technical support and make positive contributions to the local government's final victory over cholera.   On December 14, 2018, Chen Ning, Economic and Commercial Counselor of the Chinese Embassy in Zimbabwe, led the 16th team to the Huajin Cement Plant in Kulu, southwestern Zimbabwe, to provide medical examinations for company employees and local employees.  During 2019, Hurricane "Idai" seriously affected the eastern province of Zimbabwe, so the medical team went deep into the disaster area and actively carried out epidemic prevention and disaster relief.  The medical team finished its work on July 2, 2019.

project_name: Team donated medical supplies
description: ​​On May 11, 2020, a 12-person medical expert team sent by the Chinese government arrived in Harare, the capital of Zimbabwe (See Project ID#91963), with emergency aid materials. Upon their arrival a handover ceremony for the large amount of donated anti-epidemic materials was held. From May 11, 2020 to their departure on May 25, 2020, the medical team distributed these materials to the various hospitals they visited. Throughout their stay in Zimbabwe, the expert group visited medical institutions in the four provinces of Harare, Mashonaland East, Mashonaland Central and Mashonaland West  including Marondera Provincial Hospital, Chinhoyi Provincial Hospital, and Mvurwi Hospital.

project_name: 17th team dispatched to Parirenyatwa Hospital
description: On June 23, 2019, the 17th Chinese medical team arrived in Zimbabwe, beginning their one-year term of service at Parirenyatwa Hospital.  The 17th medical team was composed of 9 doctors, selected by the Hunan Provincial Health Commission. The doctors' specialties included traditional Chinese medicine, internal medicine, orthopedics, urology, radiology, obstetrics and gynecology, anesthesiology, general surgery, pediatrics, etc.. The project completion date was October 18, 2020.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 13th team to hospitals
description: On 8 April, 2013, the 13th Chinese medical team arrived in Zimbabwe.  The team consisted of 10 members to be stationed at Harare Central Hospital and Parirenyatwa Hospital.  They completed their term of service between 8 April, 2013 and 2015.   The team donated medical supplies to Epworth in November 2013, which is captured in the linked project #34933. The Chinese Government has been sending medical teams to Zimbabwe every two years since 1985.  Hunan Province has been responsible for sending the teams.

project_name: Gov't dispatched 15th team to hospitals
description: On 22 June, 2017 the 15th Chinese medical team arrived in Zimbabwe and attended a welcome reception.  The 15th medical team consisted of 10 members who were stationed at Harare Central Hospital and Parirenyatwa Hospital.  The 15th medical team was expected to complete its term of service between 22 June, 2017 and 2019.  The Chinese Government has been sending medical teams to Zimbabwe every two years since 1985.  Hunan Province has been responsible for sending the teams.

project_name: Gov't sent medical expert team
description: ​​On May 11, 2020, a 12-person medical expert team sent by the Chinese government arrived in Harare, the capital of Zimbabwe, with emergency aid materials (See Project ID#93329). Chinese Ambassador to Zimbabwe Guo Shaochun, Zimbabwe’s Local Government Minister, the Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs, and the Deputy Minister of Health met the team at the airport. A welcome and handover ceremony for donated anti-epidemic materials was held. During the welcome ceremony, Ambassador Guo thanked the Hunan Provincial Government and several hospitals for forming the aid team.    Throughout their stay in Zimbabwe, the expert group visited medical institutions in the four provinces of Harare, Mashonaland East, and Mashona Central Key and Mashonaland West. During these visits the medical team distributed medical supplies to the hospitals they visited (See Project ID#93329). The expert group also carried out work with the Zimbabwean Anti-Epidemic Inter-Ministerial Joint Working Group, the Ministry of Health, the Harare City Prevention and Control Command Organization, the Harare Community Prevention and Control Organization, and the World Health Organization Representative Office in Zimbabwe. The expert group also inspected the designated hospitals for COVID-19 in Harare and trained medical staff on prevention, control, and diagnosis and treatment for COVID-19.   On May 13, 2020, the medical expert held an exchange and discussion with the Tianjin Anti-Epidemic Inter-Ministerial Working Group and the Tianjin Ministry of Health on epidemic prevention and control. Ambassador Guo Shaochun, the Vice President of Zimbabwe, the Defense Minister, and eight other cabinet ministers and senior officials attended the event.   On May 25, 2020, the medical expert team in Zimbabwe completed their work and left Zimbabwe for Equatorial Guinea on a chartered flight. The Chinese Ambassador to Zimbabwe, Guo Shaochun, Zimbabwe’s Information Minister, and the Deputy Minister of Health went to the airport to see off the expert group.

project_name: CSCEC donates anti-epidemic supplies
description: On March 27, 2020, the Government of Algeria received a donation of medical supplies from China State Construction Engineering Corporation (CSCEC) Algeria to help combat the COVID-19 pandemic. The supplies were worth a total of USD $450,000 and included 50,000 N95 masks; 500,000 surgical masks; 2,000 units of medical protective clothing; and an unspecified number of medical isolation masks, medical gloves, and respirators.   The handover ceremony took place at Algiers International Airport and was attended by the Chinese Ambassador to Algeria Li Lianhe; CSCEC Algeria Manager Zhou Sheng; and senior Algerian officials from the Ministry of Public Works and Transportation, the Ministry of Health, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.  The supplies arrived on an Air Algerie plane from Beijing alongside a 13 person Chinese medical team, which provided technical assistance captured via Project ID#95424.

project_name: Gov't donates anti-epidemic medical supplies
description: On April 21, 2020, a handover ceremony was held at Algiers International Airport for a batch of anti-epidemic supplies donated by the Chinese government to the Algerian government. The donation included an unspecified number of N95 medical masks, disposable surgical masks, test kits, respirators, and other supplies to help mitigate the spread of the COVID-19 pandemic.   Algeria reportedly mobilized a military plane to transport the materials from Beijing.

project_name: Gov't donates anti-epidemic medical supplies
description: On April 15th 2020, Algeria received a donation of of anti-epidemic medical supplies from the Chinese Government. The donation included an unspecified number of diagnostic reagents (tests), FFP2 type masks for healthcare professionals, and protective suits.  The handover ceremony took place at the Algiers International Airport.

project_name: China Railway Construction Corporation donates ventilators
description: On April 1, 2020, a donation of 100 ventilators from China Railway Construction Corporation (中国铁建向) was handed over to the Algerian Embassy in Beijing. These ventilators were to be used in Algeria to combat the COVID-19 pandemic, but arrived in Algeria on an unknown date.

project_name: Gov't donates anti-epidemic supplies
description: On May 7, 2020, a handover ceremony was held for a new batch of medical supplies donated by the Chinese government to the Government of Algeria. The supplies, to be used to mitigate the spread of the COVID-19 pandemic, included 5 million surgical masks, 560,000 FFP2 masks, 100,000 diagnostic (test) kits, 15,000 protective goggles, and other supplies. The handover ceremony took place at the Algiers International Airport.

project_name: Gov't donates Sinopharm vaccines
description: On February 10, 2021, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi confirmed a donation of 200,000 Sinopharm vaccine doses (worth an estimated $3.6 million) on a phone call with Algerian Foreign Minister Boukadoum. The vaccines arrived on February 24, 2021 and were handed over in a ceremony at Algeria's Boufarik military airport (as captured via Project ID#94808).   Then, in September 2021, the Chinese Government donated 3.2 million doses of the Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine worth an estimated $57.6 million (as captured via Project ID#97169).

project_name: China EXIM Bank provides loan for Saurimo Municipal Hospital
description: On 3 January 2013, the Government of Angola and China Eximbank signed a loan agreement for Phase 2 of the Saurimo Municipal Hospital Construction and Equipping Project. The face value and borrowing terms of the loan are unknown.  The loan was approved under a larger China Eximbank credit line, but it is not clear which specific credit line was utilized.  The proceeds of the loan use to be used by the borrower partially finance a $17.5 million commercial contract with Sinohydro. The purpose of this project is to construct and equip Saurimo Municipal Hospital in Lunda Sul Province which is also known as Lunda Sul General Hospital and Hospital Geral de Saurimo.  This project encountered various delays; however, it was officially completed and inaugurated on 17 October 2020.

project_name: China EXIM Bank provides loan for Huambo Central Hospital
description: On November 28, 2003, the Chinese Government and the Angolan Government signed a framework agreement pertaining to a special economic cooperation arrangement (Agreement name in Chinese: 中华人民共和国商务部与安哥拉共和国财政部关于两国经贸合作特殊安排的框架协议).  Following the signing of the framework agreement, on March 2, 2004, China Eximbank entered into a $2 billion Master Loan Facility Agreement (MLFA) with the Government of Angola. All borrowings under the MLFA, which is an oil prepayment facility,  carried the following estimated borrowing terms: a 21.5 maturity, a 1.5 year grace period, an interest rate of 3-month LIBOR plus a 1.5% margin, a 0.3% management fee, and a 0.3% commitment fee.  The facility was split between a $1.0 billion Phase I facility and a $1.0 billion Phase II facility.  Availability of the Phase II facility was subject to confirmation by the lender on or prior to the date falling five years after satisfaction of the conditions precedent to the MLFA and was made available by China Eximbank during that period.  The MLFA is a framework agreement under which the Government of Angola and China Eximbank may conclude individual buyer’s credit loan agreements (ILAs or subsidiary loan agreements) for the purpose of financing up to 90% of the contract price owing to certain contractors in respect of certain contracts.  The first tranche of the facility was released in December 2004.  The facility was fully drawn down as of December 31, 2017.  Sonangol provided a source of collateral under the MLFA, and repayments were made with the proceeds of oil sales from Sonangol to UNIPEC (China international United Petroleum & Chemicals Co. Ltd, Sinopec group), which were deposited in an Angolan Ministry of Finance (MINFIN) account at China Eximbank.  The volume of oil to be sold to UNIPEC each month for repayment of the loan varied according to market oil prices.  Under the agreement, 70% of works have to be contracted with Chinese companies and the same proportion of construction material, equipment and labour has to be contracted in China.  Loan disbursements were made on a project-by-project basis.  Tendering, management and payments were jointly managed by the Chinese Ministry of Commerce and the Angolan Ministry of Finance (which coordinated the various Angolan line ministries responsible for supervising the projects).   The Angolan Ministry of Finance submitted the projects for tendering; China Eximbank selected Chinese candidate firms for the projects; and a joint commission made the final firm selections. The process was managed by an office in the Angolan Ministry of Finance -- known as Gabinete de Apoio Técnico (GAT) -- that was specifically created to manage the MLFA with China Eximbank.  In October 2005, China Eximbank and the Government of Angola signed a $32,134,308.99 subsidiary buyer’s credit loan agreement under the MLFA for the Huambo Central Hospital Rehabilitation and Equipping and Ambulance Acquisition Project.  The proceeds of the loan were used to partially finance a $36,520,308.99 commercial (EPC) contract with Sinohydro, which was signed on October 24, 2005.    The purpose of the project, which employed 57 Angolan workers and 30 Chinese workers, was to construct and equip Huambo Central Hospital and acquire 86 ambulances.  Sinohydro was the EPC contractor responsible for project implementation. The EPC contract for the project was originally scheduled to go into effect on August 1, 2006 and the originally scheduled handover date was February 1, 2008. Sinohydro ultimately delivered the ambulances on April 26, 2007. The ambulances were subsequently distributed to the following provinces:  Bengo (5 ambulances); Benguela (5 ambulances); Bie (2 ambulances); Huambo (5 ambulances);  Huila (6 ambulances); Kubango (4 ambulances);  Cunene (4 ambulances); Cabinda (2 ambulances); K.Sul (7 ambulances);  K.Norte (6 ambulances); Luanda (2 ambulances); L. Norte (4 ambulances); L. Sul (2 ambulances);  Malange (7 ambulances); Moxico (7 ambulances); Namibe (3 ambulances); Uige (5 ambulances); Zaire (3 ambulances); Reserva Central (7 ambulances). A project completion ceremony took place on November 11, 2009.

project_name: Donates Tuberculosis medicine
description: In June of 2003, the People's Republic of China was to donate medicines worth $300,000 US dollars to the Angolan Government to help with the shortage of TB-related drugs in public hospitals. The Angolan government had made a public appeal two years previous to help the people fight against tuberculosis. The medicines were to be handed over to the Health Minister, Albertina Hamukuaya, by the Chinese ambassador, Beisan Zhang. No additional information could be found regarding the completion of the donation.

project_name: CEIEC donates equipment
description: On May 15, 2020, China National Electronics Import and Export Corporation (CEIEC) donated 100 million Kz (around USD 176,200) worth of equipment and supplies to the Angolan government. Some of the goods donated included multifunctional cameras capable of taking individuals' temperatures and 20,000 surgical masks.  As of May 20, 2020, the cameras were in the process of being installed at the Quatro de Fevereiro Airport in Luanda.  Angolan Interior Minister Eugénio Laborinho thanked CEIEC and asked for China to continue supporting Angola through the COVID-19 pandemic.

project_name: Gov't provides loan for Luanda General Hospital Construction
description: On 23 May 2001, a Chinese Government delegation signed several agreements with the Angolan Government during a three-day visit to Luanda.  One of the agreements was a $6 million interest interest-free loan agreement for the Luanda General Hospital Construction Project.  Angola's Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs, George Chicoty, signed the agreement with China's Vice Minister of External Trade and Economic Cooperation, Zhang Xiang.  This project involved the construction of a 100-bed Luanda General Hospital (Hospital Geral de Luanda) in the Kilamba Kiaxi municipality of Luanda.  The hospital offers specialized services in laryngology, dermatology, neurology, opthalmology and physiotherapy.  The proceeds from the loan were used to partially finance an $8 million contract with China Overseas Engineering Group (COVEC or 中国海外工程有限责任公司). The groundbreaking ceremony was held on May 26, 2004. Construction began in July 2004 and was completed in 15 months. The hospital was inaugurated on 3 February 2006.  However, in 2010, COVEC was criticized for the poor quality of construction after cracks developed in the ceilings and walls of the hospital.  Chinese and Angolan officials subsequently met for several rounds of talks, and the Chinese Government agreed to fund the rehabilitation and expansion of the hospital, including the construction of temporary wards and sewage systems for patients to ensure the continuing operation of the hospital (see Umbrella Project #53184).

project_name: Gov't donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On August 21, 2020, the Chinese Government donated anti-epidemic materials to the Angolan Government to support Angolan citizens affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. The materials included 18,000 surgical masks, 5,000 pairs of gloves, 120 thermometers, and 360 bottles of hand sanitizer. The donation was made through the Organization of African First Ladies for Development (OAFLAD). The monetary value of the donation is unknown.  The donation occurred in a handover ceremony attended by Angolan First Lady Ana Dias Lourença and Chinese Ambassador Gong Tao.

description: Pursuant to economic and trade agreements signed during the 2006 FOCAC summit, the Chinese Government agreed to provide a grant to establish an anti-malaria center in Angola during the 2006 FOCAC summit between November 4-5. The Chinese Government also agreed to provide medical equipment and drugs to the center over a three year period following the establishment of the center.

The materials included N95 masks, medical masks, medical protective gowns, shoe covers, goggles, and infrared thermometers. The monetary value of the grant is unknown.  The supplies were delivered during a handover ceremony in Luanda, Angola. Those in attendance included Chinese Ambassador Gong Tao, Angola's State Secretary for International Cooperation, Angolan Community of Ministry of Foreign Affairs Domingos Vieira Lopes, and Secretary of State for Public Health Franco Mufinda. The supplies originally arrived in Ethiopia, where they were then shipped to 11 other African countries.

project_name: China EXIM Bank provides loan for Zaire Provincial Hospital construction
description: On 20 August, 2012, Angola's Minister of Health laid the cornerstone for the Zaire Provincial Hospital Construction Project. This project was reportedly financed by a China Eximbank loan. The value and terms of this loan are unknown. The total project cost was estimated to be about $42 million.   This hospital is located in Kiowa, on the outskirts of the city of M'banza Kongo (Mbanza-Kongo), which is the capital of Zaire Province. It was supposed to be the largest comprehensive hospital in Zaire Province, with a total construction area of ​​about 23,000 square meters and 332 beds. China Road and Bridge Corporation (CRBC) was the contractor responsible for implementation. Construction began on 7 November 2013.  Then, on 1 June, 2014, several Chinese MOFCOM officials inspected the project site. It is unknown whether of when this project was completed.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Luanda General Hospital

The Chinese Ministry of Commerce subsequently signed a series of grant agreements to finance this project.  On 31 October 2012, the Chinese Government and the Government of Angola signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) committing an RMB 100 million grant for the Luanda General Hospital Rehabilitation and Expansion Project. This is the second ETCA of three. The other financing agreements for the Luanda General Hospital Rehabilitation and Expansion Project are as follows:  (1) On 19 September 2012, the two sides signed the first ETCA committing a grant of an unknown value (See: Project #67510) (2) On 18 December 2013, the two sides signed a third ETCA committing an RMB 200 million grant (See: Project #67517) (3) In 2014, the Chinese Government provided a grant of an unspecified value for medical equipment and office furniture (See: Project #36111) (4) Also in 2014, the Chinese Government provided a grant of an unspecified value to rehabilitate the hospital's sewage system (See: Project #68458)  The Luanda General Hospital Rehabilitation and Expansion Project sought to expand the capacity of Luanda General Hospital, which primarily caters to women and children, from 100 beds to 301 beds. project_name: Gov't finances WHO Covid-19 response
description: In March 2020, Chinese government provides USD 915,186 to support WHO response to COVID-19 outbreak in Angola.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Luanda General Hospital
description: On 9 May 2014, the Chinese Government and the Government Angola signed an exchange of notes for the provision of medical equipment and office furniture for the Luanda General Hospital Rehabilitation and Expansion Project. The monetary value of the grant from China’s Ministry of Commerce that supported this project is unknown. The equipment and furniture was provided by Tianjin Machinery Import and Export Corporation and Hubei Taiva Medical Technology Co. Ltd.. The project was officially handed over to Angolan authorities on 26 February 2015. project_name: Gov't finances supply of medical equipment
description: On 29 August 2017, Presidential Orders No. 243/17 and 241/17 approved contracting procedures for the supply of equipment to the Medical and Physical Rehabilitation Center of Huambo and the provision of equipment for the Municipal Hospital of Cunene (see Project #68977), respectively. This project entry captures the supply of equipment to the Rehabilitation Center in Huambo. Both of these projects were reportedly financed through a credit line from an unspecified Chinese financial institution.  China Railway Construction Corporation (CRCC) and the Angolan Ministry of Health signed the $3,967,391.09 implementation contract. It is unclear how much of this contract was covered by the Chinese Government. Both of these projects are part of the Public Investment Program (PIP) of 2017, which provides for the provision of hospital infrastructures at the provincial and municipal levels, with a view to improving working conditions and service to the users of these units.

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria medicine
description: On April 9, 2007, China handed over anti-malaria medicine worth 2 million RMB to Angola.

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria medication
description:
On November 10, 2011, a handover ceremony was staged at the Angolan Ministry of Health in Luanda for the donation of anti-malarial medicine from the Chinese government to the Angolan Ministry of Health. Ambassador Gao Kexiang and Deputy Minister of Health Evelise Frestas were present. The donation comprised of 179,520 tablets DUOCOTEXIM, a composition made of Artemisinina and Piperaquina. China has donated 3 batches of antimalarial medicine since its commitment to combat malaria in Africa during the 2006 FOCAC Summit, and this donation is the fourth. According to Chinese Economic and Commercial Counselor Xia Xiaoling, who was also present at the ceremony, the medicines were worth a total of 2 million RMB.
 
 This donation likely follows the signing of an agreement for the donation of anti-malaria equipment to the anti-malaria center in May 2011.

description: In 2015, China Development Bank provided a $15 billion loan facility to Angola (see project #66847). It is unclear if any financing from the loan facility was committed or disbursed to this project.

project_name: China EXIM Bank provides loan for Municipal Hospitals and Health Centers
description: On November 28, 2003, the Chinese Government and the Angolan Government signed a framework agreement pertaining to a special economic cooperation arrangement (Agreement name in Chinese: 中华人民共和国商务部与安哥拉共和国财政部关于两国经贸合作特殊安排的框架协议). Those in attendance at the vaccine handover ceremony included Chinese Ambassador to Angola Gong Tao, Angolan Minister of Health Silvia Lutucuta, and Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation Lopez. In his speech, Ambassador Gong Tao said that China and Angola carried out their anti-epidemic cooperation based on the principle of putting people and life first. project_name: China's Peace Ark provides medical services
description:
On October 19, 2017, the China's Peace Ark, arrived in Angola for an 8-day mission to deliver free medical services to the local people. The ship arrived around 11:30 am in the port of Luanda. The ship left on October 26, 2017. The visit was part of its "Harmonious Mission 2017". 
 
 During its visit to Angola, the ship treated over 6,000 people and carried out 14 surgeries on-ship.
 
 The Peace Ark is a part of the People's Liberation Army Navy (PLA Navy). The ship has 110 physicians and medical workers from the Second Military Medical University and the Navy General Hospital of the People's Liberation Army. It has participated in six Harmonious Missions, the first beginning in 2010.

project_name: Ningxia Health and Welfare Commission donates medical supplies

description: On April 15, 2020, the Chinese Embassy held a donation ceremony for its donation of anti-epidemic medical equipment consisting of: 2,000 units of N95 masks, 2,000 units of medical protective gowns, 2,000 units of medical eye patches, 10,000 units of disposable medical gloves, 10,000 units of disposable medical shoe covers, 500 units of thermometers frontal and 10,000 units of medical masks to the Benin Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation. The purpose of the medical materials was to help prevention efforts against the COVID-19 coronavirus. Peng Jintao, the Chinese Ambassador to Benin, was present at the ceremony. The Office of the World Food Program in Benin for provided logistics support for delivery of the medical supplies.

project_name: Donates medical equipment for Parakou Army Instruction Hospital

The Chinese-funded Parakou Army Instruction Hospital was inaugurated on February 13, 2011, and started its clinical activities on October 4, 2011 after a phase 1 construction costing 6 billion CFAF (see Project #34144). In order to improve the functioning of the said hospital and to improve its equipment, the Chinese government had offered an additional 11.5 million yuan or 920 million CFA francs for the second phase in April 2013, which allowed the construction of the water tower, the canteen, housing for duty guards, etc (see Project #72795). The Parakou Military Instruction Hospital was then officially handed over on Thursday, April 3, 2014. After this second phase, the government decides to provide medical equipment in the form of a donation for an amount of 10 million yuan or 800 million CFA francs to the hospital in Parakou. This equipment will help improve the services of the said hospital for the benefit of the populations of Parakou and the surrounding area.
 
 Located in the Okédama district on the edge of the interstate road, it is a set of four groups of buildings on two levels arranged in a "U" and connected to each other. This set is made up of three blocks: an administrative block comprising the management and its components and an amphitheater with 256 seats; a medical-technical unit with many units: medicine, surgery, maternity, odontostomatology, emergencies, radiology services, biomedical analysis laboratory, a complex of three operating theaters, a research and fight center against malaria and a laundry room; a technical unit comprising a generator with a power of 550 KVA, a water tower with a capacity of 50,000 liters, a canteen with 100 places, a guardhouse building, a mortuary and an electrical technical room and incinerator.

Then, on January 14, 2022, Chinese Government delivered 500,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines and syringes to the Government of Benin. Then, on May 10, 2022, the Chinese Government delivered a third batch of Sinovac COVID-19 vaccine doses as well as medical supplies including syringes, x-ray machines, multi-parameter monitors, electric syringe pumps, medical beds, EKG devices, and resuscitation respirators. A handover certificate was signed by the Charge d'Affaires a.i. of the Chinese Embassy in Benin Yan Yan and the cabinet director of the Beninese Ministry of Health Petas Akogbeto in Cotonou.
