project_name: Embassy donates anti-epidemic supplies
description: On May 12, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Benin donated anti-epidemic supplies to Benin’s Independent Election Commission (CENA). The donated supplies included 80 hand-washing devices, 500 masks, and 200 packs of hand sanitizer. The purpose of this donation is to support Benin’s COVID-19 response efforts during the upcoming municipal elections to be held on May 17, 2020. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.   A handover ceremony was held for this donation. Ambassador Peng Jingtao and Chairman of Benin's Independent Electoral Commission (CENA) jointly attended the ceremony. The Political Counselor of the Embassy, the CENA Vice Chairman, and representative also attended.

project_name: Donates anti-Malarial drugs
description: On September 19, 2006, Ms. Gambo, Minister of Health of Benin, and Li Beifen, Chinese Ambassador to Benin, attended the material handover ceremony for China's donation of anti-malarial equipment worth two million RMB (150 million CFA). The Chinese Embassy in Benin, ZTE Corporation (Benin), and China National Complete Equipment Import and Export Corporation took part in the ceremony. Ambassador Li said that the 3,000 mosquito nets provided by the Chinese Embassy and Chinese companies this time are to support Benin's annual nationwide anti-malarial activities. This donation was decided during a previous visit by President Yayi’s to China.

project_name: Gov't funds Covid-19 WHO support
description: In March 2020, Chinese government provides USD 982,617 to support WHO response to COVID-19 outbreak in Benin.

project_name: CCDECB donates anti-epidemic materials to Ministry of Health
description: On June 26, 2020, PetroChina Nibei Pipeline Company, Chinese Center for Economic and Commercial Development of Benin (CCDECB), Yunnan Construction Investment Benin Branch, Hunan Road and Bridge, Zhongcheng Benin Sugar Industry Co., Ltd., China Railway Fifth Bureau Benin Branch, Yueken International (Benin) Co., Ltd. , China Railway 14th Bureau Group Benin Branch, and China Geo-Engineering Group Benin Branch donated 72.33 million CFA francs (about $122,953)-worth of cash and materials to Benin's Ministry of Health.  The Chinese Center for Economic and Commercial Development of Benin (CCDECB) donated anti-epidemic materials to the Benin Ministry of Health, and according to a photo of a large check found on the Embassy's website, the donation was worth 20,000,000 CFA francs and consisted of 3,000 protective masks, 3,000 sets of protective clothing, and 10 sets of triple packaging for transporting COVID-19 samples.  The remaining 52.33 million CFA francs donated by the other Chinese companies is captured in linked ProjectID#94254.

project_name: Embassy donates anti-epidemic materials to Ministry of Foreign Affairs
description: On May 13, 2020, the Chinese Embassy provided anti-epidemic supplies to the Benin Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The supplies included disinfectant alcohol, masks, and hand sanitizer. This donation was made to support Benin’s COVID-19 response efforts. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. Ambassador Peng Jingtao and the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Benin jointly attended the ceremony. The Secretary-General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Benin, Qiao Pei, the Director of the General Office, Kang Lan, the Director-General of the Asia-Pacific University, Wen Xinon, the Political Counselor of the Embassy, Yan Yan, and other officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs also attended.

project_name: Donates anti-Malarial drugs
description: China donated anti-malarial drugs to Benin in 2008. The specific date of donation is unclear. In an article by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China, donations of anti-malaria drugs have been an annual event since 2006.

project_name: Embassy donates anti-epidemic materials to National Assembly
description: On July 3, 2020, the Embassy of China in Benin made a donation of anti-epidemic materials to the National Assembly of Benin. Ambassador Peng Jintao and First Deputy Speaker Mariama Chabi represented the two organizations. The shipment consisted of 5,000 single-use medical masks, 40 500 mL bottles of hydro-alcoholic gel, five 25 liter cans of 80% alcohol, and five spray bottles for disinfecting. This donation was intended to aid the Government of Benin in its fight agains the COVID-19 pandemic.

project_name: Ningxia Health and Welfare Commission donates anti-epidemic supplies
description: On September 8, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Benin facilitated the handover of anti-epidemic medical materials from the National Health Commission of China and the Health Commission of Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region to the Government of Benin. Members of the 24th Chinese medical team to Benin were present at the ceremony (see ProjectID#87413).

project_name: Donates anti-Malarial drugs
description: On October 31, 2011, Ambassador Tao Weiguang and Benin’s Minister of Health Gazal attended the handover ceremony of antimalarial drugs held in the Ministry of Health of Benin. Also present at the ceremony was Zhang Shengli, the Chinese Embassy Economic and Commercial Counselor. In an article by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China, donations of anti-malaria drugs have been an annual event since 2006.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Malaria Control Center at Lokossa Regional Hospital
description: In 2008, the Chinese Government provided a grant to the Government of Benin for the establishment of a malaria control center at Lokossa Regional Hospital. An inauguration ceremony or the center was held on 10 November, 2008.

project_name: Embassy donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On August 5, 2020, the Chinese Ambassador to Benin, Peng Jintao, delivered a batch of anti-epidemic materials to the Benin Directorate of Emigration and Immigration (DEI) for the purpose of aiding Benin's fight against the COVID-19 pandemic. It is unclear what the materials consisted of and which Chinese institution was responsible for the funding.

project_name: Donates anti-Malarial drugs
description: China donated anti-malarial drugs to Benin in 2007. On May 3, 2007, Chinese Ambassador to Benin Li Beifen and Benin Health Minister Flor Gumbo attended the handover ceremony of China's 2 million yuan anti-malarial drugs to Benin. In an article by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China, it is stated that donations of anti-malaria drugs have been an annual event since 2006.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Parakou Military Instruction Hospital
description: In 2009, China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) provided an RMB 42,700,000 ($6.4 million) grant to the Government of Benin for the Phase 1 of Parakou Military Instruction Hospital Construction Project. This value of the Chinese Government’s grant commitment for this project eventually increased to 6 billion CFAF (about $12 million USD).  Phase 1 involved the construction of a modern, 100-bed hospital that provides pediatric, obstetric, gynecological, laboratory, medical imaging and mortuary services.  More specifically, the project involved the construction of an administrative building, an amphitheater with 256 seats, a medical building with various units (medicine, surgery, maternity, odontostomatology, emergencies, radiology services, biomedical analysis laboratory), a complex of three operating theaters, anti-malaria center, a laundry room; a generator, a water tower with a capacity of 50,000 liters, a canteen, a guardhouse building, a mortuary, an electrical room, and an incinerator.  The Parakou Military Instruction Hospital is located in the town of Parakou within Okédama district on the edge of an interstate road.  China Railway Group Limited was the contractor responsible for implementation.  A formal groundbreaking ceremony was held on 16 January, 2009.  Construction started on 28 April, 2009 and ended on 28 June, 2010.  The project passed final MOFCOM inspection on 2 August, 2010.  Then, a formal project handover ceremony took place on 7 October, 2010.  The hospital was inaugurated on 13 February, 2011 and it began clinical activities on 4 October, 2011.  Then, in 2013, the Chinese Government provided an RMB 11.5 million grant for the Phase 1 of Parakou Military Instruction Hospital Construction Project (captured in linked Project ID#72795).  The Government of Benin later designated the hospital (in 2014) as a University Hospital Center (CHU).  Additionally, in 2014, the Chinese Government provided a RMB 10 million grant for the provision of medical equipment to the hospital (captured in linked Project ID#72796).

project_name: Donates medical aid
description: In May 2013, through the support of the Chongqing Municipal Government, Chongqing Jinshan Science and Technology Co. donated medical equipment worth $500,000 to one of the major referral hospitals in Botswana, the Princess Marina Hospital, which is located in the capital.

project_name: Gov't provides anti-epidemic materials to Office of the First Lady
description: On July 16, 2020, the First Lady of China, Peng Liyuan, provided anti-epidemic materials to the Office of the First Lady in Botswana. The donated supplies included medical supplies, 1,000 blankets, and other cold-proof materials. Peng Liyuan provided the supplies on behalf of the Chinese government. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the Botswana Presidential Affairs Department. China’s Ambassador Zhao Yanbo, Madam Mao Xuehong, the Ambassador's wife, Wang Bangfu, the Political Counselor of the Embassy, ​​and the Acting Minister of the Botswana Presidential Affairs Department attended the event.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for AIDS-related equipment and supplies
description: On January 7, 2007, China and Botswana signed an agreement (exchange of notes) in which China committed to a grant of 2 million CNY for AIDS prevention and acquisition of AIDS-related general supplies. On August 7, 2008, China officially handed over the medical equipment for AIDS prevention to the Government of Botswana, with a handover ceremony held where certificates were signed and exchanged.

project_name: Embassy donates anti-epidemic supplies to Ministry of Health
description: On August 4, 2021, the Chinese Embassy donated a batch of Covid supplies to the Botswana Ministry of Health. The donation included an unknown quantity of oxygen generators and ventilators. The purpose of the project is to help Botswana fight the COVID-19 epidemic.

project_name: Gov't donates ophthalmic equipment
description: From June 27 to July 1, 2011, during the "Hope of Light Cataract Project" (see Project ID #30843), Botswana also received a donation of ophthalmic equipment and consumables worth BWP 20.8 million from China during the same period. On July 3rd, 2011, a ceremony was held for the 30th anniversary of China's medical aid to Botswana. In the ceremony, ophthalmic equipment and medicine was officially handed over with handover certificates signed and exchanged.

project_name: Gov't provides funding for Hope of Light Cataract Project
description: From June 27 to July 1, 2011, a team of ophthalmologists from China successfully performed about 200 cataract operations as part of the "Hope of Light Cataract Project" in Botswana. Botswana also received a donation of ophthalmic equipment and consumables during the same period (see project #30844).

project_name: Gov't provides grant for National Referral STD Treatment and Training Centre
description: During the farewell ceremony for the 11th Chinese Medical Team in 2008, Health Minister, Ms Lesego Motsumi highlighted that the Chinese government has provided a grant of approximately BWP 1.1 million to finance the construction of the National Referral STD Treatment and Training Centre in Gaborone.

project_name: Gov't funds cataract operations at Scottish Livingstone Hospital
description: In 2015, Chinese ophthalmologists composed of 11 experts would perform more than 500 cataract operations in Botswana (援博“光明行”项目).The project was implemented at Scottish Livingstone Hospital, more than 50 km away from Gaborone. The project began on June 17, 2015, and lasted around 30 days. It also involves donation of medical supplies and equipment. This was the second time Chinese government implemented ophthalmic projects in Botswana (see #30843).

project_name: Gov't donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On May 29, 2020, the Chinese government donated anti-epidemic materials to the government of Botswana. The materials included 15,000 protective medical face masks, 150,000 surgical masks, 3,000 medical protective isolation shoe covers, 5,000 pieces of disposable protective clothing, 7,000 medical protective goggles and 7,000 disposable sterilized rubber surgical gloves to the Government of Botswana. These materials will be used for COVID-19 prevention efforts by front-line anti-epidemic workers such as doctors, nurses, and border inspectors. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at Sir Seretse Khama International Airport in Gaborone, Botswana on May 29, 2020. This batch of materials was delivered over two separate days with the first arrival being on May 29, 2020 and the second flight arriving on June 1, 2022. This unique delivery scenario was due to international flight capacity constraints. China’s Ambassador to Botswana Zhao Yanbo and Botswana Minister of Health went to the airport for the handover ceremony on May 29, 2020.

project_name: Embassy donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On May 15, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Botswana handed over a donation of anti-epidemic materials to the Botswana Red Cross Society. According to the Chinese Embassy, the donated materials included masks, goggles, and protective suits. These materials will be used by BRCS staff for COVID-19 prevention efforts. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: China donates mobile clinics
description: On December 12, 2018, a handover ceremony was held for the China's Ministry of Science and Technology donation of seven modular container clinics to Botswana's Ministry of Health and Wellness in Gaborone, the capital of Botswana. The clinics are equipped with general diagnostic equipment and other basic medical equipment. They will help meet medical needs in the rural regions of the southern African country, primarily in regions with a population of less than 20,000. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donates medical equipment to Princess Marina Hospital
description: On September 18, 2015, China donated a group of medical equipment to Princess Marina Hospital in Gaborone, Botswana, through the 14th Chinese Medical Team (see project #35670). A ceremony was held attended by government officials and medical staff of the hospital.

project_name: Gov't donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On September 10, 2020, the Chinese Government provided anti-epidemic materials  to the government of Botswana. These materials will be used for COVID-19 prevention efforts in Botswana. The specific amount and monetary value of this donation are unknown.   A handover ceremony was held for this donation. China’s Ambassador to Botswana, Zhao Yanbo, the Minister of Presidential Affairs, Kabo Morwaeng, Deputy Minister of Presidential Affairs, Dumezweni Mthimkhulu, and Minister of Health Dr. Edwin Dikoloti attended the ceremony.

project_name: Shenzhen Government donates medical masks
description: On August 3, 2020, the Shenzhen Government donated medical masks to the Government of Botswana. This is part of a larger donation of 460,000 masks to 12 African countries, including Egypt, Togo, Ethiopia, Kenya, Zambia, Mali, Tunisia, Sudan, South Sudan, Botswana, Comoros and Cameroon. The specific amount of masks sent to Botswana is unknown. The monetary value of this donation is also unknown.

project_name: Embassy donates medical supplies to Sidilega Hospital
description: On August 16, 2021, the Chinese Embassy donated medical supplies to Sidilega Hospital in Gaborone, Botswana to help support the hospital's anti-COVID-19 efforts. The contents of the donation are CPAP machines, oxygen concentrators and thermometers. The medical supplies were handed over by Chinese Ambassador Wang Xuefeng and his team.

project_name: China donates anti-epidemic supplies
description: On March 28, 2020, the Chinese government provided anti-epidemic supplies to Botswana. The supplies included 1,000 face masks, 500 PPE, 300 infrared thermometers, goggles, gloves and shoe covers. The monetary value of this donation is unknown. The supplies arrived at  Sir Seretse Khama International Airport in Gaborone, the capital of Botswana.

project_name: Donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On August 5, 2021, the Chinese Embassy in Botswana, the United Nations Population Fund in Botswana and the Ministry of Health and Wellness jointly held the handover ceremony of China's anti-epidemic personal protective materials. The US$60,000 PPE includes 1,900 isolation gowns, 20 boxes of examination gloves, 40 boxes of surgical gloves, 40 boxes of surgical masks, 1,650 goggles, 1,980 face shields and 1,900 coveralls, which will be used to protect frontline workers amid the third wave of the COVID-19 pandemic.   This donation is a project carried out by China and the United Nations Population Fund under the framework of the South-South Cooperation Assistance Fund.

project_name: Shandong Province donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On May 7, 2020, the Shandong Province in China provided anti-epidemic materials to Botswana. The materials included 30,000 surgical masks, 1,000 N95 masks, and 6,000 surgical gloves. These materials will be used for COVID-19 prevention efforts. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony took place for this donation at the Chinese Embassy in Botswana. Zhao Yanbo, China’s Ambassador to Botswana, and the Minister of Health and Wellness of Botswana attended the ceremony. The ceremony coincided with the 45th anniversary of diplomatic relations between China and Botswana.

project_name: CCP donates anti-epidemic materials to Botswana Democratic Party
description: On October 23, 2020, the International Department of the CPC Central Committee donated medical supplies to the Botswana Democratic Party. These materials will be used for COVID-19 prevention efforts in Botswana. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donates Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine
description: On April 25, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Botswana.  The Chinese Government pledged to donate an additional 2 million COVID-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Botswana in 2022.

project_name: China National Complete Plant Import & Export Corp. donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On April 17, 2020, China National Complete Plant Import & Export Corp., Ltd. provided anti-epidemic materials to the Embassy of Botswana in China. This donation included masks, gloves and other anti-epidemic materials. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. Botswana's Ambassador to China, Motusi Palai, and the Political and Economic Counsellor received the supplies from Chen Ming, the general manager of the Second Engineering and Trade Division of China National Complete Plant. Guizhou Provincial Transportation Planning Survey and Design Institute also sent staff to participate in the donation ceremony.

project_name: Donates supplies to health and social promotion centers
description: On November 6, 2020 the Chinese Medical team in Burkina Faso (see project ID#94573) donated supplies to the Health and Social Promotion Center (French: Centre de santé et de promotion sociale, CSPS) in Moaga, Burkina Faso. The donation included antimalarial, antibiotic, antipyretic, analgesic, and antihemorrhoidal drugs. It also contained N95 surgical masks, hydroalcoholic gels, and disinfectants. On the same day, the team made a similar donation to the CSPS in Saatenga, a town approximately 32 kilometers from Moaga.

project_name: Gov't donates anti-epidemic equipment
description: On February 10, 2021, the Chinese Government donated a batch of anti-epidemic equipment to Burkina Faso. The equipment included 500,000 face masks and 20,000 COVID-19 screening kits. The purpose of this donation is to support Burkina Faso’s COVID-19 response efforts. The monetary value of this donation is 250 million CFA Francs.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. China’s Ambassador to Burkina Faso, Li Jian, and the Minister of Health of Burkina Faso, Charlemagne Ouédraogo, attended the ceremony.

project_name: Donates medical supplies
description: On October 2, 2020, Chinese Ambassador to Burkina Faso Li Jian, together with Burkina Faso Prime Minister Dabire, Health Minister Lugai, and the World Health Organization (WHO) representative in Burkina Faso, attended the handover ceremony of anti-epidemic supplies donated by the Chinese government to the Burkina Faso government. This batch of supplies includes 50 ventilators, 40 oxygen concentrators, 6,000 pieces of protective clothing, 100 infrared thermometers, and 10,000 N95 masks. The donation was valued at XOF 600 million.

project_name: Donates medical equipment
description: On October 30, 2018, China donated medical equipment to Burkina Faso worth 82 million CFA francs. The donation included an ECG machine, a multi-parameter monitor, surgical devices and equipment, medical consumables and personal protective equipment. This donation was made in addition to the provision of China's first medical team to Burkina Faso (see linked ProjectID#60122).

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Yalgado Ouédraogo University Hospital
description: In 2020, the Chinese Government and the Government of Burkina Faso signed a CFA 40 million grant agreement for the Covid-19 Isolation Center Construction Project at Yalgado Ouédraogo University Hospital. The purpose of the project was to construct a Covid-19 Isolation Center at Yalgado Ouédraogo University Hospital. Project implementation commenced on April 15, 2020. The project was completed on July 3, 2020.

project_name: Embassy donates medical supplies
description: On March 24, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Burkina Faso donated a batch of protective equipment to the Burkina Faso Ministry of Health to support the prevention and control of the COVID-19 pandemic. Ambassador to Burkina Faso, Li Jian, and Director General of the Medical Supplies Management Department of the Ministry of Health of Burkina Faso, Koanda, handed over the supplies at the Embassy.

project_name: Donates medical supplies
description: On April 16, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Burkina Faso provided a batch of medical supplies to the government of Burkina Faso to support the prevention and control of the COVID-19 pandemic in Burkina Faso. More than 20 Burkina Faso officials and members of the local media attended the handover ceremony, including the Chinese Ambassador to Burkina Faso, Li Jian, the Director General of the Office of the President of Burkina Faso, Zagre, the Secretary General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Burkina Faso, Sorg, the Director of the Office of the Ministry of Health of Burkina Faso, David, the representative of the World Food Program in Burkina Faso, and representatives from the World Health Organization (WHO).   The shipment was nearly four tons and included masks and other protective equipment. The supplies were intended to support a team of Chinese medical experts who arrived the same day to fight Covid-19 (see project ID#93397). The World Food Program Assisted with the transfer of supplies.

project_name: Gov't donates medical equipment to Tengandogo University Hospital
description: On June 4, 2021, the Chinese Government provided medical equipment to Tengandogo University Hospital in Benin. The supplies included technical medical equipment and medical consumables for resuscitation and cardiac surgery. The monetary value of this donation is 50 million FCFA.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. Chinese Ambassador to Burkina Faso, Li Jian, and the Minister of Health of Burkina Faso, Charlemagne Ouédraogo, attended the ceremony.

project_name: CGC Overseas Construction co. donates anti-epidemic supplies
description: Around April 10, 2020, CGC Overseas Construction Co., Ltd. (CGCOC) donated 4,800 medical suits and 96,000 medical masks to several African countries including Burkina Faso. It is unclear how many countries received this donation and how much of this larger donation was specifically sent to Burkina Faso. The monetary value of this donation is also unknown. The donation included 4800 protective suits and 96000 medical masks in total.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Bobo-Dioulasso University Hospital
description: Following the resumption of diplomatic relations between the People’s Republic of China (PRC) and Burkina Faso on May 26, 2018, the PRC Government agreed through its Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) to provide a grant worth CFA 60 billion to the Government of Burkina Faso to fully finance the Bobo-Dioulasso University Hospital Center (CHU) Construction Project.   The purpose of the project is to construct a 500-bed university hospital center. China Aviation Planning and Design Institute (Group) Co., Ltd. (AVIC CAPDI) is responsible for project design and Beijing Urban Construction Group (BUCG) is responsible for project implementation. To implement the project, the municipal council of the municipality of Bobo-Dioulasso adopted, on April 19, 2019, a decision on the partial declassification of 160,000 m2 of the classified Kua forest.   The project location become a bone of contention, as it has faced environmental and other Burkinabe opposition due to its location in the heart of Burkina Faso's Kua forest. After 18 months of protest, on August 13, 2020, in Bobo-Dioulasso, Christophe Marie Joseph Dabiré, the Prime Minister of Burkina Faso, announced the introduction of a new location, the village of Pala near the city of Bobo-Dioulasso. After the presentation of detailed architectural plans for the University Hospital of Bobo-Dioulasso to the Government of Burkina Faso on April 15, 2021, the plan were officially approved by the Chinese side as well on June 16, 2021. Then, on October 21, 2021, the Chinese Ambassador to Burkina Faso, Li Jian participated in a meeting by videoconference call with representatives of Burkinabè Ministries of Health and Foreign Affairs as well as the National BTP Laboratory on the implementation of the project. Beijing Urban Construction won the MOFCOM bid to implement the project in September 2021. Although a formal bricklaying ceremony took place on October 20, 2020, the project’s formal commencement date was December 23, 2021. The project is expected to reach completion within 36 months (December 23, 2024).

project_name: Gov't donates Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine
description: On September 18, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 400,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Burkina Faso. The vaccine handover ceremony was attended by China’s Ambassador to Burkina Faso, Li Jian, other Chinese embassy personnel, Ministerial Representative of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Burkina Faso Clarisse Uoba, Chief of Staff of the Ministry of Health Emmanuel Solgo, UN coordinator in Burkina Faso Manzi, and World Health Organization representative in Burkina Faso Alimata.

project_name: Gov't funds Covid-19 WHO support
description: In March 2020, Chinese government provides USD 1,155,000 to support WHO response to COVID-19 outbreak in Burkina Faso.

project_name: Gov't donates PPE
description: On April 28, 2020, the handover ceremony of the Chinese government's aid to the Burkina Faso government to combat the COVID-19 pandemic was held at the Ministry of Health. Ambassador Li Jian in Burkina Faso and Minister of Health of Burkina Faso Ms. Lugai signed the handover certificate on behalf of the two governments respectively. A total of more than 40 officials from the Ministry of Health of Burkina Faso, medical experts and representatives of medical and nursing staff attended the handover ceremony. The donation included gloves, coveralls, masks, face shields, and other protective clothing. The donation arrived from China in Ghana on April 6, 2020. The United Nations’ Humanitarian Response Depot (UNHRD) in Accra dispatched the supplies to Burkina Faso.

project_name: AVIC International signs memorandum of understanding
description: On January 15th, 2020, Minister of Health, Léonie Claudine and Yang Wang (General Director of AVIC International) sign a MoU in order to improve the health system in Burkina Faso. This will include the construction of the Burkina Faso Bobo-Dioulasso Hospital Project (see project ID#60057), equipping the new hospital with advanced medial equipment, and funding for other hospital rehabilitation projects.

project_name: Donates medical supplies
description: On December 9th, 2018, the People's Republic of China donated an ultrasound machine worth 19 million, cartons of milk, enriched flour, and soap to the Burkina Faso Minister of Health, Nicolas Méda.

project_name: China donates ventilators to Ministry of Health
description: On July 29, 2020 the Chinese Ambassador to Burkina Faso handed over a donation of 46 ventilators to the Ministry of Health. The ventilators were valued at XOF 200 million. They were to be used on Covid-19 patients to improve their chances of survival.

project_name: Provides emergency humanitarian aid
description: On October 3, 2019, the handover of the emergency goods that China aided to Burundi was held at the Burundi Basic Medicine Procurement Center (CAMEBU), with Ms. Josephine, Permanent Secretary Baptiste and Assistant Minister of TMinistère de la Santé Publique et de la Lutte contre le SIDA (Burundi), Sabhimac, General Manager of CAMEBU and Yuan Wang, the Minister of State Affairs Counsellor attending.  In 2019, in order to support the Burundian government to confront the serious emergency situation in the Great Lakes region, China provided emergency rescue trucks to the Burundian government to deliver goods to Burundi three times. The first 8.7 ton materials in humanitarian aid has been transported to Bujumbura International Airport on August 29, 2019, and another two will arrive in succession over the next two weeks. This is the second time that China provided aid to African countries after the outbreak of the epidemic in West African countries in 2014.（See: 中国向布隆迪提供紧急人道主义埃博拉防控物资)

project_name: Gov't provides grant for anti-Malarial drugs
description: On August 1 and 24, 2006, the Chinese Government and the Government of Burundi signed letters of exchange for the donation of a batch of anti-malarial drugs. The monetary value of this grant commitment was RMB 1 million. The drugs were successfully delivered on April 24, 2007.

project_name: Qinghai pledges funding for Gitega Hospital
description: On September 13, 2005 during a visit to Gitega, Burundi, Qinghai's vice-governor, Mr Deng Ben Tai, promised to rehabilitate the hospital equipment of Gitega hospital. The amount, current status, and start and end dates are unknown.

project_name: Donates vehicles to Ministry of Health
description: On April 23, 2012, China donated six vehicles (two ambulances, two minibusses, and two small-sized cars) worth an estimated 200,000 USD to Burundi. The vehicles were given by the Chinese government to the Burundian public health and AIDS control ministry in order to strengthen the country's health sector.

project_name: Gov't provides grant to Mpanda General Hospital
description: On December 22, 2010, the Chinese Government and the Government of Burundi signed a $1.4 million grant agreement for the provision of training and medical supplies to support Mpanda General Hospital. The donated medical supplies including ambulances, medical equipment, consumables, and biochemical reagents. These supplies were delivered and handed over to the authorities on October 12, 2012.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for anti-Malarial drugs
description: On April 24, 2007, the Chinese Government provided an RMB 1 million grant to the Government of Burundi for the provision of anti-malarial drugs. The supplier of the anti-malarial drugs is unknown

project_name: China donates AIDS medicine and medical equipment
description: On April 4, 2020, China donated AIDS medicines and medical equipment, worth USD 400,000, to the Burundi Ministry of Public Health. The materials are meant to help the country's fight against AIDS. The donated materials will be used in the resuscitation and surgery departments at the Prince Regent Charles Hospital.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for the Mpanda General Hospital
description: During the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC) in 2008, the Chinese Government and the Government of Burundi signed a grant agreement for the Mpanda General Hospital Construction Project. The reported size of the grant commitment amount was RMB 63 million. The project involved the construction of a 100-bed hospital, including a main building, annexes, and various types of medical equipment (including scanners, digital radiography, and neurological ultrasound technology). Guangdong Foreign Construction Co., Ltd (GDFC) was the contractor responsible for project implementation.   Hospital construction began on April 16, 2009. An official groundbreaking ceremony then took place on May 14, 2009. The project was officially completed and handed over to the authorities on January 19, 2011. At the opening ceremony of the hospital, China’s Ambassador to Burundi committed to provide medical equipment and staff training to the hospital (worth an additional $1.4 million, see Project ID #30065). This project may be part of an ETCA signed by Burundi and China in 2008 (#345)

project_name: Gov't provides grant for medical equipment
description: On October 27th, 2005, a transfer ceremony was held at the Grand Prince Hospital in Bujumbura for the donation of $500,000 worth of medicines and medical equipment. Shi Hu, the Chargé d’affaires of the Chinese Embassy in Burundi, and Mr. Louis Mbonegao, Chief Inspector of the Ministry of Health of Burundi, signed the handover certificate on behalf of the two governments.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for anti-Malarial drugs
description: On March 27, 2008, the Chinese Government provided a grant to the Government of Burundi for the provision of anti-malarial drugs. The monetary value of this grant is unknown.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for medical equipment
description: On September 28th, 2004 a handover ceremony was held at the Embassy in Burundi for the donation of $500,000 worth of medicines and medical equipment. Ambassador Feng Zhijun and the Minister of Public Health of Burundi signed the handover certificate on behalf of the two governments.

project_name: Embassy donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On July 27, 2021, the Chinese Embassy in Burundi donated anti-epidemic medical materials to the Burundi Ministry of Public Health and AIDS Prevention and Control. The materials included ventilators and other miscellaneous medical supplies. This was the 8th batch of materials donated by China to fight COVID-19 in Burundi. It was distributed to hospitals including the Grand Prince Hospital. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.   A handover ceremony was held for this donation. Ambassador Zhao Jiangping, Assistant Minister of Public Health Nzigi Rabamia, Economic and Commercial Counselor Xiao Guofeng, President of the Grand Prince Hospital Oscar, and members of the 20th Chinese medical team to Burundi attended the ceremony. During the ceremony, Ambassador Zhao and Assistant Nzigi Rabamia signed the donation certificate.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Malaria Control Center
description: At the Beijing Summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC) in November 2006, the Chinese Government pledged to construct a malaria prevention and treatment center in Burundi. Then, on October 12, 2007, China's Ambassador to Burundi signed an exchange of letters on the establishment of a China-Burundi Malaria Control Center.   The opening ceremony for the Center was held on March 27, 2008. The China-Burundi Malaria Control Center is located at the Institut National de Santé Publique (INSP) in Bujumbura. At least 5 Chinese experts were deployed to support the work of the Center. According to the Government of Burundi's Development Assistance Database (DAD), the Chinese Government disbursed $439,811 of grant funding in support of this project.

project_name: China donates anti-epidemic materials to University of Burundi
description: On December 3, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Burundi donated the 2nd batch of anti-epidemic materials to the Confucius Institute at the University of Burundi. The "epidemic prevention health kits" were given to the teachers and volunteers at the Institute..  This project is linked to Project ID#92110, which captures the first batch of anti-epidemic materials donated to the Confucius Institute at the University of Burundi.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Prince Regent Charles Hospital
description: In 2005, the Chinese Government provided a grant to the Government of Burundi for the construction of a CT scanning room at Prince Regent Charles Hospital. Anhui Foreign Economic Construction Group (AFECC) was the contractor responsible for implementation. The project launched on December 9, 2005. A 2011 (date-stamped photograph of the CT scanning room being used suggests that this project was successfully completed.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for anti-Malarial drugs
description: On July 2, 2009 and July 9, 2009, the Chinese Government and the Government of Burundi signed an agreement related to the donation of a new batch of anti-malaria drugs. The monetary value of this donation is unknown. This was the 4th batch of anti-malaria drugs the Chinese Government donated to Burundi since 2006. The drugs arrived in Burundi in October 2009 and were handed over to the authorities on February 12, 2010.

project_name: Qinghai Province donates anti-epidemic supplies
description: On May 28, 2020, China's Qinghai Province donated anti-epidemic supplies to Burundi. The supplies included 1,000 sets of disposable medical protective clothing, 30,240 medical surgical masks, 3,000 medical protective masks, 300 goggles, and 20 infrared induction thermometers from Qinghai Provincial Health and Health Commission.

project_name: Donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On November 3, 2020, China donated its 7th batch of anti-epidemic materials, worth USD 550,000, to Burundi. The materials donated included 50 respirators, 50 oxygen concentrators, 200 respirator accessories, 160,000 N95 masks, 50,000 surgical masks, 500 infrared thermometers, and other medical equipment. The handover ceremony took place in Burundi's Basic Medicine Procurement Center..

project_name: Donates to Bird Flu relief
description: On August 31, 2006, China donated $100,000 USD in cash assistance to Cape Verde to help prevent the spread of bird flu. On this date, the cash assistance was officially handed over to Cape Verdean government through the signing of its handover certificate. This project is completed.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for OB-GYN building
description:
On December 20, 2012, the Chinese Ambassador to Cape Verde and the Cape Verdean Minister of Foreign Affairs signed an implementation agreement for the OB-GYN Building Refurbishment Project. 
 
 China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) was the source of grant funding for this project, but the monetary value of the financial commitment is unknown. The purpose of this project was refurbish the basement of the obstetrics and gynaecology (OB-GYN) building (妇产科楼地下室进行局部改造) in Agostinho Neto Hospital (HAN or Praia Central Hospital or 普拉亚中心医院). The Chinese Government also funded the initial construction of the OB-GYN building, which is captured in Project ID#35064. China Liaoning International Cooperation Group (辽宁省国际经济技术合作集团有限) was the contractor responsible for implementation. 
 
 The expected duration of its construction contract with MOFCOM was seven months. The project passed the final MOFCOM inspection in November 2013 and the official handover ceremony took place on December 30, 2013.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Praia Central Hospital
description:
On December 20, 2001, the Chinese Government and the Government of Cape Verde signed an exchange of letters regarding the Praia Central Hospital Inpatient Department Construction Project. China’s Ministry of Commerce was the source of grant funding for this project, but the monetary value of this financial commitment is unknown. 
 
 The project involved the construction of an inpatient department (住院部) at Praia Central Hospital (Agostinho Neto Hospital or 普拉亚中心医院). The contractor responsible for implementation is unknown. Construction officially began on March 6, 2004. Then, from August 18-26, 2004, five Chinese experts carried out a mid-term project inspection on behalf of MOFCOM and found its implementation to be excellent. The project handover ceremony took place on August 30, 2005.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Praia Central Hospital
description:
In 2011, China’s Ministry of Commerce provides provided grant funding equivalent to approximately RMB 9.5 million to the Government of Cape Verde for the Praia Central Hospital Outpatient Consultation Center and OB-GYN Building Equipping Project. The purpose of this project was to facilitate the provision and installation of medical equipment in the OB-GYN building and outpatient consultation center at Agostinho Neto Hospital (HAN or Praia Central Hospital or 普拉亚中心医院), which is located in the capital city of Praia. 
 
 China Liaoning International Cooperation Group (辽宁省国际经济技术合作集团有限) was the contractor responsible for implementation. It was awarded a MOFCOM contract in 2011. The project was officially completed and handed over to the Government of Cape Verde on April 29, 2011.

project_name: Gov't provides loan for Praia Central Hospital
description: On January 11, 2006, Chinese Foreign Minister Li Zhaoxing made an official visit to Cape Verde. During his visit, he signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA), which committed EUR 2 million for the Praia Central Hospital Outpatient Consultation Center and OB-GYN Building Construction Project (captured in Project ID#35064).  Hunan Constructing Engineering Group and China Liaoning International Cooperation Group (辽宁省国际经济技术合作集团有限) were the contractors responsible for implementation. Construction agreements were signed in May 2008. However, construction itself did not begin until March 1, 2009. An inauguration ceremony for the outpatient and OB-GYN buildings took place on May 20, 2011.

project_name: Funds Baptista de Sousa Hospital
description: On January 28, 2021, the Chinese ambassador to Cabo Verde, Du Xiaocong, exchanged letters with the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Cabo Verde, Rui Figueiredo Soares, for the Chinese funding of a new maternity and pediatric building at Cabo Verde’s Baptista de Sousa Hospital.   On the same day, Du Xiacong and Rui Figueiredo Soares signed an inter-governmental economic and technical cooperation agreement (ETCA). The agreement will go toward projects within the São Vicente Marine Special Economic Zone (captured in Project ID #93126). The exchange of letters and ETCA are worth a combined RMB 100 million; the financial breakdown between projects is unknown.

project_name: Funds health project
description: In 2015, the Deputy Minister and Health of Cape Verde and the head of the Chinese Embassy affairs signed a protocol, ​​worth 280,000,000 Cape Verde Escudo. It stated the construction of a maternity ward with four infirmaries, which includes a puerperium, gynecology, obstetrics and neonatology, 92 beds, an obstetric and surgical center.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Praia Central Hospital
description: On December 20, 2001 an exchange of letters was signed between China and Cabo Verde for the Praia Central Hospital Surgical Ward Construction Project. In 2002, China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) provided a grant to the Government of Cabo Verde for this project. The monetary value of this grant commitment is unknown. However, it is known that the Chinese Government committed EUR 1.9 million for this project and the Chinese Medical Team Housing Project (as captured via Project ID#56916). For the time being, AidData estimates that MOFCOM evenly divided the funds across the two projects (committing EUR 950,000 to each project.  The Praia Central Hospital Surgical Ward Construction Project involve the construction of a new 120-bed surgical ward (外科病房楼 or bloco cirúrgico or enfermaria) at Praia Central Hospital (普拉亚中心医院 or Hospital Central da Praia or Hospital Agostinho Neto). China Shaanxi International Economic and Technical Cooperation was the contractor responsible for implementation. A foundation-laying ceremony took place on July 8, 2003.   The project was originally scheduled for completion and delivery in mid-2004 but its precise completion date is unknown. As of December 2010, the surgical ward was reportedly still in its final stage of construction.

project_name: Donates medical equipment
description:
In 2011, Liaoning International Economic and Technical Cooperation Group won a contract to donate medical equipment and supplies to Cabo Verde. The supplies were financed through a grant from the Chinese government.
 
 On August 3, 2012, China officially handed over this equipment worth 135 million CVE to the intensive care unit in Agostinho Neto Hospital (HAN or Praia Central Hospital). The donation is a product of the Fourth Ministerial Conference of the Forum for Economic and Trade Cooperation between China and Africa.

project_name: Gov't provides loan for Praia Central Hospital
description: In December 2005, the Chinese Government and the Government of Cape Verde signed a financing framework agreement for the Praia Central Hospital Outpatient Consultation Center and OB-GYN Building Construction Project. Then, on January 11, 2006, the two governments signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA), which committed an EUR 2 million interest-free loan for the project. In December 2008, the two governments signed another Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA), which committed another interest-free loan for the project. In total, China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) lent approximately RMB 31 million to the Government of Cape Verde for this project. It also provided grant funding equivalent to approximately RMB 9.5 million for the provision and installation of medical equipment at Praia Central Hospital (captured in Project ID#359).   The Praia Central Hospital Outpatient Consultation Center and OB-GYN Building Construction Project involved the construction of a new obstetrics and gynaecology (OB-GYN) building (妇产科楼地下室进行局部改造) and outpatient consultation center at Agostinho Neto Hospital (HAN or Praia Central Hospital or 普拉亚中心医院) in the capital city of Praia. The outpatient building was expected to occupy 782 square meters and provide eleven specialty services: medicine, urology, ophthalmology, surgery, ear nose and throat services, trauma services, orthopedics, stomatology, allergy services, cardiology and gastroenterology. The OB-GYN center was expected to occupy 2,128 square meters.   Hunan Constructing Engineering Group and China Liaoning International Cooperation Group (辽宁省国际经济技术合作集团有限) were the contractors responsible for implementation. Construction agreements were signed in May 2008. However, construction itself did not begin until March 1, 2009. An inauguration ceremony for the outpatient and OB-GYN buildings took place on May 20, 2011. The Chinese Government later funded the refurbishment of the OB-GYN building in 2012 (see Project ID#35065).

project_name: Donates medical equipment to Praia Central Hospital
description:
On March 1, 2016, a ceremony was held where the Chinese medical team in Cape Verde's Hospital Agostinho Neto (HAN or Praia Central Hospital) officially donated medical equipment to the hospital. This ceremony was attended by Chinese Ambassador to Cabo Verde Du Xiaocong.
 
 On December 19, 2016, another group of medical supplies was donated to Hospital Agostinho Neto as part of the "annual Chinese aid" of medical supplies to Cape Verde. The medical equipment donated included surgery equipment, testing equipment, and medical clothing. The value of these donations are not known. This project is completed.

project_name: Donates surgery equipment to Praia Central Hospital
description:
On August 25, 2017, the Sichuan National Health and Family Planning Commission of China donated 2 video laparoscopic surgery devices to Cape Verde's principal hospital, Hospital Agostinho Neto (HAN or Praia Central Hospital). The Sichuan Provincial Health and Family Planning Commission Maternal and Child Health Experts Group also stayed in Cape Verde for one week to provide training on laparoscopic surgery for doctors and nurses in the Cabo Verdean hospital.
 
 The exact value of this donation and training is unknown. This project is completed.

project_name: Gov't provides loan for Praia Central Hospital
description:
On November 4, 2013, the Chinese Government and the Government of Cape Verde signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA), which committed an RMB 50 million interest-free loan for multiple projects (see Project ID#72610). The Government of Cape Verde used RMB 12.42 million (CVE 146 million) of the proceeds from this loan to finance the Praia Central Hospital Laundry Room Project. 
 
 Then, in February 2015, the two government signed an exchange of notes on the Praia Central Hospital Laundry Room Project. This project involved the construction of a laundry room at Agostinho Neto Hospital (HAN or Praia Central Hospital or 普拉亚中心医院). It also involved the installation of a pump house, diesel generator, drying room, a gate, and walls. The laundry room (“lavandaria”) washes clothes for the hospital and other facilities on the island of Santiago. 
 
 On December 17, 2015, Cape Verde's Ministry of Health and China National Trade Engineering Design and Research Institute signed a design contract for the project. Then, on June 28, 2016, Chinese and Cape Verdean government officials signed an implementation agreement for the project with Jiangsu Construction Engineering Group as the contractor. A groundbreaking ceremony took place on October 18, 2016, and works were originally scheduled for completion in July 2017. The laundry room was officially opened on March 2, 2018.

project_name: Gov't donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On July 15, 2020, the Government of China donated anti-epidemic materials to the Government of Cabo Verde. The contents of the donation are unknown.

project_name: Gov't donates medical supplies
description: On April 20, 2020, the Chinese Government donated medical supplies to the Government of Cabo Verde. The donation includes  12,000 masks, 2,000 personal protective suits, 500 infrared thermometers, 2,000 pairs of goggles, 10,000 gloves and 10,000 disposable shoe covers. The Health Minister of Cabo Verde received the donations. The donation is used to fight the COVID-19 epidemic as it goes through Cabo Verde.

project_name: Gov't donates Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine
description: On June 12, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 50,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines and over 50,000 syringes to the Government of Cape Verde. During the handover ceremony for the vaccines at Nelson Mandela International Airport in the capital city of Praia, Cape Verdean Prime Minister Ulisses Correia e Silva expressed gratitude for China's support, saying his country would fulfill its vaccination plan to vaccinate 70 percent of the population by the end of this year.

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: On August 3, 2009, China and Cameroon signed agreements on the donation of 2 million RMB for the purchase and shipping of a batch of anti-malaria drugs.

project_name: Embassy donates anti-epidemic supplies
description: On November 5, 2020, the Chinese Embassy donated anti-epidemic supplies to the Cameroon Institute of International Relations. The donation is intended to increase the School of International Relations' ability to fight the COVID-19 pandemic. The specific amount/type of supplies and the monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. Counselor Wang Dong of the Chinese Embassy and the Secretary General of the Cameroonian Institute of International Relations attended the ceremony.

project_name: CGC Overseas Construction co. donates anti-epidemic supplies
description: Around April 10, 2020, CGC Overseas Construction Co., Ltd. (CGCOC) donated 4,800 medical suits and 96,000 medical masks to several African countries including Cameroon. It is unclear how many countries received this donation and how much of this larger donation was specifically sent to Cameroon. The monetary value of this donation is also unknown. The donation included 4800 protective suits and 96000 medical masks in total.

project_name: Embassy in cameroon donates medical supplies
description: On November 16, 2021, the Chinese embassy in Cameroon held a handover ceremony for the donation to the Chantal Biya Foundation to help people with disabilities. Counselor Wang Dong of the embassy and Professor Xie Luo, director of the Technical and Medical Division of the Maternal and Child Center of the Chantal Biya Foundation, attended the ceremony.

project_name: MOFCOM provides grant for Gyneco-Obstetric and Pediatric Hospital
description: On August 3, 2009, China's Ministry of Commerce signed a grant agreement -- through China Development Bank (CDB) -- worth RMB 50,000,000 with Cameroon's Ministry of Public Health for the construction of and equipment for the Gyneco-Obstetric and Pediatric Hospital in the city of Douala (Projet de construction et d’équipement de l’hôpital gynéco­obstétrique et pédiatrique de Douala (HGOPD)).  Shanxi Construction Engineering was responsible for the implementation of this project.  Construction for the Gyneco-Obstetric and Pediatric Hospital was completed November 17, 2015, and it was handed over on the same day.  Two interest-free loans from MOFCOM were also provided for this specific project (one worth RMB 30 million, as captured in linked ProjectID#58705, and one worth RMB 50 million, which is captured in linked Project ID#314.  In February 2007, the Chinese Government pledged the provision of expertise on studies for the construction of the Gynaeco-Obstetrics and Paediatric Hospital of Douala worth FCFA 44,800,000 (see linked ProjectID#22839).

project_name: Donates anti-Malarial medicine
description: On July 8th, 2015, the Chinese ambassador to Cameroon, Wei Wenhua, and Cameroon's Minister of Economy, Planning and Regional Development, Nganou Djoumessi Emmanuel, signed an agreement for the grant of anti-malarial drugs to Cameroon in Yaounde. On November 19th of the same year, the handover certificate was signed between the Chinese Ambassador to Cameroon, Wei Wenhua and Cameroon's Minister of Public Health, Andre Mama Fuda. This project is completed. The exact amount of anti-malarial drugs which were given to Cameroon is unclear.

project_name: Gov't donates Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine
description: In 2021, the Chinese Government donated approximately 1.2 million doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Cameroon. The Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Cameroon on April 11, 2021. Then, on December 14, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 1 million donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Cameroon.

project_name: Embassy donates PPE to Ministry of Health
description: On May 29, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Cameroon donated PPE to the Cameroon Ministry of Health. The donated materials included gloves, masks, gowns, and protective footwear. Details about the number of supplies and the monetary value are unknown.  A handover ceremony took place for this donation. The Cameroon Minister of Health and China’s Ambassador to Cameroon, Wang Yingwu, attended the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't donates medical equipment to Buea Regional Hospital
description: On May 6, 2020, the Chinese government provided a donation of anti-epidemic supplies to the Buea Regional Hospital of Cameroon. The donated supplies included an ambulance, two imaging machines, and two portable ultrasound machines, along with 100 hospital beds, 100 mattresses, and an unknown number of surgical kits. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.  Bernard Okalia Bilai, a governor of the Southwest region of Cameroon, received the consignment of supplies at the Southwest Governor's Office in Buea. According to Bilai, the supplies will be used for COVID-19 prevention efforts in the region.

project_name: MOFCOM provides loan for hospital
description: On January 31, 2007, China's Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and Cameroon's Ministry of Public Health signed an RMB 30,000,000 loan agreement for the Douala Gyneco-Obstetric and Pediatric Hospital Construction and Equipping Project. The loan, which is captured via Project ID#58705, carried the following borrowing terms: a 21 year maturity, a 7 year grace period, and a 0% interest rate. As of December 31, 2020, this loan had achieved a 100% disbursement rate and its outstanding amount was zero. Then, on August 3, 2009, the Chinese Government provided a grant worth RMB 50 million to the Government of Cameroon for the Douala Gyneco-Obstetric and Pediatric Hospital Construction and Equipping Project (captured via Project ID#59618). Several months later, on November 5, 2009, China's Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) issued the Government of Cameroon a RMB 50 million loan — through an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) — for the Douala Gyneco-Obstetric and Pediatric Hospital Construction and Equipping Project. The loan, which is captured via Project ID#314, carried the following borrowing terms: a 20 year maturity, a 10 year grace period, and a 0% interest rate. As of December 31, 2020, this loan had achieved a 100% disbursement rate and its outstanding amount was zero.  The purpose of the project was to construct and equip the Douala Gyneco-Obstetric and Pediatric Hospital (Projet de construction et d’équipement de l’hôpital gynéco-obstétrique et pédiatrique de Douala, or HGOPD).  Shanxi Construction Engineering was the contractor responsible for project implementation. Construction began in October 2009 and the the hospital was handed to the Cameroonian authorities on November 17, 2015.

project_name: Gov't donates equipment to hospital
description: Between January 30-February 1, 2007, at a ceremony attended by Chinese President Hu Jintao and Cameroonian President Paul Biya, the Chinese Government donated equipment to the Gynaeco-Obstetrics and Paediatric Hospital of Yaounde worth FCFA 64,000,000.

project_name: Donates equipment to Mbalmayo and Guider hospitals
description: In 2003, China agreed to refurbish the Chinese constructed Mbalmayo and Guider hospitals. In subsequent years, the Guider hospital received a generator to produce electricity in the event of a power cut by the national electricity company and other equipments valued at 91 million FCFA (140,000 euros). This included a multi-purpose x-ray machine, two electrocardiographs, one sonar imaging machine, four cardioscopes, one multi-functional anaesthetic machine, one ophthalmoscope, one electric bed, one dental chair, two computers, one pressurised disinfector, one surgical microscope, two infrared lamps, two life-support machines, and one digital photocopier. The Guider hospital received the generator in 2004.

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria medical equipment
description: On July 20, 2011, the governments of China and Cameroon signed documents in which China will supply medical equipment for the anti-malaria fight estimated at 1.5 million yuan (about FCFA 107 million). The agreements were signed by Hu Jintao and Cameroonian President Paul Biya. The status of the agreement is uncertain.

project_name: Provides grant for new medical supplies
description: An MOU was signed on December 5th of 2011 between China and Cameroon for the China-Cameroon Capsule Endoscopy New Diagnostic and Clinical Technology Demonstration and Training Center at the Yaounde Women and Children Hospital in Cameroon. The center was built by the Ministry of Science and Technology of China and implemented by Chongqing Jinshan Technology (Group) Co., Ltd. The company has presented a batch of capsule endoscopic equipment and capsules to Yaounde Women and Children Hospital as well as conducted a four-day technology training for local doctors. The center and training was completed on December 10th, 2011 (Ministry of Commerce of the People's Republic of China).

project_name: Gov't donates anti-epidemic equipment to government
description: On June 17, 2020, the Chinese government donated 8.3 tons of anti-epidemic equipment to the Cameroonian government. This batch of equipment consisted of 10,032 test kits, 20,000 N95 masks, 300,000 surgical masks, 15,000 protective suits, 15,000 pairs of protective glasses, 15,000 pairs of surgical gloves, and 3,000 pairs of surgical shoes. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony took place for this donation in Yaoundé, the capital of Cameroon. The Chinese Ambassador to Cameroon Wang Yingwu, a representative of President Biya, the Minister of State and Secretary-General of the Presidential Office, the Minister of Public Health of Cameroon, ​​the State Secretary of the Ministry of Public Health, the Governor of the Central Region, the Defense Attache Chai Xiaojiang, and the Economic and Commercial Counselor Wei Shengzi attended the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't donates Covid-19 WHO pandemic relief
description: In March 2020, Chinese Government provides USD 1,192,990 to support the World Health Organization response to COVID-19 outbreak in Cameroon.   This project is captured in UNOCHA Financial Tracking Service as Flow ID #218731.

project_name: Company donates diesel generator to hospital
description: On July 1, 2003, Hainan International Company donated a set of diesel generator 64GFZ to a hospital in Buea Cameroon. The donation consisted of 1 diesel engine, 1  generator, and 1 power distribution cabinet worth RMB 60,000 in total.

project_name: Funds CT scanner for yaounde Gyaeco-Obstetric and Paediatric Hospital
description:
In 2010, the technical cooperation group of Yaounde Women and Children Hospital of Cameroon carried out key maintenance on the CT scanner (model Neusoft CT-2800) of Yaounde Gynaeco-Obstetrics and Paediatric Hospital. This CT scanner was donated to the Cameroon Women and Children's Hospital during President Hu Jintao's visit to Cameroon in 2007. The repair of this CT scanner has been completed.
 
 As of December 2010, the technical cooperation of the Yaoundé Women and Children Hospital in Cameroon has been carried out to the fifth phase, which is implemented by the China Medical and Health Foreign Technical Cooperation Corporation (中国医疗卫生对外技术合作公司). Its main task is to provide medical treatment for Yaoundé Women's and Children's Hospital, Mbarmayo Hospital and Buea Hospital Equipment for maintenance (Mofcom).

project_name: Xinjiang Communications Construction group donates anti-epidemic supplies
description: On November 5, 2020, Xinjian Communications Construction Group donated anti-epidemic supplies to the Cameroon Ministry of Public Works. The donated supplies included 3,000 masks, 20 protective suits, 20 sets of goggles, and 100 capsules of Lianhua Qingwen. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. Mr. Tang Ahanda Barnabe, the Deputy Minister of the Ministry of Public Works of Cameroon, and a representative of Xinjiang Communications Construction Group attended the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't donates Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine
description: In 2021, the Chinese Government donated approximately 1.2 million doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Cameroon. The Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Cameroon on April 11, 2021. Then, on December 14, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 1 million donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Cameroon.

project_name: MOFCOM donates anti-Malarial drugs for Ministry of Health
description: On September 25, 2012, China's Ministry of Commerce signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) with Cameroon's Ministry of Public Health to provide 4 million CNY worth of anti-malarial drugs manufactured in China (Projet de fourniture des médicaments antipaludiques).  The anti-malarial drugs were delivered on September 25, 2013.  Since 2010, China has put effort into treating malaria in Cameroon as well as other African countries.

project_name: Embassy donates anti-epidemic kits to cMinistry of Defense
description: On June 15, 2020, the Chinese Ambassador to Cameroon, Wang Yingwu, handed over a donation of anti-epidemic kits worth XAF 164.5 million to the Cameroon Ministry of Defense. The kits included 50,000 regular masks, 6,000 surgical masks, 4,200 protective glasses, and various other anti-epidemic materials for disinfection and patient services.

project_name: Nanjing provides funds for epidemic prevention
description: On March 27, 2020, Nanjing provided relief funds to Bamenda, Cameroon for COVID-19 prevention. This donation was provided through the International Cities of Peace Initiative. The specific amount of the donation is not listed but was part of a larger donation initiative to 13 African countries, including Cameroon.   Professor Liu Cheng, the current chair host of Nanjing University UNESCO Peace Studies organized this donation. After receiving several letters from various African countries asking for help, Liu Cheng contacted the headquarters of the International Peace Cities Association in order to reach an agreement on the areas of Africa that would be the main objects of assistance. Following this agreement, and with the support of the Propaganda Department of the Nanjing Municipal Party Committee, the monetary donation was sent out on March 27, 2020. Bamenda, Cameroon has used the funds for a marketing campaign to create public awareness about the severity of the COVID-19 pandemic.

project_name: Gov't donates anti-epidemic supplies to Ministry of External Relations
description: On October 16, 2020, the Chinese Government donated anti-epidemic supplies to Cameroon's Ministry of External Relations. These supplies included 200 masks, 222 respirators, 2,000 surgical masks, and other anti-epidemic equipment. In total, over 20,000 pieces of equipment were donated. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation in Yaoundé, Cameroon. Wang Yingwu, China’s Ambassador to Cameroon, attended the ceremony and handed over the supplies to the Minister of External Relations of Cameroon, Lejeune Mbella Mbella.

project_name: Beijing Urban Construction Group donates masks and thermometers
description: On June 5, 2020, Beijing Urban Construction Group donated 10,000 masks and 10 no-contact infrared thermometers to the Cameroonian National Assembly. The supplies are intended to help Cameroonian COVID-19 prevention efforts. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A donation ceremony was held for this donation. Cui Jinpeng, the site engineer of the Beijing Urban Construction Group, handed over the supplies to the National Assembly First Deputy Speaker, Hon. Hilarion Etong.  In 2017, China provided a donation of RMB 400 million to construct the National Assembly building in Cameroon. Beijing Urban Construction Group was the implementing agency for this project (see Project ID#72109). A previous RMB 99 million grant for the project is cataloged in Project ID#53477.

project_name: Embassy donates anti-epidemic supplies
description: On November 5, 2020, the Chinese Embassy donated a batch of anti-epidemic supplies to Cameroon Press and Publishing Corporation (SOPECAM). The materials included gloves, liquid soap, surgical masks, and disinfectant. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the Chinese Embassy in Yaoundé, Cameroon. Ambassador to Cameroon, Wang Yingwu, Counselor of the Embassy, Wang Dong, and the General Manager of Cameroon Press and Publishing Company, Marie-Claire Nnana, attended the ceremony.

project_name: Embassy donates anti-epidemic supplies to Presidential Palace
description: On September 17, 2020, the Chinese Embassy donated anti-epidemic supplies to the Cameroon Presidential Palace. The specific type, amount, and monetary value of this donation are unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for the donation. Counselor Wang Dong of the Chinese Embassy in Cameroon and the Deputy Secretary-General of the Cameroonian Presidential Office attended the ceremony and signed the handover certificate.

project_name: Gov't donates respirators and PCR tests
description: On August 8, 2020, the third batch of sanitary equipment donated by China arrived at the Yaoundé International Airport in Cameroon. This donation included 30 non-invasive respirators and 30,000 PCR tests. These supplies will be used to strengthen the capacities of medical personnel in Cameroon. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony took place for this donation at Yaoundé International Airport. China’s Ambassador to Cameroon, Wang Yingwu, and Cameroon Public Health Minister Manaouda Malachie were present at the ceremony.

project_name: Shenzhen donates masks
description: On August 3, 2020, the Shenzhen government held a handover ceremony for the donation of 460,000 masks to 12 African countries, including Cameroon. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Buéa District Hospital
description: In 2003, China provided a grant worth 6 million to rehabilitate and modernized the Buéa district hospital, and by April 2003 work was in an 'advanced state.' At the end of 2003, this project was completed.

project_name: Donates funds for hospital
description: In 2007, China donated the construction of personnel accommodation at Yaounde's Hospital of Gynecology, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics worth $3 million.

project_name: Gov't provides technical assistance for hospital
description: On September 11, 2013, Minister Nganou Djoumessi and Ambassador Wo Ruidi signed an agreement pledging China’s technical assistance for the proper functioning of the Yaounde Gynecological and Pediatrics Hospital and those of Buea and Mbalmayo in the South West and Centre Regions, respectively. The project’s factsheet shows that focus will be on assuring the maintenance of hospital equipment and the training of Cameroonian technicians. The two-year (September 19, 2013 to September 18, 2015) maintenance work will consists in training seven Cameroonian health specialists in China in the domains of radiology, anesthesia monitoring equipment, medical electro-physiology equipment et al as well as in the supply of part of the medical equipment, their materials and spare parts.

project_name: Provides grant to promote maternal health
description: On December 31, 2020, it was reported that the Chinese government made a donation of USD $1 million to Cameroon through the Chinese Development Cooperation Agency (CIDCA). This donation is intended to support maternal and child health in Cameroon. These funds will also allow the acquisition of materials for vaccination against Measles-Rubella and COVID-19 personal protective equipment.  This donation is the result of a partnership between UNICEF and the Chinese government, and the initiatives funded by this donation will be implemented by the Government of Cameroon, especially the Ministry of Public Health. The support funded by this donation will be distributed to 7 health districts in the East, Center, and Littoral regions of Cameroon.

project_name: Embassy donates Covid-19 medical supplies
description: On December 10, 2021, the Chinese Embassy in Cameroon donated medical materials and office supplies to Cameroon National Radio and Television (CRTV) to defend Covid-19. Chargé d'Affaires Wang Dong attended the material handover ceremony. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Provides grant for Gyneco-Obstetric and Paediatric Hospital
description: On December 28th, 2007, Chinese Ambassador to Cameroon Huang Changqing and Cameroon Minister of Public Health André Mama Fouda formally exchanged notes on the fourth phase of the technical cooperation project of Chinese aid for the Yaounde Gyaeco-Obstetric and Paediatric Hospital Technical Cooperation Project (Mofcom). China will send a working group of 8 technical experts to carry out two-year technical support and equipment support for Buea Hospital, Mbarmayo Hospital and Yaounde Gynaeco-Obstetrics and Paediatric Hospital. This project has been completed.

project_name: Provides cataract surgeries
description: In June 2016, as part of the “Light Action” ("Action Lumiere") campaign, Chinese experts conducted 627 free surgery operations to Cameroonians suffering from cataracts. This project was funded by China and implemented in Cameroon through the Ministry of Public Health. The Gyneco-Obstetric and Paediatric Hospital of Yaounde and the Mbalmayo hospital were selected as managers of these surgeries (Cameroun Web). Numerous surgeries have been performed in African countries since the launch of China's China-Africa Brightness Action initiative in 2010. Eyebright Medical Technology, a Chinese company, provided the artificial lenses for a medical team in Cameroon. This project is completed.

project_name: Provides medical personnel for hospitals
description: On August 31, 2018, MINEPAT Minister Alamine Ousmane Mey and Cameroonian President Paul Biya signed an economic and technical cooperation agreement with Chinese President Xi Jinping providing Chinese technical assistance to three hospitals in Cameroon: Yaoundé Gynaecology, Obstetrics and Pediatrics Hospital, Buea Regional Hospital, and the Mbalmayo District Hospital. As of October 11, 2018, Chinese personnel were working in Yaoundé, although the extent of Chinese technical assistance in Buea and Mbalmayo is unclear.

project_name: Donates medical supplies to Gynaecological-Obstetrics and Paediatrics Hospital
description: On July 20, 2011, China signed an agreement to offer Cameroon batches of medical equipment and supplies for the Gynaecological- Obstetrics and Paediatrics Hospital under construction in Cameroon’s economic port city of Douala amounting to 10 million Yuan (about FCFA 713 million). The agreements were signed by Hu Jintao and Cameroonian President Paul Biya. In November of 2015, the supplies were handed over to the Gynaecological-Obstetrics and Paediatrics Hospital in Douala.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Malaria research center
description: On March 26, 2009, the Chinese Government officially inaugurated a malaria research center at the Yaounde Gynaecology, Obstetrics and Pediatrics Hospital (HGOPY). It reportedly provided RMB 3 million ($440,000) of grant funding to facilitate the completion of the project.

project_name: MOFCOM provides loan for Gyneco-Obstetric and Pediatric Hospital
description: On January 31, 2007, China's Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and Cameroon's Ministry of Public Health signed an RMB 30,000,000 loan agreement for the Douala Gyneco-Obstetric and Pediatric Hospital Construction and Equipping Project. The loan, which is captured via Project ID#58705, carried the following borrowing terms: a 21 year maturity, a 7 year grace period, and a 0% interest rate. As of December 31, 2020, this loan had achieved a 100% disbursement rate and its outstanding amount was zero. Then, on August 3, 2009, the Chinese Government provided a grant worth RMB 50 million to the Government of Cameroon for the Douala Gyneco-Obstetric and Pediatric Hospital Construction and Equipping Project (captured via Project ID#59618). Several months later, on November 5, 2009, China's Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) issued the Government of Cameroon a RMB 50 million loan — through an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) — for the Douala Gyneco-Obstetric and Pediatric Hospital Construction and Equipping Project. The loan, which is captured via Project ID#314, carried the following borrowing terms: a 20 year maturity, a 10 year grace period, and a 0% interest rate. As of December 31, 2020, this loan had achieved a 100% disbursement rate and its outstanding amount was zero.  The purpose of the project was to construct and equip the Douala Gyneco-Obstetric and Pediatric Hospital (Projet de construction et d’équipement de l’hôpital gynéco-obstétrique et pédiatrique de Douala, or HGOPD).  Shanxi Construction Engineering was the contractor responsible for project implementation. Construction began in October 2009 and the the hospital was handed to the Cameroonian authorities on November 17, 2015.

project_name: Embassy donates anti-epidemic supplies
description: On September 9, 2020, the Chinese Embassy donated anti-epidemic supplies to the Cameroon State Security Administration. The supplies are intended to aid Cameroonian police in maintaining national security and stability during the COVID-19 pandemic. The specific type, amount and monetary value of this donation are unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation by the Chinese Embassy in Cameroon and the Cameroonian General Administration of National Security. The Ambassador to Cameroon, Wang Yingwu, Defense Attaché, Chai Xiaojiang, the General Delegate for National Security, Martin Mbarga Nguele, the Secretary-General, and the Finance Director attended the ceremony.

project_name: POWERCHINA donates anti-epidemic supplies
description: On July 27, 2020, POWERCHINA donated anti-epidemic supplies to Cameroon's Ministry of Water Resources and Energy. The specific amounts and monetary value of this donation are unknown.  A donation ceremony was held for this donation in Yaoundé, the capital of Cameroon. Cameroonian Minister of Water Resources and Energy Elendou Essumba and a country representative of POWERCHINA Cameroon attended the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't donates medical supplies to Yaounde Hospital
description: On 11 July, 2014, the Chinese Government provided grant funding worth 800,000 CFA for the provision of a CAT scanner, two digital radiography machine, a conventional radiography machine, two ultra sound machines, 20 incubators, and 10 ultraviolet photometric machines to Yaounde-Gynaeco-Obstretric and Paediatric Hospital (YGOPH).

project_name: Gov't donates to UNICEF Covid-19 pandemic relief
