description: On November 2020, Chinese Government provides USD 1,000,000 aid to United Nations Children's Fund to relieve the COVID-19 pandemic in Cameroon.  This project is captured in UNOCHA Financial Tracking Service as Flow ID #223681.

project_name: Gov't donates to Covid-19 WFP pandemic relief
description: In February 2021, Chinese government provides USD 1,000,000 to School Meals Programme to support 72,000 school children in Logone and Chari, Mayo Sava and Mayo Tsanaga Divisions in the Fra North Region (COVID-19).  This project is captured in UNOCHA Financial Tracking Service as Flow ID #231677.

project_name: National Health Commission of China donates medical supplies
description: On March 15, 2021, the National Health Commission of China to Cameroon donated a batch of medical equipment to fight the Covid-19 pandemic at the Yaounde Central Hospital. Guo Jianjun, Economic and Commercial Counselor of the Chinese Embassy in Cameroon, participated in the handover ceremony and signed the handover certificate with Hassan, Director of the Cooperation Department of the Ministry of Health of Cameroon.   This batch of equipment was donated by the National Health and Sanitation Committee of China to the Ministry of Health of Cameroon under the cooperation mechanism of 30 Chinese-African counterpart hospitals (the Chinese and Cameroonian hospitals are respectively the First Hospital of Shanxi Medical University and the Central Hospital of Yaoundé), including respiratory machine, expectoration machine, electrocardiogram machine, blood oxygen saturation monitor and oxygen generator.

project_name: Gov't donates to WFP Covid-19 pandemic relief
description: In February 2021, Chinese government provides USD 2,000,000 unconditional food Assistance to Nigerian Refugees in Minawao site - Far North (COVID-19).  This project is captured in UNOCHA Financial Tracking Service as Flow ID #231682.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for anti-Malaria center
description: In October 2009, the Chinese Government supported the establishment of an anti-malaria center at the Friendship Hospital (Hôpital de l'Amitié) in the capital city of Bangui. The monetary value of this grant commitment is unknown. This project was successfully completed on October 31, 2009.

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: On July 20 and 24, 2009, China and the Central African Republic signed letters of exchange for a batch of antimalarial drugs to be granted to the Central African Republic. The drugs were handed over to the Central African Republic on February 26, 2010, in Bangui. This was the 4th out of 5 batches of drugs as agreed upon at the Beijing Summit of the China-Africa Cooperation Forum.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Friendship Hospital
description: In early October 2006, the Chinese Government and the Government of the Central African Republic signed letters of exchange related to the the Friendship Hospital Rehabilitation and Expansion Project. The Chinese Government committed RMB 41.2 million of grant funding. This project involved the rehabilitation of the 12,450-square-meter, 232-bed Friendship Hospital ((Hôpital de l'Amitié) in the capital city of Bangui. It sought to increase the hospital’s capacity from 232 beds to 300 beds. Xinjiang International Economic and Technical Cooperation was the contractor responsible for implementation. The project commenced on July 20, 2008 and ended on October 31, 2010. A formal project handover ceremony took place on February 5, 2010. The construction of this hospital was originally funded by the Chinese Government during the late 1980s.

project_name: China donates anti-Malaria drugs and medical equipment to Ministry of Public Health
description: On November 9, 2012, the Chinese embassy donated anti-malaria drugs and medical equipment to the Central African Republic's Ministry of Public Health. The value of the donation is unknown. The extent of the donation is also unknown.  It is unclear if this donation is connected to other donations of anti-malaria supplies.

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: On December 22, 2011, the Chinese embassy donated antimalarial drugs to Central African Republic government. The value of the donation is unknown. This donation is one of several anti-malarial donations from China.

project_name: Gov't donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: On June 9 and 14, 2011, the Chinese government and Central African Republic government exchanged letters in which China agree to increase amount of anti-malaria drug aid to CAR. It is unclear which donations of anti-malaria drugs might have been given as a result of this agreement.

project_name: Provides medical services to cataract patients
description: In December of 2018, the Chinese embassy announced that the Chinese government pledged in a September 2018 meeting between President Tudavela and Xi Jinping to launch the Guangmingxing, or "Bright Action" project in 2019 to provide free medical services to cataract patients. On September 16th, 2019,  the China-Africa "Bright Action" advance investigation team arrived in Bangui. Investigator Niu Fangzheng of the Cooperation and Exchange Office of Zhejiang Provincial Health Commission, in collaboration with Ni Songtao, member of the Party Committee of the Eye Optometry Hospital Affiliated to Wenzhou Medical University, and accompanying doctors Chang Pingjun and nurse Shi Xinwei from the Hangzhou Branch of the Eye Optometry Hospital were a part of this advance team. After their plans for implementation was approved by the Chinese Embassy, an expert team of 9 people from the Eye Optometry Hospital Affiliated to Wenzhou Medical University appointed by the National Health Commission and Zhejiang Provincial Health Commission, went to the Central African Republic to perform the "Bright Action" cataract eye surgery for China and Africa Free clinic activities from November 18th to December 6th. On November 25, the Chinese Embassy in Central Africa invited the "Bright Action" team and the 17th batch of doctors from the China-Africa Medical Team to the Embassy to conduct compulsory health examinations and hold health knowledge lectures for employees of Chinese-funded enterprises and overseas Chinese in China and Africa . About 70 people including Chen Dong, the ambassador to China and Africa, embassy staff , Chinese employees of Chinese- funded enterprises , and overseas Chinese participated in the event. On November 27, 2019, the “Bright Action” team, in conjunction with the Friendship Hospital in Bangui, carried out free clinic activities at the Friendship hospital (Project ID#86383). Niu Fangzheng, head of the China-Africa "Bright Action" expert group, said that with the cooperation of the Ministry of Health of China and Africa and the Friendship Hospital, the expert group carried out more than 200 free rejuvenation operations. On the same day, a donation ceremony was held at the hospital to mark the completion of the donation of a batch of ophthalmic equipment, medicines and supporting supplies.  Central African President Touadéra, Ambassador to the Central African Republic, Chen Dong, Director of the General Office of the Ministry of Health of China and Africa, Warikma, and the Director of the Bangui Friendship Hospital, Kate, were all present at the ceremony. The Bright Action project concluded on December 5th, the same day the free clinic activities ended with 221 successful eye surgery operations conducted.

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria drugs
description:
On July 9, 2009, a handover ceremony was held for the donation of antimalarial drugs from the Chinese government to the Central African Republic Ministry of Public Health and Population. It is unclear how much the donation cost, though the Agence Centrafricaine de Presse reports that in 2009 China donated drugs and medical devices amounting to RMB 400,000. Since this estimate combines the apparent cost of total drugs donated in 2009, as well as medical devices, the transaction amount for the specific donation captured in this project has been left blank.
 
 This project is distinct from project #56234, which captures letters of exchange signed later in July 2009 for a donation of antimalarial drugs, which were eventually handed over to the Central African Republic in February 2010.

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: On September 9, 2006, China and the Central African Republic (CAR) signed letters of exchange for the Chinese donation of 52 million CFA Francs worth of anti-malaria drugs to the CAR. It is unclear when the anti-malaria drugs were physically handed over to the Central African Republic.

project_name: Embassy donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: On January 23, 2004, the Chinese government paid for and the embassy donated anti-malaria drugs to the Unit for the Transfer of Medicines (UCM) in the Central African Republic. A media article put the value of the drugs at 140 million CFA, but the amount cannot be confirmed by any official sources.

project_name: Embassy donates medical supplies to Ministry of Health
description: On June 5th, 2018, the Chinese Embassy handed over a donation of medical supplies to the Central African Republic Ministry of Health. The exact equipment donated is unknown. The value of the supplies is unknown. It appears to be a one-time donation.

project_name: Gov't donates drugs to Friendship Hospital
description: On March 21, 2017,  the Chinese government signed a memorandum of understanding with the Central African Republic's government for the renewal of medical cooperation. As part of the signing of this MOU, the Chinese government donated 150 million CFA worth of hospital drugs to the China Friendship Hospital in Bangui.

project_name: Bright Action group donates to the China-Africa Friendship Hospital
description: Led by Niu Fangzheng, the China-Africa "Bright Action" (光明行) (Project ID#56093) expert group cooperated with the Central African Ministry of Public Health and Population to perform more than 200 rejuvenation operations and a batch of ophthalmic equipment, medicines, and supporting supplies that worth 2.42 million RMB to the China-Africa Friendship Hospital. The operations started on November 18th and concluded on December 6th, 2019. The donation ceremony was held on Novermber 27th.  On November 27th, 2019, a donation ceremony was held at the hospital to mark the completion of the donation. The hospital is located within the Central African Republic in Bangui. Central African President Faustin-Archange Touadéra, Ambassador to Central Africa, Chen Dong, Director of the General Office of the Ministry of Health of the Central African Republic, Warikma, and the Director of the Bangui Friendship Hospital, Kate, were all present at the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't donates PPE
description: In June 2020, the Chinese Government provided 18,000 surgical masks and 120 frontal guards to the Central African Republic. The First Lady of China, Peng Liyuan, donated the supplies on behalf of the Chinese Government, and the Organization of African First Ladies for Development (OAFLAD) coordinated the donation. Brigitte Touadera, First Lady of the Central African Republic, received the supplies. The monetary value of the donations is unknown.   The donation detailed in the project is part of a series of donations from the Government of China to 53 African countries across the OAPDAD. Further information regarding the agreement can be found in Project ID #92937.

project_name: Embassy donates anti-Malaria drugs for Ministry of Health
description: On February 6th of 2018, the Chinese Embassy donated antimalarial drugs to the Central African Ministry of Public Health and Population. At the Handover Ceremony held in the Ministry of Public Health and Population, Chinese Ambassador to the Central African Republic Ma Fulin and Minister of Health and Population Pierre Somse signed the certificate of the handover. The value of the donation is unknown. This donation is part of a 5-year antimalarial drug plan provided by the Chinese government to the CAR from 2016 to 2020

project_name: Provides anti-epidemic materials
description: On June 11, 2020, the Chinese government provided a second batch of anti-epidemic materials to the Central African Republic. These materials were sent in response to a notice from the Central African Republic that test kits were running out in Africa. This donation, therefore, included test kits and other anti-epidemic materials. In addition to the Chinese government and the Chinese embassy in the Central African Republic, contributions to the donation came from the Chinese People's Association for Friendship with Foreign Countries, China Railway 11th Bureau (a subsidiary of China Railway Construction) , and Gezhouba Group. The China Railway 11th Bureau's contribution consisted of at least 5,000 nucleic acid testing kits. The contributions by the other entities and the monetary value of these donations are unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at Bangui International Airport located in Bangui, the capital of the Central African Republic.  Central African President Faustin-Archange Touadéra, China’s Ambassador to Central Africa, Chen Dong, the Central African Minister of Health, the Minister of Economic Cooperation, and a WHO Representative in Central Africa attended the ceremony.  According to the Chinese Embassy in the Central African Republic, this is a second batch of materials provided by the Chinese government. Details on the first batch are provided in Project ID#92974.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Elisabeth Domitien Hospital
description: In November 2006, the Chinese Government announced that it would fund the construction of the Elisabeth Domitien Hospital in the Central African Republic at the Forum on China-African Cooperation in Beijing. The Chinese Ministry of Commerce subsequently committed an RMB 100 million grant for this project. This project involved the construction of a 100-bed hospital in the city of Bimbo, which is the capital of the Ombella-M'poko prefecture. The hospital offers surgical services, gynaecological services, obstetrical services, pediatric services, ophthalmological services, radiology and dental treatments.   China Electronics Engineering Design Institute was the contractor responsible for implementation. A formal groundbreaking ceremony was held on October 30, 2009. However, construction itself did not begin until March 2020. Construction ended in September 2011, and a formal hospital inauguration ceremony took place on October 4, 2011. It was attended by the Central African Republic's President Francois Bozize and the Chinese Ambassador to the Central African Republic, Sun Haichao.  The Chinese Ambassador indicated that the Chinese Government would provide equipment worth $1.5 million to ensure proper functioning of the hospital. The total value of the grant commitment for this project, including construction and equipment, was 4.5 billion CFA, according to African Economic Outlook.

project_name: Gov't provides anti-epidemic materials
description: On March 23, 2020, the Chinese government provided anti-epidemic materials to the Central African Republic. These materials consisted of 4,000 gloves, 3,000 masks, 150 coveralls and 100 protective glasses. These materials will be distributed to various health centers for COVID-19 response efforts. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation in Bangui, Central Africa. At the ceremony, China’s Ambassador to the Central African Republic, Chen Dong, handed over the materials to the President of the Central African Republic, Faustin-Archange Touadéra. The Ambassador of France,  The Central African Minister of Health Pierre Somsé, Éric Gérard, and others also attended the ceremony.

project_name: Fujian Police Institute donates anti-epidemic supplies
description: On May 20, 2020, the Fujian Police Institute of China provided anti-epidemic supplies to the Central African Republic. These supplies will be used for COVID-19 prevention efforts in the Central African Republic. These supplies included 5,000 nose masks, 20 coveralls, 20 goggles and 8 frontal guns. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the Presidential Palace of the Central African Republic. The President of the Central African Republic, Central African Minister of State and Chief of Staff of the Presidential Office, the Presidential Press Advisor, the Presidential Political Advisor, the Minister of National Defense, the Minister of Economic Planning and International Cooperation, the Commander of the National Gendarmeria, the Superintendent of the police, and Chinese Ambassador Chen Dong attended the ceremony.  This handover ceremony also included the handover of supplies from the Chinese government. The details of that donation is outlined in Project ID’s #92974.

project_name: Signs humanitarian aid project certificate for medical care assistance
description: On July 24, 2015, China signed a humanitarian aid project certificate with the Central African Republic Minister of Economic Planning and International Cooperation. The amount of the aid is unspecified, but it will go toward alleviating the lack of medical care. It is unclear if and when the project will commence beyond the commitment phase.

project_name: Gov't donates Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine
description: On March 3, 2021, the Chinese Ambassador to the Central African Republic announced that his government would donate a batch of COVID-19 vaccine doses to the Government of the Central African Republic. Then, on July 6, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 150,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Central African Republic.

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: In May 2016, China donated medicine for children suffering from malaria to Central African Republic, at a cost of 60 million CFA. In addition to the drug gift, Chinese doctors were deployed in health facilities around Bangui.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Elisabeth Domitien Hospital
description: On December 7, 2016, the Chinese Government and the Government of the Central African Republic signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA), which committed RMB 200 million of grant funding for multiple projects, including the Elisabeth Domitien Hospital Rehabilitation Project. Then, in September 2018, the Chinese Government and the Government of the Central African Republic signed another ETCA, which committed another RMB 200 million of grant funding for multiple projects, including the Elisabeth Domitien Hospital Rehabilitation Project. Roughly nine months later, on June 25, 2019, the Chinese Government and the Government of the Central African Republic signed a third ETCA, which committed CFA 16 billion for multiple projects, including the Elisabeth Domitien Hospital Rehabilitation Project. The total amount of grant funding that China’s Ministry of Commerce committed for the Elisabeth Domitien Hospital Rehabilitation Project is unknown.   The purpose of the project is to rehabilitate Elisabeth Domitien Hospital (Hôpital Maman Elisabeth Domitien), which is located in the city of Bimbo, which is the capital of the Ombella-M'poko prefecture. As of August 2022, AidData had not yet identified any evidence of project implementation.

project_name: Zhangzhou Public Security Bureau donates masks
description: On August 3, 2020, the Red Cross Society of China, the Fujian Provincial Association for Friendship with Foreign Countries, and the Zhangzhou Public Security Bureau of the Fujian Province jointly provided anti-epidemic materials to the Central African Republic. The Red Cross Society provided five ventilators to the Central African government (captured via #92941). The Fujian Provincial Association for Friendship with Foreign Countries provided 4,000 masks and 40 forehead thermometers to the Prime Minister’s office (captured via ##95290). The Zhangzhou Public Security Bureau of the Fujian Province provided 10,000 masks to the Central African Ministry of Internal Affairs and Public Security (captured via #95291).  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the office of the Prime Minister of the Central African Republic. Chinese Ambassador Chen Dong, representatives of the Prime Minister of the Central African Republic, the Minister of Health, and the Director of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Public Security attended the ceremony.

project_name: Fujian Provincial Association for Friendship with Foreign Countries donates PPE
description: On August 3, 2020, the Red Cross Society of China, the Fujian Provincial Association for Friendship with Foreign Countries, and the Zhangzhou Public Security Bureau of the Fujian Province jointly provided anti-epidemic materials to the Central African Republic. The Red Cross Society provided five ventilators to the Central African government (captured via #92941). The Fujian Provincial Association for Friendship with Foreign Countries provided 4,000 masks and 40 forehead thermometers to the Prime Minister’s office (captured via ##95290). The Zhangzhou Public Security Bureau of the Fujian Province provided 10,000 masks to the Central African Ministry of Internal Affairs and Public Security (captured via #95291).  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the office of the Prime Minister of the Central African Republic. Chinese Ambassador Chen Dong, representatives of the Prime Minister of the Central African Republic, the Minister of Health, and the Director of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Public Security attended the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't donates to WHO Covid-19 relief
description: In March 2020, Chinese government provides USD 986,600 to support WHO response to COVID-19 outbreak in Central African Republic.

project_name: Gov't provides anti-epidemic supplies
description: On May 20, 2020, the Chinese government provided the first batch of anti-epidemic supplies to the Central African Republic. The monetary value of this donation is unknown. This is the first of two batches of anti-epidemic materials provided by the Chinese government to the Central African Republic. The second batch was provided in June of 2020 and the details of that donation are outlined in Project ID#92889.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the Presidential Palace of the Central African Republic. The President of the Central African Republic, Central African Minister of State and Chief of Staff of the Presidential Office, the Presidential Press Advisor, the Presidential Political Advisor, the Minister of National Defense, the Minister of Economic Planning and International Cooperation, the Commander of the National Gendarmeria, the Superintendent of the police, and Chinese Ambassador Chen Dong attended the ceremony.  This handover ceremony also included the handover of supplies from the Jack Ma Foundation, a donation from the Fujian Police Institute, (project ID #93597) and a donation from the Chinese Embassy (project ID #93598).

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: On August 7, 2007, the Chinese embassy, on behalf of the Chinese government, in Central African Republic delivered 800,000 RMB worth of anti-malarial drugs to the government of the Central African Republic. The two governments had exchanged letters for this project in July 2007.

project_name: Co-launches anti-Malaria campaign
description: On March 17, 2019, in the village of Gailing, 30 kilometers away from the capital Bangui, the Chinese Embassy in Central Africa and the Ministry of Health of the Central African Republic launched the Central African National Anti-malarial Campaign to distribute anti-malarial drugs and food to local villagers. Central African President Faustin-Archange Touadéra and his wife Tina, Ambassador to the Central African Republic Chen Dong , Minister of health central african republic Pierre Somse, Chairman of the National Assembly Friendship Group Ma Kango, The 16th Chinese-Central African Medical Team (ID#55646), representatives of some Chinese-funded enterprises, Nearly 1,000 members of the Central African National Assembly, government officials, and villagers from Damara city and the village of Gailing participated in the launching ceremony. Subsequently, President Tuvadela and Ambassador Chen jointly distributed medicines, food and anti-malarial leaflets to the local government and heads of medical institutions. On April 25, 2019, the “World Anti-Malaria Day”,  The Ministry of Health of the Central African Republic held a large-scale “Central African National Anti-Malarial Campaign” launching ceremony in Pissa. International organizations such as UNICEF, Red Cross, and Médecins Sans Frontières as well as the 16th mission of the Chinese-Central African Medical Team participated in the launch. At this ceremony, Anti-malarial drugs were handed over to the PISSA City Medical and Health Care Center, and medical teams from the Friendship Hospital as well as the Chinese-Central African Medical team provided consultation, diagnoses, and treatments This campaign is part of the Chinese Government’s efforts to implement the "Eight Major Actions'' announced by China at the Beijing Summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation in September 2018.  The exact value of these donations and services that China offered during the campaign and its launch are unknown.

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria drugs and medical equipment
description: On October 27, 2010, the Chinese government donated anti-malaria drugs to the Central African Republic Ministry of Health. This is the 5th batch of drugs as agreed upon at the Beijing Summit of the China-Africa Cooperation Forum.  The value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Zhejiang Provincial Government donates medical equipment
description: On August 6, 2018, the Chinese National Health Commission and the Zhejiang Provincial Government donated 2 billion CAF worth of medical equipment — including digital ultrasound machine, a digital x-ray machine, an anesthesia machine, a blood aspirator for surgical procedures, a ventilator, and other medical equipment (including boxes of the antimalarial drugs) — to the China-Africa Friendship Hospital in the capital city of in Bangui (where a Chinese medical team is stationed, as captured via Project ID#55646). China’s Ambassador to the Central African Republic (CAF), Chen Dong, and the CAF Minister of Health of Central Africa Pierre Somse signed the equipment handover certificate at the donation ceremony. Faustin-Archange Touadéra, the President of the Central African Republic, Pascal Mbereso, head of the China-Africa Friendship Hospital, and Zhu Decai, the leader of the Chinese medical team, were also present at the ceremony.

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: On December 12, 2012, China donated anti-malaria drugs to Chad. The agreement was signed by Chinese Ambassador Hu Zhiqiang and Chadian Minister of Public Health. Government Counselor Qian Jin and the president of China-Chacha Friendship Hospital attended the signing ceremony. The donation came about as part of results of the Fifth Conference of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation, where it was announced that China-Africa medical cooperation would be developed. The value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donates athletic supplies
description: On January 21, 2015, the Chinese government donated sports materials to Chad. Hu Zhiqiang, the Chinese Ambassador to Chad, and the Chadian Minister of Culture, Youth, and Sports attended the handover ceremony at the Dijon Stadium in N’Djamena. Some of this batch of materials are sporting goods specially designed and made for the disabled. The exact materials and their values are unknown.

project_name: Embassy donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On June 24, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Chad provided anti-epidemic materials to the Supreme Council of Islamic Affairs in Chad. The materials included 3,000 medical surgical masks. These masks will be used to help religious buildings reopen safely during the pandemic. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the headquarters of the Higher Council of Islamic Affairs in Chad. China’s Ambassador to Chad, Li Jinjin, the Committee Chairman and the Vice Chairman of the Supreme Council of Islamic Affairs attended the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: On December 4, 2010, Chinese government donated anti-malaria drugs to the Ministry of Public Health of Chad. This is the fifth batch of antimalarial drugs provided by the Chinese government to Chad since the resumption of diplomatic relations between China and Chad. My Ambassador to Chad Yang Guangyu and Chad’s State Secretary of Public Health Muhammad Mamadou Adi signed the handover certificate on behalf of the two governments.

project_name: Embassy provides anti-epidemic materials to police
description: On June 26, 2020, the Chinese Embassy provided anti-epidemic materials to the National Police Department of Chad. The donated materials consisted of 5,000 medical masks. These materials were raised by the Chinese Embassy in Chad. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held at the National Police Headquarters of Chad. Secretary Yusuf and other officials attended the meeting.

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: On May 12, 2008, the anti-malaria drugs donated by Chinese government arrived in N’Djamena, the capital of Chad. On May 14, the governments of the two countries held a grand handover ceremony at the Liberty Hospital. Chinese Ambassador to Chad Wang Yingwu and Chad Minister of Public Health Awoksuma Jonah signed the handover certificate on behalf of the two governments. Chinese medical team members, officials from the Ministry of Health and medical staff from Liberty Hospital attended the handover ceremony. According to Ambassador, this is the second batch of anti-malaria drugs donated to Chad since 2006.

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: According to Chinese media Xinhua, in November 2013, China donated anti-malaria drugs worth USD 680,000 million to Chad's national medicine agency. The donation amount USD 680,000 million is very large, and we infer that it might be USD 680,000. Chad's Health Minister Mahamat Annou Wadak thanked China for the aid and noted that it was in line with the government's plans of fighting against malaria. This is the second batch of Chinese anti-malaria aid; the first was in January 2013 (#30852).

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: On March 25, 2015, Chinese Ambassador to Chad Hu Zhiqiang delivered anti-malaria medicines to Pharmaceutical Purchasing Center (CPA), the public institution responsible for the purchase, storage and wholesaling medicines in Chad. At the ceremony, Ambassador Hu Zhiqiang and Secretary-General Waddak signed the certificate of handover of the antimalarial drug project in Chad. The cost of the medicine was USD 500,000.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for anti-Malaria center
description:
At the Beijing Summit of the China-Africa Forum in 2006, the Chinese government announced that it would assist in the construction of malaria control centers in 30 African countries. Then, in 2007, China’s Ministry of Commerce provided a grant to the Government of Chad for the establishment of an anti-malaria center. The monetary value of this grant is unknown. On December 28, 2007, an opening ceremony for the China-Chad Malaria Control Center was held (中国--乍得疟疾防治中心). It was the first of the 30 centers to be unveiled. The center is located at the at the China-Chad Friendship Hospital (also known as the Liberty Hospital) in the capital city of N'Djamena.. 
 
 On June 11, 2010, the center was officially opened, and Yang Guangyu, the Chinese Ambassador to Chad, and Mahamadou, Secretary of State of the Ministry of Public Health of Chad, inspected the China-Chad Malaria Control Center.

project_name: Gov't donates Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine
description: On June 2, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Chad’s Ministry of Public Health. Chinese Ambassador to Chad Li Jinjin and the Chadian Minister of Public Health and National Solidarity Abdoulaye Saber Fadoul were present for the arrival of the vaccine donation at the N'Djamena International Airport.

project_name: Embassy donates materials to National Blood Transfusion Center
description: On April 26, 2012, Chinese Embassy in Chad donated materials to Chad's National Blood Transfusion Center. Chinese Ambassador to Chad, Qian Jin, oversaw the agreement and made a speech in which he discussed the state of Chinese-Chad healthcare relations. The donation included a television and a computer, among other things. The total value of the donation is not known.

project_name: Provides medicine and equipment for cataract surgeries
description: On September 28, 2018, China donated medical equipment and medicine worth 2 million yuan to Chad as part of the opening ceremony of the "Bright Action" Surgery Project ("Action la Lumiere" or "光明行"). The ceremony for the Bright Action Surgery Project was held at Chad Friendship Hospital Eye Center, and was attended by Chinese Ambassador Li Jinjin, the Chadian Minister of Health Saleh, and a number of Chinese medical aid workers. The project was announced at the Beijing Summit of the China-Africa Cooperation Forum and is to last for 3 years, including sending a team of experts to carry out surgery for cataract patients, providing medical equipment and medicine, and inviting local doctors to study and study in China (described in #56022).  This project is linked to #56022, the Bright Action Cataract Surgery Project.

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: According to Xinhua news, in January 2013, China donated USD 720,000 worth of anti-malaria drugs to Chad's Pharmaceutical Purchasing Center (CPA), a state-owned body that is involved in the purchase, storage and large scale sale of drugs in Chad. The donation was signed during the  Sino-Africa cooperation Forum by the Chinese ambassador to Chad, Hu Zhiqiang.  This batch of anti-malaria drugs was donated under the auspices of the Sino-Africa cooperation Forum whose 5th ministerial conference was held about six months before the donation.  On January 9th, 2013, ambasador Hu Zhiqiang and Secretary-General Waddak signed the certificate of handover of the antimalarial drug.

project_name: Gov't donates anti-epidemic materials to Ministry of Health
description: On April 2, 2020, the Chinese government provided anti-epidemic materials to the Chad Ministry of Health. The materials included six renovated container rooms, masks and other medical supplies. These materials will be used to improve the COVID-19 response efforts of the Chad Ministry of Health. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the National Drug Procurement Center in Chad. Li Jinjin, the Chinese Ambassador to Chad, and the Minister of Health of Chad attended the ceremony. The heads of various departments of the Ministry of Health of Chad and the team leader of the Chinese medical team in Chad were also present.

project_name: Gov't donates to WHO Covid-19 relief
description: In March 2020, Chinese government provides USD 200,000 to support WHO response to COVID-19 outbreak in Chad.

project_name: Provides cataract surgeries
description: On September 28, 2018, the opening ceremony of the "Bright Action" Surgery Project ("Action la Lumiere" or 光明行) was held at the China-Chad Friendship Hospital and was attended by Chinese Ambassador Li Jinjin as well as Chadian Minister of Health Saleh, and a number of Chinese medical aid workers. The project will be done under the guidance of the International Exchange and Cooperation Center of the National Health Commission, organized by the Jiangxi Provincial Health Commission, and have experts from the Affiliated Eye Hospital of Nanchang University. This ophthalmological campaign, the cost of which is estimated at nearly 100,000,000 FCFA, is entirely financed by the Government of the People's Republic of China. Medical equipment worth 2 million RMB was donated to Chad during the ceremony (described in project #56021).   On October 15, 2018, the 2018 team returned to China after performing 233 surgeries.   As of October 31st, 2019, a total of 494 free cataract surgeries were completed through the project, with 9 cases of free complex ocular fundus disease and glaucoma surgery being carried out in 2019 alone. The "Bright Action" project has had 2 phases so far, with the first phase starting in September 2018 and the second phase spanning from August 31st to September 9th, 2019 (linked to #86658). Per the agreement, there will be more Bright Action Programs each year.

project_name: Embassy donates for Friendship Hospital
description: On June 6th, 2019, the Chinese Embassy in Chad held a handover ceremony for a new gate for the China-Chad Friendship Hospital. The project was financed by the Chinese Embassy through a grant of 34 million CFa. Li Jinjin, the ambassador to Chad, Hammett, the representative of the Minister of Public Health of Chad, and Umar, director of the China-Chad Friendship Hospital, attended the event and delivered speeches.

project_name: Gov't provides anti-epidemic materials to the great love foundation in chad in june 2020 (linked to project id#91956)
description: On June 18, 2020, the Chinese government provided anti-epidemic materials to the Great Love Foundation in Chad. This donation is in response to the African First Ladies Development Federation's request for assistance. These materials will be used for COVID-19 prevention and response efforts for those in need throughout Chad. The specific type, amount and monetary value of this donation are unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the Great Love Foundation headquarters. China’s Ambassador to Chad, Li Jinjin, the Secretary-General of the Great Love Foundation, and other executives of the Foundation attended the ceremony. Ambassador Li and Secretary-General Saulba signed the handover certificate at the ceremony. See Project ID#91956 for a similar project in response to the same request from the African First Ladies Development Foundation in Zimbabwe.

project_name: Chongqing Municipal Government provides anti-epidemic materials
description: On July 15, 2020, the Chongqing Municipal Government provided anti-epidemic materials to the government of N'Djamena, the capital city of Chad. This donation will be used to improve COVID-19 response and prevention efforts in N'Djamena. The specific type, amount and monetary value of this donation are unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation in the office building of the N'Djamena government.  China’s Ambassador to Chad, Li Jinjin, the mayor of N'Djamena, four deputy mayors, the Secretary General of the city government, and representatives of the district governments of N'Djamena attended the ceremony. Ambassador Li and the mayor of N'Djamena signed the material handover certificate at the ceremony.

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: On May 12, 2017, China donated anti-malaria drugs to the Ministry of Public Health of Chad. Chinese Ambassador Wu Jie and the Chadian Minister of Health oversaw the signing of the agreement. The value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: China Three Gorges University provides anti-epidemic materials
description: On June 18, 2020, China Three Gorges University provided anti-epidemic materials to the University of N'Djamena in Chad. The donation included 18 boxes of disinfectant and 50 boxes of hand sanitizer. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the University of N'Djamena in Chad. The main leaders of N'Djamena University, heads of departments, and teacher representatives attended the ceremony. Fang Yunlong, the Political Counselor of the Chinese Embassy in Chad, and the President of UNU also attended the ceremony.   This handover ceremony also included the handover of a donation of 3000 masks from the Chinese Embassy to the University of N'Djamena in Chad. The details of that donation are outlined in Project ID#93266.

project_name: Embassy donates anti-epidemic materials to the University of N'djamena
description: On June 18, 2020, the Chinese Embassy provided anti-epidemic materials to the University of N'Djamena in Chad. The donation included 3,000 medical masks. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the University of N'Djamena in Chad. The main leaders of N'Djamena University, heads of departments, and teacher representatives attended the ceremony. Fang Yunlong, the Political Counselor of the Chinese Embassy in Chad, and the President of UNU also attended the ceremony.   This handover ceremony also included the handover of a donation from China Three Gorges University to the University of N'Djamena in Chad. The details of that donation are outlined in Project ID#93713.

project_name: Gov't provides anti-epidemic materials for Ministry of Health
description: On August 5, 2020, the Chinese government provided anti-epidemic materials to the Ministry of Public Health in Chad. The materials included 100 ventilators, 60 oxygen generators, and other related accessories and consumables. These materials will be used to improve COVID-19 response and prevention efforts in Chad. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.   A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the National Drug Procurement Center of the Ministry of Public Health of Chad. The Secretary of State for Public Health of Chad, the National Health Response Coordinator, and the Director of the National Drug Procurement Center attended the ceremony. China’s Ambassador to Chad, Li Jinjin, also attended the ceremony.

project_name: Donates medical supplies for Friendship Hospital
description: On March 4, 2021, a ceremony was held for the donation of Medical Supplies from the Chinese Government to the China-Chad Friendship Hospital. The medical equipment was purchased by the National Health Commission of China and First Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang University and is intended to combat COVID-19. This batch of equipment has an overall cost estimated at 32 million FCFA.  The Chinese Ambassador to Chad, the Secretary of State for Public Health of Chad, and the President of the China-Chad Friendship Hospital attended the ceremony. The donation is part of the China-Africa Counterpart Hospital Cooperation Mechanism.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Friendship Hospital
description: On December 28, 2009, China’s Ambassador to Chad, Yang Guangyu, and Chad’s Minister of Foreign Relations, Moussa Faki Mohammed, signed letters of exchange related to the China-Chad Friendship Hospital Renovation Project. China Ministry of Commerce provided grant funding for this project, but the monetary value of the grant commitment is unknown.   The project involved renovation of Freedom Hospital (known locally as L’hôpital de la liberté or L'hôpital de l'amitié Tchad-Chine or 新建医疗队住房项目) in the capital city of N'Djamena, which was constructed in 1996 with financial support from the Chinese Government. More specifically, it involved interior and exterior decorations of the hospital, electrical renovations, updating of the sewage and drainage system, the provision of of medical equipment, and the construction of 14 housing units for Chinese medical team members.   China Geo-Engineering Corporation International Ltd. (CGCINT) was the contractor responsible for implementation. It signed a construction contract on December 4, 2010. Then, a groundbreaking ceremony took place on April 29, 2011. During the ceremony, the Freedom Hospital of Chad was renamed China-Chad Friendship Hospital. The project was officially completed and handed over to the Government of Chad on June 21, 2013. The Minister of Health of Chad, Minister of Human Rights of Chad, and Chargé d'Affaires of the Chinese Embassy Qian Jin attended the handover ceremony.

project_name: Gov't donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: On January 21, 2010, Chinese government donated anti-malaria drugs to the Ministry of Public Health of Chad. This is the fourth batch of antimalarial drugs provided by the Chinese government to Chad since the resumption of diplomatic relations between China and Chad. This donations is one of the aid packages provided to African countries announced at the fourth ministerial meeting of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation. Chinese Ambassador to Chad Yang Guangyu and Chad Minister of Public Health Ngombaya Jaibe signed the handover certificate on behalf of the two governments

project_name: Embassy donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On August 31, 2020, the Chinese embassy provided anti-epidemic materials to the Chad Military Hospital. This donation will be used to help the army of Chad respond to COVID-19. The specific type, amount and monetary value of this donation are unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. Senior Colonel Hu Jihui, the Defense Attache of the Chinese Embassy in Chad, Brigadier General Suleiman, the Director of Health Services of the Ministry of National Defense of Chad, and Brigadier General Salkato, the Director of Military Cooperation, attended the ceremony.

project_name: Provides cataract surgery
description: On September 28, 2018, the opening ceremony of the "Bright Action" Surgery Project ("Action la Lumiere" or 光明行) was held at the China-Chad Friendship Hospital and was attended by Chinese Ambassador Li Jinjin as well as Chadian Minister of Health Saleh, and a number of Chinese medical aid workers from Nanchang University's affiliated eye hospital.   The doctors began working on September 1st and finished on the 8th of September 2019.  While the 1st phase of project (#56022) cured 233 cataract patients, the second phase performed 270 surgeries.

project_name: Donates materials for University of Comoros
description: In 2012, China donated materials to create a Confucius classroom at the University of Comoros in Moroni.

project_name: Donates for Guangzhou University Malaria study
description:
In June of 2007, Li Guoqiao and a team of Chinese medical researchers from the Tropical Medicine Institute at the Guangzhou University of Traditional Chinese Medicine proposed to take the anti-malaria drug artemisinin and dispense it in combination with another drug as a mass treatment to the 40,000 people living on Moheli Island in Comoros. The World Health Organization offered to support the Chinese government-funded project. Beijing would pay the estimated $320,000 for the drugs used in the Moheli treatments and would also meet the cost of additional drugs used to clear up remaining infections over a five-year period, according to World Health Organization officials. In December of 2010, it was reported that 11 Chinese researchers had initiated the project. ID #30101 contains details of the final project implementation. 
 
 According to a 2011 Working Series report, the highest incidence is 94.4 per cent and malaria is the most common cause of death in children under the age of five. In 2007, a joint project between Moheliand the Tropical Medicine Institute at Guangzhou University of Traditional Chinese Medicine (GUTCM) in southern China was started with the purpose of eradicating the parasite from the human body.
 
 This project has been linked to projects #30101, #57366, #57367, and #34813 because they all relate to anti malaria efforts made by China in Comoros as part of the campaign initiated by this project.

project_name: Gov't donates Covid-19 vaccine
description: On March 17, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 100,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Comoros, captured at Project ID#95377. Then, on July 1, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered another 100,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Comoros, captured at Project ID#93183. The Chinese Government delivered another (third) batch of donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Comoros on November 6, 2021.

project_name: Embassy donates Covid-19 supplies and office equipment
description: On August 5, 2021, He Yanjun, the ambassador to Comoros, handed over a batch of anti-epidemic materials and office equipment to the wife of the President of Comoros to support the Comoros Women's Union in carrying out related work. The aid of the anti-COVID materials and office equipment aims to help the department improve the medical diagnosis and treatment capabilities of women, children, and vulnerable groups in order to better fight the epidemic.

project_name: Donates drugs and medical devices to Krumlov Hospital
description: On April 20, 2016, the handover ceremony of drug and medical device from China was held at the Krumlov Hospital. Xiao Ming, Ambassador of the Comoros, Vice President and Minister of Health Muhaji, President of the Malouf Hospital, and Mr. Hu Bingyi, the business office of the Embassy of the Comoros, and members of the aid medical team attended the handover ceremony.

project_name: Donates medicine and medical equipment
description: On June 13th, 2019, Chinese ambassador He Yanjun and Comoros Minister of Health Hasid Mohammed Mubahaka Fatma signed a certificate acknowledging the handover of a grant of medicine and medical devices. The donation was valued at 800,000 RMB. The first secretary of the Chinese Embassy in Comoros, the ​​director of the Comoros Health Bureau, the dean of Marouf Hospital, and Zhou Quan, captain of the 13th Chinese medical team in Comoros was present at the handover ceremony.  The location of the handover ceremony is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donates Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine
description: On March 17, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 100,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Comoros, captured at Project ID#95377. Then, on July 1, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered another 100,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Comoros. The Chinese Government delivered another (third) batch of donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Comoros on November 6, 2021, captured at Project ID#93181.

project_name: People's Hospital of Guangxi Zhuang donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On November 7, 2020, Guangxi Autonomous Region People's Hospital donated medicines, protective clothing, isolation gowns, disinfectants and other anti-epidemic materials to Angdao Zhongke Friendship Hospital. The donation held a total value of about RMB700,000.   Zhou Quan, the captain of the 13th batch of medical teams in China, and Ahmed Anliane, the President of the Sino-Science Friendship Hospital, signed the donation certificate on behalf of both parties and received the supplies.

project_name: Donates anti-Malarial medicine, lab equipment and other supplies
description: On April 21, 2012, the Chinese Embassy donated 800,000 doses of Artequick, two motocycles, laboratory equipment, and office equipment to the Comoran Ministry of Health.  This donation is planned to help eradicate malaria in the country and better prevent the disease in pregnant women and children under five years old. This donation was made as a part of the 2007 program initiated by the Guangzhou University of Chinese Medicine (GZUCM) for the island of Moheli in the Comoros to eliminate malaria (see project #409).  Since the start of the program, the persistence of malaria has been significantly decreased.

project_name: Embassy donates Covid-19 materials to Office of the First Lady
description: On March 26, 2021, Chinese Ambassador to Comoros He Yanjun handed over the anti-epidemic materials from China to the Comoros President's wife. The President's wife Ambari Azali, the chief executive of Dake Island, and Meng Qiang, the captain of the short-term anti-epidemic medical team, attended the handover ceremony. These materials will help primary and secondary schools and other institutions specifically. China is willing to work with African countries including Comoros to build a closer China-Africa health community.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Bambao-Mtsanga Hospital
description: On November 27, 2009, the Government of Comoros and the Chinese Urban Construction Research Institute signed a design contract for the Bambao-Mtsanga Hospital Construction Project. Then, on April 1, 2010, the Chinese Government and the Government of Comoros signed an exchange of letters related to a grant for the Bambao-Mtsanga Hospital Construction Project. China’s Ministry of Commerce was the source of funding and it reportedly committed RMB 75,630,000 in total.   The project involved the construction of a 120-bed hospital — with pediatric, gynecology, surgery, outpatient, and emergency units — in the town of Bambao on the island of Anjouan (approximately 20 km from the Anjouan capital of Mutsamudu). The hospital also has a mortuary, a waste incinerator, and a radiology and digital imaging department.   China Jiangsu International Economic and Technical Cooperation Group, Ltd was the contractor responsible for implementation. On February 5, 2011, the Government of Comoros agreed on a physical site for the hospital. Then, on December 16, 2011, a construction contract was signed.  A groundbreaking ceremony took place on May 28, 2012 and the project was completed in July 2014. However, the hospital did not officially open until May 25, 2017.    As of March 2019, the hospital was seriously underutilized due to staff and equipment shortages. Also, the poor quality of the road between Mutsamudu and Bambao made it difficult for patients to get to the hospital. According to France24, the hospital “looks .. like a ghost ship, with a handful of patients wandering its corridors in stifling heat.”

project_name: Gov't donates Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine
description: On March 17, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 100,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Comoros. Then, on July 1, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered another 100,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Comoros, captured at Project ID #93183. The Chinese Government delivered another (third) batch of donated doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Comoros on November 6, 2021, captured at Project ID#93181.

project_name: Gov't donates anti-Malarial supplies
description: On July 16, 2019, a handover ceremony was held for a Chinese grant of medicine and supplies to Comoros. The grant was related to a previously established Chinese anti-malarial technical cooperation project.  The location of the handover ceremony, and the financial value of the donated materials are unknown. This grant was likely provided under the Artemisinin Compound Malaria Control Project (青蒿素复方疟疾防治项目), but this is not explicitly stated in sources.

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: On May 19 and 20, 2017, China donated anti-malarial medicine to Hanamboini village on Grande Comore and asked all the villagers to take the medicine for the anti-malaria campaign (see project #409 for details). The campaign experienced an exceptionally high rate of efficacy. Not only is China said to have provided the medication, but Chinese medical experts from Guangzhou University also helped devise the distribution strategy and were on-site to help deliver the medication.

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: On August 7 and 8, 2017, China donated malarial medicine to Hantsindzi village on Grande Comore island to aid an anti-malaria campaign (see project #409).

project_name: Gov't provides grant for anti-Malaria medical center
description: In July 2009, China established an anti-malaria medical center in Comoros. After the establishment of the anti-malaria center, Chinese experts could set up and test the facilities, exchange ideas with local specialists and give technological training to medical staff. For the following three years, the Chinese government provided the center facilities and drugs free of charge.

project_name: Provides cataract surgeries
description: On May 25th, 2016, Xiao Ming, the Chinese Ambassador to Comoros, attended the launching ceremony of the China aided Guangmingxing Project held at the El-Marrouf Hospital. The project aimed to perform 500 cataract surgeries but eventually performed 537. The Guangmingxing project was a project under the China-Africa Cooperation Forum Action Plan. The project also included the training of local ophthalmologists and the handover of equipment to Comoros for future use free of charge. On June 20, 2016 President Azali of Comoros met at the Presidential Palace with a group of Chinese experts who came to implement the project. The team of experts would return to China on June 20th.  There is no available information indicating the funding source and value of the project.

project_name: Embassy donates medical equipment to comoros Ministry of Health
description: On February 2, 2021, the Chinese Embassy in Comoros to the Comoros Ministry of Health to help Comoros deal with the second wave of the new crown pneumonia epidemic. The donation included 2 VG70 respirators, 2 5105 respirators, 4 oxygen concentrators, 3 airway mucus removal machines, 1 electrocardiograph, and 1 oximeter.   Ambassador He Yanjun and Comoros Minister of Health Ms. Zaidu signed the handover certificate. The Minister of Health of the Division spoke highly of the medical and health cooperation between the Division and China and thanked the Chinese side for its generous donation. This equipment will be placed in the designated hospitals for COVID-19 and will increase the effectiveness of treatment.

project_name: Gov't provides repair for X-ray machine at Anjouan Hospital
description: In July 2017, the Chinese Government dispatch sent a technical expert to repair an X-ray machine at a local hospital on the island of Anjouan in Comoros. The technician remained in Comoros from July 16, 2017 to July 26,2017 to work on the machine

project_name: Gov't donates Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021 and 2022, the Chinese Government donated approximately 540,000 doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of the Republic of Congo.   On February 4th, 2021,  Chinese ambassador, Ma Fulin, held an audience with the President of the Republic, Denis Sassou N'Guesso, where he stated China's intent to donate 100,000 doses of the coronavirus vaccine to the government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. This donation came alongside a debt cancellation agreement (see: Project ID# 88157) and a donation of FCFA 35 billion. Then, on February 10th, 2021, the Chinese embassy in the Republic of the Congo stated Congo would soon receive 100,000 doses of the COVID-19 vaccine. The doses are intended to cover fifty thousand people. Then, on March 10th, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 100,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of the Republic of Congo. The handover ceremony was held in Brazzaville, Congo. The ceremony was attended by Chinese Ambassador to Congo Ma Fulin, Congolese Foreign Minister Gacoso, Minister of Health Mikolo, Minister of Defense Moncho (Coordinator of the National Anti-epidemic Mechanism), and WHO Representative in Congo Manga. This donation allowed Congo to launch its vaccination campaign on March 25th, 2021.  Then, on March 25, 2021, the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) of China donated an additional 40,000 Sinopharm vaccine doses to the Congolese Ministry of National Defense. The Chinese Ambassador to the Republic of Congo, Ma Fulin, and the Congolese Minister of National Defense, Mr. Charles Richard Mondjo, received the batch of vaccines and they were then delivered to the Congolese Ministry of National Defense on March 26, 2021.   On May 14, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 200,000 additional donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of the Republic of Congo.  The vaccines arrived at Maya-Maya airport in Brazzaville, Congo. This donation was given by Ma Fulin, Chinese Ambassador to Congo, to the Congolese Government represented, by Mrs. Jacqueline Lydia Mikolo, the Minister of Health in Congo.   Approximately 6 months later, in January 2022, the Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of the Republic of Congo.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Sino-Congolese Friendship Hospital
description: In 2013, China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) announced that the Chinese government would provide an RMB 10 million grant for the Sino-Congolese Friendship Hospital Equipment Project.  The purpose of this project was to equip the Sino-Congolese Friendship Hospital (or Hôpital d'amitié sino-congolaise de M’Filou or l'Hôpital de base de Mfilou or 中刚友好医院) in M’Filou with modern medical equipment, including surgical equipment, stomatology instruments, ultraviolet lamps, incubators, ultrasound machines, respirators, and endoscopy equipment sterilizers. This batch of equipment was successfully delivered on January 13, 2017.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Agricultural Technology Demonstration Center
description: In 2008, China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) provided an RMB 40 million grant to Republic of Congo for the Agricultural Technology Demonstration Center Construction Project (captured in Project ID#59183). This grant commitment fulfilled a pledge that was first made at the 2006 Beijing Summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation.   This project, which is also known as Phase 1 of the Agricultural Technology Demonstration Center project, involved the construction of an Agricultural Technology Demonstration Center (ATDC) in the town of Kombé. The ATDC occupies an area of about 59 hectares and the project site had a total construction area of over 5,000 square meters. The construction of the ATDC included offices, training facilities, production facilities, housing accommodations. It also involved the creation of demonstration fields, the installation of irrigation facilities, and the procurement of agricultural machinery and equipment. The Chinese Academy of Tropical Agricultural Sciences was the contractor responsible for implementation. On September 21, 2009, a groundbreaking ceremony was held and attended by the Chinese Ambassador, the Congolese Minister of Agriculture and Animal Husbandry, and technical experts from the Chinese Academy of Tropical Agricultural Sciences. Then, in April 2011, the project passed its final MOFCOM inspection. It was officially completed and handed over to the Congolese authorities on December 19, 2011.   Then, in 2012, China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) provided an RMB 14 million grant to Republic of Congo for Phase 2 of the Agricultural Technology Demonstration Center Project (captured in this project, ID#72959). Phase 2 involved the dispatching of Chinese agricultural experts to the ATDC to provide training and technical assistance — related to cassava, corn, vegetables, chickens, and other animals — to local officials, agricultural technicians, and farmers. Phase 2, which appears to have been financed with an RMB 14 million grant from MOFCOM, began implementation on January 1, 2012 and ended on December 31, 2014.

project_name: Donates to prevent ebola
description: On September 30, 2014 China pledged to donate aid worth 5 million Yuan (approximately 400 million CFA) to Congo to address the threat of Ebola. The donation would include protection masks, medical examination rubber gloves, shoe covers, protective glasses, and hand and back sprayers. The donation was received November 1, 2014.

project_name: PLA donates Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021 and 2022, the Chinese Government donated approximately 540,000 doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of the Republic of Congo. The Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of the Republic of Congo on March 10, 2021. The handover ceremony was held in Brazzaville, Congo. The ceremony was attended by Chinese Ambassador to Congo Ma Fulin, Congolese Foreign Minister Gacoso, Minister of Health Mikolo, Minister of Defense Moncho (Coordinator of the National Anti-epidemic Mechanism), and WHO Representative in Congo Manga.   Then, on March 25, 2021, the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) of China donated an additional 40,000 Sinopharm vaccine doses to the Congolese Ministry of National Defense. The Chinese Ambassador to the Republic of Congo, Ma Fulin, and the Congolese Minister of National Defense, Mr. Charles Richard Mondjo, received the batch of vaccines and they were then delivered to the Congolese Ministry of National Defense on March 26, 2021.   On May 14, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 200,000 additional donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of the Republic of Congo.  The vaccines arrived at Maya-Maya airport in Brazzaville, Congo. This donation was given by Ma Fulin, Chinese Ambassador to Congo, to the Congolese Government represented, by Mrs. Jacqueline Lydia Mikolo, the Minister of Health in Congo.   Approximately 6 months later, in January 2022, the Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of the Republic of Congo.

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria
description: On April 20, 2010, there was an exchange of letters for malaria drugs. According to a report on the Embassy and Commercial Counselor's Office of the Embassy of China in Congo-Brazzaville, on July 30, 2011, the fourth batch of anti-malaria drugs (330 boxes/containers/cartons) were given by the Chinese government to the Congolese government Ministry of Health and Population.

project_name: Gov't donates equipments for loandjili General Hospital
description: On May 20, 2017, the Chinese Vice Minister of Commerce visited Brazzaville and signed a cooperation agreement to provide equipment for the Loandjili General Hospital in Pointe-Noire(黑角卢旺基里医院). The exact contents and value of the equipment is unknown.  The other four cooperation agreements were also signed: cash assistance for monkey pox(see project #57818), a transition from analogue to digital television(see project #57584), the 3rd phase of the national telecommunications coverage(see project #57531), and a donation of RMB 100 million for unspecified purposes( aee project #57955).  The Loandjili General Hospital was originally built with Chinese Aid, for more details see project #57864.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for construction of hospitals
description: On December 28, 2009, the Republic of the Congo received a CFA 3.5 billion CFA grant from the Chinese Government to update the country’s health facilities. The grant agreement was signed between Congolese Finance Minister Gilbert Ondongo and Chinese Ambassador Li Shuli. No additional details were disclosed.

project_name: Provided grant for fighting SmallPox
description:
On May 20, 2017, the Chinese Vice Minister of Commerce, Qian Keming, visited Brazzaville and signed five cooperation agreements with Republic of Congo, including a USD 700,000 cash assistance for fighting small pox. 
 
 The other four cooperation agreements are: a transition from analogue to digital television(#57584), the 3rd phase of the national telecommunications coverage(#57531), staffing of the general hospital equipment Loandjili Pointe-Noire(#57868), and a donation of RMB 100 million for unspecified purposes(#57955).

project_name: Gov't provides technical assistance to loandjili General Hospital
description: The Chinese Government provided a grant in 2011 for the Loandjili General Hospital Technical Cooperation Project (Phase 3). A team of 7 were sent to the hospital as part of the project. This Loandjili General Hospital is located in Pointe Noire. This project began on June 4, 2011 and end on June 3, 2013.

project_name: National Health Commission donateS anti-pandemic supplies
description: On January 15, 2021, a handover ceremony was held for the National Health Commission of China's donation of anti-pandemic medical supplies to Congo. The ceremony was held at the Sino-Congo Friendship Hospital, in Brazzaville, Congo. The donation was worth 74 million FCFA.   The materials were to be dispersed to the Sino-Congolese hospital of Mfilou in Brazzaville and the hospital of Loandjili in Pointe-Noire. The donation was part of China's initiative to mitigate the spread of COVID-19 in the Republic of the Congo.

project_name: Gov't donates anti-pandemic materials
description: On June 9, 2020, the Chinese Government donated 150 thousand simple and sophisticated masks, 10 thousand reactive tests, respirators, thermometers, gloves, overalls protection, and many other materials intended for the response to the covid-19 coronavirus. The total value of this donation is unknown.   The donation was handed over by the Chinese Ambassador to Congo, Ma Fulin, and was made to help Congo combat the Covid-19 pandemic.

project_name: IDCPC donates anti-epidemic materials to the Party of Labour
description: On July 23, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Congo handed over the anti-epidemic materials on behalf of the International Liaison Department of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (IDCPC) to The Congolese Party of Labour, the ruling party in Congo. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.  The handover ceremony was held at the Brazzaville Municipal Party Committee of the Congo Party. More than 40 people attended, including Ambassador Ma Fulin, General Secretary of the Congo Party Moussa, members of the Executive Secretariat of the Congo Party Central Committee, and the head of the Brazzaville Municipal Committee.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Sino-Congolese Friendship Hospital
description: In 2009, the Chinese Government and the Republic of Congo signed a grant agreement for the Sino-Congolese Friendship Hospital Construction Project. China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) was the source of grant funding and it reportedly committed RMB 70 million (approximately 5.6 billion CFA francs or $10 million) in total.   This project involved the construction of a 100-bed hospital in M’Filou (Mfilou), which is the 7th arrondissement of the capital city of Brazzaville. The hospital occupies an area of more than 6,300 m2 and it consists of an outpatient building, emergency building, medical technology building, ward building, and dormitory building. It is equipped with a laboratory, an operating theater, a mortuary, and modern medical technology.   China State Construction Engineering Corporation Ltd. (CSCEC) was the contractor responsible for project implementation. They signed a construction contract on September 23, 2009. The project commenced on August 9, 2011 and it was completed on March 30, 2013. The hospital was officially inaugurated on March 30, 2013 by Chinese President Xi Jinping. It reportedly employs 260 doctors and nurses.

project_name: Launches medical campaign 'Operation Light'
description:
In 2014, China established a medical campaign called “Light Operation” in Republic of Congo (中国“光明行”医疗援助项目). The project was implemented by the Tianjin Municipal Health and Family Planning Commission. After 2 years preparation, the project was launched in 2016. A team of Chinese doctors from Tianjin Eye Hospital will come to Congo to operate free of charge those suffering from cataracts and nearly 500 patients will be treated at the Sino-Congolese Friendship Hospital of M'Filou in Brazzaville and that of Loandjili in Black Point. 
 
 On August 4, 2016, a team of 7 experts led by Dean Tang Xin of Tianjin Eye Hospital arrived in Congo (Brazzaville) to carry out the project. The program has an execution period of 40 days. The project started on August 24, 2016 and was completed on September 14, 2016. 512 cases of cataract recovery surgery were completed within 20 days.

project_name: Embassy donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On July 1, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Congo donated anti-epidemic materials to the Organization of African First Ladies for Development (OAFLAD). The donation was in response to the OAFLAD's request for assistance to help women and children in Congo stay protected against the Covid-19 epidemic.  The donation was made in Brazzaville, Congo. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Donates medical equipment and anti-Malaria drugs
description: On August 13, 2008, the National Public Health Laboratory opened its center for the prevention and treatment of malaria in Brazzaville. The opening of the center was linked to a Chinese donation consisting of medical equipment and pharmaceutical drugs estimated to be worth 300 million CFA francs that was received by the Minister of Health, Social Affairs and Family, Emilienne Raoul. The center's goal is to conduct in-depth analysis and research on malaria. The Chinese government sent four experts, equipment, pharmaceuticals and reagents to ensure the operation of the center. These Chinese experts worked at the center for 45 days to train the Congolese staff.

project_name: Donates medical equipment
description: On June 19, 2006 during Chinese Premier Wen Jiabao's visit to Congo, he presented a donation of medicines and computers to the Congolese government for use in hospitals where Chinese medical teams were serving.  The value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: On January 20, 2009,  Chinese Ambassador to Congo (Brazzaville) Li Shuli presented a batch of anti-malarial drugs to the Congolese government on behalf of the Chinese government. Ambassador Li and Ms. Raoul, Minister of Health of Gang attended the signing ceremony of the handover certificate. This batch of antimalarial drugs can treat 100,000 patients.

project_name: Gov't donates Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021 and 2022, the Chinese Government donated approximately 540,000 doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of the Republic of Congo. The Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of the Republic of Congo on March 10, 2021. The handover ceremony was held in Brazzaville, Congo. The ceremony was attended by Chinese Ambassador to Congo Ma Fulin, Congolese Foreign Minister Gacoso, Minister of Health Mikolo, Minister of Defense Moncho (Coordinator of the National Anti-epidemic Mechanism), and WHO Representative in Congo Manga.   Then, on March 25, 2021, the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) of China donated an additional 40,000 Sinopharm vaccine doses to the Congolese Ministry of National Defense. The Chinese Ambassador to the Republic of Congo, Ma Fulin, and the Congolese Minister of National Defense, Mr. Charles Richard Mondjo, received the batch of vaccines and they were then delivered to the Congolese Ministry of National Defense on March 26, 2021.  On May 14, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 200,000 additional donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of the Republic of Congo.  The vaccines arrived at Maya-Maya airport in Brazzaville, Congo. This donation was given by Ma Fulin, Chinese Ambassador to Congo, to the Congolese Government represented, by Mrs. Jacqueline Lydia Mikolo, the Minister of Health in Congo. Approximately 6 months later, in January 2022, the Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of the Republic of Congo.

project_name: Gov't donates medical equipment
description:
In 2011, the Chinese government agreed to provide 51 boxes of commonly used drugs and medical equipment to the three hospitals where the Chinese medical teams work in the Republic of Congo. The medicine and medical equipment arrived in Congo on October 10, 2011.
 
 On November 16, 2011, the Congolese side held a handover ceremony for the batch of medicines and medical devices at Dalungai Hospital. The value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Gives Congo medical equipment
description: In 2016, Chinese Ambassador to Republic of Congo gave the Congolese government a batch of medical equipment worth 620 million FCFA, intended to equip the ophthalmic departments of hospitals. This donation is apart of a larger operation titled "opération lumière", a campaign for free screening and treatment for cataracts in Congo.

project_name: Gov't donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On April 15, 2020, the anti-epidemic materials donated by the Chinese government arrived in Brazzaville, Congo to fight the Covid-19 epidemic. The donation was made in response to the epidemic prevention materials that are about to run out throughout Congo. The donation consisted of 2,000 medical masks, 2,000 medical protective suits, 10,000 gloves, 2,000 protective glasses, and 500 electronic thermometers. The materials were distributed on April 16, 2020. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.  A ceremony was held for the donation and was held at the Congolese Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Ambassador Ma Fulin to Congo and Congolese Foreign Minister Gakoso signed a handover certificate.

project_name: Embassy provides vaccines to Relief Foundation for Children's Health
description: On July 12, 2021, a handover ceremony was held to celebrate the Chinese Embassy's donation of child-safe pneumococcal and typhoid vaccines to the Congolese Relief Foundation. At the ceremony, Congolese children were vaccinated using the donated vaccines. The monetary value of the grant is unknown.

project_name: Embassy donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On March 17, 2020, a handover ceremony was held for the Chinese Embassy in Congo's donation of protective materials to the Congolese government to fight against the Covid-19 epidemic. The specific type and monetary value of the donation are unknown.   The ceremony was held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Congo. More than 60 people including Ambassador Ma Fulin, Minister of Health Mikolo of Congo, Secretary-General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Mamina, and officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Health attended the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Loandjili General Hospital
description: In 2002, the Chinese Government and the Republic of Congo signed a grant agreement for the Loandjili General Hospital Construction Project. China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) was the source of grant funding and it reportedly committed RMB 80 million in total. This project involved the construction of the Loandjili General Hospital in the city of Pointe Noire.  The hospital occupies 10,000 m^2 and it has 200 beds. It is reportedly able to accommodate 400 patients a day.    The project was first approved on March 2, 1975. A construction design was completed in 1987, but then the Congolese side chose a different project site in 1994. The two governments signed an exchange of letters on July 22 and 28, 1994 to confirm that the Chinese Government would dispatch a team to inspect the new project site.
