Then, according to the exchange of letters signed by the two governments on February 23 and March 8, 2000, the Chinese Government dispatched another team in June 2000 to conduct a supplementary inspection of the project site and signed a project design contract. The Republic of Congo subsequently sent a representative in February 2001 to China to review the project design plans.   Ultimately, Tianjin Architecture Design Institute (天津市建筑设计院) was selected to design the project and Liaoning Construction (辽宁金帝建设集团股份有限) was designated as the contractor responsible for implementation. A formal groundbreaking ceremony took place in February 2002. However, project implementation did not begin until May 1, 2002. Then, from December 30, 2002 to January 8, 2003, MOFCOM’s Foreign Aid Department dispatched a five-person mid-term project inspection team to the Republic of Congo. A project acceptance and handover certificate was signed on February 19, 2004. Then, on February 20, 2004, a project completion ceremony was held.

project_name: China EXIM Bank donates for Oyo Hospital
description: On June 19, 2006, China Eximbank and the Republic of Congo signed a $1.6 billion loan framework agreement — also known in the Republic of Congo as the “strategic partnership” (“partenariat stratégique”) — that allowed the Republic of Congo to obtain China Eximbank loans for infrastructure projects through a securitization mechanism: Société Nationales des Pétroles Congolais (SNPC)—the country’s state-owned oil company—agreed to deposit a portion of the cash proceeds from its oil exports into an escrow account that is controlled by China Eximbank. This framework agreement (captured in Project ID#60219) was ratified on October 26, 2006.   One of the subsidiary loans that was approved through the framework agreement was a $26 million loan in 2006 for the Oyo Hospital Construction Project. This loan reportedly carried the following terms: a 0.25% interest rate, a maturity of 20 years, and a grace period of 5 years. It was fully repaid by the borrower. The loan’s (principal) amount outstanding was $0 as of December 31, 2019.   The Oyo Hospital Construction Project involved the construction of a 200-bed hospital in the town of Oyo, the district of Oyo, the Central Cuvette Department, and the health district of Alima-Oyo (which serves 53,000 local residents). The hospital has several departments, including administration, general medicine, surgery, cardiology, ophthalmology, ENT, otolaryngology, urology, pharmacy, morgue, radiology, and laboratory analysis.    Beijing Uni.-Construction Group Co., Ltd. (BUCC) — also known as Beijing Residential Development & Construction Group Corporation（BRCC) — was the contractor responsible for project implementation. The project was plagued by various delays. A foundation-laying ceremony took place on May 7, 2008 and the originally scheduled project completion date was June 30, 2012. However, the hospital was not open to the public until March 10, 2017.

project_name: Gov't donates AIDS supplies and agricultural equipment
description:
On December 1, 2017, Chinese Embassy in Republic of Congo donated anti-AIDS supplies and agricultural equipment to the Congolese Relief Foundation led by the President of Congo's wife, Mikolo (向刚果救助基金会捐赠抗击艾滋病物资和农用器具). More than 100 people, including Ambassador Xia Huang to Congo, Mongo, Secretary-General of the Congo Relief Foundation, representatives of diplomatic envoys and international organizations, and Mrs. Xia Huang’s wife Liu Hong, and business counselor Yang Peipei, attended the donation ceremony.
 
 The value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: On May 6 2010, the Chinese Ambassador to the Republic of Congo, Li Shu Li, donated malaria drugs to the Congolese health authorities on behalf of China. This is the 3rd batch of anti-malaria drugs China has donated to Congo since 2006.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Sino-Congolese Ophthalmology Center
description: In April 2017, the Director of the China’s Health Planning Commission signed an intergovernmental agreement with the Republic of Congo’s Minister of Health regarding the Sino-Congolese Ophthalmology Center Project. Then, in May 2018, the Tianjin Ophthalmology Hospital signed a counterpart assistance agreement with the Sino-Congolese Friendship Hospital (or Hôpital d'amitié sino-congolaise de M’Filou or l'Hôpital de base de Mfilou) regarding this project, which was supported by a grant worth RMB 5.5 million.   This project involved the installation of an Ophthalmology Center at the Sino-Congolese Friendship Hospital (or Hôpital d'amitié sino-congolaise de M’Filou or l'Hôpital de base de Mfilou) in M’Filou, which is located in the 7th arrondissement of the capital city of Brazzaville. It involved, among other things, the training of local ophthalmologists. The center’s opening ceremony took place on December 12, 2018.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for establishment of anti-Malaria center
description:
In 2006, the Chinese Government and the Government of the Republic of Congo signed a framework agreement regarding the establishment of an anti-malaria center in Congo. Then, on December 26, 2007 and January 11, 2008, the Chinese Government and the Government of the Republic of Congo signed letters of exchange regarding the establishment of an anti-malaria center. 
 
 On August 13, 2008, the center (known locally as ‘Centre Chine-Congo de Prevention et de Traitment du Paludisme’) was officially inaugurated at the Congolese National Institute for Public Health Laboratory. 4 Chinese experts were dispatched to the center to conduct training activities.

project_name: Jiangsu Provincial Construction Group donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On May 13, 2020, the Jiangsu Provincial Construction Group Co., Ltd. donation of anti-pandemic materials arrived in Brazzaville, Congo. Congolese Minister of Health, Jacqueline Lydia Mikolo, received the donation. The donation consisted of 8000 single-use masks, 1200 protective gloves, 400 medical goggles, infrared thermometers, and five hundred test reagents. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.`11jn  The tests and thermometers helped carry out large-scale screenings across Congo.

project_name: International Liaison Department provides anti-epidemic materials
description: On August 11, 2020, the International Liaison Department of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China provided anti-epidemic materials to the Rally of the Republicans (RDR), the ruling party of Côte d'Ivoire. The donated materials included 40,000 disposable medical masks, 1,000 protective suits, and 400 forehead thermometers.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the Party Office of the Rally of the Republicans (RDR) Party of Côte d'Ivoire. Wan Li, the Chinese Ambassador to Côte d'Ivoire, and the Executive Secretary of the Rally of the Republicans (RDR) Party of Côte d'Ivoire attended the ceremony.  Zhou Yi, the Director of the Political Section of the Embassy, ​​the Executive Deputy Secretary of the Rally of the Republicans (RDR) Party, the Minister of Cleaning and Sanitation in Côte d'Ivoire, the Executive Deputy Secretary and Minister of Sports, and the Executive Deputy Secretary in charge of relations with the Côte d'Ivoire countryside were also present.

project_name: Gov't provides anti-epidemic materials
description: On September 15, 2020, the Chinese government provided anti-epidemic materials to Koumassi City in Côte d'Ivoire. The donated materials included about 15,000 single-use masks. These masks will be distributed to about 2,000 female traders within Côte d'Ivoire. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.   A handover ceremony was held for this donation at Koumassi City Hall in Côte d'Ivoire. China’s Ambassador to Côte d’Ivoire, Wan Li, the Secretary of State for Women's Affairs, and UN Women's Representative attended the meeting. The Deputy Mayor of Koumassi City and representatives of dozens of female traders in the city also attended the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Malaria research and control center project
description: On 1 September 2008, the Chinese Government and the Government of Cote d'Ivoire signed an exchange of notes in which the Chinese Government agreed to provide an RMB 3 million grant for the Malaria Research and Control Center Project. According to the Chinese Ministry of Commerce, from March 14th to April 26th, experts from the Chinese Aid Malaria Prevention and Treatment center arrived to work. It should be noted that training was provided in addition to the grant. This project involved the establishment of a Malaria Research and Control Center (Centre de Recherche et de Lutte contre le Paludisme or CRLP) at the National Institute of Public Health (Institut national de Santé Publique or INSP) in the Adjame district of Abidjan. The implementing contractor is unknown. On 7 April 2009, Ivorian and Chinese government officials attended the opening ceremony for the center.  The Malaria Research and Control Center was badly damaged during the 2011 post-election crisis. The Chinese Government subsequently provided another grant to support rehabilitation of the center (see Project #66116).

project_name: Gov't provides worth of anti-epidemic materials
description: On May 13, 2020, the Chinese government provided a second batch of anti-epidemic materials to Côte d'Ivoire. The specific contents of the donation are unknown but the materials have an estimated value of USD $680,000. This donation is reported as the second batch of materials provided by the Chinese government. Information on the specifics of the first batch is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at Abidjan International Airport in Côte d'Ivoire. Wan Li, the Chinese Ambassador to Côte d'Ivoire, a representative of the Minister of Health and Public Health, a representative of the Chief of Staff, the representative of the Minister of Foreign Affairs and the Director General of Bilateral Cooperation, and the President of the National Institute of Public Health attended the ceremony.

project_name: China donates anti-Malaria medicine
description: On June 28, 2007, China donated a batch of anti-malaria medicine to the Government of Cote d'Ivoire. It is unclear what the value of the medicine is.

project_name: Provides masks to orphanage institution
description: On August 6, 2020, China provided 15,000 medical masks to an orphanage in Cocody, a suburb of the Abidjan Region of Côte d'Ivoire. These masks will be distributed to children on welfare living in Cocody to improve their protection against COVID-19.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. China’s Ambassador to Côte d'Ivoire, Wan Li, the Ivorian Minister of Women, Children, and Families, Lee-Bakayoko, and a representative from UNICEF attended the ceremony. More than 40 representatives of teachers and students also attended. During the event, representatives of children in the orphanage  presented self-made paintings to Ambassador Wan Li and other guests.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Gagnoa Hospital
description: In 2009, China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) provided an RMB 49.98 million (CFA 4 billion) grant to the Government of Cote d'Ivoire for the Gagnoa General Hospital Construction Project. The grant proceeds covered 100% of the commercial contract cost but the Government of Cote d'Ivoire also contributed CFA 2 billion.  This project involved the construction of a hospital in Gagnoa, which is the hometown of President Gbagbo. The 104-bed hospital is 6,531 square meters and it has departments for internal medicine, surgery, pediatrics, gynecology, medical imaging, laboratory analysis, and administration. Wuhan Architectural Design Institute was the contractor responsible for project design, and Gansu Geo-Engineering Co. Ltd (甘肃海外工程总公司) was the contractor responsible for project implementation.   On April 4, 2009, a foundation-laying ceremony took place. Construction took place between April 18, 2009 and August 31, 2010. Then, on November 25, 2011, the project was officially completed and handed over to the Ivorian authorities. The handover ceremony was delayed due to a presidential election crisis in Cote d'Ivoire. The hospital was officially inaugurated on March 4, 2013.   The Chinese Government then funded three technical assistance projects between 2013 and 2019 to support the maintenance and operations of this hospital. On July 5, 2013, the Chinese Government and the Government of Cote d'Ivoire signed a CFA 640,625,000 grant agreement for Phase 1 of the Gagnoa Hospital Technical Cooperation Project (captured via Project ID#92286). According to the Government of Côte d'Ivoire’s Aid Management Platform (AMP), Phase 1 was implemented between July 5, 2013 and July 4, 2015. The Chinese Government disbursed CFA 635,129,402.87 of grant funding in support of Phase 1 on June 30, 2014.   Then, in August 2016, the Chinese Government and the Government of Cote d'Ivoire signed letters of exchange regarding Phase 2 of the Gagnoa Hospital Technical Cooperation Project (captured via Project ID#66030). The monetary value of the grant commitment that supported Phase 2 is unknown. A Phase 2 completion ceremony was held on December 3, 2018.   Then, on October 17, 2019, the Chinese Government and the Government of Cote d'Ivoire signed a grant agreement for Phase 3 of the Gagnoa Hospital Technical Cooperation Project (captured via Project ID#87873). The monetary value of the grant commitment that supported Phase 3 is unknown

project_name: Grants funds for Health Center
description:
In 2014, China granted funds for a health center (Centre de sante or 阿加美卫生中心) in Adjamé, Abidjan, Cote d'Ivoire. The official completion ceremony took place on 8 July 2014. The project value and construction start date are unknown. 
 
 This project is part of the Sino-Africa People to People Friendship Action program (中非民间友好行动).

project_name: First Lady provides anti-epidemic materials
description: On August 25, 2020, the Chinese Ambassador to Côte d'Ivoire, Wan Li, on behalf of Mrs. Peng Liyuan, the First Lady of the People's Republic of China, provided a batch of medical equipment to Mrs. Dominique Ouattara, the First Lady of the Republic of Côte d'Ivoire. The donated materials included 18,000 single use surgical masks and 120 temperature guns. These materials will be distributed to women, children, and adolescents in Côte d'Ivoire as part of the country’s COVID-19 response effort. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony took place for this donation in the meeting room of the General Secretariat of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Côte d'Ivoire. China’s Ambassador to  Côte d'Ivoire, Wan Li, the First Lady of Côte d'Ivoire, Dominique Ouattara, the Deputy Secretary-General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the Director of the Asia-Pacific Department attended the ceremony. A handover certificate was signed at the ceremony.

project_name: Embassy donates
description: On April 23, 2020, the Chinese Embassy provided a 8,500,000 CFA cash donation to the Abobo City Government in the Abidjan Region of Côte d'Ivoire. This monetary donation will be used to improve COVID-19 prevention and response efforts in Côte d'Ivoire.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. Wang Yi, the Political Counselor of the Chinese Embassy in Côte d'Ivoire, the Deputy Mayor of Abobo City, and the Minister of State and Defense Minister attended the ceremony.

project_name: Provides anti-epidemic materials to Ministry of Sports
description: On May 14, 2020, China provided anti-epidemic materials to the Ministry of Sports in Côte d'Ivoire. The donated materials include 1,150 surgical masks, 200 buckets, 200 bottles of hand wash, and 4 infrared thermometers. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. Wan Li, the Chinese Ambassador to Côte d'Ivoire, and Dan Ao, the Minister of Sports of Côte d'Ivoire, jointly attended the ceremony.

project_name: COMPLANT provides anti-epidemic supplies
description: On September 2, China Complete Equipment Import and Export Group provided anti-epidemic supplies to Côte d'Ivoire. The donated materials included 2 ambulances, 430,000 medical masks, 3,000 protective suits, 3,000 pairs of goggles, 160,000 medical gloves, and 500 forehead thermometers. The monetary value of this donation is an estimated 280,000,000 CFA.  A handover ceremony took place for this donation at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Côte d'Ivoire. China’s Ambassador to Côte d'Ivoire, Wan Li, and the Section Foreign Minister attended the ceremony. The Minister of Presidential Affairs, Secretary-General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Director of the General Office, Director of the General Office of the Ministry of Health, and representatives of China National Complete Plant and Regional Chairman also attended the ceremony. Ambassador Wan Li and Foreign Minister Coulibaly delivered speeches respectively. During the ceremony, representatives of China Complete Group also signed the material handover certificate with Foreign Minister Coulibaly.

project_name: Provides anti-epidemic supplies
description: On August 18, 2020, China provided anti-epidemic supplies to Côte d'Ivoire’s Commission for Mosques and Islamic Affairs (COSIM). The donation included 5,000 single-use masks. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony took place for this donation at the Grand Mosque in Tashville, Côte d'Ivoire. Wan Li, China’s Ambassador to Côte d'Ivoire, and the Chairman of the High Commission for Mosques and Islamic Affairs (COSIM) attended the ceremony. More than 10 COSIM members were also present.

project_name: Signs exchange of notes for anti-Malaria medicines
description: On 1 September 2008, China signed an exchange of notes for donating anti-malaria medicines to Cote d'Ivoire worth 2 million RMB (130 million CFA). These funds were sourced either from the grant (project #66188) or interest-free loan (project #70529) signed that day.

project_name: International Liaison Department provides anti-epidemic materials
description: On December 16, 2020, China’s Yunnan Provincial Government provided anti–epidemic materials to Côte d'Ivoire’s Ministry of Tourism and Leisure. The donated materials included  200,000 face masks and 200 digital infrared thermometers. The donation was sent in 55 packages of 536 kg in equipment. These materials will be used to combat the COVID-19 pandemic in Côte d'Ivoire.  The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. The Director of Cabinet, Camille Kouassi, and the Director General of the Société des Palaces de Cocody, Ms. Maférima Diarrassouba, attended the ceremony.

project_name: Donates materials to combat avian influenza
description: In 2008, Chinese government provided the Government of the Republic of Côte d'Ivoire with equipment for the fight against avian influenza, which consisted mainly of laboratory equipment to strengthen the analytical capacity of Côte d'Ivoire, particularly in the area of ​​bird flu. The handover ceremony occurred on May 7th, 2008 at the Veterinary Bureau of the Ministry of Animal Products and Aquatic Resources ("我举行援科防治禽流感物资援助交接仪式"). The donation totals 1,000,00 RMB (about 130 million CFA Francs).

project_name: Gov't provides grant
description: On May 30, 2012 and August 22, 2012, the Chinese Ambassador to Cote d'Ivoire and the Ivorian Foreign Minister signed letters of exchange in which China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) agreed to finance the Malaria Research and Control Center Rehabilitation Project. Then, on September 26, 2012, the parties signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) regarding the rehabilitation of the Center for Research and the Fight against Malaria, which is known in French as Centre de Recherche et de Lutte contre le Paludisme (CRLP). According to the Government of Cote d'Ivoire’s Aid Management Platform (AMP), the Chinese Government and the Government of Cote d'Ivoire signed a CFA 335,937,500 grant agreement to support the Malaria Research and Control Center Rehabilitation Project on January 1, 2014. CFA 369,364,504.22 was disbursed in support of this project in a single tranche on December 31, 2014.   The purpose of the project was to rehabilitate the CRLP, which was originally built with financial support from the Chinese Government in 2009 (as captured via Project #718) but was badly damaged during the 2011 post-election crisis. The CRLP is located at the National Institute of Public Health in Adjamé. Jiangsu Provincial Construction Group Co., Ltd. (JPC) was the contractor responsible for project implementation. It signed a rehabilitation contract on October 31, 2013 and completed all rehabilitation works on November 19, 2014. Then, on April 8, 2015, the rehabilitation project passed inspection and was officially handed over to the Ivorian Ministry of Health. The keys to the rehabilitated building were delivered on April 14, 2015.

project_name: Gov't donates supplies to combat Ebola
description: On January 2, 2014, the Chinese Government and the Government of Cote d'Ivoire signed an RMB 5 million (CFA 450 million) grant agreement for the provision of supplies to combat the Ebola epidemic. On October 31, 2014, a shipment of supplies to combat the Ebola epidemic worth RMB 5 million arrived by special freight in Abidjan. The donation consisted of protective clothing, gas masks, disposable rubber gloves, shoe covers, goggles, sprayers, infrared thermometers, body temperature detectors, and body bags. An official handover ceremony was held on November 11, 2014. According to the Government of Côte d'Ivoire’s Aid Management Platform (AMP), the grant that supported this project was fully disbursed as of December 31, 2014.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Gagnoa Hospital
description: In 2009, China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) provided an RMB 49.98 million (CFA 4 billion) grant to the Government of Cote d'Ivoire for the Gagnoa General Hospital Construction Project. The grant proceeds covered 100% of the commercial contract cost but the Government of Cote d'Ivoire also contributed CFA 2 billion.   This project involved the construction of a hospital in Gagnoa, which is the hometown of President Gbagbo. The 104-bed hospital is 6,531 square meters and it has departments for internal medicine, surgery, pediatrics, gynecology, medical imaging, laboratory analysis, and administration.  Wuhan Architectural Design Institute was the contractor responsible for project design, and Gansu Geo-Engineering Co. Ltd (甘肃海外工程总公司) was the contractor responsible for project implementation. On April 4, 2009, a foundation-laying ceremony took place. Construction took place between April 18, 2009 and August 31, 2010. Then, on November 25, 2011, the project was officially completed and handed over to the Ivorian authorities. The handover ceremony was delayed due to a presidential election crisis in Cote d'Ivoire. The hospital was officially inaugurated on March 4, 2013.  The Chinese Government then funded three technical assistance projects between 2013 and 2019 to support the maintenance and operations of this hospital. On July 5, 2013, the Chinese Government and the Government of Cote d'Ivoire signed a CFA 640,625,000 grant agreement for Phase 1 of the Gagnoa Hospital Technical Cooperation Project (captured via Project ID#92286). According to the Government of Côte d'Ivoire’s Aid Management Platform (AMP), Phase 1 was implemented between July 5, 2013 and July 4, 2015. The Chinese Government disbursed CFA 635,129,402.87 of grant funding in support of Phase 1 on June 30, 2014.   Then, in August 2016, the Chinese Government and the Government of Cote d'Ivoire signed letters of exchange regarding Phase 2 of the Gagnoa Hospital Technical Cooperation Project (captured via Project ID#66030). The monetary value of the grant commitment that supported Phase 2 is unknown. A Phase 2 completion ceremony was held on December 3, 2018.   Then, on October 17, 2019, the Chinese Government and the Government of Cote d'Ivoire signed a grant agreement for Phase 3 of the Gagnoa Hospital Technical Cooperation Project (captured via Project ID#87873). The monetary value of the grant commitment that supported Phase 3 is unknown.

project_name: Gov't provides anti-epidemic materials
description: On April 9, the Chinese government provided anti-epidemic materials to Côte d'Ivoire. The materials included 2,000 protective suits, 2,000 N95 type masks, 10,000 surgical masks, 500 temperature guns, 2,000 pairs of protective goggles, 10,000 pairs of disposable surgical gloves and 10,000 pairs of disposable overshoes. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation on April 17, 2020 in Abidjan, the economic capital of Côte d'Ivoire. Côte d'Ivoire's Minister of Health and Public Health, Avel Eugene Aka, and the Chinese Ambassador to Côte d'Ivoire, Wan Li, attended the ceremony.

project_name: Embassy in cote d’ivoire donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: On March 8, 2019, the Chinese Ambassador to Côte d’Ivoire, Tang Weibin, was invited to visit Saoundi Village in the suburb of Bouaké to inspect the village’s livelihood infrastructure. Ambassador Tang also visited the local primary school, medical office, youth home, and other public facilities accompanied by Diabat, and donated antimalarial drugs to the village medical office. The monetary value of the donation is not known.

project_name: Gov't donates supplies to anti-Malaria center
description: On February 11, 2020, the Chinese government provided supplies to the Antimalarial Center of the National Institute of Public Health at the National Institute of Public Health in Côte d'Ivoire. The donated supplies included equipment and consumables for malaria treatment and scientific research.   A handover ceremony was held for this donation. Wan Li, the Chinese Ambassador to Côte d'Ivoire, and the Minister of Health and Public Health of Côte d'Ivoire attended the ceremony and signed a handover certificate. The two officials also delivered speeches. The Director of the National Institute of Public Health of Côte d'Ivoire, representatives from the Côte d'Ivoire Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Finance, and Ministry of Higher Education also attended the ceremony. Following the ceremony, Ambassador Wan Li and the Minister of Health visited the anti-malaria center located at the National Institute of Public Health, which was built with Chinese aid (Project ID# 66116, 718).

project_name: Provides funds for nutrition center
description:
On 21 February 2014, the Chinese Ambassador attended the handover ceremony for a nutrition center (Centre de Nutrition suplémentaire-CNS or 辅助营养中心) in Korhogo, Cote d'Ivoire. The project was jointly managed by the Chinese Red Cross and Ivorian Red Cross. Financial assistance came from the Chinese Embassy and an unspecified local Ivorian company selected by the Ivorian Red Cross carried out the works. The project included renovating several buildings, new sanitary facilities such as toilets and other unspecified equipment. The project value and construction start date are unknown. 
 
 This project is part of the Sino-Africa People to People Friendship Action program (中非民间友好行动).

project_name: Provides grant for the provision of anti-Malaria assistance
description: On March 15, 2018, Tang Weibin, the ambassador to Côte d’Ivoire, and the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Côte d’Ivoire, Marcel Amon-Tano, signed two intergovernmental assistance agreements between China and Côte d’Ivoire. One of these agreements was an Exchange of Notes regarding the provision of 2.1 million RMB worth of material assistance by the Chinese government to the National Anti-malarial Research Center of Côte d’Ivoire. According to the exchange, the Chinese government will provide a batch of office and laboratory equipment to the Anti-malarial Center of Cote d’Ivoire, and actively discuss with the department to assist in the construction of a general hospital to effectively improve the medical and health conditions of the department.   The other agreement signed at this ceremony, an agricultural ETCA, is coded in Project ID#87822.  These agreements are the result of "One of the results of the implementation of the Ten Major Plans for China-Africa Cooperation”.

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria medicine
description:
In May 2006, the Chinese Government officially donated anti-malarial and other medication to the Cote d'Ivoire Ministry of Health. These drugs were produced by LIC Pharm, the Ivorian-Chinese laboratory (project #70380). The value and quantities of this donation are unknown. 
 
 The Ivorian-Chinese Pharmaceutical Laboratory is a joint venture established using a preferential loan from China Eximbank committed in 1996.

project_name: Provides masks to Bishop's Conference
description: On August 27, 2020, China provided 5,000 medical masks to the Bishop's Conference in Côte d'Ivoire. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony took place for this donation. Wan Li, the Chinese Ambassador to Côte d'Ivoire, and the Chairman of the Catholic Bishops' Conference of Côte d'Ivoire attended the ceremony.

project_name: Provides anti-epidemic materials
description: On August 17, 2020, China provided anti-epidemic materials to Côte d'Ivoire’s Ministry of Security and Citizen Protection. The donated materials included 3,000 disposable medical masks and 5 forehead thermometers. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.   A handover ceremony was held for this donation. Wan Li, the Chinese Ambassador to Côte d'Ivoire, and Lieutenant General Vagondo, the Minister of Security and Citizen Protection of Côte d'Ivoire, jointly attended the ceremony. Senior Colonel Song Feng, the Defense Attaché of the Embassy, ​​Brigadier General Bunet, the Foreign Affairs Advisor to the Minister of Security and Citizen Protection, and other officials also attended the event.

project_name: Gov't donates Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: The Chinese Government delivered 100,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Cote d'Ivoire on June 23, 2021. The donation from the People's Republic of China was received by the Ivorian Minister in charge of Health, Mr. Pierre N'gou Dimba, in the presence of the Chinese Ambassador to Côte d'Ivoire. Then, on September 17-18, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 818,400,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Cote d'Ivoire. The shipment arrived in Cote d'Ivoire at the Felix Houphouet Boigny airport in Abidjan.  Ivorian Minister of Health, Public Hygiene and Universal Disease Coverage M. Pierre N'gou DIMBA, and the UNICEF country representative received the donation.

project_name: Embassy provides masks
description: On July 10, 2020, the Chinese Embassy provided 14,000 medical masks to students and colleagues in 14 high schools in Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire. These masks will be used for COVID-19 prevention. The monetary value of this donation is unknown, as well as the names of most of the schools.  A handover ceremony took place for this donation at the Alassane Ouattara High School in Anyama, Côte d'Ivoire.

project_name: Gov't donates Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021, the Chinese Government donated approximately 1.3 million doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Djibouti. The Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Djibouti on March 18, 2021. Then, on November 30, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 1,100,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Djibouti.

project_name: Donates medicines and medical equipment to General Peltier Hospital
description: On 17 November, 2012, the Chinese government officially donated and delivered medicines and medical equipment to General Peltier Hospital in Djibouti. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donates medical supplies
description: On August 4th 2021, the Chinese government donated medical supplies to the Djibouti Ministry of Health. This donation includes ventilators, oxygen concentrators, and medical masks. The purpose of this donation was to help Djibouti fight against the pandemic.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Arta Hospital Construciton Project
description: In 2009, the Chinese government granted RMB 66 million (USD $8.2 million) grant the Government of Djibouti for the Arta Hospital Construction Project (other project names: 阿尔塔医院科研中心 or 中国援吉阿尔塔医院启 or Hôpital Régional d'Arta or La première pierre du nouvel hôpital régional d'Arta). This grant covered all construction and equipment costs.   The construction of this 128-bed hospital included four buildings, seven departments (including maternity, surgery, and cardiology), and an emergency room. On 2 April, 2009, Chinese and Djibouti officials signed the cooperation agreement for this project. China Jiangxi Corporation for International Economic & Technical Cooperation was the contractor responsible for project implementation. The survey and design unit of this project was Gansu Provincial Architectural Design and Research Institute, and the construction supervision unit was Shenyang Engineering Supervision Consulting Co., Ltd. The groundbreaking ceremony took place on 11 June 2009 and the official handover ceremony was held on 26 October 2011. It was opened for public use on 18 October 2012.

project_name: Donates medical equipment
description: On 3 March 2012, the Chinese Ambassador to Djibouti, Zhang Guoqing, presented a donation of 1.5 tons of medical equipment to Djibouti's Minister of Health. Most of the donated equipment was for the detection of malaria but also included a light microscope for DNA testing, a biological microscope, an incubator, and various materials to be used in hospitals.

project_name: Gov't donates via WHO for Covid-19 pandemic relief
description: In March 2020, Chinese government provides USD 350,000 to support WHO response to COVID-19 outbreak in Djibouti.  This project is captured in UNOCHA Financial Tracking Service as Flow ID #218735.

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: On 5 December 2007, the Chinese Ambassador Wang Xiaodu officially handed over anti-malaria medicine worth 12 million DJF (approximately 500,000 RMB) to the Djibouti Ministry of Health. The ceremony took place at the Central Purchasing Center for Essential Materials and Medicines headquarters in Djibouti.

project_name: Gov't donates anti-epidemic materials to National Women's Union
description: On August 5, 2020, the Chinese government donated anti-epidemic materials to the National Women’s Union of Djibouti. The wife of President Xi Jinping, Peng Liyuan, donated these materials on behalf of the Chinese government. These materials will be used for COVID-19 response and prevention efforts in Djibouti. The specific type, amount, and monetary value of this donation are unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. At the ceremony, China’s Ambassador to Djibouti, Zhuo Ruisheng, met with the National Women's Union of Djibouti Vice Chairman and handed over the materials. The Minister of Women and Family, representatives from the National Assembly, and the Minister of Health also attended the ceremony. Ambassador Zhuo and Vice Chairman Hasna signed the handover certificate on behalf of China and Djibouti respectively.

project_name: Donates medicine and medical equipment to General Peltier Hospital
description: On 22 December 2014, the Chinese government handed over a donation of medicines and medical equipment to General Peltier Hospital in Djibouti. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On May 11, 2020, the Chinese government donated anti-epidemic materials to Djibouti. These materials will be used to improve COVID-19 prevention efforts in Djibouti. The specific type, amount, and monetary value of this donation are unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the Djibouti-Ambouli International Airport. China’s Ambassador to Djibouti, Zhuo Ruisheng, the Foreign Minister of Djibouti, and the Health Minister of Djibouti attended the ceremony. Ambassador Zhuo and Foreign Minister Yusuf signed the handover certificate on behalf of their respective governments.

project_name: Donates medicines and medical equipment to General Peltier Hospital
description: On 29 October 2013, the Chinese government handed over a donation of medicines and medical equipment to General Peltier Hospital in Djibouti. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: China Merchants Group donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On April 7, 2020, the China Merchants Group donated anti-epidemic materials to Djibouti. The materials included medical masks, protective clothing, goggles, fluorescent quantitative PCR instruments, and visible infrared thermometers. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. China’s Ambassador to Djibouti, Zhuo Ruisheng, the Minister of Health of Djibouti, the Secretary-General of the Ministry of Health, the Chairman of the Port and Free Trade Zone Authority, and the Chief Representative of China Merchants Group in Djibouti attended the ceremony.

project_name: Donates medicines and medical equipment for Bright Journey Project
description: On 30 March 2016, the Chinese government officially handed over a donation of medical equipment and medicines to Djibouti. This donation is part of the "Guangmingxing" (光明行) or "Bright Journey" project initiated by China, which involved the provision of medical supplies and free cataract surgeries to 10 countries in Africa. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: International Liaison Department donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On September 7, 2020, the International Liaison Department of the Communist Party of China donated anti-epidemic materials to the People's League for Progress of Djibouti. The materials included medical masks and protective clothing. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the Jianmeng headquarters. Zhuo Ruisheng, the Chinese Ambassador to Djibouti, the National Secretary of the People's League, and the Minister of Social Affairs and Solidarity attended the ceremony. The National Secretaries of the Human League were also in attendance.

project_name: Donates for construction of kidney dialysis ward
description: On 29 March, 2007, China Jiangxi International Economic and Technical Cooperation Corporation and the Djibouti Ministry of Health signed a supplementary contract for the construction of a kidney dialysis ward at General Peltier hospital (other project names: Une salle de dialyse à l'Hôpital Général Peltier or Création d’une unité de dialyse à Djibouti or 吉布提肾透析病房项目). According to a report from the World Health Organization (source ID 112332 p. 39), China granted DJF 40 million for this project.   China Jiangxi International Economic and Technical Cooperation Corporation was the contractor responsible for implementation. The project was completed and handed over to the authorities on 17 January 2008.  China previously donated dialysis equipment to Djibouti in 2003 (#59170) and trained Djibouti healthcare workers for this new dialysis center in 2008 (#72358).

project_name: Trains healthcare workers in General Peltier Hospital
description: In 2007, the Chinese government granted funds for building a a kidney dialysis ward at General Peltier Hospital (project #59168). In order to help Djibouti healthcare workers, China also sent a 6-member team to train their counterparts in dialysis treatment, tools, and techniques. It is unclear when the training took place but AidData assumes it is complete.   China previously donated dialysis equipment to Djibouti in 2003 (project #59170).

project_name: Gov't donates Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021, the Chinese Government donated approximately 1.3 million doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Djibouti. The Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Djibouti on March 18, 2021. Then, on November 30, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 1,100,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Djibouti.

project_name: People's Liberation Army Navy organizes 'Bright Eyes Operation'
description: On November 28, 2019, China's Ministry of National Defense announced that the Chinese People's Liberation Army Support Base in Djibouti would host free cataract surgeries and medical treatment for the local Djiboutian population from December 1 to December 25, 2019, as part of the Bright Eyes Operation (Chinese: 光明行动). The project was organized by the People's Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) and the Ministry of Health of Djibouti. The medical team consisted of personnel from the PLA Support Base Hospital in Djibouti and the PLA Naval Military Medical University.  The opening ceremony was held on December 5, 2019, although the first diagnosis, screenings, and surgeries began on December 1 at the PLA Logistics Support Base, with the remainder set to occur at General Peltier Hospital. The medical team also interacted with local counterparts at General Peltier Hospital during the project. The project was completed on schedule on December 25. During the 25-day project period, the medical team performed 117 cataract surgeries for 103 local people between December 1 and December 25.

project_name: Donates for the Tadjourah Regional Hospital
description: On 15 January 2014, a Chinese government official signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) granting $16.5 million USD to Djibouti. An unspecified portion of this ETCA was used to finance the Tadjourah Regional Hospital Construction Project. According to Djib Live, the Chinese government contributed a total of $20 million USD for this project.   The hospital was supposed to include pediatric and radiology pavilions, a maternity ward, a surgical unit, emergency and dental care services for a capacity of 100 beds. Construction is yet to begin. In December 2019, the Chinese government dispatched a team of technical experts to Djibouti to conduct a feasibility study for this project. The implementing contractor is unknown.

project_name: Ministry of Health donates medicines and medical equipment
description: On 6 March 2017, the Chinese Ministry of Health donated medical equipment and medicine to the Djibouti Ministry of Health. The value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donates medicine and medical equipment to hospital
description: On 11 December 2011, the Chinese government held a ceremony to officially hand over a batch of medicines and medical equipment to General Peltier Hospital (吉贝尔蒂医院) in Djibouti. This donation is part of a Chinese effort to improve Djibouti's healthcare industry. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: Donates for kidney dialysis equipment
description: In 2003, the Chinese government provided an RMB 937,853 (or DJF 19,999,997) grant to the Government of Djibouti for the provision of kidney dialysis equipment. According to a document from the Djibouti Ministry of Finance, disbursements began in July 2003 and, as of 2005, 100% of the grant funds had been drawn down. The equipment was officially handed over to the Djibouti Ministry of Health on 8 October 2006.   Project #59168 captures the financing for the construction of the new dialysis center in which this equipment was implemented. The training of Djiboutian healthcare workers to use the new equipment is recorded in project #72358.

project_name: Gov't donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: On 27 August and 13 September 2006, Chinese and Djibouti government officials signed an Exchange of Letters agreement in which China committed to donating anti-malaria drugs to Djibouti.  On December 5, 2007, the handover ceremony for the anti-malarial drug project was held at the Djibouti Ministry of Health's Drug Procurement Center. The handover certificate was signed by the Chinese Ambassador Wang Xiaodu and the Secretary General of the Djibouti Ministry of Health, Sareh Banoi Taouha.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for automated and refrigerated vaccine storage
description: In April 2020, Sinovac Biotech Ltd., (SINOVAC) — a private Chinese biopharmaceutical company that focuses on the R&D, manufacturing, and commercialization of vaccines that protect against human infectious diseases — and Egypt’s Holding Company for Biological Products and Vaccines (VACSERA) signed a cooperation agreement for joint vaccine production. Under the terms of the agreement, the parties agreed that Sinovac vaccines would be locally manufactured in VACSERA’s factory in Egypt, with the final product carrying the VACSERA-Sinovac label. Then, in January 2021, Sinovac and VACSERA signed a cooperation agreement to establish a cold storage facility for vaccine storage and preservation in Egypt with approximately $33 million of grant funding for the Chinese Government. The parties subsequently signed a tripartite agreement with China State Construction Engineering Corporation Ltd. (CSCEC) for the Automated and Refrigerated Vaccine Storage Complex Construction Project.   The purpose of the project was to construct a fully-automated cold storage facility in VACSERA’s new factory complex in Giza’s 6th of October City. The cooling complex is built on area of 3,180 square meters, with a capacity to produce 100-150 million doses of vaccine annually. The new facility comprises two cooling rooms at a temperature of 2-8 degrees Celsius over an area of ​​​​661 square meters and nine meters high each. The rooms are designated for the storage of vaccines. It also includes three areas for receiving refrigerated trucks, loading and unloading shipments as well as a compartment for checking and recording shipment data, and a freezing room at a temperature of -20 degrees Celsius for storing the analysis materials. In addition, the complex includes a storage zone over an area of ​​290 square meters, and a height of 3.45 meters for storing the ready-to-pack bales at a temperature of 2-8 degrees. The storage zone is completely separated from the final product storage area. Each cold room is controlled via a dual cooling system; one for use and another as a backup, with the complex's control and monitoring room containing screens to monitor the vaccine transfer process and monitor temperatures as well as an alarm system and fire extinguishing system. The complex is managed automatically without any human intervention in using the warehouse management system WMS, which controls the storage of vaccines in a way that improves work efficiency and organizes storage spaces. CSCEC was the contractor responsible for project implementation. Construction began in April 2022 and the project completion (handover) ceremony took place on September 24, 2022.

project_name: Chinese People's Liberation Army donates Covid-19 vaccines
description: On September 1, 2021, the Chinese People's Liberation Army donated COVID-19 vaccines to the Egyptian army.  The Central Military Commission (CMC) of China approved the donation. The number of vaccines provided and the monetary value of the donation are unknown.

project_name: Gov't provides for Covid-19 support via WHO
description: In March 2020, Chinese government provides USD 486,270 to support WHO response to COVID-19 outbreak in Egypt.

project_name: China Family Planning Association donates to hospitals
description: On July 8, 2020, China Family Planning Association donated EGP 1.60 million (100,000 USD) to the Egyptian Family Planning Association and civil hospitals. The funding from the donation will be used to purchase COVID-19 prevention supplies. The supplies arrived in Cairo on July 20, 2020.

project_name: Donates laptops, school bags, and toys
description: On September 16th, 2009, the wife of the Chinese Ambassador to Egypt, Mrs. Wu Jingya, presented laptops, school bags, and toys, to the Children's Cancer Hospital Foundation in Cairo, Egypt, worth approximately EGP 300,000. According to the Chinese Embassy to Egypt, the donation of laptops was intended to assist hospital staff in serving patients. The donation was part of the Chinese Embassy's annual initiative to do charitable work during Ramadan.

project_name: Gov't provides Covid-19 supplies through OAFLAD
description: On July 29, 2020, a handover ceremony was held for the donation of anti-epidemic materials from the Chinese Government to the Assistant Minister of Health and Population of Egypt, Dr. Entissar Amer. Dr. Entissar Amer is the wife of Egyptian President Sisi. The Organization of African First Ladies for Development (OAFLAD) facilitated the handover.  The donation was made to help women, children, and teenagers in Egypt fight Covid-19. The value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donates Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021 and 2022, the Chinese Government donated approximately 12.6 million doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Egypt. The Chinese Government delivered 300,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Egypt on February 23, 2021. Then, in March 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 300,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Egypt.  The Chinese Government delivered an additional 2 million donated Sinovac COVID-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Egypt on November 1, 2021. project_name: Gov't donates Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine doses

The Chinese Government delivered 300,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Egypt on February 23, 2021. Then, in March 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 300,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Egypt.  The Chinese Government delivered an additional 2 million donated Sinovac COVID-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Egypt on November 1, 2021. Then, on September 24, 2022, the Chinese Government delivered 10 million donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Egypt.

project_name: Embassy donates protective clothing
description: On August 18, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Egypt donated 800 sets of protective clothing to the Egyptian Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research. The purpose of the donation was to combat the COVID-19 pandemic in Egypt.  The sets will be used to support front-line medical staff in hospitals affiliated with universities under the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research of Egypt. The value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: China State Construction Engineering Corporation donates Covid-19 aid
description: On April 21, 2020, a handover ceremony was held for the donation of Covid-19 aid from China State Construction Engineering Corporation to the Egyptian Government. The donation consisted of 10 invasive ICU ventilators, 500,000 medical surgical masks, 50,000 protective medical masks, 2,000 sets medical protective clothing, 2,000 isolation masks, and 6,000 pairs of medical disposables gloves. This donation is worth of 13 million Egyptian Pound.  The Egyptian government was represented by the Egyptian Minister of Housing Essam, the Deputy Minister of Housing Abbas, the Assistant Minister of Health of Egypt Mohammad, and the General Manager of Hospital Administration of the Ministry of Health Ashraf.

project_name: Embassy donates disposable medical masks
description: In September 2020, The Chinese Embassy in Egypt donated 100,000 disposable medical masks to the Egyptian Ministry of Education and Technical Education.   The purpose of the donation was to provide primary and secondary school students in Egypt with masks to aid the resumption of schooling in Egypt. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't provides Covid-19 aid
description: On May 10, 2020, a handover ceremony was held for the second batch of Covid-19 aid donated to Egypt by the Chinese government. The donation consisted of 10,000 N95 masks, 10,000 sets of protective clothing, and 70,000 nucleic acid testing reagents. In total, the donation weighed about 4.7 tons. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.  The Chinese Ambassador to Egypt facilitated the handover of the supplies. The Egyptian Assistant Minister of Health and Population General Wail Say and Mohammad Shoki, Commercial Counselor Han Bing of the Embassy, ​​and Spokesman Counselor Zhao Jixian attended the event.  The batches of materials are captured in the following projects: first batch (#94241), second batch (#94242) and third batch (#94256).

project_name: Tianjin University of Technical and Education donates mask
description: On July 28, 2020, Tianjin University of Technical and Education and Tianjin Transportation Vocational College in China donated 30,000 masks in total to Egypt’s Ain Shams University in Cairo. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donates Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses

The Chinese Government delivered 300,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Egypt on February 23, 2021. The Chinese Government delivered an additional 2 million donated Sinovac COVID-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Egypt on November 1, 2021. Then, on September 24, 2022, the Chinese Government delivered 10 million donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Egypt.

project_name: Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region in China donates Covid-19 supplies
description: On April 19, 2020, the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region donated Covid-19 supplies to the Egyptian Ministry of Higher Education & Scientific Research. The handover of the materials was conducted by the Chinese Embassy in Egypt, and Minister Khalid, the current Minister of Health and Population in Egypt, accepted the donation.   The donation consisted of 100,000 medical masks, 15,000 N95 masks, 1,000 items of protective clothing, and 1,200 new coronavirus nucleic acid detection reagents. The purpose of the donation was to help provide COVID-19 relief to students of the Confucius Institutes in Egypt. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Provides grants to WHO for health aid to Syrian refugees in Egypt
description: According to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) Financial Tracking Service (flow ID #154782), on 1 March 2017, the Chinese government donated $100,000 USD to the World Health Organization (WHO) for "addressing health consequences of conflict-affected displaced Syrians and refugees" in Egypt (UN project code is SRRP-17/MS/109731). This is part of the UNDP/UNHCR Regional Refugee & Resilience Plan (3RP) 2017-2018 which aims to assist Syrian refugees as well as host governments like Egypt trying to assist them.

project_name: Gov't donates Covid-19 aid
description: On May 16, 2020, the handover ceremony for the third batch of Covid-19 aid donated by the Chinese Government was held in Cairo, Egypt. The donation was estimated to cost 57 million Egyptian pounds (3.6 million USD). The donation consisted of 180,000 N95 masks, 1 million medical surgical masks, 90,000 pieces of medical protective clothing, 80,000 testing reagents, 70,000 disposable surgical gloves, and 1,000 thermometers. It is estimated that the batch exceeded 35 tons.  The batches of materials are captured in the following projects: first batch (#94241), second batch (#94242) and third batch (#94256).

project_name: Gov't donates Covid-19 aid
description: On April 16, 2020, a handover ceremony was held for the donation of Covid-19 aid to the Egypt government. The donation consisted of 20,000 N95 face masks, 10,000 articles of protective clothing, and 10,000 Covid-19 tests, and weighed over four tons. The donation was the first donation donated directly from the Chinese government to Egypt. The ceremony was held at the Cairo International Airport.  The batches of materials are captured in the following projects: first batch (#94241), second batch (#94242) and third batch (#94256).

project_name: Gov't provides grant to support Covid-19 response activities
description: On February 4, 2020, the Chinese Government provided a $2 million cash grant to the Government of Equatorial Guinea to supports its COVID-19 response activities.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for anti-Malaria center at Bata General Hospital
description: On June 7, 2009 the opening ceremony for a Chinese Government-funded anti-malaria center was held in Bata, Equatorial Guinea. The project is also referred to as a Diseases Prevention and Control Center. The anti-malaria center is housed within the General Hospital of Bata. The Zhejiang Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention implemented the project, and the Chinese Government provided equipment and medicines.

project_name: Gov't donates Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: On February 10, 2021, a shipment of 100,000 Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses donated by the Chinese Government to the Government of Equatorial Guinea arrived in Malabo, the capital of Equatorial Guinea. Then, on March 26, 2021, the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) of China delivered 20,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Armed Forces of Equatorial Guinea. Several weeks later, on April 19, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Equatorial Guinea.

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: According to a report on June 18, 2008, the Chinese Ambassador Xiaomin Yan donated anti-malaria drugs to the government of Equatorial Guinea on behalf of the Chinese government. The financial value of the aid is 1 million Chinese yuan.

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: On June 1, 2009, the Chinese government donated antimalarial drugs worth over 1 million yuan to the Equatorial Guinean government has arrived and held for a handover ceremony in Malabo..

project_name: China donates anti-Malaria drugs
description: On September 27, 2007, Chinese Ambassador to Equatorial Guinea Li Zhongliang and Equatorial Guinean Foreign Minister Jose Essono Micah signed an exchange of notes on the Chinese government's provision of 1 million yuan of antimalarial drugs to the Equatorial Guinean government.

project_name: Donates Covid-19 anti-epidemic supplies
description: In June 2020, China donated medical supplies to the Equatorial Guinea Ministry of Education as a part of a greater effort to fight against the COVID-19 pandemic. The donation included 1,000 masks and 150 infrared thermometers. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On June 8, 2020, a ceremony was held for the handover of anti-epidemic materials from the Government of China to the Government of Equatorial Guinea. The Chinese Ambassador to Equatorial Guinea, Qi Mei, and José Ntutumu Edu Nchama, the Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Equatorial Guinea, attended the ceremony. The supplies provided by the Chinese Government included testing kits, masks, gloves and protective suits.  This project is the second batch of anti-epidemic materials provided by the Chinese Government to the Government of Equatorial Guinea. The first batch of supplies was delivered on April 15, 2020 (see: project ID #92785).

project_name: Donates anti-Malaria medicine
description: On June 19, 2009, and February 4, 2010, China and Equatorial Guinea exchanged notes on the donation of anti-malaria drugs worth 1 million RMB. The medicine was handed over in August 2010.

project_name: Gov't donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On September 22, 2020, a ceremony was held for the handover of anti-epidemic materials from the Chinese Ambassador to Equatorial Guinea, Qi Mei on behalf of the to the Minister of State for National Security of Equatorial Guinea. The exact contents and value of this donation are unknown.

project_name: Gov't donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On April 15, 2020, a ceremony was held for the handover of anti-epidemic materials from the government of China to the government of Equatorial Guinea. The supplies provided by the Chinese Government included N95 masks, general medical masks, medical protective clothing, gloves, shoe covers, goggles and forehead temperature guns.  The materials arrived at the Malabo International Airport in Equatorial Guinea on April 15, 2020. The Chinese Ambassador to Equatorial Guinea, Qi Mei, and José Ntutumu Edu Nchama, the Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Equatorial Guinea, attended the ceremony. A second batch of materials was sent in July, and is captured in Project ID# 92784.

project_name: Gov't donates for anti-Malaria drugs
description: On October 18, 2007, the Chinese Government donated RMB 500,000 to Equatorial Guinea for antimalarial drugs). The donation came after a signing of letters exchanged in September 2007 concerning this donation of antimalarial drug funding and the provision of Chinese technical staff at Equatorial Guinea's Malabo TV Center (Project ID#32333).

project_name: Gov't donates anti-epidemic materials
description: On April 20, 2020, a ceremony was held for the handover anti-epidemic materials donated by the Chinese Government to the Government of Equatorial Guinea. The donation will help the Government of Equatorial Guinea fight COVID-19.

project_name: Donates medical equipment
description: On December 8, 2017, the Chinese Embassy in Equatorial Guinea handed over 720,000 RMB worth of medical equipment to the Equatorial Guinean government. Equatorial Guinea's Ministry of Health State Secretary Daniel Cima and Commercial Counselor Su Jianguo attended the ceremony and representatives of the two governments signed the transfer certificate. The donation included medicine, white coats, bed sheets and medical equipment. The handover ceremony was held in Malabo.

project_name: CSEC donate surgical masks
description: On July 1, 2020, the China State Construction Engineering Corporation (CSEC) donated 6,000 surgical masks to the Government of Equatorial Guinea. The donation goes towards combatting the spread of COVID-19 in Equatorial Guinea. The type and value of the masks are unknown.

project_name: Donates medicine and medical equipment to mMalabo Regional Hospital
description: On February 19, 2019, the 29th Chinese Medical team (project #62283) in Equatorial Guinea handed over 624,000 RMB worth of medicine and medical supplies to Equatorial Guinea's Malabo Regional Hospital. Chen Lei, the captain of the Chinese medical team, and President of the Malabo Regional Hospital Mba signed a certificate for the delivery of aid drugs. The donation included laparoscopic surgery- and cataract surgery-related medicine and equipment. The ceremony was attended by Counselor Su Jianguo.

project_name: Gov't donates Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: On February 10, 2021, a shipment of 100,000 Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses donated by the Chinese Government to the Government of Equatorial Guinea arrived in Malabo, the capital of Equatorial Guinea. Then, on March 26, 2021, the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) of China delivered 20,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Armed Forces of Equatorial Guinea. Several weeks later, on April 19, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Equatorial Guinea.

project_name: Gov't donates ambulances and anti-Malaria drugs
description: On March 12, 2015, the representatives of the Chinese Embassy in Equatorial Guinea and the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare of the Republic of Equatorial Guinea signed documents for the donation of two ambulances and antimalarial drugs to Equatorial Guinea. The donation was a continuation from the prior year, in which the Chinese had also donated two ambulances. The cost of the ambulances and antimalarial drugs is unclear.

project_name: Chinese People's Liberation Army donates Covid-19 vaccines
description: On February 10, 2021, a shipment of 100,000 Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses donated by the Chinese Government to the Government of Equatorial Guinea arrived in Malabo, the capital of Equatorial Guinea. Then, on March 26, 2021, the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) of China delivered 20,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Armed Forces of Equatorial Guinea. Several weeks later, on April 19, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Equatorial Guinea.

project_name: CNOOC funds construction of Community Health Center
description: In 2014, China National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC) funded the construction of a community health center in Equatorial Guinea. It is unclear when construction on the project began and was completed. The funding to the center is worth 100,000 USD.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for China-Equatorial Guinea Friendship Hospital
description: In January 2019, the Chinese Government and the Government of Equatorial Guinea signed an exchange of notes on the China-Equatorial Guinea Friendship Hospital Construction Project. Then, on October 17, 2019, Deputy Director of the Economic Cooperation Bureau of China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) Ai Yinfang and Equatorial Guinea’s Minister of Foreign Affairs Oyono signed an implementation agreement for the China-Equatorial Guinea Friendship Hospital Construction Project. A supplementary project implementation agreement was signed on October 17, 2020. The monetary value of the MOFCOM grant commitment for the China-Equatorial Guinea Friendship Hospital Construction Project is unknown.   The purpose of the project is to construct a 100-bed hospital — that occupies a surface area of 5,700 m² — on the outskirts of the city of Niefang and decongest health centers in the city of Bata. More specifically, the project involves the construction of an outpatient and emergency building, a medical technology building, a general inpatient building, an infectious disease building, a logistics building, a sewage treatment station, a garbage treatment station, and supporting infrastructure. The hospital is expected to include clinical departments for obstetrics and gynecology, pediatrics, internal medicine, surgery, medical examination, emergency services, intensive care, and X-ray and laboratory services.   Sinohydro Bureau 6 Co. Ltd. is the contractor responsible for implementation. It was selected by MOFCOM (through a bidding process) on August 4, 2020. Project implementation officially launched on August 26, 2020. Then, a formal foundation stone laying ceremony took place on November 30, 2020. Then, on December 2, 2021, the project successfully passed mid-term acceptance. On October 27, 2021, the hospital was renamed the 'China-Equatorial Guinea Friendship Hospital'. Then, on March 8, 2022, the Chinese Ambassador to Equatorial Guinea visited the project site and note that the COVID-19 pandemic had led to implementation delays. The project was originally expected to reach completion by July 2022. It was ultimately completed in December 2022.

project_name: Donates medicine and medical equipment
description: On April 25th 2019, the donation ceremony of medicine and medical equipment from China to Eritrea was held in Asmara, Eritrea. This ceremony was held by the Chinese Embassy in Eritrea and the Ministry of Health of Eritrea. The handover certificate for the donation was signed by Chinese Ambassador to Eritrea Yang Ziqang and Eritrean Minister of Health Amina Nurhussien. The value of this donation is unknown. This project is completed.

project_name: Donates medical equipment
description: On June 17th 2021, according to the website of Economic and Commercial Office of the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in the State of Eritrea, Chinese Ambassador to Eritrea Cai Ge and Eritrean Minister of Health Amina jointly attended the ceremony for the donation of medical equipment from China to Eritrea and signed the handover certificate on behalf of the two governments respectively. Economic and Commercial Counsellor Yu Jinming, the 14th batch of medical aid to Eritrea, Zhao Yanbing and key officials from the Ministry of Health of Eritrea attended the ceremony.  The amount or the value of this donation is not specified. This donation fully reflects the friendship of the Chinese people to the Eritrean people, and helps to the development of medical and health care in Eritrea.

project_name: Gov't provides loan for Orotta Referral Hospital project
description: In 2000, the Chinese Government provided an RMB 80 million (equal to about $10 million) interest-free loan to the Government of Eritrea for the Orotta Referral Hospital Construction Project. This project involved the construction of a 200-bed hospital in the capital city of Asmara in an area that occupies 10,000 square meters. About 100 Chinese workers were employed to support this project. China Tianjin International Economic and Technical Cooperation Group Corporation was the implementing contractor. Construction began in October 2000 and the project was officially handed over to the Eritrean authorities on May 31, 2003.  In 2009, the Chinese Government provided a $5 million grant for the renovation and expansion of this hospital (see Project #30533).

project_name: Sponsors public health training
description: From September 6, 2019 to September 26, 2019, the "2019 Overseas Training Program on Public Health Aid" was held in Asmara, Eritrea. The training was organized by China Red Cross, which had representatives attend some parts of the course. 40 Eritrean trainees attended the course. This course was one of ten trainings sponsored by China in Eritrea in 2019 (projects #87507, 87506, 87504, 87401, 87500, and 87499)

project_name: Donates medicine and medical equipment
description: On April 24th 2018, the Chinese Embassy in Eritrea and the Eritrean Ministry of Health jointly held a donation ceremony for medical equipment in Asmara, Eritrea. The medicines and medical equipment that China donated covers Pediatrics, Obstetrics and Gynecology, Critical care, Emergency and trauma medicine, Cardiovascular disease, Gastroenterology, Neurosurgery, Ophthalmology, general surgery, Urology, Thoracic Surgery, Orthopedics, Spine Surgery, Anesthesiology, Acupuncture and Physiotherapy, Chinese Medicine, etc. Additionally, based on the need of the hospital, the Chinese medical aid team also donated some urgently needed medicines and equipment. The Chinese Ambassador to Eritrea, Yang Zigang, and the Eritrean Minister of Health Amina Nurhussein, signed the handover certificate of this donation. The value of this donation is unknown. This donation is completed.

project_name: Gov't provides grant for Orotta Referral Hospital project
description: On December 24, 2009, the Chinese Government signed an exchange of letters with the Government of Eritrea providing a $5 million grant for the Orotta Referral Hospital Renovation and Expansion Project. Then, on December 28, 2010, the Eritrean Ministry of Health and Tianjin International Economic and Technical Cooperation Group Corporation signed an agreement related to the implementation of this project. The agreement was signed by Amna Nurhusein and Li Liliansheng, the Chinese Ambassador to Eritrea.   This project involved the renovation and expansion of the Orotta Referral Hospital in Asmara, which is also known as Mekane Hiwot Hospital or مستشفى ميكان هيوت. More specifically, it involved the construction of a cardiac and neurology center, the construction of a physiotherapy and oxygen production facility, the construction of an underground pond with the capacity of 500 cubic meters of water, and the repair of water pipelines and other facilities. Tianjin International Economic and Technical Cooperation Group Corporation was the contractor responsible for implementation. This project commenced on December 28, 2010 and it was completed on October 14, 2014. The Chinese Government also provided an RMB 80 million interest-free loan for the original construction of this hospital (captured in Project ID#493).

project_name: Gov't donates through the International Organization for Migration
description: In May 2020, Chinese government provides USD 52,790 as Emergency Shelter Support for Displaced Persons in Ethiopia.  This project is captured in UNOCHA Financial Tracking Service as Flow ID #219156.

project_name: Gov't donates medical supplies to improve newborn health
description: On June 11, 2021 the China International Development Cooperation Agency (CIDCA) handed over medical supplies to the Ministry of Health procured by UNICEF to improve the quality of health care provided to newborn babies in two zones of Tigray and SNNPR (Southern Nations, Nationalities, and People's Regions) regions in Ethiopia. The supplies handed over to the Ministry include continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) bubbles with canula for newborn babies, hand operated neonate resuscitators, oxygen concentrators, neonatal room thermometers, pulse oximeters, midwifery kit/equipment, delivery beds, and other essential supplies crucial for the survival of newborns.  The medical supplies are part of the project entitled 'Improving the quality of health care provided to newborn babies in two zones of Tigray and SNNP regions, Ethiopia,' launched in March 2020. It covers 61 health centres, 229 health posts, and six primary hospitals in the two regions. An estimated 94,000 pregnant women and newborn babies are expected to benefit from the project.

project_name: Gov't donates Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021 and 2022, the Chinese Government and the Chinese Red Cross Society donated approximately 14 million doses of Sinopharm and Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Ethiopia and the Ethiopian Red Cross Society. The Chinese Government delivered 300,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Ethiopia on March 29, 2021 (see project ID#95864). Then, on May 13, 2021, China's Ministry of Defense delivered 100,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to Ethiopia's Ministry of Defense (see project ID#95866). Approximately one month later, on June 19, 2021, the Chinese Red Cross Society delivered 100,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Ethiopian Red Cross Society (see project ID#95868). Two months later, on August 19, 2021, China's Ministry of Defense delivered an additional 200,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to Ethiopia's Ministry of Defense (see project ID#95869).  On August 23, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 300,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Ethiopia’s Ministry of Health (see project ID#95944). Approximately one month later, on October 24, 2021, Chinese Government delivered 800,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Ethiopia’s Ministry of Health (see project ID#95946). Then, in December 2021, the Chinese Government announced that it had donated 2 million additional doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Ethiopia via COVID-19 Vaccines Global Access (COVAX) — a worldwide initiative aimed at equitable access to COVID-19 vaccines directed by the GAVI vaccine alliance, the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations, the World Health Organization, and UNICEF (see project ID#95947). Then, on January 20, 2022, the Chinese Government delivered 2.2 million donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Ethiopia (see project ID#96127). The Chinese Government delivered an additional 10 million donated Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Ethiopia’s Ministry of Health on June 27, 2022 (see project ID#96143). According to the Chinese Government, its cumulative donations of Covid-19 vaccine doses to Ethiopia amounted to 500,000 doses as of June 2021, 1.8 million doses as of October 2021, 5 million doses as of December 2021, 7 million doses as of January 2022, 9.7 million doses as of March 2022, and 14 million doses as of June 2022.

project_name: Gov't donates for China-Ethiopia Malaria prevention and treatment center
description: According to the Government of Ethiopia’s Aid Management Platform (AMP), the Chinese Government and the Government of Ethiopia signed an ETB 4,262,307 grant agreement for the China-Ethiopia Malaria Prevention and Treatment Center Establishment Project on July 17, 2008. The purpose of this project was to construct and equip an anti-malaria center in Adama (formerly known as Nazareth or Nazrēt) within the Oromyia Region. An opening ceremony for the anti-malaria center took place on December 26, 2008. Then, the Chinese Government dispatched a 4-person team to the center from June 27, 2009 to August 10, 2009 to install the donated equipment and training local anti-malarial staff.

project_name: Gov't donates Covid-19 medical supplies
description: On May 25, 2021, Chinese government donated medical supplies and equipment to the Tigray interim administration in support of efforts to stop the spread of coronavirus in Tigray region in Ethiopia. The donation included 7 ventilators, 2 high-flow heated respiratory humidifiers, 36,000 masks, and 1,500 pieces of personal protective equipment (PPE). It was handed over to the Chief Executive of the Interim administration of the Tigray region, Dr. Abreham Belay.

project_name: Builds 3 new medical centers at Tirunesh-Beijing Hospital
description: In December 2016, the Chinese and Ethiopian governments signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for constructing a trauma center and nursing unit at Tirunesh-Beijing Hospital. The completion of the additions to the hospital were inaugurated on August 1, 2017, though it is unclear when construction on them began. Altogether, the China Trauma Center, the China Maternal and Child Health Center and the China Telepathology Consultation Center were added on to Tirunesh-Beijing Hospital. project_name: CCECC, Dongguan and Chinese companies donate anti-epidemic supplies
