project_name: CIDCA donates to neonatal and maternal health services
description: Around April 2, 2020, the China International Development Cooperation Agency (CIDCA) provided a $1 million grant to Ethiopia for the purpose of neonatal and maternal health care. UNICEF helped negotiate the grant and will help the Ethiopian Ministry of Health with organizing and distributing the money.   The money is to go to improving newborn intensive care units (ICU), integrated management of newborn and childhood illnesses, community-based newborn care, and clinical mentorship. The project will cover health care in 49 health centers, 219 health posts, and six primary hospitals in Ethiopia, with a focus on underserved regions. The grant will help an estimated 94,000 pregnant women and newborns.  This grant is a part of a larger $8 million USD grant from CIDCA to improve maternal and neonatal services in 8 African countries.

project_name: Gov't donates Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021 and 2022, the Chinese Government and the Chinese Red Cross Society donated approximately 14 million doses of Sinopharm and Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Ethiopia and the Ethiopian Red Cross Society. The Chinese Government delivered 300,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Ethiopia on March 29, 2021 (see project ID#95864). Then, on May 13, 2021, China's Ministry of Defense delivered 100,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to Ethiopia's Ministry of Defense (see project ID#95866). Approximately one month later, on June 19, 2021, the Chinese Red Cross Society delivered 100,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Ethiopian Red Cross Society (see project ID#95868). Approximately one month later, on October 24, 2021, Chinese Government delivered 800,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Ethiopia’s Ministry of Health (see project ID#95946). project_name: Gov't provides grant for the Tirunesh-Beijing Hospital Project
description: In November 2006, at the first Forum on China-Africa Cooperation, the Chinese Government agreed to support the construction of 30 hospitals across Africa, one of which included the Tirunesh-Beijing Ethio-China Friendship Hospital (Chinese name: 提露内丝-北京医院). Then, according to the Government of Ethiopia’s Aid Management Platform (AMP), the Chinese Government issued an RMB 80 million (ETB 91,924,840) grant for Phase 1 of the Tirunesh-Beijing Hospital Project on September 26, 2008.    The project’s first phase included the construction of an outpatient building, and an in-patient building with 100 patient beds. It also involved the provision of modern and high-tech medical equipment. A team of 15 Chinese medical professionals was also assigned to the hospital to work alongside Ethiopian professionals. The hospital is located in Akaki, around 25 km south of the country's capital, Addis Ababa. The state-of-art hospital was named after Tirunesh Dibaba, an Ethiopian female athlete who won two gold medals at the 2008 Beijing Olympics. On July 29, 2009, the signing ceremony for the contract for the implementation of Phase 1 of the Tirunesh-Beijing Ethio-China Friendship Hospital was held in the Ministry of Health of Ethiopia. A representative of China Jiangxi International Economic and Technical Cooperation Corporation and Ethiopia’s Minister of State of the Ministry of Health of the Ethiopian Ministry of Health, Kebeide, signed the implementation contract. A foundation stone laying ceremony was held on June 6, 2009. Then, a formal kick-off ceremony for the project was held on October 23, 2009. Phase 1 was completed and officially handed over to the Ethiopian Government on November 16, 2011. The hospital was put into full operation on March 4, 2016.

He also witnessed the donation of medicine and equipment to this hospital by the Chinese Embassy in Gambia. During the President Barrow's visit, the medical team treated more than 400 local patients and donated 1 million dalasis worth of medicines and medical equipment to the Bansang Hospital.  The day before China donated 700,000 dalasis worth of medical items and equipment to the Basse Health Center, this is captured in project #86791.

project_name: Gov't donates medical equipment to hospital
description: On December 13, 2017, the Chinese Government officially delivered medical equipment to the Government of The Gambia at a handover ceremony held at the Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital in Banjul. The Chinese government donated surgical instruments, baby health equipment and tablet medicines to the Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital. According to the Health Commission of Liaoning Province, the donation had a value of RMB 700,000. Chinese Ambassador to the Gambia Zhang Jiming attended the handover ceremony.

project_name: Unveiled and donated to gynecology endoscopy center
description: On June 14th, 2019, the unveiling ceremony was held for the Zhonggang Cooperation Gynecology Endoscopy Center (中冈合作妇科内镜中心) in Banjul, Gambia at the Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital (EFSTH). In the Chinese Embassy article, it was stated that the Chinese medical staff working at the EFSTH began a counterpart support cooperation project. This project aided the building of the obstetrics and gynecology clinic, where the staff demonstrated medical teachings and gave training. Alongside this, important medical equipment was donated to the clinic multiple times. In particular, a second batch of equipment was donated to the hospital at the ceremony, including two world class color Doppler Ultrasound equipment to the EFSTH, coupled with a three month course for nineteen local radiologist; where these students were trained on how to maintain CT and MRI scans in the country's referral hospital. At the ceremony, Ambassador Ma Jianchun and Minister Samat signed the certificate of medical device handover and jointly unveiled the China-Guangzhou Cooperation Gynecological Endoscopy Center.  The exact source of Chinese financing and the amount is not known. The commitment date and start date of the project isn't known. This project is completed.

project_name: Gov't donates a batch of Covid-19 supplies
description: On March 12, 2021, the handover ceremony of the anti-epidemic materials aided by the Chinese government to Gambia was held in Banjul. The donation included 20,000 medical protective face masks, 100 forehead thermometers, 190 non-invasive ventilators, 50 oxygen concentrators and related accessories. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  Ambassador Ma Jianchun and Gambia Minister of Health Samat attended the ceremony and delivered speeches. Mr. Jeta, Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Health of Ganga, attended the meeting. Ambassador Ma Jianchun reviewed the history of China and Gambia fighting side by side to fight against the epidemic in the past year, and spoke positively of the series of cooperation between China and Gambia in the field of medical and health care. results. Ambassador Ma said that the Chinese government will continue to firmly support Gambia in its fight against the epidemic, and actively provide assistance for African countries to recover their economies in the post-epidemic era.

project_name: Donates medical suppliesMinistry of Health
description: On July 28, 2021, China donated medical supplies worth GMD 31 million to Gambia's Ministry of Health through Chinese government funding. The medical supplies included 400,000 gloves, maternal and newborn care supplies, hygiene products, as well as other medical supplies. The purpose of this donation was to provide support for Gambia in response to COVID-19. This donation was organized and handed over by the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), and was done through the South-South Cooperation Fund organized by China.

project_name: Embassy donates sewing machines to the First Lady
description: On July 24, 2020, the Chinese embassy to the Gambia donated 15 electric sewing machines to the office of the First Lady of the Gambia, Lady Fatoumatta Bah-Barrow. According to the Chinese ambassador, the sewing machines were intended to complement Gambia's domestic face mask production.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation and a concurrent donation of medical supplies (see project #92803) at the Presidential Palace of Gambia. China’s Ambassador to China, the First Lady of Gambia, and other officials attended the ceremony.

project_name: Donates medical supplies for 'Brightness Action'
description: On January 23rd, 2019, the China "Brightness Action" Campaign opening ceremony occurred at the Sheikh Zayed Regional Eye Care Center in Kanifing, Gambia. At the ceremony, RMB 2.1 million worth of medical equipment was donated to the Gambian government from China. As part of this program, China brought together 12 experts who will be conducting a 10-day free cataract surgery at the Regional Eye Care Center in Kanifing (project #67569). Additionally, patients who had regained eyesight had their eye patches removed at the ceremony. This is part of a larger "Brightness Action" Campaign held in many countries.

project_name: Embassy assists the AIDS National Parade Publicity Campaign
description: In December of 2018, the Chinese Embassy in the Gambia assisted the AIDS National Parade Publicity Campaign for World AIDS Day in Gambia. This event was organized by the Gambian First Lady's Office in December 2018, and was an AIDS prevention publicity event organized for World AIDS Day. On December 22, 2018, the closing ceremony of this project in Gambia was held. This ceremony was attended by Chinese Ambassador to the Gambia Ma Jianchun, the Gambia's First Lady Fatoumatta Bah Barrow, and the Executive Director of the National AIDS Prevention and Control Secretariat Ba Jie.  During the Beijing Summit earlier in 2018, the China-Africa AIDS Prevention and Control Conference was held. At this meeting, China's three-year "China-Africa Youth AIDS Prevention and Community Health Promotion Project" through joint promotion of publicity and advocacy, health education, etc., was announced. This AIDS prevention publicity campaign is likely part of this larger China-Africa AIDS prevention campaign.  The amount of funding for this project is unclear. This project is completed.

project_name: Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region provides medical supplies
description: On July 24, 2020, the government of the Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region of China donated medical supplies to the Gambian government. According to The Voice News, the donation comprised 10,000 medical masks, 1,000 N95 respiratory masks, 100 protective suits, 100 safety goggles, and 79 infrared thermometers. The Guangxi Autonomous region has a sister city relationship with Banjul, capital of the Gambia.   A handover ceremony was held for this donation and a concurrent donation of sewing machines (see Project ID #94645) at the Presidential Palace of Gambia. China’s Ambassador to China, Ma Jianchun, the First Lady of Gambia, Lady Fatoumatta Bah-Barrow, and other officials attended the ceremony. The materials were distributed to the Gambia Nurses and Midwives association for COVID-19 prevention efforts.

project_name: Donates medical equipment to the Basse Health Center
description: On November 25, 2019, President Barrow of Gambia presided over the donation of medical items, equipment, and other consumables worth 700,000 dalasi from the People’s Republic of China to the Basse Health Center in Gambia.  The day after this, China donated 1 million dalasi worth of medical equipment to the Bansang Hospital (captured in project #86182).

project_name: Gov't provides sanitation supplies to Kanifing Municipal Council
description: On November 12, 2020, the Chinese Embassy provided sanitation supplies to the municipal council of Kanifing in Gambia. The supplies included personal protective equipment, hand washing buckets, disinfectant, and disinfectant sprayers. These materials were to be used to support primary and secondary schools that resumed in-person classes during the COVID-19 pandemic. The exact monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. Ma Jianchun, China’s Ambassador to Gambia, and Lord Mayor Talib Ahmed Bensouda of Kanifing attended the donation ceremony. During the ceremony, Mayor Bensouda spoke highly of the cooperation between Gambia and China and thanked China for the donation.

project_name: Gov't donates Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine
description: On December 1, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of The Gambia.  China’s Ambassador to The Gambia, Ma Jianchun, and Gambia Foreign Affairs Minister, Hon. Mamadou Tangara, went to Banjul International Airport to receive the vaccines and attend the handover ceremony.

project_name: Nanning donates medical supplies
description: Sometime between March to April 2020, Nanning Municipal Government donated medical supplies to the city of Banjul, Gambia.

project_name: Gov't provides anti-epidemic supplies
description: On April 20, 2020, the Chinese government provided a batch of anti-epidemic supplies to Gambia. The supplies included 2,000 medical N95 masks, 10,000 ordinary medical masks, 2,000 pieces of medical protective clothing, 2,000 medical isolation goggles, 10,000 disposable medical gloves, 10,000 disposable medical shoe covers, and 500 forehead temperature guns.   A handover ceremony was held for this donation at Banjul International Airport where the supplies were delivered. China’s Ambassador to Gambia, Ma Jianchun, Gambia's Foreign Minister, Gambia’s Health Minister, and other representatives attended the ceremony at the airport. Both Ambassador Ma Jianchun and the Gambian Foreign Minister delivered speeches at the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't provides medical supplies
description: On June 19, 2020, the Chinese government donated medical supplies to the office of the First Lady of the Gambia. These supplies will be used for epidemic prevention in the Gambia. The donation included face masks and forehead thermometers.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the Gambia Presidential Palace. Present at the ceremony were Chinese Ambassador Ma Jianchun, First Lady Fatoumatta Bah-Barrow, Foreign Minister Dr. Mamadou Tangara, and Minister of Basic and Secondary Education Claudia Cole. Following the handover of the supplies from the ambassador to the First Lady, the First Lady passed on the supplies to the Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education for classroom use as local primary and secondary schools planned to return to in-person classes.

project_name: Embassy provides equipment to Ministry of Health
description: On March 10, 2020, the Chinese Embassy provided equipment to the Gambia Ministry of Health. The equipment included two Foton View CS2 ambulances, medicine, and medical items. These supplies are valued at over D10 million and will be part of Gambia’s COVID-19 response and prevention.  The two ambulances will be used in two hospitals in Banjul to assist in ambulance work in remote communities.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the Central Medical Store in Kotu, Gambia. China’s Ambassador to Gambia, Ma Jianchun, Modou Njie, the Director of Health Promotion and Education at the Ministry of Health, Modou Lamin Jaiteh, the Permanent Secretary, Ousman Sillah, the Chairperson of the National Assembly Select Committee on Health, and Dr. Ahmadou Lamin Samateh, the Minister of Health of Gambia, attended the ceremony and delivered speeches.

project_name: Gov't donates to health support
description: In April 2021, Chinese government donates USD 78,750 to provide health assistance to Sao Tome and Principe and Gambia in West and Central Africa Region for COVID-19 pandemic response.

project_name: Gov't hosted training on med. PLAnts for Ghanain officials
description: From June 23, 2010 to July 23, 2010, the Chinese Government organized a seminar on medical plants for officials from 15 developing countries (including Ghana) in Beijing.

project_name: Embassy donated PPE to GCAA
description: On June 19, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Ghana donated personal protective equipment (PPE), including 10,000 disposable medical face masks, 10 infrared thermometers, 400 bottles of hand sanitizer, and a thermal temperature scanner to the Ghana Civil Aviation Authority (GCAA). This donation is intended to aid Ghana's continued fight against COVID-19.

project_name: South-South Coop fund donated to unicef for Covid-19 relief
description: On February 26, 2021, China donated $1 million USD from the South-South Cooperation Assistance Fund to a UNICEF program that will help Ghana respond the COVID-19 pandemic. This money will be used to help the government of Ghana improve newborn care and child health, prevent, detect and treat severe acute malnutrition. The COVID-19 pandemic had worsened already tenuous conditions for child mortality, with the MICS (Multiple Indicators Cluster Survey) estimating between 27 and 56 deaths per 1000 live births respectively.  Through this grant, UNICEF will continue supporting the Government of Ghana with the provision of nutrition supplies such as iron-folic tablets, vitamin A supplements, weighing scales and height boards, ready-to-use therapeutic foods, therapeutic milk and essential medicine and neonatal intensive care equipment to help newborns survive and thrive.

project_name: Hunan construction engineering group donated anti-epidemic supplies
description: On March 28, 2020, Hunan Construction Engineering Group donated anti-epidemic medical supplies to five countries, including Ghana. The donation consisted of 10,000 N95 masks, 100,000 disposable medical masks, and 30,000 medical gloves intended to help fight the COVID-19 pandemic.  The five countries among which the donation was split included Ghana, Senegal, Bangladesh, Niger, and Burundi.

project_name: Gov't donated batch of Anti-Malarial drugs
description: On June 18, 2006, the Chinese Government and the Government of Ghana signed an agreement to donate a batch of anti-malarial drugs worth RMB 2 million to a newly-established malaria center at Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital (see Project ID#1745). The drugs were manufactured by Chinese pharmaceutical companies Huali Ketai Pharmaceutical and Guilin South Pharmaceutical and were shipped to Ghana in May 2007. They were officially delivered and handed over to the Ghanaian authorities on September 5, 2007.

project_name: Fujian Municipal Gov't donated supplies to friendship association
description: On August 18, 2020, Fujian Municipal Government donated medical supplies to the Ghana-China Friendship Association. The purpose of this donation was to help Ghana in fighting against the COVID-19 pandemic.

project_name: Gov't donated med. equipment to Korle-Bu teaching hospital
description: On June 22, 2011, the 1st Chinese medical assistance team to Ghana donated some medical equipment worth 870,000 RMB to Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital in Accra. This is the second time the medical team has donated medical supplies since November 2010. The equipments include Insight Monitors, Syringe Pumps, Pump of Infusions, Recording Page for ECG, Spine Surgery Instrument Monitor, and General Surgery Instruments. The rest are Foreign Body Forceps, Nephrocope, Pneumatic Shock Type and Medical Injection Pump. The departments to benefit are Medical, Child Health, Physiotherapy, Anesthesia, Neurology and Urology.

project_name: Embassy donated supplies to the Muslim association
description: On April 17, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Ghana donated supplies to the Office of the National Chief Imam of Ghana (ONCI). The supplies, which was comprised of 2,000 bags of rice, 3,000 liters of cooking oil, and 6,000 face masks (and worth about GH¢110,000), was to be distributed to the various Muslim communities in Accra to alleviate the food shortage of some poor groups due to COVID-19, the restriction of movement, and also for Ramadan.

project_name: Gov't sign a cooperation agreement for maternal & child health project
description: On September 1, 2018 during Ghanaian President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo's state visit to China, he and Chinese President Xi Jinping signed a cooperation agreement to carry out a maternal and child health project. Following the signing, Ghana's Deputy Minister of Health Alexander K. Abban had selected a 25-member Ministerial Steering Committee to operationalize the agreement signing and fashion out strategies for the project.   On July 20, 2019, China and Ghana started implementing the project, and also inaugurated the 25-member committee.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for Malaria Prophylactic Therapeutic demo project
description: On June 18, 2006, the Chinese Government and the Government of Ghana signed a grant agreement for the establishment of a center that could perform anti-malarial treatments at the Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital in Accra. The monetary value of this grant commitment is unknown. This project was officially completed and handed over to the Ghanaian authorities on October 27, 2009 at a ceremony that held at the Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital. The Chinese Government also donated a batch of anti-malarial drugs worth RMB 2 million to the center (captured in Project ID #1750).   This project is linked to project #1741, which captures a $66 million low-interest loan to fund a telecommunications upgrade and other projects in the country, including expansion and upgrading of the telecommunication network (#43357), and the construction of a primary school, and a malaria center (this project).

project_name: Gov't donated med. equipment to Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital
description: On August 1, 2012, the 2nd medical assistance team to Ghana donated some medical equipment worth 300,000 USD to Karle-Bu Teaching Hospital. This is the 3rd time the Chinese medical teams have donated to the hospital.  The second medical team arrived on December 21, 2011 (captured in #35239).

project_name: Embassy donated mosquito nets to infant Malaria prevention foundation
description: On December 6, 2006, Chinese Ambassador to Ghana Zhang Keyuan donated a large quantity of mosquito nets to the Infant Malaria Prevention Foundation, a local NGO in Accra. The nets are to be distributed to the poor at no cost.

project_name: Embassy donated supplies to Ministry of Defense for Covid relief
description: On April 20, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Ghana donated medical supplies to Ghana's Ministry of Defense for its fight against the COVID-19 pandemic. This donation includes one accurate temperature measurement thermal device and 6000 face masks, valued at 70,000 Cedis.

project_name: Embassy & expatriate community donate PPE supplies to hospital
description: On June 18, 2020, the Embassy in Ghana and the expatriate community in Ghana donated personal protective equipment (PPE) supplies worth GHS 480,000 to the University of Ghana Medical Center Hospital. This donation included 15 ventilators, 20,000 medical masks, 1,600 N95 masks, 120 protective suits, 60 face shields, 100 medical googles, in addition to 150 cartons of milk, 30 cartons of cocoa powder, 75 cartons of cereal, and other epidemic prevention and living materials to cater for the nutritional needs of the patients.

project_name: PowerChina donated PPE Ministry of Roads & Highways
description: On April 14, 2020, on behalf of its parent organization, the Power Construction Corporation of China (POWERCHINA), PowerChina International Group Limited (PCIGL) donated personal protective equipment (PPE) supplies to Ghana's Ministry of Roads and Highways. The total value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donated PPE to the gov't of Ghana for Covid-19 relief
description: On September 17, 2020, the Chinese Government donated personal protective equipment (PPE) supplies to the Government of Ghana after the two nations signed the "Certificate of Handover between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Republic of Ghana on Medical Supplies Assistance Project" on the same day. This is the second batch of medical supplies from the Chinese Government. The medical supplies presented through Ghana's health ministry included 20,000 N95 protective face masks, 350,000 surgical masks, 10,000 disposable coveralls, 15,000 medical goggles, 15,000 pair of disposable nitrile gloves, and 3,000 pair of disposable shoe covers. The value of this donation are not specified, but the purpose of this donation is to help Ghana in fighting against the pandemic.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for Dangme East District Hospital const. project
description: In 2000, the Chinese Government agreed to provide an $8 million grant for the Dangme East District Hospital Construction Project. This project involved the construction of a 60-bed hospital (with a Consulting Room, Obstetrics and Gynecology Department, Children Health Center) that is located in Ada, about 100 km east of Accra. Construction began in January 2000. The project was completed in April 2002 and the hospital is now in operation. It reportedly treats 5000 patients a year.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for Teshie General Hospital construction project
description: On January 5, 2009, the Chinese Government provided a $7.28 million grant to the Government of Ghana for for Teshie General Hospital Construction project. The total cost of the project was $13 million, with the additional funding coming from the Government of Ghana. This project involved the construction of a 100-bed comprehensive hospital that is located in the west of Teshie City. China Geo-Engineering Corporation was the contractor responsible for implementation. A groundbreaking ceremony took place on April 29, 2009. Construction began in April 2009 and ended in October 2010.  The project was officially completed and handed over to the authorities on December 21, 2010.  Media reports suggest that Teshie General Hospital was understaffed and in poor condition as of 2012.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for provision of med. supplies (Ebola)
description: On September 29, 2014, the Government of Ghana and People’s Republic of China signed a grant agreement worth RMB 5 million for the provision of medical supplies to respond to an Ebola outbreak. H. E. Sun Baohong, China Ambassador to Ghana signed the agreement on behalf of China and Hon. Cassiel Ato Forson, MP, Deputy Minister of Finance, signed the agreement on behalf of the Government of Ghana. These medical supplies included protective equipment, sprayers, non-contact infrared body thermometers, and body temperature detectors. These materials were successfully delivered to the Ghanaian authorities on October 31, 2014.

project_name: Gov't hosts 22 Ghanaian healthcare workers for maternity care seminar
description: From September 11 to December 9, 2015, 22 Ghanaian healthcare workers attended a maternity care seminar in Chengdu, Sichuan. The financial value and implementing organization of this training is unclear. This project was completed and is a part of a series of training seminars that China has provided to Ghanaians since 2003.

project_name: Gov't donated via UN children's fund for Covid-19 pandemic relief
description: In March 2020, Chinese government provides USD 1,000,000 to support COVID-19 response in Ghana (SM200730).  This project is captured in UNOCHA Financial Tracking Service as Flow ID #223683.

project_name: State-owned joint venture Sunon Asogli Power ltd. donated Covid relief
description: On March 29, 2020, the Chinese state-owned joint venture, Sunon Asogli Power (Ghana) Ltd. and Africa World Airlines (AWA) donated $200,000 USD to the Government of Ghana as COVID-19 relief aid. Each organization donated $100,000 USD.  Sunon Asogli Power (Ghana) Ltd. in Ghana is one of the largest Chinese-funded projects in Ghana, generating 20%-25% of Ghana's total electricity supply and making great contributions to Ghana's economic and social development and improvement of people's living standards. Sunon Asogli Power (Ghana) Limited is jointly owned by Shenzhen Energy Group (60%) and the China Africa Development Fund (40%). It is the first successful Independent Power Producer (IPP) in Ghana.

project_name: Gov't donated med. equipment to Korle-Bu teaching hospital
description: On November 24, 2010, the 1st Chinese medical assistance team to Ghana donated medical equipment and drugs worth 100,000 RMB to the Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital. This is the first time the medical team has donated medical supplies to this particular hospital.

project_name: Gov't donated med. equipment to Korle-Bu teaching hospital
description: In 2009, the Chinese Ambassador to Ghana donated 55 pieces of medical equipment worth $447,000, contributing to the Anti-Malaria Research Centre at the Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital in Accra. The equipment includes microscopes, ultra-violet flouresce, microwaves, clean benches, centrifuges, and water heaters. The donation took place at the sod-cutting ceremony for the establishment of the research center.   According to a 2011 Working Series report, the anti-malaria medical center in Accra started to operate on 28 October 2009. After the establishment of the anti-malaria center, Chinese experts could set up and test the facilities, exchange ideas with local specialists and give technological training to medical staff. For the following three years, the Chinese government provided the center’ facilities and drugs free of charge. It is important that the center should serve as national bases not only for laboratory and clinical departments, but also, and more importantly, for research into anti-malaria strategies (including malaria prevention), for exchanges of advanced technology and for training medical staff.

project_name: Gov't gave grants for anti-Malaria drugs
description: On 3 September 2008, the Chinese Government agreed to donate a batch of anti-malarial drugs worth $250,000 to the Government of Ghana. The agreement was signed between Ghana's Finance Minister Kwadwo Baah Wiredu and China’s Deputy Minister of Commerce Fu Ziying. Then, on December 4, 2008, the drugs were officially delivered and handed over to the Ghanaian authorities.

project_name: Gov't donated supplies to women, children, & youth for Covid relief
description: On July 22, 2020, the Chinese Government donated medical supplies to the Government of Ghana to be distributed to women, children, and youth in the country. The purpose of this donation is to help women and children in Ghana better fight against the epidemic and enhance the welfare of women and children in Ghana. The Executive Secretary of the African First Ladies Federation for Development (OAFLAD), Mamaya, Director of the Office of the First Lady of Ghana, Shirley, and Director of the Political Office of our Embassy, Danzhu Lou, attended the donation ceremony. The amount and value of this donation are not specified, but the purpose of this donation was to help Ghana in fighting against the COVID-19 pandemic.

project_name: Guangzhou gov't donated PPE to Accra metropolitan gov
description: On August 12, 2020, Guangzhou Municipal Government donated 16,000 medical face masks and 100 infrared thermometers to Ghana's Greater Accra Regional Government, the Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA). The Mayor of the AMA, Mohammad Sowah, the Director of External Relations, Jennifer Bullock, and the Director of the Political Office of the Embassy, Danzhu Lou, attended the donation ceremony. The purpose of this donation was to help Ghana's Greater Accra Region overcome the COVID-19 pandemic and resume economic development as soon as possible.

project_name: Embassy donated med. masks to the confucius institute at university
description: On June 25, 2020, on behalf of the Chinese Embassy, Shiting Wang, the Ambassador to Ghana, donated 46,000 medical masks to overseas Chinese people and the Confucius Institute at the University of Ghana. The purpose of this donation was to help Ghana in fighting against the COVID-19 pandemic.

project_name: Gov't donated PPE
description: On April 6, 2020, the Chinese Government donated personal protective equipment (PPE) supplies to Ghana. This batch of medical assistance arrived in Accra, capital of Ghana. The purpose of this donation is to help Ghana combat the COVID-19 pandemic outbreak.  The items are part of 60 tonnes of materials that have been donated to Ghana and 17 other countries for the fight against the disease. The items, which arrived at the Kotoka International Airport on board a chartered Chinese aircraft, would be distributed from Ghana to the other African countries with the support of the World Food programme's (WFP) Ghana office. The other African countries are Nigeria, Senegal, Gabon, Sierra Leone, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Cote d'Ivoire, the Gambia, Liberia and Mali, Burkina Faso, Equatorial Guinea, Togo, Benin, Republic of Congo, Cape Verde, and Sao Tome and Principe.

project_name: Gov't donated med. equipment Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital
description: On September 12, 2013, the third Chinese medical team deployed in Accra, Ghana, on behalf of the Chinese government, donated 400,000 RMB worth of medical equipment to Ghana's Korle-Bu Hospital. This was apparently the 4th donation of medical equipment from a medical team. According to a Chinese Ministry of Commerce source, the donation included x-ray film viewers, cervical traction beds, renal pelvis ureter mirrors, syringe pumps, ophthalmoscopes, hammers for the brain, infant warmers, and stainless steel infant beds.

project_name: Fujian Municipal gov't donated supplies to greater Accra region
description: On August 6, 2020, on behalf of Fujian Provincial People's Association for Friendship with Foreign Countries, the Chinese Ambassador to Ghana donated medical supplies to the Government of Ghana in order to be distributed to the people of the Greater Accra Region. Fujian is the sister city of Ghana's Greater Accra Region, and the purpose of this donation is to help Ghana in fighting against the COVID-19 pandemic.

project_name: Gov't donated med. equipment to Lekma Hospital
description: On May 26, 2016, the Chinese government donated medical equipment worth 475,000 cedi to the China-Ghana Friendship Hospital (Lekma Hospital) which is located in Teshie, Accra. The equipment is said to have included ultrasound diagnostic instruments, fiberoptic bronchoscopes, and spinal traction rehabilitation beds.  The donation came from the 5th medical team from China in Ghana at the time, who were led by Zheng Jianghua (the medical team project is captured in #57992).

project_name: Gov't offered scholarships to Ghanaians
description: In 2009, the Chinese Ambassador to Ghana Yu Wenzhe announced that the government of China will offer scholarships and training programmes to Ghanaians who want to study medicine in China. This study abroad program will help to reduce malaria and improve the living standards of Ghanaians. It appears that the project was announced in October 2009, however the current status of the project is uncertain.

project_name: Gov't donated anti-Malarial drugs to Lekma Hospital
description: On November 17, 2015, China donated 600,000 doses of anti-malarial drugs to Lekma Hospital in Ghana (also known as Teshie General Hospital or China-Ghana Friendship Hospital), which is located in the west of Teshie city. Since 2006, China had been periodically supplying Ghana with anti-malarial drugs, as well as offering education in treatments. One source estimates the medication to be worth roughly USD $1.3 million. The handover ceremony was attended by the Chinese Ambassador to Ghana and Ghana's Minister of Health.

project_name: Embassy & CECCG jointly donated PPE supplies to local orphanages
description: On April 28, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Ghana and the Ghana-Chinese Enterprises Chamber of Commerce (CECCG) jointly donated approximately GH 50,000-worth of personal protection equipment (PPE) supplies to the Ghana's Ministry of Gender, Children, and Social Protection. The donation ceremony took place at the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Security in Ghana, and according to Shiting Wang, the Chinese Ambassador to Ghana, children, especially orphans, are more in need of help due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Therefore, the purpose of this donation is to help children in need in Ghana.  The donated materials included 1,200 bottles of hand sanitizer, 16,000 baby wipes, 6,800 baby diapers, 3,000 masks, 2,520 bars of soap and 1,200 rolls of toilet paper. The above materials will be distributed to local orphanages through the Ghana Gender, Children and Social Security section to protect local vulnerable children from the impact of the new crown pneumonia epidemic.

project_name: Gov't donated med. supplies to Ghana's Lekma Hospital
description: On November 27, 2019 a batch of China-aided medical supplies worth 901,000 Chinese Yuan was donated to Ghana's Ledzokuku-Krowor Municipal Hospital (LEKMA Hospital, China-Ghana Friendship Hospital) at the 8th medical team's clinic. The equipment donated included respirators, wheelchairs, along with other equipment. The director of the LEKMA hospital, Akua Afriyie Gyimah-Asante, and the chief of the 8th batch of Chinese medics in Ghana, Liu Qiuhong attended the donation ceremony.

project_name: Gov't & private sector companies provided PPE to Ministry of Health
description: On May 15, 2020, Ghana's Ministry of Health received a donation of ventilators, KN95 and surgical nose masks, goggles, surgical gloves, isolation gowns, medical shoe covers, gun thermometers, disinfectants and wipes from the Ghana Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The supplies originated from a combination of the Chinese Government, Chinese private sector companies, and Chinese state-owned companies, with the Ghana Ministry of Foreign Affairs acting as the implementing agency. The full donation is valued at approximately USD $400,000.

project_name: Gov't donated a batch of anti-Malarial drugs
description: On August 24, 2011, the Chinese government donated a batch of anti-malaria drugs to Ghana. At the donation ceremony, a speech was delivered by Gao Wenzhi, the Economic & Commercial Counsellor of the Chinese Embassy in Ghana. The Chinese Embassy reports that this donation was worth roughly RMB 3,000,000 while Modern Ghana News cites a figure of USD 460,000 which is roughly the same value. A second official Chinese source also cites the amount of RMB 3 million. The donation was accepted by Ghana's Minister of Health, Joseph Yileh Chireh, and was just the most recent development in a long history of anti-malaria cooperation.

project_name: Gov't donated batch of anti-Malarial drugs
description: On July 8, 2011, the Chinese Government officially handed over a donation of anti-malarial drugs worth RMB 3 million to the Government of Guinea.

project_name: Gov't donated med. devices & medicine to friendship hospital
description: On December 6, 2014, the Chinese Ambassador to Guinea, Bian Jianqiang, signed a handover certificate marking the official donation of medical devices and medicines to the Sino-Guinean Friendship Hospital. The value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donated 2nd batch of anti-Covid-19 pandemic supplies
description: On June 18th, 2020, the second batch of anti-COVID-19 pandemic supplies donated by the Chinese government to Guinea arrived in Conakry. Chinese Ambassador Huang Wei and Guinean Foreign Minister Toure went to the airport to receive the supplies.  Ambassador Huang and Foreign Minister Toure signed handover certificates on behalf of the two governments respectively and were interviewed by several national TV stations and other local mainstream media. The first batch of medical supplies sent by China to address the COVID-19 pandemic was sent to Guinea in April 2020 (Project ID# 92697).

project_name: Gov't donated equipment to the Ministry of Health & Public Hygiene

project_name: Gov't provided grant for the provision of anti-Malarial drugs
description: In 2006, the Chinese Government and the Republic of Guinea signed letters of exchange related to the provision of anti-malarial drugs. Guinea’s Ministry of Cooperation recorded the value of this grant commitment as $125,000.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for friendship hospital construction project
description: In 2008, the Chinese Government agreed to provide a USD $10 million grant to the Government of Guinea for Phase 1 of Sino-Guinean Friendship Hospital Construction Project (captured via Project ID#13330). This project involved the construction of a 120-bed, "Class A" specialist hospital for cardiology, neurology, radiology, acupuncture and rehabilitation, thoracic surgery, therapeutic surgery, orthopedics, general surgery, brain tumor surgery, emergency, and resuscitation units. The new facility also houses Chinese medical teams.   On April 28, 2008, representatives from a Chinese design firm and the Guinea Ministry of Health had a preliminary design meeting in Wuhan for this hospital. Sichuan Huashi Overseas Investment & Engineering Co., LTD was the contractor responsible for implementation. Construction began on March 31, 2009 and ended on July 25, 2010. The first phase of the project was then officially handed over to the local authorities on April 13, 2011. Then, in 2017, the Chinese Government provided an RMB 100 million grant for Phase 2 of the Sino-Guinean Friendship Hospital Construction Project (captured via Project ID#64425). Phase 2 involved the construction of several surgical and intensive care units and the provision and installation of medical equipment, such as Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scanners. Sinohydro Bureau 3 Co. Ltd. was the contractor responsible for implementation. An official groundbreaking ceremony took place on December 7, 2018. As of November 28, 2019, the project had achieved a 70% completion rate. A project completion ceremony took place on January 19, 2022. The original anticipated commencement date was November 1, 2018, and the originally anticipated completion date was April 30, 2020. It appears that the project experienced some implementation delays because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for China-Guinea Malaria control center project
description: On August 24 and 28, 2009, the Chinese Government and the Republic of Guinea signed letters of exchange related to the China-Guinea Malaria Control Center Project (中国-几内亚疟疾防治中心.or le centre antipaludique). On November 6, 2009, the center was officially inaugurated at the Ignace Dean Hospital.

project_name: Gov't donated 200,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021, the Chinese Government donated approximately 300,000 doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Guinea. The Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Guinea on March 3, 2021. project_name: Gov't donated a 2nd batch of Covid-19 vaccines

project_name: Gov't donated anti-Ebola devices & office supplies

project_name: Gov't provided grant to guinea for Ebola response activities
description: On November 19, 2014, the Chinese Government and the Republic of Guinea signed a grant agreement worth $5 million USD to combat the Ebola epidemic. project_name: Gov't donated the 1st batch of anti-Covid-19 pandemic supplies
description: On April 18th, 2020, the Chinese government donates the first batch of anti-COVID-19 supplies to Guinea has arrived in Conakry, the capital of Guinea. Representatives from the World Health Organization and the World Food Programme in Guinea attended the ceremony. The Guinean health department expresses its deep gratitude to the Chinese government and will properly arrange the use of materials to improve the ability to respond to the pandemic.

project_name: Gov't & Shanxi Province donated a batch of Covid pandemic supplies
description: On June 19th, 2020, a handover ceremony was held for a donation from the Shanxi Province to Guinea.The donation consisted of 10,000 pieces of medical protective clothing, 350,000 pieces of medical surgical masks, 15,000 pairs of goggles, 15,000 pairs of disposable medical examination gloves, 3,000 pairs of disposable shoes, 20,200 pairs of N95 masks, and 10,000 sets of test kits. project_name: Gov't donated medication to Canchungo hospital

description: On June 18, 2020, China donated a batch of medical supplies to Guinea-Bissau. project_name: Eximbank provided loan for research & referral construction project
description: The Kenyatta University Teaching, Referral & Research Hospital project was conceptualized in 2008. The Government of Kenya, through various line ministries, supported the idea developed by Kenyatta University Management led by the then Vice-Chancellor, Prof Olive Mugenda. The idea came to fruition with the signing of an MoU on April 21, 2011, between the Chinese and Kenyan governments.   Then, on June 17, 2011, China Eximbank and the Government of Kenya’s National Treasury signed an RMB 744,560,000 government concessional loan (GCL) agreement for the Kenyatta University Teaching Research & Referral Hospital Construction Project. The face value of the loan was subsequently revised to RMB 716,983,703.70. The loan carried the following borrowing terms: a 2% interest rate, a 20.75 year maturity, and a 7.25 year grace period. The loan was scheduled for semi-annual repayment installments beginning on September 21, 2018, and ending on March 21, 2032.    The National Treasury on-lent the proceeds of the GCL to Kenyatta University Teaching, Referral & Research Hospital (KUTRRH), which is a Kenyan state corporation. The proceeds of the loan were to be used by the ultimate borrower to finance a commercial contract between the Government of Kenya and China Jiangxi Corporation for International Economic and Technical Co-operation (CJIC), which was signed on August 12, 2010.  The borrower made principal repayments worth RMB 27,576,296 between July 1, 2020 and June 30, 2021 (Fiscal Year 2020-2021) and RMB 55,152,592.00 between July 1, 2021 and June 30, 2022 (Fiscal Year 2021-2022).  The loan’s amount outstanding was RMB 661,831,110.11 as of June 30, 2020, RMB 606,678,517.52 as of June 30, 2021, and RMB 551,525,924.93 as of June 30, 2022.  The project involved the construction of Kenyatta University Teaching Research & Referral Hospital (肯雅塔大学教学转诊医院) in Nairobi. The hospital covers an area of more than 600 acres with a total construction area over 80,000 square meters, has a total of more than 650 beds, 8 high-grade operating rooms, 1 maternal center, 1 neonatal intensive care unit (NICU), 1 intensive care unit (ICU), 1 special intensive care unit (HDU), as well as medical imaging center, central supply room, oxygen, and medical gas system, boiler and laundry, medical waste treatment, funeral facilities, restaurant, teaching center, dormitory, and other supporting facilities. Construction of the 650-bed hospital involved the expansion and equipping of anatomy and basic science laboratories and the establishment of pre-clinical and clinical teaching departments at the university.    CJIC was the contractor responsible for implementation.  The project was originally scheduled to enter implementation in 2012 and reach completion by June 30, 2019. Construction commenced on November 1, 2012 and ended on December 14, 2016.   A formal project handover ceremony took place on May 24, 2019. However, the hospital did not open its doors to the first patient until October 28, 2019 after successfully conducting a ‘dry run’ from September 27, 2019 to October 27, 2019, followed by a successful 'soft run' from October 28, 2019 to November 24, 2019. To operationalize the first 160 beds, the hospital operationalized the oncology, renal dialysis, accident and emergency, trauma and orthopaedics, ICU, radiology, laboratory, pharmacy, mortuary, and other allied services. The hospital was designated as an isolation and treatment center on March 24, 2020 with over 400 beds designated for COVID-19 patients. A formal hospital opening ceremony took place on September 10, 2020. Then, in October 2021, an advanced cancer imaging center (known as the Integrated Molecular Imaging Centre Hospitality and Accommodation Centre) was launched at the hospital.   There are indications that the China Eximbank loan for the Kenyatta University Teaching Research & Referral Hospital Construction Project financially underperformed vis-a-vis the original expectations of the lender and Kenya's National Treasury. As of October 17, 2018, 85% of the China Eximbank loan (worth 8,756,025,600 Kenyan shillings) had been disbursed and utilized. However, the remaining 15% of the loan (worth approximately 1.37 billion Kenyan shillings) had not yet disbursed in support of the personnel and capacity building component of the loan because disbursement was conditional upon the training of personnel (who were yet to be recruited by Kenyatta University due to ‘budgetary constraints’). KUTRRH was ultimately unable to meet its loan repayment obligations (due to the fact that it was generating insufficient revenue) and the National Treasury had to step in to ensure repayments to China Eximbank. Then, in December 2021, it was revealed by the Kenyan Government that KUTRRH was converted into an independent parastatal entity (and severed from Kenyatta University) on January 25, 2019 in order to use its future revenues to recover the funds needed to repay the China Eximbank loan.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for Nairobi East District Hospital const project

The ship is equipped with a rescue helicopter, 300 hospital beds, 428 medical doctors, nurses and supporting staff from 32 medical departments including ICU, emergency treatment, internal medicine, surgery, respiratory, ophthalmology, neurology, dermatology, radiology, blood transfusion, traditional Chinese treatment, and more. The monetary value of the aid is unknown.

project_name: Gov't granted 1 million USD to build Mama Lucy Kibaki Hospital
description:
On 2009 July 1, the Chinese government donated 1043710 USD (85,550,000 Ksh) for the construction Of Nairobi East District Hospital (援肯东区医院). The project is in Kayole North in Embakasi district under administration of Nairobi county. The 112-bed hospital of 7012 square meters is located in Embakasi District. Kenya's Ministry of Health is implementing the project, and construction is done by the China Wuyi Company. The hospital was completed and handed over to Kenya on Aug 5 2011.  The hospital is also referred to as Mama Lucy Kibaki Hospital (齐贝吉夫人医院). 
 
 See #1267 for a previous donation, 7126400 USD donated by Chinese government on 2009 July 20.

project_name: Gov't bank provided credit loan for CT scanners to gok project
description: On December 11, 2017, China Development Bank and the Government of Kenya’s National Treasury signed a buyer’s credit loan agreement worth $67.3 million (KES 7 billion) for the supply of computed tomography (CT) scanners to 37 public county hospitals. The loan carried the following borrowing terms: a 5.66-year maturity (final maturity date: April 15, 2023) and an annual interest rate of LIBOR plus a 4.95% margin. It was scheduled for repayment in semi-annual installments and backed by a Sinosure credit insurance policy. The borrower was expected to use the proceeds of the loan to finance approximately 80% of the cost of a commercial contract between Neusoft Medical Systems Co., Ltd (东软医疗系统有限公司) -- a Chinese medical equipment manufacturer -- and Kenya’s Ministry of Health, which was signed in August 2017. The Government of Kenya was responsible for directly financing the remaining 20% of the commercial contract cost.   The borrower made principal repayments worth $20,000,000 between July 1, 2020 and June 30, 2021 (Fiscal Year 2020-2021) and $20,000,000 between July 1, 2021 and June 30, 2022 (Fiscal Year 2021-2022). The loan’s amount outstanding was $50,300,000 as of June 30, 2020, $30,300,000 as of June 30, 2021, and $10,300,000 as of June 30, 2022.   The purpose of the project was to supply, install, and maintain computed tomography (CT) scanners in 37 of Kenya’s public county hospitals, including Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital and Kenyatta National Hospital. The project, which is officially considered to be part of the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), also involved 37 Kenyan radiologists and radiographers traveling to China to train on the use of the machines.   Neusoft Medical Systems Co., Ltd was the contractor responsible for project implementation. Project implementation commenced on May 12, 2018. All 37 CT scanners were shipped to Kenya in 2018. However, in 2018, a probe into the procurement process for the project erupted in scandal as members of Parliament's Public Accounts Committee charged that the machines had been overpriced fourfold to benefit senior government officials in the Ministries of Health and National Treasury. A Kenyan government audit came to the following conclusion: ‘[t]he Ministry [of Health] in 2017/18 financial year paid [KES] 1,740,000,000 for Computed Tomography (CT) scanners. This was 20% of the contract value which was paid as a condition precedent for the Government of Kenya to obtain a loan of [KES] 7,000,000,000 from the People’s Republic of China to finance the purchase of the CT scanners. The scanners were procured through Neusoft Medical Systems Co. Ltd. However, no procurement documents for Neusoft Medical Systems [were] provided at the time of conclusion of the audit review. Information available indicate[s] that Neusoft Medical Systems was proposed by the Government of the People’s Republic of China as a leading manufacturer of CT scans. Consequently, it was not possible to ascertain whether due diligence and fidelity to the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, 2015 was observed. In particular, Section 85 which requires tenders to be evaluated by the evaluation committee of the procuring entity for the purpose of making recommendations to the Accounting Officer through the head of procurement to inform the decision of the award of the contract to the successful tenderers. Under the circumstances, procurement laws and regulations may have been flouted as the necessary procurement documents were not provided for audit review.’

project_name: Gov't donated anti-Malaria drugs
description: On April 28, 2006, Chinese President Hu Jintao and Kenyan President Mwai Kibaki signed a joint communique opposing Taiwanese independence as well as 8 different agreements and exchange of letters. One of these agreements stipulated that China grant 500,000 RMB (440 million Ksh) to the Kenya Ministry of Health for purchasing anti-malaria drugs. The medicines were delivered and handed over to the Kenya side on August 8, 2007.

project_name: Gov't donated 200,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: On September 18, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccines to the Government of Kenya. This donation was made to support Kenya’s COVID-19 response efforts. The monetary value of this donation is USD $3.6 million.  Susan Mochache, the Principal Secretary of Kenya's Ministry of Health, and Zhang Yijun, the Minister Counselor at the Chinese Embassy in Kenya, attended the vaccine handover ceremony at the Jomo Kenyatta International Airport.

project_name: Gov't funds expansion of Moi teaching & referral hospital
description: In July 2013, it was announced that China would fund the expansion of the Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital (MTRH) in Eldoret at a cost of about 17 billion Kenyan shilling. In order to receive funding, the hospital was required to hire a Chinese firm to conduct the construction. The new wing of the hospital will house 1000 beds. The hospital signed a deal to engage China Aerospace Construction Group to carry out upgrading and expansion of the facility in October 2012. However, on May 3, 2013, the hospital entered into another deal with China Wu Yi for the same project, without canceling the first.   On November 19, 2013, a contract with China Machinery Engineering Corporation (CMEC) for the upgrading of MTRH at a value of USD291 million (about Sh25 billion) was signed. In February 2014, Hospital director John Kibosia told the National Assembly departmental committee on health China failed to approve the Sh25 billion project for funding and the contract would have to be renegotiated or a new financier sought. MTRH and CMEC had entered into the provisional agreement for the construction of a 1,000-bed complex, a four-story car park to accommodate 500 vehicles, a 500-kilowatt-hour solar plant, an incinerator, and access roads. The agreement will expire in August 2014.   Dr. Kibosia said a final contract was to be signed after approvals by government officials and after securing a loan from a Chinese bank. The committee questioned the variation in the cost estimates, which CMEC put at Sh25.1 billion ($291.6 million) against MTRH’s Sh17.7 billion ($205.9 million). Dr. Kibosia said MTRH estimates did not include the incinerator, electricity overhaul, fire protection, solar power generation, elevators, survey, and engineering, which would cost Sh7.5 billion  Business Daily Africa reports that the Chinese Government ultimately decided to not fund the project. However, Kenya's National Treasury Cabinet Secretary, Mr. Henry Rotich, claims that the Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital project has benefited from Chinese development assistance.

project_name: Gov't donated 8 infant incubators to Pumwani Maternity Hospital
description: On September 2, 2014, First Lady Margaret Kenyatta donated eight infant incubators to Pumwani Maternity Hospital in Nairobi as part of the efforts to reduce mother and child mortality in the country.These incubators were purchased by the Chinese government which is intended to increase the hospital’s capacity to handle new born premature babies.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for gatundu level iv hospital expansion project
description: August 13, 2013, construction was launched for a Chinese-funded expansion to a Gatundu District Hospital (卡通都医院), Gatundu Level IV Hospital, in Kenya. The 5300 square meter expansion includes a modern medical wing with five-floors, four elevators, outpatient services, an emergency department, 12 ICU beds, 84 beds, medical laboratory, maternity unit, operating theater, wards, and several units of medical equipment, including CT scanners and X-ray scanners. The assistance by China is in response to a request by President Kenyatta in 2011, and is estimated to cost 11 million USD. Construction started August 13, 2013 and was completed March 16, 2016 (Liu Xianfa attended the handover ceremony).

project_name: ComPLAnted to build hospital in Machakos funded by Chinese loan
description: On Dec 26 2018, Chinese state-owned enterprise China National Complete Plant Import & Export (CNCPIEC, COMPLANT) signed a contract with Nairobi-based project owner Lianard Holding for a 47,758,830 USD (Ksh 4.8 billion) healthcare community project "肯尼亚湖畔医疗城项目".   The project aims to build a 13,400 square-meter comprehensive hospital and surrounding apartment building includes 300 apartments inside with a gross floor area of 25,500 square meters. The location is in Machakos, Kenya, 68 kilometers southeast of its capital Nairobi. The contract will become effective after Lianard signs a loan agreement with a Chinese bank. Details of negotiation on the loan contract is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donated anti-epidemic supplies
description: On April 17, 2020, China donated a batch of anti-epidemic supplies to Kenya, which was received by Health Cabinet Secretary Mutahi Kagwe, Interior Cabinet Secretary Fred Matiang'i, and Transport Cabinet Secretary James Macharia. It is unclear if this is another batch of donation from Jack Ma or directly from the Chinese Government. The medical supplies consisted of testing kits, protective gear, and medical equipment.

project_name: Gov't pledged to aid kenya's health sector with increased Malaria aid
description: In 2014, China and Kenya signed several cooperation pacts, including an MoU on Agricultural Cooperation between the two countries on health cooperation and preventing malaria. Wang Liji, vice-director for international cooperation at the National Health and Family Planning Commission, pledged recently that China will assist the African Union in building centers for disease control and prevention. He also stated China will devote more resources to cultivating health and medical talent. The cooperation MoU agreements are detailed below.

project_name: Embassy donated med. equipment to maternal health charity.
description: On March 8, 2018, the Chinese Embassy in Kenya donated 130,000 USD worth of medical equipment through Beyond Zero Charity (“超越零点”基金会) which is initiated by the First Lady of Kenya. The donated medical equipment included beds, operating tables, infusion pumps, syringe pumps, and baby incubators and will be distributed via the Beyond Zero Charity to Nairobi and Tana River Counties for improving maternal and child health. In attendance at the donation ceremony were the Chinese Ambassador to Kenya, Liu Xianfa, First Lady of Kenya, Margaret Kenyatta and Kenya's Minister of Health Sicily Kariuki.   According to a publication for the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Chinese government marked the occasion with a 5-year commitment to the charity.

project_name: China Development Bank provided buyer’s credit loan for MRI equipment
description: In 2014, China Development Bank and the Government of Kenya signed a buyer’s credit loan agreement worth $27,120,000.20 for the Magnetic Resonance Imaging Equipment (MRI) Project. The borrowing terms of this loan were as follows: a 2 year grace period, a 5 year maturity, and an annual interest rate of LIBOR plus a 3% margin. The loan was scheduled for repayment in semiannual installments from June 4, 2016 to June 4, 2019. Under the loan agreement, the amount outstanding as of June 2019 was KES 409,193,200. There was no amount outstanding as of June 2020. As of June 2019, the borrower had repaid an amount equivalent to KES 422,920,000.   The purpose of the project was to facilitate the acquisition of 20 pieces of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) equipment from Neusoft Medical Systems.

project_name: Gov't donated anti-Malaria drugs
description: On September 13, 2003, China donated 10 boxes of Cotecsin dihydroarteminsinin tablets and 20 boxes of Cotecsin dihydroartemisinin suspension, worth 3.9 million KES, to Kenya to be distributed to health centers around the country. Chinese Ambassador to Kenya Guo Chongli handed over the medicine to Kenyan Permanent Secretary for Health Wellington Godo.

project_name: Gov't CSIC pledged to construct new hospital in Mombasa
description: Description: According to a media report published in December 2013, China Sinopharm International Corporation, and CSIC's local partner, Pharmken Ltd, pledged to construct a new hospital in Mombasa that will focus on oncology, cardiology, orthopedics, and renal medicine. While a firm financial figure was not discussed, a budget between $30-50 million (2.58-4.3 billion KSh) was proposed. This project is a part of an effort to provide greater medical coverage across Kenya.

project_name: Embassy donated crutches & wheelchairs to fund for the disabled
description: On June 5, 2008, the Chinese Embassy in Kenya donated 50 pairs of armpit crutches, 50 pairs of elbow crutches and 5 wheelchairs to the National Fund for the Disabled of Kenya (NFDK). Mr. Xue Bing, Charge D'affaires of the Chinese Embassy handed over the donation to Mr. R. N. Muchiri, Chief Executive of the NFDK.

project_name: Gov't constructed an anti-Malaria center at Kenyatta Hospital
description: According to a 2011 Working Series report, China planned to construct an anti-malaria center in Kenya in 2006. Specific funding amounts were not found. An embassy statement by the Chinese ambassador to Kenya in 2013 confirms that China provided grants to Kenya for the construction of an anti-malaria center at Kenyatta Hospital in Kenya, though the year is unclear as to when an agreement/commitment was made to build the center.

project_name: Gov't donated 2nd batch of Covid-19 med. materials
description: On July 28, 2020, the Chinese government donated the second batch of anti-pandemic materials to Kenya. The donation will aid Kenya in its fight against Covid-19 and represents the friendship and mutual trust between Kenya and China. Chargé d'Affaires Zhao Xiyuan and Deputy Minister of Health of Kenya, Ms. Susan Mochacher, signed the handover certificate on behalf of the two governments respectively. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Embassy donated 500 KN95 masks to the Nairobi Hospital
description: On May 15, 2020, the Nairobi Hospital received 500 KN95 masks from the Chinese Embassy in Kenya. The masks were donated to assist the hospital workers with COVID-19 cases.

project_name: Gov't funds UNICEF maternal, newborn, & children's health project
description: In December 2019, the Chinese government signed an agreement to contribute $1 million to the UN Children Fund's (UNICEF) procurement and distribution efforts regarding medical equipment and medicines in Kenya through the South-South Cooperation Assistance Fund (SSCAF) through December 31, 2021. On June 30, 2022, the Chinese Embassy in Kenya and the UN Children's Fund (UNICEF) held a ceremony to celebrate the completion of this "maternal, newborn, and children's health project". The project offered medical materials and training to 159 health facilities in 8 counties across Kenya, reported as benefiting more than 3 million people, especially in the remote parts of the country. Similar projects were launched in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ethiopia, Niger, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Sudan, and Zimbabwe.

project_name: Gov't donated reproductive med. equipment
description: On October 23, 2007, a delegation team from the Chinese National Health and Family Planning commission (CNHFPC) donated reproductive medical equipment to the Kenya government. The equipment will be used to improve the reproductive health of the Kenyan people. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donated 203,340 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: On August 20, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 203,340 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Lesotho. The Chinese Ambassador to Lesotho Lei Kezhong and the Minister of Health of Lesotho Hon. Semano Sekatle attended the vaccine handover ceremony.

project_name: Gov't provided Covid-19 response via UN's population fund
description: In April 2021, Chinese government provides USD 500,000 providing health Assistance to Botswana and Lesotho in East and South Africa Region for COVID-19 pandemic response.

project_name: Gov't donated med. supplies for Covid-19 relief
description: On August 19th, 2021, the Chinese government donated equipment meant to fight COVID-19 to the Ministry of Health in Lesotho. The donation included a mouthpiece, a thermometer, and an oxygen box. The purpose of this donation is to help Lesotho fight against the pandemic.

project_name: Embassy donated med. equipment to the Motebang Hospital
description: On August 14, 2017, the Chinese Ambassador officially donated medical equipment worth 100,000 M to Motebang Hospital in Leribe, Lesotho. The donation includes basic supplies such as gowns and scrubs.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for hospital & eye clinic construction project
description: On January 10, 2018, the Chinese Ambassador to Lesotho and Lesotho’s Minister of Development Planning signed an exchange of letters, which committed approximately RMB 430 million of grant funding for the Maseru District Hospital and Eye Clinic Construction Project. The grant proceeds were partly drawn from an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) that the Chinese Government and Government of Lesotho signed on December 18, 2017 and another ETCA that the two governments signed on March 15, 2018.   The purpose of the project is to construct a 200-bed hospital -- on the plot of land where Queen Elizabeth II Hospital resides — with the capacity to serve 400,000 Basotho in Maseru District and surrounding areas. It will provide a variety of health services, including eye care, cancer treatment, tuberculosis, HIV and non-communicable diseases. The modern facility will also have state-of-the-art medical equipment as well as training facilities and dormitories for trainee doctors and nurses. Upon completion, it is expected that the Maseru District Hospital and Eye Clinic will operate as the country’s second referral hospital after Queen ‘Mamohato Memorial Hospital (QMMH), relieving the latter of its ever-increasing patient load. Shanghai Construction (Group) Corporation (SCG) is the contractor responsible for implementation.   As of February 2019, the design of the project was complete. However, one year later, in February 2020, Queen Elizabeth II Hospital had still not been demolished to make way for the new Maseru District Hospital and Eye Clinic (due to disagreements between the Ministry of Health and Ministry of Public Works over the costs of demolition). Queen Elizabeth II Hospital was finally demolished in April 2020. On February 24, 2021, a groundbreaking (sod-turning) ceremony took place. The project is expected to reach completion within 30 months (on or around August 24, 2023). It is also expected to generate 100 jobs for Bosotho during the construction period.

project_name: China donated anti-tuberculosis drugs
description: On November 14, 2002, China handed over 300 boxes of anti-tuberculosis tablets, enough to serve about 3,000 patients in Maseru. Lesotho Health Minister Motloheloa Phooka praised the donation when it was received at the ceremony held at the Chinese Embassy. Chinese Charge D'affaires Xu Xian also spoke at the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't donated anti-epidemic supplies to fight Covid-19
description: On August 27, 2020, a handover ceremony was held for the Chinese government's donation of anti-epidemic supplies to Lesotho. This package included 50 000 surgical masks, 10 000 respirators, 50 ventilators and 200 thermometers, with a promise of another shipment of 40 oxygen machines. This was the third batch of medical aid sent by China to Lesotho to address the Covid-19 pandemic. Ambassador to Lesotho Lei Kezhong and Lesotho Deputy Minister of Health Moazi were present at the ceremony and signed the handover certificate.

project_name: Gov't grants scholarships to med. students to study in China
description: In an interview on March 31, 2009, Motumi Ralejoe, a Lesotho parliamentarian said that China provided scholarships for Basotho medical students to study in China. The financial value for these scholarships is unknown and their exact date is also unknown, but a Chinese source indicated that the Chinese government gives these students two scholarships annually, and that 8 students are currently in China.

project_name: Gov't donated med. equipment to Motebang Hospital
description: In April 2012, China's Vice Minister of Health, Liu Qian handed over medical equipment to Motebang Hospital in Leribe. Reports say it totaled "230,000 equipment", but it does not specify units. The equipment included an infant scale, gynecological and obstetrical sets, a blood sugar test unit, a portable ultrasonic diagnostic instrument, an electrocardiogram instrument, a fetal heart check unit and a high pressure steam sterilization pot.   The donation was handed over during the Vice Minister's three-day visit to Lesotho.

project_name: Chinese donation of anti-Malaria drugs
description: On May 11, 2006, Chinese Ambassador to Liberia Li Songtian handed over 20,000 doses of anti-malaria drugs to the government of Liberia. It has been reported that the drugs worth 1 million Chinese Yuan.

project_name: Cchinese assistance PLAnned for Liberia's healthcare system
description:
In January of 2007 it was reported that China would help revive Liberia's healthcare sector. According to a report, China would construct 30 hospitals across Liberia and a malaria treatment centre. Financial details regarding the new hospitals were not revealed. The malaria treatment center may be here #1631.  May be related to project #1673.
 
 Chinese investments will help to rebuild the primary-care system, which is plagued by medicine shortages and crumbling infrastructure.

project_name: Gov't provided $10 million grant for hospital construction project
description:
In November 2006, Chinese President Hu Jintao pledged to construct 100 bedroom hospital in Liberia at the Beijing Summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation.
 
 On December 24, 2008, the PRC signed a US$10 million contract with the Government of Liberia for the construction of the 100 bedroom Tappita F Jackson Doe Regional Referral Hospital in Nimba County. Construction began on March 25, 2009 and was completed on July 23, 2010. However, the hospital did not officially open until February 12, 2011 due to the inadequacy of medical workers in Liberia. China Henan International Cooperation Group Co. (CHICO) implemented the construction. The hospital is 23,000 square meters and will include outpatient building, medical technology building, inpatient building, comprehensive building and corridor, and other auxiliary buildings.
 
 The US$10 million contract was financed through a Chinese grant; however, the date and financial details of this grant are unknown. Additional funding was provided through an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement in 2013 (#30738).
 
 May be one of the 30 hospitals listed in Project ID #1646.

project_name: Gov't donated funds via UN children's fund to Liberia for Covid relief
description: On March 11, 2020, Chinese government provided USD 1,000,000 to United Nations Children's Fund for COVID-19 response in Liberia (SM200730).  This project is captured in UNOCHA Financial Tracking Service as Flow ID #223682.

project_name: Gov't donated USD 570,655 via WHO to support Covid-19 in Liberia
description: On March 3, 2020, the Chinese government committed a grant of USD 570,655 to support WHO response to the COVID-19 outbreak in Liberia.  This project is captured in UNOCHA Financial Tracking Service as Flow ID #218740.

project_name: Donation of a consigment of drugs
description: On October 23, 2006 China donated a consignment of drugs valued over US$30,000 to the Liberia's Health Ministry. The drugs were intended to help fight Lassa fever epidemics in Nimba and Bong counties. The total consignment was reportedly three hundred treatment medicines that can be used to treat three hundred lassa fever patients. Chinese Ambassador Lin Songtian presented the drugs to Health and Social Welfare Minister Dr. Walter Gwenigale at the Health Ministry.

project_name: China grants $20,000 USD in cash for Ebola response
description: In March 2014, the Chinese government provides a $20,000 cash aid to Liberia to support them fight the Ebola virus.  Other Ebola-related assistance provided by the Chinese Government in 2014 is captured in umbrella ProjectID#60642.

project_name: China donated 3 million YUAN of Malaria medicine to Liberia
description:
From April 22 to 25, 2010, a Chinese delegation, including the Deputy Minister of Commerce, Fu Ziying, carried out a four-day official visit to Liberia. Followng Bilateral Discussions, a signing ceremony between the two governments took place for the exchange of 3 Million RMB worth of malaria medicines. The handover date is unknown.
 
 At the same ceremony, China donated equipment to the China-Liberia Malaria Prevention and Treatment Center (#1726), medical supplies to Tappita Hospital (#1724), and an ETCA (#1723).

project_name: Gov't donated the 2nd batch of anti-Covid-19 pandemic med. supplies
description: On June 12th, 2020, Charge d'Affaires Xu Kun of the Chinese Embassy in Liberia was invited to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Liberia to attend the donation ceremony of the second batch of anti-pandemic materials aided by the Chinese government. This batch of anti-pandemic materials assisted by the Chinese government includes COVID-19 detection reagents and sampling and extraction materials, N95 masks, medical masks, protective clothing, isolation goggles, gloves, and shoe covers.   As a friendly province, the Henan Provincial People's Government also assisted medical masks and other materials to Liberia. The purpose of this donation is to help Liberia fight against the pandemic.

project_name: Gov't provided med. training for 20 Liberian staff at hospital
description: In FY 2017-2018, the Chinese Government provided two months of medical training for 20 Liberians including medical doctors, physicians, registered nurses, a midwife, a lab technician, a radiology technician, a social worker, and administrative staff. The training was conducted within China and was aimed at improving the capabilities of the staff at the Jackson F. Doe Hospital.

project_name: Gov't donated to NPHIL for Ribavirin injections & tablets
description: In October 2020, the Chinese Embassy received a formal request from the National Public Health Institute of Liberia (NPHIL) for assistance with both ribavirin injections and tablets.  The Chinese government made a special arrangement to urgently procure and transport a consignment of 9,090 packs of ribavirin injection and 1,200 packs of ribavirin tablets to support Liberia in tackling the ongoing Lassa fever outbreak.

project_name: Additional med. materials to Tappita Hospital
description:
From April 22 to 25, 2010, a Chinese delegation, including the Deputy Minister of Commerce, Fu Ziying, carried out a four-day official visit to Liberia. Followng Bilateral Discussions, a signing ceremony between the two governments took place for the provision of 10 million RMB by the Chinese Government for additional medical materials to the Tappita Hospital to support hospital operations.
 
 The materials may have been donated when the hospital was completed in July 2010 (see project #1673).
 
 At the same ceremony, China donated 3 Million RMB worth of malaria medicines (#1727), an ETCA (#1723), and equipment to the China-Liberia Malaria Prevention and Treatment Center (#1726).

project_name: China-Liberia Malaria prevention center
description: From November 3-5, 2006, during the China-Africa Cooperation Summit, China agreed to create many anti-malaria centers across Africa, including Liberia. Preperations began shortly after the meeting (Chinese Medical Cooperation In Africa, pg17). Starting from 30 January, Chinese President Hu Jintao began a tour around Africa, visiting Cameroon, Liberia, Sudan, Zambia, Namibia, South Africa, and Mozambique. The purpose of the tour is to follow up on the China-Africa Beijing summit in November last year. While in Monrovia, Hu talked with Liberian President Ellen Johnson-Sirleaf. The two leaders witnessed the signing of seven documents on cooperation in economy, technology, health, education and agriculture, and also attended the inauguration of a malaria prevention and treatment center at the John F. Kennedy Medical Center in Sinkor, which was supported by China.  According to a 2011 Working Series report, China established an anti-malaria medical center in Monrovia, Liberia on 1 February 2007.
