After the establishment of the anti-malaria center, Chinese experts could set up and test the facilities, exchange ideas with local specialists and give technological training to medical staff. For the following three years, the Chinese government provided the center’ facilities and drugs free of charge. It is important that the center should serve as national bases not only for laboratory and clinical departments, but also, and more importantly, for research into anti-malaria strategies (including malaria prevention), for exchanges of advanced technology and for training medical staff.  On March 12, 2007, China donated malaria medicine to the center (captured in #1647).

project_name: China donated materials to combat Coronavirus
description: On March 18, 2020, the China donated medical supplies. The materials were given to the Liberian Ministry of Health, and included e 50 barrels, 200 pair of gloves,100 sets of protective clothing, eight cases of isopropyl rubbing alcohol, among others.  The purpose of this donation is to help Liberia fight against the pandemic.

project_name: Chongqing International Construction Corp. donated Covid materials
description: On March 28th, 2020, The Liberia branch of Chongqing Foreign Construction Co., Ltd. donated 20 hand-washing and sanitizing buckets, 120 bottles of disinfectant water, and 5 boxes of hand-sanitizing powder, and other anti-pandemic materials to the King Grey community. The purpose of this donation is to help Liberia fight against the pandemic.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for national clinical reference laboratory
description: On March 6, 2018, the Chinese Government and the Government of Liberia signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) regarding funding for the construction and equipping of a National Clinical Reference Laboratory. The National Clinical Reference Laboratory will be built as an addition to the 14th Military Hospital, which is operated by the Liberian Ministry of National Defense, in Margibi County. It is set to be the ‘leading laboratory in West Africa’ according to the Chinese Embassy in Liberia.  Then, in January 2019, the Chinese Government and the Liberian Ministry of National Defense signed a technical agreement regarding the project. Then, in September 2022, Chinese Ambassador to Liberia Ren Yisheng announced that this project was in the tendering and procurement phase. According to the Liberian Ministry of National Defense, the laboratory will cost $20 million.

project_name: China donation of anti-Malaria drugs to Liberia
description: On January 25, 2011 the Chinese Ambassador to Liberia Zhou Yuxiao donated anti-malaria drugs on behalf of the Chinese Government. Bernice T Dahn, Deputy Minister for Health Services and Chief Medical Officer for the Ministry of Health accepted the donation. The medication was reported to be mostly Artosunate and Hydrochroide tablets.

project_name: China donated Covid-19 supplies to gov't of Liberia
description: On May 4, 2021, China donates 180 ventilators, 50 oxygen concentrators, 1800 full face masks, 500 tubing parts, 17,600 medical protective face masks and 100 infrared thermometers to help the Covid-19 crisis in Liberia. The Chinese Ambassador H.E. Ren Yisheng and Liberian President H.E. Dr. George Manneh Weah attended the handover ceremony.

project_name: Gov't donated the 3rd batch of anti-Covid-19 pandemic med. supplies
description: On July 13th, 2020, the Chargé d'affaires of the Chinese Embassy in Liberia, Xu Kun, handed over the anti-epidemic materials donated by China to Liberia. This donation included forehead thermometers, masks, and a batch of rice.  Professor Peng Liyuan donated the materials on behalf of the Chinese government to the office of the wife of the President of Liberia. Gaelle Mediem, Director of the Office of the First Lady of Lebanon, Sherdrick Jackson, Assistant Minister of Foreign Affairs of Lebanon, and Li Jiang, Economic and Commercial Counselor attended the ceremony.  This batch of materials is the third batch of anti-epidemic materials donated by the Chinese government to Liberia. It also supports Professor Peng Liyuan, wife of Chinese President Xi Jinping, in helping women, children, and adolescents in African countries, including Liberia, fight the pandemic. In addition to masks and forehead thermometers, the Chinese Embassy also donated a batch of rice. China will continue to firmly support Liberia's anti-pandemic development, implement the consensus reached by the two countries' leaders, and continuously advance the friendship between China and Liberia.

project_name: Embassy in Liberia donated Covid med. supplies & daily necessities
description: In November 2020, The Chinese Embassy in Liberia donated anti-pandemic medical supplies, and other daily necessities like grain and oil to government departments such as the Presidential Palace, the Vice Presidential Palace, Parliament, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, as well as the media, think tanks, civil organizations and other social circles in Liberia in batches.

project_name: Chinmed-16 provided 1st aid training to Liberians
description: In or around 2013, CHINMED-16, a Chinese medical team part of the UN Mission in Liberia, organized a two week-long training in First Aid for some 20 Liberian participants, including LNP officers, school administrators (including a teacher from the Tubman Wilson Institute in Zwedru), and students from various high schools in Zwedru. The participants were trained in ways to stop bleeding, dress wounds and deal with fractures, as well basic life support techniques, with the expectations they would share this knowledge and skills.

project_name: Gov't provided supplies to the National Public Health Institute
description: On January 11, 2021, the Chinese Government donated medical supplies to the National Public Health Institute of Liberia. The supplies included 9,090 packs of Ribavirin injections, 1,200 packs of Ribavirin tablets and 1,800 pieces of PPE. The purpose of this donation is to support the government of Liberia in tackling Lassa Fever. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the National Public Health Institute of Liberia’s offices located in Congo Town. China’s Ambassador to Liberia, Ren Yisheng, and the Director General of NPHIL, Jane MaCauley, attended the ceremony.

project_name: China donated a batch of Covid med. supplies to Ministry of Health
description: On September 23rd, 2020, The Political Counselor of the Chinese Embassy in Liberia, Xu Kun, and the Minister of Health of Liberia, Jala, jointly attended the handover ceremony for the donation of anti-COVID-19 pandemic materials held at the Overseas Chinese Chamber of Commerce in Liberia. The contents and value of the donation is unknown.  This batch of anti-pandemic material assistance from China is very timely and will help to enhance the nucleic acid detection capability of Lili and make every effort to prevent and control the COVID-19 pandemic.

project_name: China grants funds to survey construction project
description: On July 10, 2009, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Liberian Vice President Joseph Boakai witnessed the signing of an economic and technical cooperation agreement (ETCA #85176) granting 70 million RMB for multiple projects. Of that amount, 400,000 RMB was allocated to sending a Chinese technical team to survey the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare Construction Project in Congo Town. The survey was a success so the Chinese government later granted $4.2 million USD for construction of the new building (#1731).

project_name: Gov't donated equipment to Malaria prevention & treatment center
description: From April 22 to 25, 2010, a Chinese delegation, including the Deputy Minister of Commerce, Fu Ziying, carried out a four-day official visit to Liberia. Following bilateral discussions, a signing ceremony between the two governments took place for the provision of RMB 1.5 Million RMB in medical equipment for the China-Liberia Malaria Prevention and Treatment Center.  At the same ceremony, China donated RMB 3 Million worth of malaria medicines (#1727), medical supplies to Tappita Hospital (#1724), and signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) (#1723).

project_name: China donated $500,000 USD to liberia for anti-Malaria drugs
description: On June 28, 2013, Zhao Jianhua, Chinese Ambassador to Liberia, handed over US$500,000 anti-malaria drugs on behalf of the Chinese government, to Walter T. Gwenigale, Liberian Minister of Health and Social Welfare. Chinese Government also gave sophisticated medical equipment recently and provided drugs to the John F. Kennedy Hospital. Some Chinese medical experts are currently at the JFK Hospital assisting with health- related problems.

project_name: Donation of med. equipment to Jackson Doe referral hospital
description: On September 13, 2012, the Chinese government donated medical equipment and supplies valued at 1.5 million USD to the Liberian government for used at the Jackson F. Doe Memorial Referral Hospital in Tappita, Nimba County. The equipment includes a mammogram machine, transurethral resection of prostate sets, a urological surgery instrument parcel, an abdominal surgery operation parcel, Galactophore surgery operation parcel, among other items. As part of the agreement, Chinese experts helped to install the equipment.

project_name: China grants 2 million RMB to Liberia for anti-Malarial drugs
description: On July 10, 2009, Chinese and Liberian government officials signed an economic and technical cooperation agreement granting 70,000,000 RMB (ETCA #85176) for multiple projects. Of that total amount, 2 million RMB was allocated for purchasing anti-malaria drugs. This donation was delivered and officially handed over on January 28, 2010.

project_name: China provided med. testing for staff at Ministry of Youth & Sports
description: On January 11th, 2019, Chinese doctors visited the Ministry of Youth and Sports of Liberia to give medical examinations to members of the Ministry of Youth and Sports staff. These doctors were guests as a part of the Ministry of Youth and Sports Bamboo and Rattan program, which was funded by China (see Project ID#18816). 75 staff were treated for illnesses ranging from diseases, back pains, waist pains, and leg pains. They also were given medicine to treat their illnesses.

project_name: China agreed to train med. & technical personnel from Liberia
description: In March of 2011, Chinese Ambassador to Liberia Zhou Yuxiao announced that his government had begun reconstruction work on a new health ministry, and that China was also prepared to send five technicians and train 25 medical and technical personnel in China as obligations under the Tripartite Memorandum of Understanding signed with the Liberian and Egyptian governments. The Memorandum of Understanding was signed on February 1, 2011, on trilateral cooperation between Egypt, China and Liberia regarding running the Tappita Hospital in Liberia. It has been reported that 25 Chinese experts are in Liberia to jumpstart the management of the hospital.

project_name: China grants 1 million RMB worth of anti-Malarial drugs
description: On February 1, 2007, Chinese President Hu Jintao signed agreements to donate anti-malaria drugs to Liberia. On March 12, 2007, 1,000,000 RMB worth of anti-malaria drugs (93,840 doses) were donated to the Liberia-China Malaria Control Center at the John F. Kennedy Medical Center in Sinkor. The Charge d'affairs of the Chinese Embassy, Mr. Gou Haodong made the presentation of the drugs to the Deputy Minister and Chief medical officer of the Republic of Liberia, Dr. Bernice Dahn on behalf of his country. The Liberia-China Malaria Control Center is captured in #1631.

project_name: Gov't donated med. supplies to 14th military hospital
description: On July 2, 2020, the Government of the Peoples’ Republic of China (PRC) donated $3 million worth of drugs and equipment to the Liberian Ministry of National Defense for use by the 14th Military Hospital, located in Margibi County. Items donated include two intensive care unit ambulances, medical devices, laboratory equipment, emergency department equipment, obstetrics equipment, surgical equipment, and out-patient equipment.   Only a portion of the materials were donated on July 2. The rest arrived in Liberia on September 25, 2020. The purpose of the donation ws to help alleviate the shortage of medical supplies on the continent in Liberia. The Minister of National Defense, Major General Daniel D. Ziankahn, Jr., (Rtd) received the donation on behalf of the Commander-in-Chief of the AFL, President George M. Weah.   At the turnover ceremony of the medical equipment, the Chinese ambassador to Liberia, Ren Yisheng, promised the construction of a $20 million clinical reference lab (captured via Project ID#55600).    The 14th Military Hospital is used by the Liberian military and other sectors of society.

project_name: China grants 3 million RMB of anti-Malaria drugs
description:
On June 23, 2011, the Liberian government and the People’s Republic of China signed a bilateral agreement for the provision of 3 million RMB worth of anti-malaria drugs. The Chinese ambassador to Liberia, Zhao Jianhua signed the agreement, along with the Liberian Foreign Minister, Dr. Toga McIntosh.
 
 On March 21, 2012, 466 cartons of anti-malaria medicines were donated to Liberia through the Chinese Embassy for the 'fulfillment of an exchange of letters signed June 23, 2011 between the two governments.

project_name: China donated anti-Malaria & lassa fever medicine
description: On August 4, 2008, the Commercial Office of the Chinese Embassy in Liberia extended a donation of anti-malaria and lassa fever medicine, on behalf of the Chinese Ministry of Health, to the Liberian Ministry of Health and Social Welfare. The donation was initially pledged by the Chinese Deputy Minister of Health in February 2005, during a health delegation visit. 10,000 doses of artesunate and 2,100 boxes of ribavirin injection were donated. The value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't provided 3 ambulances
description: On September 30, 2021, the World Health Organization delivered three ambulances that had been financed by the Chinese government to eastern Libya. Two of the ambulances will go to the Emergency Health Centre of Benghazi, and one will go to the Ras Al-Helal Health Center.

project_name: Gov't provided USD 3,602,133 via WHO responding to Covid-19
description: In March 2020, Chinese government provides USD 3,602,133 to support WHO response to COVID-19 outbreak in Libya.

project_name: Ministry of Health offers med. training to combat Covid-19
description: On March 23, 2020, the Libyan Ministry of Health announced that the Chinese Ministry of Health formally offered to train Libyan doctors to combat COVID-19. The Chinese government proposed a training program for Libyan Ministry of Health officials administered by experienced Chinese doctors.   The Libyan Health Ministry stated that the training program will be conducted using "distance training techniques," including an introduction to the methods China has implemented to address its domestic outbreak of the coronavirus pandemic. The program will also provide training on ways to deal with the obstruction of the respiratory passages of infected patients.  It is unclear from the sources available whether the program was actually implemented. According to the Charge d'affaires ad interim of the Chinese embassy in Libya, Libyan experts did participate in virtual conferences held by the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Chinese National Health Commission.

project_name: Gov't donated anti-epidemic materials to ministry
description: On July 17, 2020, a handover ceremony was held for the donation of anti-epidemic materials from the Chinese government to the Libyan government. The purpose of the donation was to mitigate the spread of COVID-19 in Libya, particularly among women, children, and teenagers. The Chinese Charge d'Affaires to Libya, Wang Qimin, and the Libyan Charge d'Affaires to Tunisia, Mohamed Bin Mustafa, signed the handover certificate in Tunis, Tunisia. The exact materials donated are unknown.   This project is part of a larger initiative by the Chinese First Lady, Peng Liyuan. The initiative involved providing COVID relief supplies for vulnerable women and children to 53 African countries at the behest of the Organization of African First Ladies for Development.

project_name: Gov't donated anti-epidemic materials to the libyan gov't
description: On June 10, 2020, anti-Covid-19 materials donated by the Chinese government arrived at Carthage International Airport in Tunisia. On June 11, a handover ceremony was held for the donation at the Chinese Embassy in Tunisia. Chargé d'affaires ad interim of the Chinese embassy in Libya, Wang Qimin, and Chargé d'affaires ad interim of the Libyan embassy in Tunisia, Khalifa Azabi, signed the handover certificate.  The aid included 834 nucleic acid diagnostic kits, 5,000 medical protective suits, 15,000 N95 masks, 100,000 surgical masks, 5,000 goggles, and 5,000 pairs of medical gloves. The exact monetary value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't provided med. aid & training to Ministry of Health
description: In June 2018, Chinese Charge d'Affaires in Libya Wang Qimin and the UN-backed Libyan government's Health Minister Omar al-Tahir Bashir signed a $6,000,000 grant agreement for the provision medical aid and training after their meeting in the headquarters of the Libyan Ministry of Health, Tripoli.   The medical aid package arrived at the Port of Tripoli on May 20, 2018. As of June 11, 2018, the package had been delivered to Ministry of Health warehouses and was pending distribution to various cities and groups affected by displacement and those who had recently returned to the cities from where they were displaced (in particular, the city of Tawergha).   The proceeds of grant were also used to finance the training of Libyan technical personnel in specialized medical fields in China. The source of the grant funding for this project was China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and its China International Center for Economic and Technical Exchanges (CICETE).

project_name: Gov't provided grant to Libyan gov't for telemedicine & other support
description: On September 17, 2013, the Chinese Ambassador to Libya, Li Zhiguo, and the Minister of Health of the Libyan Interim Government, Noureddine Dagman, signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) (Chinese agreement name: 《中国与利比亚临时政府经济技术合作协定》) on behalf of their respective governments. The agreement committed an unspecified amount of Chinese grant funding for telemedicine and other forms of health sector support in Libya. According to the Economic and Commercial Office of the Chinese Embassy in Libya, this was the first unpaid assistance agreement between China and Libya in history.

project_name: Embassy donated Covid materials to the municipal gov't of Antananarivo
description: On April 2nd, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Madagascar donated anti-COVID-19 materials to the Municipal Government of Antananarivo in Madagascar. Ambassador Yang Xiaorong and Mayor Naina of Antananarivo attended a video conference for the donation, which included medicines and other unspecified materials. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donated 300,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: On September 24, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 300,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Madagascar.

project_name: Gov't donated batch of anti-Malarial drugs
description: On September 10th, 2013, the Chinese Government signed a handover certificate with the Malagasy Ministry of Health for the donation of a batch of anti-malaria medicines, according to the Chinese Ministry of Commerce. Chinese Ambassador Yang Min and Malagasy Minister of Health and Family Planning Joanita Naimananram attended the ceremony and signed the certificate.

project_name: Gov't donated batch of medicines & med. equipment
description:
On January 2, 2010, a handover ceremony for Chinese assistance to Madagascar of medicines and medical equipment was held in the capital Antananarivo. The Chinese Embassy in Madagascar and Madagascar Deputy Prime Minister responsible for the Public Health Service House chief of staff Amad attended the handover ceremony on behalf of their respective governments to sign the handover agreement. According to the agreement signed by the governments of the two countries, China annually sends to Madagascar batches of drugs and medical devices for the use of the Chinese medical team in Madagascar. 
 
 China's assistance to Madagascar medical team captain Zhongliang Ting told reporters, work in Madagascar, the 17th Chinese medical team of 30 people, work in four medical clinics across the country. The donated equipment went to those four sites: Ambovombe, Mahitsy, Sambava, and Vatomandry.

project_name: Gov't donated batch of medicines & med. equipment
description: On the April 17th, 2007, the Chinese government held a handover ceremony for the donation of medicines and medical equipment to the Malagasy Ministry of Health. The donation was committed to in 2006. Chinese Ambassador to Madagascar, Li Shuli, and the Malagasy Minister of Health and Family Planning, Jean-Louis Robinson, attended the ceremony and signed the handover agreement.  As part of a protocol signed by the two governments to send Chinese medical teams to Madagascar, the batch of medicines and medical equipment are distributed annually to the teams. These yearly package include the following projects: Chinese Government donates medicine and medical equipment to Madagascar in 2008 (#19694), in 2009 (#59711), in 2010 (#59716), and in 2016 (#59719).

project_name: Gansu province provided traditional Chinese medicine
description: In September of 2021, the Gansu Provincial Government donated RMB 700,000 worth of traditional Chinese medicine to Madagascar. The donation included four different types of medicine targeted: one designed to boost immune systems of susceptible people; one aimed to treat mild to severe cases of COVID-19; one for serious infections; and another to help patients recover.

project_name: Gov't provided anti-epidemic equipment
description: On August 27, 2021, the Chinese Government donated anti-epidemic equipment to the Government of Madagascar. The equipment included dual ultraviolet disinfection carts, visual laryngoscopes and portable phlegm aspirators. The purpose of this donation is to support Madagascar’s COVID-19 response efforts. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. China’s Ambassador to Madagascar, Guo Xiaomei, Madagascar’s Public Health Minister, Zely Arivelo, and other official members of Madagascar’s Ministry of Public Health attended the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for Malaria prevention & construction project
description: In 2009, the Chinese Government provided a $439,174 grant to the Government of Madagascar for the Malaria Prevention and Treatment Center Construction Project. The project involved the establishment of a Sino-Malagasy Center for Prevention and Fight Against Malaria (Centre Sino-Malagache de Prevention et De Lutte Contre Le Paludisme) at Befelatanana General Hospital in Antananarivo. The project officially commenced on the January 10, 2009. The center became operational on October 6, 2009.

project_name: Gov't donated batch of med. equipment to fight PLAgue
description: On November 8, 2017, the Chinese government handed over a shipment of medical equipment including cleaning, sanitation, and disease prevention supplies to two Madagascar districts in order to fight a plague outbreak. This is one of several donations made in 2017 from China to Madagascar; the Chinese government also sent medical experts to consult on the treatment and containment of the plague (#60995) and provided additional assistance (projects #58725, #58729).

project_name: Gov't donated batch of anti-Malarial drugs
description: In 2006, the Chinese Government donated a batch of anti-malarial drugs to the Malagasy Ministry of Health

project_name: Gov't donated batch of medicines & med. equipment
description: On May 18th, 2016, the Chinese government held a handover ceremony for the donation of medicines and medical equipment worth 100,000 USD to the Chinese Medical Team of Madagascar at the Ministry of Health. Malagasy Public Health Minister, Andrea Manaribu, and Economic and Commercial Counselor of the Chinese Embassy to Madagascar, Zhou Mansheng, attended the handover ceremony and signed the agreement. Chinese Ambassador to Madagascar Yang Xiaorong addressed the attending audience. At the Johannesburg Summit for the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation in December 2015, Chinese President Xi Jinping announced 10 cooperation programs, including the Public Health Program for which this project contributes toward.  As part of a protocol signed by the two governments to send Chinese medical teams to Madagascar, the batch of medicines and medical equipment are distributed annually to the teams. These yearly package include the following projects: Chinese Government donates medicine and medical equipment to Madagascar in 2007 (#59703), same project in 2008 (#19694),  in 2009 (#59711), in 2010 (#59716), in 2017 (#61023)

project_name: Embassy provided anti-epidemic supplies to hospitals in Amoron'i Mania
description: On April 21, 2021, the Chinese Embassy in Madagascar donated a batch of anti-epidemic materials to hospitals in the Amoron'i Mania region of Madagascar. The materials were donated to the National Assembly of Madagascar, who will then distribute them to the hospitals. The materials donated include ventilators, oxygen concentrators, forehead thermometers, medical masks, and KN95 masks. The purpose of this donation is to support local medical staff in their COVID-19 response efforts. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  An online handover ceremony was held for this donation. Guo Xiaomei, China’s Ambassador to Malaysia, Minister Counselor Zhang Wei of the Embassy, and the Speaker of the National Assembly of Madagascar jointly attended the ceremony.

project_name: Embassy donated Covid-19 supplies to Antananarivo municipal gov't
description: On June 21st, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Madagascar held a handover ceremony for donating anti-epidemic materials to the city government of Antananarivo, the capital of Madagascar. Ambassador Guo Xiaomei and Mayor Naina attended the ceremony together.   The Chinese Embassy donated medical equipment such as ventilators and oxygen generators to Antananarivo to help the city's pandemic prevention and control.

project_name: Gov't pledged loan to support university hospital system
description: In 2018, the Chinese Government pledged to provide three different loans, each worth MGA 300 million, to the Madagascar Ministry of Public Health to support the university hospital system. Project ID#60030 captures the MGA 300 million loan committed in 2019, Project ID#89056 captures the MGA 300 million loan committed in 2020, and Project ID#89057 captures the MGA 300 million loan committed in 2021. The borrowing terms are unknown. Implementation details are also unclear.  In 2018, the Chinese Government also provided a grant worth MGA 446 million for the same project (see Project ID #60031).

project_name: Gov't provided grant for the Anosiala Hospital technical project
description: On January 12, 2015, the Chinese Government signed a grant agreement with the Government of Madagascar for Phase 1 of the Anosiala Hospital Technical Cooperation Project. According to the Government of Madagascar’s Aid Management Platform, the Chinese Government officially committed $2,880,204 of grant funding for this project. This project involved the dispatching Chinese technicians to help maintain Anosiala University Hospital, which was constructed with a separate grant from the Chinese Government (captured in Project ID#53131). It is also linked to #72748, the $1,979,282 grant from the Chinese government for the phase 2 of the project.

project_name: Gansu Tcm Hospital donated medicines & materials to medicine center
description: On September 2, 2019, the Chinese Ambassador to Madagascar, Yang Xiaorong, signed a project agreement with Malagasy Health Minister Rakutunilina for the Chinese Government to fund the development of the China-Madagascar Traditional Chinese Medicine Center (中国—马达加斯加中医中心) (see linked ProjectID#89163). The center would be part of Anosiala University Hospital Center (French: Centre Hospitalier Universitaire Anosiala), in Ambohidratrimo, on the outskirts of Antananarivo. The center will spread information on traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) and carry out activities such as itinerant clinics in Madagascar. The financing structure supporting this project is uncertain, but the center was eventually unveiled on November 5, 2019, by Chinese Vice Premier Sun Chunlan, while on a state visit to Madagascar.  According to a press release by the Gansu Provincial Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, on February 1, 2021, the Gansu TCM hospital provided 860,000 yuan-worth of prepared Chinese medicines and epidemic prevention materials to the center (see ProjectID#89163). The medicines included Duzhong Yaotong Pills, Fuzheng Biwen Pills, Fangfengganmao Granules, Damage Capsules, Bu Nao Ointment, and Xiaoding Ointment among others. The hospital also sent Chinese medicine experts to carry out personnel training, technology promotion, and free medical consultations. Since 1975, China's Gansu Province has sent medical teams to Madagascar and has additionally provided medical supplies for the teams to use.

project_name: Gov't donated cleaning tools to city of Antananarivo, Madagascar
description: On October 9, 2018, the Chinese Ambassador to Madagascar, Yang Xiaorong, attended a ceremony commemorating the donation of cleaning tools to Madagascar's capital city, Antananarivo, and the six districts under its jurisdiction. Based on pictures provided by the Chinese Embassy, the cleaning supplies included wheelbarrows and shovels.   The donation is a continuation of the Chinese Government's assistance to Madagascar to combat plague in Madagascar. Plague is endemic in Madagascar and cases are reported each year in bubonic and pneumonic forms.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for phase 2 of the Anosiala hospital project
description: On January 16, 2017, the Chinese Government signed a grant agreement with the Government of Madagascar for Phase 2 of the Anosiala Hospital Technical Cooperation Project. According to the Government of Madagascar’s Aid Management Platform, the Chinese Government officially committed $1,979,282 of grant funding for this project. This project involved the dispatching Chinese technicians to help maintain Anosiala University Hospital, which was constructed with a separate grant from the Chinese Government (captured in Project ID#53131).  It is also linked to #72747, the $2,880,204 grant from the Chinese government for the phase 1 of the project.

project_name: Gov't donated 2nd batch of anti-Covid-19 pandemic materials
description: On July 13th, 2020, a donation ceremony for the second batch of anti-pandemic materials was held at the Chinese Embassy in Madagascar. Minister Naharimamy, the Minister of Population, Social Protection and Promotion of Women, Chinese Ambassador Yang Xiaorong, and Brigadier General Elack Andriankaja, General Coordinator of COVID-19, were in attendance. The donation was made to the Fitia association, a charitable organization founded by Mialy Rajoelina Razakandisa, wife of Andry Rajoelina, the president of Madagascar. The grant was organized on the initiative of Peng Liyuan, the first lady of China, and was given by the Chinese government through the the African First Ladies Federation for Development (OAFLAD).   This batch of supplies included medical masks, forehead thermometers, and 7.5 tons of rice. The first donation was in May 2020 (see project ID#91877), and the third batch was handed over in August 2020 (see project ID#91912).

project_name: Gov't provided grant for provision of medicines to Ministry of Health
description: In 2006, the Chinese Government provided a grant to the Government of Madagascar for the provision of medicines to Madagascar’s Ministry of Health. This project was completed and officially handed over to the Malagasy authorities on April 28, 2006.

project_name: Gov't donated 3rd batch Covid-19 med. supplies
description: On August 19th, 2020, China donated 30 respirators and 20,000 PCR test kits to Madagascar. Chen Xiaolei, Chargé d'Affaires of the Chinese Embassy in Madagascar, went to Iwatu International Airport in Antananarivo to attend the handover ceremony of the anti-epidemic materials. Duval Solofomanana, the secretary-general of Madagascar's Ministry of Health, was also present at the handover ceremony.  The first batch was received in May 2020 (see project ID#91877), and the second batch was received in July 2020 (see project ID#91915)

project_name: Gov't donated a batch of anti-Malarial drugs
description: On June 8th and June 30th, 2014, the Chinese Government donated a batch of anti-malaria medicine to the Malagasy Ministry of Health. Chinese Ambassador Yang Min and Malagasy Foreign Minister Beatrice Jeanin Attara attended the exchange in Antananarivo.

project_name: Embassy donated Covid-19 supplies to 3 hospitals in Tamatave region
description: On April 29th, 2021, the Chinese Embassy in Madagascar donated a batch of anti-pandemic materials to three hospitals in the Tamatave region to support local medical staff in their fight against the COVID-19 pandemic. The donation ceremony was held online.  The materials donated by the Chinese Embassy to Analankininina Hospital, Morafeno Hospital, and Mahivagna Medical Center in Tamataf this time include ventilators, oxygen generators, forehead thermometers, medical masks, KN95 masks, etc.

project_name: Gov't donated 1st batch of anti-Covid-19 pandemic med. supplies
description: On May 2, 2020, the Chinese Ambassador to Madagascar Yang Xiaorong went to Ivato International Airport to attend the handover ceremony of the first batch of anti-pandemic material projects from the Chinese government to Madagascar. He signed the project handover certificate with the Madagascar Minister of Public Health Ahmad Amhad on behalf of the two governments. Minister of Transport of Madagascar, Deputy Secretary-General of the Presidential Office, and Economic and Commercial Counselor Liang Shaomin attended the ceremony. According to FOCAC,  the donation included surgical and N95-type masks, protective suits, thermometers, goggles, gloves and shoe covers for health professionals. The monetary value of the donation was not specified.     The second donation was received in July 2020 (see project ID#91915), and the third donation was received in August 2020 (see project ID#91912).

project_name: Gov't provided grant to Anosiala Uni Hospital Center constr. project
description: In 2013, the Chinese Government provided an RMB 120 million grant to the Government of Madagascar for the Anosiala University Hospital Center Construction Project. This project involved the construction of a hospital with 150 beds, an X-ray machine, CT scanner, biochemical analyzer, and anesthesia machine. The 8,700 square meter project site is located in the city of Anosiala within Manakara District and Vatovavy-Fitovinany Region. Société de l’économie extérieure et de construction de Madagascar (Sogecoa), a branch of the Anhui Foreign Economic Construction Group (a Chinese state-owned company) was responsible for project implementation. According to the Chinese Embassy in Madagascar, the Chinese Government disbursed $13.5 million in support of this project in 2013 and 2014. The Government of Madagascar's Aid Management Platform (AMP) records $13,467,200 as the total amount of grant funding disbursed for this project as of September 30, 2014.  The project officially commenced on July 25, 2013 and it passed inspection on September 10, 2014. Then, on September 19, 2014, the Chinese Government and the Government Madagascar signed the project handover certificate. An official hospital opening ceremony took place on June 24, 2015. Since its construction, the Chinese Government has stationed Chinese medical teams at this hospital (see Project ID#60028 and Project ID#72728). Through two separate grants for Phase 1 and Phase 2 of the Anosiala Hospital Technical Cooperation Project, the Chinese Government has deployed Chinese technicians to help maintain Anosiala University Hospital (see Project ID#72747 and #72748).

project_name: Gov't agreed to develop TCM center
description: On September 2, 2019, the Chinese Ambassador to Madagascar, Yang Xiaorong, signed a project agreement with Malagasy Health Minister Rakutunilina to develop the China-Madagascar Traditional Chinese Medicine Center (中国—马达加斯加中医中心). The center would be part of Anosiala University Hospital Center (French: Centre Hospitalier Universitaire Anosiala), in Ambohidratrimo, on the outskirts of Antananarivo. The center will spread information on traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) and carry out activities such as itinerant clinics in Madagascar. The financing structure supporting this project is uncertain although one source reports the National Health Commission of China and the Ministry of Health of Madagascar will be cooperating on the project.  According to a press release by the Gansu Provincial Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, the Gansu TCM hospital provided 860,000 yuan-worth of prepared Chinese medicines and epidemic prevention materials to the center (see linked ProjectID#89164). The medicines included Duzhong Yaotong Pills, Fuzheng Biwen Pills, Fangfengganmao Granules, Damage Capsules, Bu Nao Ointment, and Xiaoding Ointment among others. The hospital also sent Chinese medicine experts to carry out personnel training, technology promotion, and free medical consultations. Since 1975, China's Gansu Province has sent medical teams to Madagascar and has additionally provided medical supplies for the teams to use.  The center was unveiled and inaugurated on November 5, 2019, by Chinese Vice Premier Sun Chunlan, while on a state visit to Madagascar.

project_name: Gov't donated batch of anti-Malarial drugs
description: On July 28, 2007, the Chinese Government and the Government of Madagascar signed an RMB 2 million grant agreement for the provision of anti-malarial drugs. Then, on August 14, 2008, the Chinese Government held a handover ceremony for a batch of anti-malaria drugs to the Malagasy Ministry of Health. A total of 183,440 cases of Artesunate and Amodiaquine Tablets were provided. The Chinese Ambassador and Malagasy Minister of Health and Family Planning attended the ceremony and signed the handover certificate.

project_name: Gov't donated batch of anti-Malarial drugs
description: On June 14, 2007, the Chinese Government delivered a batch of anti-malarial drugs to the Malagasy Ministry of Health. The medicine includes 39,940 doses of Dihydroartemisinin and Piperaquine Phosphate T and 41,000 boxes of Artesunate and Amodiaquine tablets. The donation ceremony was attended by Chinese Ambassador to Madagascar Li Shu-li and Malagasy Minister of Family Planning Jean-Louis Robson, who signed the handover certificates on behalf of their respective governments.

project_name: Gov't donated batch of medicines & med. equipment
description: On November 13, 2012, the Chinese government held a ceremony to officially donate a batch of drugs and medical equipment to Madagascar. The donation is meant to strengthen the relationship between China and Madagascar, and to further China's goal of improving healthcare in Madagascar. The value of the donation is not included in the official source.

project_name: Gov't donated batch of medicines & med. equipment
description: On November 26th, 2010, the Chinese government held a handover ceremony for the donation of medicines and medical equipment to the Chinese Medical Team of Madagascar at the Ministry of Health. The donation is valued at 1.28 million RMB. Economic and Commercial Counselor of the Chinese Embassy to Madagascar, Zhou Mansheng, and Secretary General of the Malagasy Ministry of Health, Mr. Lakutumanga, attended the handover ceremony and signed the agreement.   As part of a protocol signed by the two governments to send Chinese medical teams to Madagascar, the batch of medicines and medical equipment are distributed annually to the teams. These yearly package include the following projects: Chinese Government donates medicine and medical equipment to Madagascar in 2007 (#59703), in 2008 (#19694), in 2009 (#59711), and in 2016 (#59719).

project_name: Gov't donated batch of medicines & med. equipment
description: On January 3rd, 2008, the Chinese government held a handover ceremony for the donation of medicines and medical equipment to the Malagasy Ministry of Health. The donation was committed in 2007. Minister of Health Jean-Louis Robinson and Chinese Ambassador Wo Ruidi attended the ceremony and signed the handover agreement. These drugs and equipment are used in four medical clinics in the country.  As part of a protocol signed by the two governments to send Chinese medical teams to Madagascar, the batch of medicines and medical equipment are distributed annually to the teams. These yearly package include the following projects: Chinese Government donates medicine and medical equipment to Madagascar in 2007 (#59703), in 2009 (#59711), in 2010 (#59716), and in 2016 (#59719).

project_name: Embassy donated a batch of anti-Covid med. supplies to Diana Region
description: On February 9th, 2021, the Chinese Ambassador to Madagascar Guo Xiaomei, and the Diana Region Chief Executive Daodo attended the video conference on the donation of anti-pandemic medical supplies by the Chinese Embassy to the Diana Region, Madagascar.  The Chinese Embassy donated masks, goggles, protective clothing, and other anti-pandemic materials to the Diana region. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donated med. equipment as part of action brilliant campaign
description: On June 6, 2018, a Memorandum of Understanding was signed between Chinese Ambassador to Madagascar Yang Xiaorong, and Madagascar's Minister of Public Health, Lalatiana Andriamanarivo, in which the Chinese Government agreed to a donation of $250,000 USD in medical equipment to the Malagasy Ministry of Public Health. The equipment was handed over on the same day.  This donation was part of the 2 week long "Action Brilliant" campaign that began in Antananarivo on May 31st, 2018 to offer free cataract treatment in the country. The equipment will be left in the Joseph Ravoahangy Andrianavalona Hospital. The Action Brilliant campaign may also be known as Bright Journey Project or Brightness Action campaign. As part of the program, 11 ophthalmic experts from China were sent to the capital in 2017 (see linked ProjectID#60024).

project_name: Gov't pledged loan to support university hospital system
description: In 2018, the Chinese Government pledged to provide three different loans, each worth MGA 300 million, to the Madagascar Ministry of Public Health to support the university hospital system. Project ID#60030 captures the MGA 300 million loan committed in 2019, Project ID#89056 captures the MGA 300 million loan committed in 2020, and Project ID#89057 captures the MGA 300 million loan committed in 2021. The borrowing terms are unknown. Implementation details are also unclear.  In 2018, the Chinese Government also provided a grant worth MGA 446 million for the same project (see Project ID #60031).

project_name: Gov't donated a batch of supplies to fight Yersinia Pestis Plague
description:
On October 12th, 2017, China donated a package of medical supplies worth 220,000 USD to the Malagasy Ministry for Public Health to fight the Yersinia pestis plague which, at the time, had resulted in 57 fatalities. Chinese Ambassador to Madagascar Yang Xiaorong spoke at the ceremony held in Antananarivo. The package, which includes medical equipment, antibiotics, clothing, masks, and protective gloves, was ready to use immediately. A November 2017 report by ReliefWeb noted that 220,000 USD in medicines were received by the Malagasy government.
 
 The leader of the 21st Chinese medical team (project #60028) attended the ceremony. This is part of a protocol signed by the two governments to regularly dispatch Chinese medical teams to Madagascar. A few days before this ceremony, the leader of the 21st medical team also gave a public lecture on plague prevention at the Chinese Embassy in Madagascar (project #61025).
 
 This is linked to projects #58725, #60995, and #60996.

project_name: Women's group of embassy hosts lecture on chinese traditional medicine
description: On May 11, 2018, the Women's Group of the Chinese Embassy in Madagascar invited Chinese medicine experts to hold a lecture on Chinese medicine health care at the embassy. The objectives of the lecture were to increase the medical knowledge of the audience and to promote understanding of traditional Chinese medicine. Chinese medicine experts introduced the pathogenesis of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases, diabetes and other common diseases and the knowledge of daily disease prevention and health care, and used manual therapy on the spot to diagnose and treat. Participants said that the lecture was practical, interesting, and not only enhanced the awareness of fitness and disease prevention, but also deepened their understanding of Chinese culture.

project_name: Gov't donated batch of medicines & med. equipment
description: On December 29th, 2009, the Chinese government held a handover ceremony for the donation of medicines and medical equipment to the 17th Chinese Medical Team of Madagascar at the Ministry of Health. The medical team includes 30 members working in four Malagasy medical centers. Commercial Counsellor of the Chinese Embassy to Madagascar, Mr. Zhou Mansheng, and Director of the Office of the Deputy Prime Minister of Public Health, Amade Amade, attended the ceremony.   As part of a protocol signed by the two governments to send Chinese medical teams to Madagascar, the batch of medicines and medical equipment are distributed annually to the teams. These yearly package include the following projects: Chinese Government donates medicine and medical equipment to Madagascar in 2007 (#59703), in 2008 (#19694), in 2010 (#59716), and in 2016 (#59719)

project_name: Embassy & association jointly donate supplies to hospital
description: On August 26, 2021, the Chinese Embassy in Madagascar and the Association of Former Malagasy Students in China jointly donated medical supplies to Mahitsy Hospital.  Ambassador Guo Xiaomei attended the donation ceremony online. The donation consisted of 4 respirators, 4 oxygen concentrators, 10 forehead thermometers, 2000 masks surgical masks and 500 KN95 masks. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Embassy donated anti-Covid-19 supplies to the gov't of Antananarivo
description: On January 20, 2021, the Chinese Embassy in Madagascar donated anti-epidemic supplies to the government of Antananarivo, the capital of Madagascar. The contents and monetary value of the donation are unknown.

project_name: Gov't donated supplies to Dep of Disaster Management Affairs in Malawi
description: On August 11, 2020, the Chinese Government donated medical supplies to Malawi to assist health workers in the fight against COVID-19. The donated supplies included 150,000 surgical masks, 15,000 N95 masks, 7,000 protective clothing, 7,000 goggles, 7,000 pairs of gloves and 300 pairs of shoe covers.  The medical supplies were handed over to the Malawi Department of Disaster Management Affairs (DODMA) in Lilongwe by Chinese Embassy’s Deputy Chief Wang Xiusheng. The supplies were received by the Chair of the Malawi Presidential COVID taskforce Dr. John Phuka.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for hospital & cancer centre construction project
description: On October 12, 2015, the Chinese government granted $23 million for the construction of the Blantyre District Hospital and Cancer Centre, located in Kameza within the Blantyre District of Malawi. According to the Business and Economics source, construction of the hospital and cancer center began in 2016. Construction status and details are unknown.

project_name: Gov't grants med. supplies to Kamuzu Central Hospital
description: On October 17, 2013, the Chinese government granted pharmaceutical equipment to Kamuzu Central Hospital in Lilongwe. The value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donated batch of anti-epidemic supplies to Malawi
description: On September 27, 2020, a batch of anti-epidemic supplies donated by the Chinese government arrived in Malawi. The two parties held a handover ceremony at the Kamuzu International Airport in Lilongwe, the capital of Malawi. The Economic and Commercial Counselor of the Chinese Embassy in Malawi, Liu Guoyu, and the Deputy Minister of Health of Malawi, Chrissie Kanyasho, attended the event. Officials from the Malawian Disaster Management Agency were also in attendance. Counselor Liu Guoyu and Deputy Minister Kanyasho signed the handover certificate for this batch of anti-epidemic medical supplies on behalf of the governments of China and Malawi.   The donation was valued at USD 1,000,000 and included 20,000 test kits and 30 ventilators, which were to be distributed to hospitals. The supplies arrived in Malawi on the same chartered plane as a Chinese medical team (see project #88336).

project_name: Embassy grants med. equipment worth to Kamuzu Central Hospital
description: On September 6, 2016, the Chinese embassy granted medical equipment worth 35 million Kwacha to Kamuzu Central Hospital in Lilongwe, Malawi.

project_name: Embassy provided grant for construction of mother & baby ward
description: On June 23, 2010, the Chinese embassy provided a small grant for the construction of a mother and baby ward at a rural health clinic in Southern Malawi. The amount of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for Mzuzu central hospital CT scan room project
description: In 2021, the Chinese Government provided a $30 million grant to the Government of Malawi for the construction of a computerized tomography (CT) scan room at Mzuzu Central Hospital and other unspecified activities. The Mzuzu Central Hospital Computerised Tomography (CT) Scan Room Construction Project was completed on December 14, 2021.

project_name: Embassy donated anti-epidemic supplies to CHAM
description: On June 1, 2020, a handover ceremony was held in which the Chinese Embassy handed over personal protection equipment to the Christian Health Association of Malawi (CHAM). The ceremony was held at the Chinese Embassy. The Political Counselor of the Chinese Embassy in Malawi Wang Xinsheng, the Executive Director of CHAM Happy Makala, and Ethel Kapyepye, the Chief Director in the Ministry of Health responsible for safe motherhood and maternal health, attended the event and delivered speeches. Nearly 50 people, including officials from the Malawi Ministry of Health, CHAM representatives, media reporters, and embassy staff also attended the event.  According to The Nation, the donated materials included 5,000 face masks and 2,500 hospital caps. These materials donated by China will be distributed to medical staff at the 179 health facilities run by CHAM across Malawi.

project_name: Embassy donated epidemic prevention materials to Amitabha Care Center
description: On August 4, 2021, the Chinese Embassy in Malawi donated a batch of epidemic prevention materials to the Amitabha Care Center (ACC). The USD value of the donation is unknown. The donation will be used to help Malawi protect the health and safety of its people.

project_name: Gov't donated med. supplies to malawi's 3 major hospitals
description: On April 24, 2020, a handover ceremony was held for the donation of medical supplies from the Chinese government to Malawi’s three major hospitals. The hospitals were Lilongwe Kamuzu Central Hospital, Blantyre Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital, and Mzuzu Central Hospital. The handover ceremony was held at the Chinese Embassy in Lilongwe, Malawi.  Chinese Ambassador Liu Hongyang, the mayors of Lilongwe, Blantyre, and Mzuzu, and the directors of Lilongwe Kamuzu Central Hospital, Blantyre Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital, and Mzuzu Central Hospital were in attendance. Nearly 50 other people including media reporters, embassy staff, and Chinese medical workers also attended the event.  Each of the three central hospitals were to get 10,000 disposable medical masks, 7,000 surgical masks, 300 N95 masks, 300 sets of protective suits and goggles, 1,000 pairs of gloves and 20 thermometers while each of the three city's councils were to get 2,000 disposable medical masks and 2 infrared thermometers.

project_name: Congress of China donated anti-epidemic materials to Malawi parliament
description: On April 29, 2020, Ambassador Liu Hongyang and Malawi Speaker of Parliament Catherine Gotani Hara jointly attended a handover ceremony for a donation of COVID-19 prevention materials from the Chinese National People's Congress to the Malawi Parliament. The donated materials included 1,000 masks and 2 infrared thermometers. The masks were intended for the use of members of parliament and parliament staff.  The ceremony took place at the August House in Lilongwe.

project_name: 1st Lady of China donated anti-epidemic supplies to 1st Lady of Malawi
description: On July 28, 2020, a ceremony was held at the Kamuzu Presidential Palace for the donation of anti-epidemic materials to Malawi's First Lady, Monica Chakwera, on the behalf of China’s First Lady Peng Liyuan.  Chinese Ambassador to Malawi, Liu Hongyang, the First Lady of Malawi, and Malawi’s Minister of Health attended the ceremony and delivered speeches. The supplies, which included thermometers and face masks, are intended to help mothers, youths, and health workers.  The donation was made at the behest of the Organization of African First Ladies for Development and was part of a larger donation initiative of COVID supplies to 53 African countries.   The Political Counselor of the Chinese Embassy in Malawi and the Malawi Minister of Health signed the handover certificate for the anti-epidemic materials on behalf of the two governments.

project_name: Ministry of Health donated Malarial drugs to Salima Regional Hospital
description: On April 21, 2017, the Chinese Ministry of Health granted 58 million kwacha of antimalarial drugs (specifically artemisinin) to the Salima Regional Hospital, according to China MOFCOM and Nyssa Times. It appears to be a one-time donation.

project_name: China donated med. supplies to the shaping our future foundation
description: On December 3, 2021, the Chinese Government donated K40 million in medical supplies to the First Lady's Shaping Our Future Foundation in Malawi. The donation occurred at a handover ceremony which was held at the Presidential Palace of Malawi. Ambassador Liu Hongyang, President Ma's wife Monica Chakwila, and Vice Minister of Health Chrissy Kanyasho attended the ceremony and delivered speeches.  The donation will be used to protect the health of Malawian citizens and will be distributed to health facilities across the country. During the ceremony, the Chinese Government also donated K24 million (Project ID#97702) to the foundation to support girls' education.

project_name: Gov't donated med. equipment & drugs to Malawi hospitals
description: On February 1, 2018, the Chinese government donated medical equipment and other supplies worth 129 million Kwacha to Kamuzu Central Hospital and Mzuzu Central Hospital. The ceremony was held at the Malawi Ministry of Health, with Ambassador Shi Ting Wang, Minister of Health Atupule Muluzi, and Deputy Inspector Of the Shaanxi Provincial Health and Planning Commission Han Rongchao attending the ceremony and delivering speeches. The delegation of the Shaanxi Provincial Health and Planning Commission along with members of the current medical team, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Health and representatives of public hospitals participated. During the ceremony, Chinese Ambassador Wang said the Chinese Government donates to Kamuzu Central and Mzuzu Central Hospitals annually.

project_name: Embassy donated med. supplies to gov't of Malawi
description: On February 4, 2021, the handover ceremony of medical supplies donated by the Chinese Embassy to the Malawi government was held at the Malawi Ministry of Health. Ambassador Liu Hongyang and Malawi’s Minister of Health Kumbize Chiponda attended the ceremony and delivered speeches. The Deputy Minister of Health of Malawi and the Permanent Secretary also attended the event.

project_name: Embassy grants maternity room at Salima Regional Hospital
description:
On September 25, 2013, the foundation stone laying ceremony was held for a 36 bed maternity room granted by the Chinese embassy at the Salima Regional Hospital in Malawi, according to the Chinese Embassy. It is part of the “Prepare Maternal and Child Plan” for Malawi, run by Malawi's government. The project was funded through a 30 million kwacha grant. An article from The Nation reports that the room was completed and handed over on June 19, 2014.
 
 This project was encouraged by the Malawi government Presidential Initiative on Maternal Health and Safe Motherhood.

project_name: Peking Uni builds research & teaching base of School of Public Health
description: On November 21, 2017, an unveiling ceremony was held for the Malawi Research and Teaching Base of Peking University School of Public Health. The establishment of this public health campus was co-financed by the Malawi Participatory Rural Development Organisation (PRDO) and by Peking University School of Public Health. The commitment date of the project is unclear.

project_name: Embassy donated med. supplies to Ministry of Health
description: On November 2, 2020, a handover ceremony for medical supplies donated by the Chinese Embassy in Malawi was held at the Malawian Ministry of Health. Ambassador Liu Hongyang and Minister of Health of Malawi, Khumbize Chiponda, attended the ceremony and delivered speeches. Major officials of the Ministry of Health of Malawi and representatives of the Chinese medical team in Malawi also attended the event. It is unclear exactly what materials were donated.

project_name: Embassy granted anesthesia machine to Lilongwe Central Hospital
description: On November 10, 2009, the Chinese embassy donated an anesthesia machine to Lilongwe Central Hospital in Malawi, according to the Chinese Embassy in Malawi and MOFCOM. The value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't sent students to study hospital management in China
description: On May 4, 2017, the Chinese embassy held a reception to welcome back 25 Malawian students that the Chinese government had funded to study hospital management in China.  The reception was attended by Ambassador Wang, Director General of the Malawi Ministry of Health Chisa Miller, and other officials from the Ministry of Health.  The value of this training is unknown.

project_name: China donated anti-epidemic materials & med. equipment
description: On June 2, 2021, the Chinese government donated the fourth batch of anti-epidemic materials and medical equipment to Malawi. The donation was performed during a handover ceremony at the Malaysian Ministry of Health. The USD value of the donation is unknown.   The donation is part of the China-Africa Counterpart Hospital Cooperation Mechanism. Liu Hongyang, the Chinese ambassador to Malawi, and Kumbize Chiponda, the Minister of Health of Malawi, attended the ceremony. Li Xiaogang, the captain of the Chinese medical team to Malawi, and Mwasabbo, the permanent secretary of the Ministry of Health of Malawi, also attended the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't donated med. equipment & drugs Ministry of health
description: On January 24, 2019 the Chinese government donated medical equipment and drugs worth 700,000 RMB to the Malawi Ministry of Health.  A donation ceremony was held at the Ministry of Health, attended by Chinese Ambassador Liu Hongyang, Minister of Health at Aupelle Muluzi, Malawian health officials, and representatives of two of the most famous public hospitals in Malawi. The donation of medical devices and medicines adds to the continuous medical assistance given to Malawi by the Chinese government since the establishment of diplomatic ties between the two countries.

project_name: Embassy donated epidemic materials to UNHCR office to support refugees
description: On June 3, 2021, the Embassy in Malawi held a handover ceremony for the donation of epidemic prevention materials to the UNHCR Representative Office in Malawi. The donation will be used for the protection of Malawi refugees. The USD value of the donation is unknown.   The ceremony was attended by Liu Hongyang, Ambassador to Malawi, and Modeste Kuameh, the representative of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees in Malawi.

project_name: Gov't donated anti-epidemic materials to Malawi
description: On March 31, 2020, the handover ceremony for the anti-epidemic materials donated by the Chinese government to Malawi was held at the Kamuzu International Airport in Lilongwe. Chinese Ambassador Liu Hongyang and Malawian Minister of Disaster Management Everton Chimulirenji attended the event and delivered speeches. Nearly 50 people also attended the event, including officials from the Ministry of Disaster Affairs, media reporters and airport staff.   Before the ceremony, Ambassador Liu distributed masks to event attendees to remind everyone to take protective measures. After the event, Ambassador Liu also accepted a joint interview with media from China and Malawi.  The materials donated included protective face masks, disposable medical protective clothes, infrared thermometers, protective medical goggles, sterilized surgical gloves and medical isolation shoes.

project_name: Nanning municipal gov't donated med. supplies to Lilongwe
description: Sometime between March to April 2020, Nanning Municipal Government donated medical supplies to the city of Lilongwe, Malawi.

project_name: China donated 230 million CFA Francs of anti-Malarial medicine
description:
On February 12, 2009, Chinese President Hu Jintao and Minister of Commerce Chen Deming signed an agreement to donate a batch of anti-malarial drugs to Mali on behalf of the Chinese government.  The drugs were delivered at a handover ceremony on November 10, 2009.  The Counsellor of the Economic and Commercial Office of the Embassy of Mali, the Director of the General Office of the Ministry of Health of Mali, the Director of Medicine, and the head of the Mali medical team attended the ceremony.  The donation included 230 million CFA francs of antimalarial drugs. 
 
 The donation also included equipment and medicines worth 50 million CFA francs to be delivered to Kati Hospital (See Project #30664) and equipment and medicines worth 85 million CFA francs for the use of the Chinese medical mission hospitals in Kati, Sikasso and Markala (See Project #30665).

project_name: N-sukala donated alcoholic solution for the fight against Covid
description: On April 27, 2020, N-Sukala, a Chinese-owned sugar and alcohol production company, donated 10,000 liters of a self-produced alcoholic solution to Mali's Department of Health and Welfare as part of the fight against COVID-19. N-Sukala is a subsidiary of Sinolight Holdings, which is itself a subsidiary of China Poly Group, a state owned enterprise.  A handover ceremony was held. In attendance were Zheng Yining, deputy general manager of Sinolight Holdings, Chinese Ambassador to Mali Zhu Liying, Mali's Minister of Industry and Trade, Mohamed Ag Erlaf, and Mali's Minister of Health, Michel Hamala Sidibé.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for Malaria prevention & control center
description: On April 18, 2008, the Chinese and Malian governments signed an exchange of notes on the establishment of an anti-malaria center at the National Hospital of Kati in the town of Kati. The China-Mali Malaria Prevention and Control Center, which was built with the grant assistance from the Chinese Government, was officially launched by President Hu Jintao of China and the President of Mali at a ceremony on February 13, 2009. The monetary value of the grant commitment for this center is unknown.   Upon the establishment of the anti-malaria center, it was envisaged that Chinese experts could test the facilities, exchange ideas with local specialists, and provide technical training to medical staff. The Chinese Government also agreed to donate anti-malarial drugs and equipment over a period of three years following the establishment of the center.

project_name: China donated Covid-19 nucleic acid testing reagents to Mali
description: On February 25, 2021, the Chinese Government donated 20,000 nucleic acid testing reagents to the Mali Ministry of Health and Social Development. The reagents are to be used to detect COVID-19 in Mali. The Chinese Ambassador to Mali and Mali's Minister of Health and Social Development signed the handover certificate on behalf of their governments.

project_name: China donated 3 million CNY of antiMalarial drugs
description:
On June 1, 2012, the Malian Minister of State, Mr. Sadio Lamine Sow, signed an agreement with the Ambassador of the People's Republic of China to Mali, Mr. Cao Zhang Ming. The agreement included a donation of antimalarial drugs worth 3 million CNY, or 210 million CFA francs (XOF).  The drugs were handed over on December 19th by Chinese Ambassador Cao Zhongming to Malian Health Minister Diallo Madeleine Ba.  
 
 At the same time, the Chinese government donated 3,000 tonnes of grain (Project #30228).

project_name: China donated antiMalarial drugs to Mali
description: On April 19, 2007, the Director of the Office of the Minister of Health of Mali, Mr. Simaka, and the Secretary-General of the Ministry and the Commercial Counsellor of the Embassy of Malaysia, Zhang Youhua, signed the handover certificate for the Chinese government's donation antimalarial drugs to Mali's Ministry of Health. Members of China's current medical mission to Mali, the 19th Medical Team, were in attendance (Project #60170). The drugs were previously delivered to Bamako in February and distributed to several medical facilities in Mali.

project_name: China donated 80 million XOF to Mali in med. materials for Ebola
description: In September 2014, China donated XOF 80 million francs worth of Ebola prevention materials to Mali. The donation included 1,000 sprays, 1,000 protective gears, 30 medically-equipped isolation tents, 600 protective masks, 600 shoes and 1,000 thermometers.

project_name: China donated med. supplies to the Mali hospital
description: On February 6, 2013, China donated $527,280.28 worth of medical supplies to the Mali hospital. The donation included an ambulance, radiography equipment, ultrasound facilities, and other advanced medical equipment.

project_name: China donated $380,000 of med. equipment
description: On October 21st, 2008, a ceremony was held in Bamako to celebrate the 40th anniversary of medical cooperation between China's Zhejiang Province and Mali. During the ceremony, Chinese Ambassador to Mali Zhang and Deputy Governor Zheng signed two handover certificates for Drugs and Medical Equipment (药品和医疗设备) and X-Ray machines, B-scan ultrasound machines and laparoscopes (美元的X光机、B超机和腹腔镜等医疗设备), worth USD $80,000 and USD $300,000 respectively, to the three 3 hospitals (Sikasso, Kati, and 马尔格拉) that the Chinese medical teams work in. The 20th Chinese Medical Team was working in Mali at the time of the donation (Project #59534).

project_name: China donated 400 million CFA worth of materials to fight Ebola
description:
In November 2014, Chinese Ambassador to Mali announced that China will grant 400 million CFA of materials to help fight Ebola.  The handover ceremony for the materials occurred on November 8, 2014.  Officials from the presidential palace, the prime minister's office and officials of the Ministry of Health attended the ceremony.  
 
 Pan African News Agency reported that the donation consisted of 7,000 protection kits, 17,000 dish-clothes, 17,000 pairs of latex gloves for single use, 17,000 pairs of shoe-covers, 17,000 units of protective glasses, 200 units of sprayers, 200 units of infrared thermometers, 5 body temperature detectors and 3,000 mortuary bags.  However no official source has confirmed this.

project_name: China donated 300,000 antiMalarial medication treatments to Mali
description: In September 2017, China donated 300,000 antimalarial medication treatments to Mali.  The total cost of the donation are not known.

project_name: China grants medicine & med. equipment to aid in health services
description: On April 18, 2019, China granted Mali medical equipment to aid in the development of health services in the Hospital of Mali. The equipment will go to assist current efforts by the 26th Chinese medical team at the Hospital of Mali. The handover ceremony was led by Ambassador Zhu Liying, Mali's Minister of Health, doctors China had previously provided to Mali, Malian doctors, and some French medical staff. Nearly 200 people attended the ceremony. This is a part of China's continuing aid to Mali in developing their health services.

project_name: China donated 2 million RMB of anti-Malaria drugs to Mali
description: On July 22, 2008, the Chinese government held a handover ceremony of anti-malaria drugs to support the at the Malian Ministry of Health. The drugs, which had a total value of 2 million RMB, were previously sent by air in two lots to Bamako. Chinese Ambassador to Mali, Zhang Guoqing, and Mali Health Minister, Umar Ibrahima Dour, signed the handover certificate.

project_name: Ambassador to Mali donated small box of medicines to Mali hospital
description: On January 16, the Chinese Ambassador to Mali, Zhu Liying, visited the ophthalmology team from China temporarily stationed at Mali Hospital in Bamako (see project #93589 for more information on the medical team). The ambassador was accompanied on his visit by Mali's minister of health, Michel Sidibe.  In honor of his visit, the Ambassador donated a small box of medicines to the hospital. The exact number and type of medications is unknown.

project_name: China donated to fight against Covid-19 in Mali
description: On April 17, 2020, the Chinese government donated 2,000 medical masks, 10,000 general medical masks, 2,000 protective suits, 500 infrared electronic thermometers, 2,000 medical isolation goggles, 10,000 pairs of surgical gloves, and 10,000 pairs of medical shoe covers to Mali. Chinese Ambassador to Mali Zhu Liying and the Health Minister of Mali Michel Sidibé attended the handover ceremony at the Bamako Airport and signed the handover certificate on behalf of the two governments.  The supplies were transported to Accra, Ghana, and then transferred to Mali on a World Food Program chartered flight.

project_name: China donated anti-Malarial drugs to Mali
description: On July 31st and August 2nd 2006, the Chargé d’affaires of the Chinese Embassy in Mali, Yu Qiuzhong, and Mali’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Mokdar Vane, held an exchange of letters confirming the Chinese government's donation of anti-malarial drugs to Mali. On September 29th, a ceremony was held in Bamako to officially handover the drugs and medical equipment to the 19th Chinese Medical Team stationed in Mali (Project #60170). The total value of the donated equipment is unknown.

project_name: Embassy donated 126 million CFA worth of med. supplies to Mali
description: On July 15th, 2021, the Chinese Embassy in Mali donated medicine and medical supplies from to the Mali Department of Health and Social Development. The equipment donated was worth 126 million CFA Francs. The donation is intended to build the capacity of Mali Hospital, which recently hosted the 27th Chinese medical mission.

project_name: 1st lady of China donated materials to 1st lady of Mali against Covid
description: On July 28th, 2020, Zhu Liying, the Chinese Ambassador to Mali, and his wife handed over the donation of anti-epidemic materials on behalf of Peng Liyuan, the first lady of China, to Keïta Aminata Maïga, the first lady of Mali. Peng Liyuan's donation, in turn, was on behalf of the Chinese Government. The donated supplies included masks, thermometers, household appliances, and school supplies kits. The handover ceremony took place at Base B, Bamako, Mali.

project_name: China donated 100,000 RMB of med. equipment to Mali
description: From October 19th to 23rd, 2007, a delegation from the Zhejiang Province Health Department visited the 20th Medical Team in Mali (Project #59534) and donated medical equipment worth 100,000 to the team, funded by the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University. The handover ceremony for the equipment, which included modern electric scalpels and supporting equipment, was held September 7th in Bamako.

project_name: China donated drugs & med. devices to Mali
description: On September 30th, 2005, Zhang Youhua, Counselor of the Economic and Commercial Office of the Chinese Embassy in Mali, and Mamadou Sidibe, Technical Advisor of the Ministry of Health of Mali, signed a handover certificate for the Chinese government's donation of medicine and medical devices during the handover ceremony in Bamako. The captain of the current Chinese medical mission to Mali, the 19th Medical Team, was in attendance (Project #60170).

project_name: Chinese enterprises donated hospital beds for the fight against Covid
description: On May 11th, 2020, Ambassador Zhu Liying attended the handover ceremony of hospital beds donated by Chinese-funded enterprises to the Malian Government. This donation included 400 medical beds and matching mattresses and pillows. The monetary value of this donation is 46 million CFA francs or 548,000 yuan.   This donation was organized and initiated by the Chinese Embassy in Mali at the request of the Ministry of Health in Mali, and led by China Overseas Engineering, with additional cooperation from other state owned enterprises, including the China Road and Bridge Corporation, CGCOC, Sinolight Holdings, China Hydropower, Sinohydro, and the Gezhouba Group. Two private companies, the Qingjian Group and Huawei also donated.. How much each company donated specifically is unknown.

project_name: China donated med. equipment & supplies to Mali hospital
description: On February 24, 2017, China donated medical equipment and supplies to the Mali Hospital.  More than 100 people attended the handover ceremony, including Ambassador Lu Huiying, and Mali's Health Minister, Ms. Dogo.  The 24th Chinese medical team also attended the ceremony (#59583). The type of equipment and total cost of the project are unknown.

project_name: Gov't donated 835,200 Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: On October 4, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered donated 835,200 doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Mali via COVID-19 Vaccines Global Access (COVAX) — a worldwide initiative aimed at equitable access to COVID-19 vaccines directed by the GAVI vaccine alliance, the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations, the World Health Organization, and UNICEF. Then, on January 26, 2022, the Chinese Government delivered 300,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Mali. Then, on October 27, 2022, the Chinese Government delivered 300,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Mali.”

project_name: China donated medicine & med. equipment to Kati hospital
description: On November 9, 2009, Mali's Minister of Health Oumar Ibrahima Touré received a donation of medical equipment and supplies from Zhang Guoqing, China's Ambassador in Mali. The donation included equipment and medicines worth 50 million CFA francs to be delivered to Kati Hospital. The donation also included 230 million CFA francs of antimalarial drugs (See Project #30663) and equipment and medicines worth 85 million CFA francs for the use of the Chinese medical mission hospitals in Kati, Sikasso and Markala (See Project #30665).

project_name: China donated med. equipment & equipment to Mali hospital
description: On January 21, 2016, China donated medical equipment and supplies to the Government of  Mali at a handover ceremony at the Mali Hospital. The total cost of the project is unknown.

project_name: China donated $214,000 worth of equipment & medication to Mali
description: On August 31 2012, China signed an agreement with Mali for the donation of medication and health equipment. The total value of the donation is 214,000 USD. One piece of equipment is a medical imaging table used to repair vertebrae during neurosurgery. Visiting Chinese medical teams and Malian doctors will use the equipment.  According to a 2011 Working Series report, China has been sending medical teams to Mali since 1968.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for Mali hospital construction project
description: On December 27, 2008, the China’s Ministry of Commerce agreed to provide an RMB 48 million grant fo the Government of Mali for the Mali Hospital Construction Project. This project involved the construction of a 150-bed Mali Hospital (Hôpital du Mali or 3ème centre hospitalier de référence) on the right bank of the Niger River in Yirimadio within Commune 6 and Bamako District.   The hospital includes emergency services for medicine-resuscitation, obstetrics, pediatrics, and medical imaging. It also includes a laboratory, a pharmacy, a surgery department with three operation rooms, and services such as laundry, mortuary, canteen, and guardhouse. Domestic Trade Engineering Design and Research Institute was responsible for project design. QUILU Construction Group was responsible for project implementation. project_name: China donated med. equipment to Bamako general hospital

description: On September 30, 2011, the Zhejiang Provincial Health Department of China donated medical equipment worth 600,000 yuan to the Mali Hospital in Bamako.  The donation will be used by Chinese medical technicians to carry out medical services in Mali Hospital.  Chinese Ambassador Cao and Malian Health Minister Diallo signed the gift agreement at the handover ceremony. project_name: China donated medicine & med. equipment to The Mali Hospital
description: On September 30, 2011, the Chinese government donated medicine and medical equipment worth 800,000 yuan to the Chinese-funded Mali Hospital in Bamako.
