Chinese Ambassador Cao and Malian Health Minister Diallo signed the gift agreement at the handover ceremony. At the same ceremony, the Zhejiang Provincial Health Department donated an additional 600,000 yuan of medical equipment (Project #59693).

project_name: China donated Covid relief supplies to National Institute of Health
description: On June 29, 2020, the Chinese government donated COVID-19 relief medical supplies to the Mauritanian National Institute of Health. The exact contents and value of this donation are unknown. The donation is a part of a working protocol of the Chinese medical team signed by China and Mauritania.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for friendship hospital rehabilitation project
description: On September 20, 2017, the Chinese Government agreed to provide an RMB 36.69 million grant to the Government of Mauritania for the Nouakchott Friendship Hospital Construction Project. The funding for this project was drawn from an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA), which the Chinese Government and the Government of Mauritania signed on March 31, 2017 (see Project ID#56861). This project involved the rehabilitation of administrative buildings, a pharmacy, multifunctional rooms, and a personnel department at the Nouakchott Friendship Hospital (Al-Saddaaqah Hospital or l’Hôpital de l’Amitié à Nouakchott or مستشفى الصداقة), which is located in the capital city of Nouakchott. It also involved the provision and installation of medical equipment. Nantong Construction Group Company Ltd. (南通建工集团有限公司) was the contractor responsible for implementation. Project implementation commenced on July 25, 2018. The project was successfully completed and handed over to the local authorities on March 31, 2020. The Chinese Government also financed the construction of this hospital in 2009 (as captured via Project ID#32980).

project_name: Gov't provided cash assistance to help with Ebola response activities
description: On April 3, 2015, the Chinese Government signed an agreement with the Government of Mauritania to provide cash assistance to help with Ebola prevention, monitoring, and control activities. The monetary value of this cash grant is unknown. The implementation status of this project is also unknown.

project_name: Gov't donated 1 million Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021 and 2022, the Chinese Government donated approximately 1.93 million doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Mauritania. project_name: Ministry of Health donated testing equipment to Institute of Health
description: On May 23, 2012, a handover ceremony was held for the donation of medical testing equipment to the Mauritanian National Institute of Health from the Chinese Ministry of Health. The value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Embassy held the 5th 'bright action' free clinic
description: On December 12, 2019, Zhang Jianguo, Chinese ambassador to Mauritania, and Mauritian Minister of Health, Hamid, went to the China-Mauritian Ophthalmology Cooperation Center to inspect the fifth "Bright Action" (第五次“光明行”) free clinic. China has carried out the "Bright Action" ophthalmology free clinic in Mauritania for five consecutive years. This free clinic would last for more than a week. Chinese experts dispatched by the Heilongjiang Health Commission would perform 250 cataract surgeries for Mauritanian patients. In the future, China will continue to deepen China-Mauritian medical cooperation, benefiting more local people.  On December 12, 2019, Chen Junqi, Economic and Commercial Counselor of the Chinese Embassy in Mauritania, and Budaya, Director of Mauritania National Medical Center, signed a certificate for the handover of medical supplies for the "Bright Action" free clinic supported by China government for free. project_name: Embassy donated food & other living necessities to Mauritanian poor

project_name: Gov't provided grant for Kiffa Health Center project & provision
description:
According to the Government of Mauritania’s Development Assistance Database (DAD), the Chinese Government and the Government of Mauritania signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) on December 29, 2010, which committed an RMB 60 million interest-free loan for the Kiffa Health Center Project. Then, on April 12, 2011, the Chinese Government and the Government of Mauritania signed letters of exchange, which committed an additional RMB 60 million grant for the same project. Finally, on January 8, 2013, the Chinese Government provided an additional RMB 100 million grant for the Kiffa Health Center Project as well as the provision of school materials. The RMB 60 million interest-free loan is captured in Project ID#18750. The RMB 60 million grant is captured in Project ID#34154. The RMB 100 million grant is captured in Project ID#56843.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for Nouakchott friendship hospital project

The hospital, with a total floor area of 7,410.2 square meters, has 88 beds and a variety of departments, including clinic service, emergency treatment, operation rooms, X-ray section, clinical laboratory, and inpatient departments. 
 
 The No.1 building has two floors, and the other buildings have a single floor. The buildings are capable of resisting magnitude 7 earthquakes and second-grade fires. China Geo-Engineering Corporation International Ltd. (CGC) was the contractor responsible for implementation, Construction began on May 30, 2009, and ended on November 7, 2010. project_name: Chinese embassy donated food to Mauritanian poor

project_name: China donated Covid-19 relief med. equipment

project_name: Gov't provided grant for INRSP expansion & upgrade project
description: On May 17, 2017, the Chinese Government completed a feasibility study for  National Public Health Institute (CNRSP) Expansion and Upgrade Project. China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) subsequently issued a grant for the National Public Health Institute (CNRSP) Expansion and Upgrade Project. Then, on October 30, 2019, the Chinese Government and the Government of Mauritania signed a grant agreement worth 746,000,000 new ouguiyas (7.46 billion old ouguiyas) for the  National Public Health Institute (CNRSP) Expansion and Upgrade Project. The purpose of this project is to construct a new headquarters for the National Public Health Institute (Institut national de recherches en santé publique or CNRSP or INRSP) in Nouakchott. The facility will included a main building, three auxiliary buildings, a storage area, laboratories for bacterial diagnosis, parasitic virology, molecular biology and quality control (water and food), outdoor squares, roads, parking lots, and walls. China Aviation Planning and Design Institute Limited (also known as China Aviation Planification Co. Ltd) is the contractor responsible for project design. Jiangsu Zhongnan Construction Co. Ltd. (also known as Jiangsu Zhongnan Construction Industry Group Co., Ltd. or 江苏中南建筑产业集团有限责任公司) is the contractor responsible for implementation. Between October 10, 2019 and November 5, 2019, China Aviation Planning and Design Institute Limited dispatched a team to Mauritania to conduct project preparation activities. A project implementation agreement was signed on October 30, 2019. MOFCOM then issued a construction contract to Jiangsu Zhongnan Construction Co. Ltd. on December 17, 2020. A formal groundbreaking ceremony took place on August 31, 2021. Since the start of construction, on-site measurement, excavation, and site leveling activities have been carried out. The first concrete was successfully poured on September 16, 2021. The project is scheduled to reach completion on or around October 1, 2023.

project_name: Gov't provided loan for new operation theater & ward block at hospital
description: In July 2008, China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and the Government of Mauritius signed an RMB 29,310,000 loan agreement for the New Operation Theaters and Wards Block at Victoria Hospital Project. This loan carried the following borrowing terms: a 20 year maturity, a 10 year grace period, and a 0% interest rate. It was originally scheduled for repayment via annual installments between August 2018 and August 2028. Then, in December 2008, China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and the Government of Mauritius signed an RMB 40,000,000 loan agreement for the New Operation Theaters and Ward Blocks at Victoria Hospital Project. It carried the following borrowing terms: a 20 year maturity, a 10 year grace period, and a 0% interest rate. It was originally scheduled for repayment via annual installments between January 2019 and January 2029.  As of December 31, 2020, the Government of Mauritius had made an RMB 8 million repayment on the RMB 40,000,000  loan. Then, in March 2021, MOFCOM waived the Government of Mauritius’ obligation to repay the loan’s outstanding amount (RMB 32 million).  In 2009, the Chinese Government also provided an RMB 32 million grant for the New Operation Theaters and Ward Blocks at Victoria Hospital Project. description: On April 18, 2020, a first batch of anti-epidemic supplies donated by the Chinese government arrived in Mauritius on a chartered plane. project_name: Supported the foundation of a center for TCM
description: On December 9, 2019, the China-Mauritius Center for Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) was opened at City Clinic in Port Louis, Mauritius. The China-Mauritius Center for Traditional Chinese Medicine was being developed as part of a deal signed between the Shanghai Yueyang Hospital of Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western Medicine, which is affiliated with Shanghai University, and City Clinic in Mauritius. This project was a part of the Belt and Road Initiative under the National Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine and is supported by the Chinese government. With the assistance of the Shanghai Caitongde Pharmacy, the Yueyang hospital will send experienced two TCM experts and a pharmacist to the center, providing acupuncture, massage and herbal therapy. Since the opening of the center, the center has been treating 30 patients on average every day.  The value of the center and exact funding is unknown.

project_name: Gov't pledges to donate equipment for health sector
description: On the anniversary of Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam's historic visit to China on the 10th of July, 1972, the current Prime Minister Navinchandra Ramgoolam and Financial Minister Rama Sithanen made an official visit to Beijing in 2007 and were offered, among other things, the provision of equipment for the health sector. The current status of this project is yet unknown. The other offers made on this same visit are captured in #1152, #20184, #20178, and #20814.

project_name: China development bank provided anti-epidemic supplies to Morocco
description: On May 14, 2020, the Chinese Development Bank provided anti-epidemic supplies to Morocco. The supplies arrived at Casablanca International Airport in Morocco. The supplies included 36 ventilators and 98,000 disposable medical masks. These supplies will be used to improve COVID-19 response efforts in Morocco. The monetary value of this donation is unknown, but "the value of this donation is the highest among all those made by the Chinese bank abroad to date," said Bank of Africa (BOA) in a press release.

project_name: Gov't commited to establish center for traditional medicine
description: On August 18, 2019, Chinese delegations from the Chinese National Health Commission proposed the establishment of a Chinese-Moroccan Center for Traditional Medicine in Casablanca. The meeting was held at the 2nd Chinese-Arab Health Forum.   On January 3, 2020, the Chinese ambassador to Morocco signed the agreement with the Moroccan authorities to officially establish this center. The Hassan II University in Casablanca and Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine will implement the project.

project_name: 1st lady provided anti-epidemic supplies to l’union des Femmes
description: On July 21, 2020, the Chinese First Lady, Peng Liyuan, provided anti-epidemic supplies to the  l’Union des Femmes Marocaines in Morocco. These supplies will be used to improve COVID-19 response efforts in Morocco. The specific type, amount, and monetary value of this donation are unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. Mao Jun, the Chargé d'affaires of the Chinese Embassy in Morocco, handed over the supplies on behalf of Peng Liyuan and the Chinese Government. Mrs. Fatima Dahbi and Mrs. Farida El Khamlichi, respectively vice-president and general secretary of the union, attended the ceremonny. After handing over the supplies, a handover certificate was jointly signed by China and Morocco.

project_name: Ningxia Hui gov't provided anti-epidemic supplies to Morocco
description: On June 8, 2020, the government of Ningxia Hui, a city in China, provided anti-epidemic supplies to Morocco. The supplies included 2,000 medical masks, 25,000 surgical masks, and 2,000 personal protective suits. The supplies were transported from Yinchuan, the regional capital, to Casablanca-Settat in Morocco where they will be distributed across the Casablanca-Settat region of Morocco to improve COVID-19 response efforts. They will be delivered through the Chinese embassy in Morocco. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  The region of Casablanca-Settat signed an agreement on establishing relations of friendly exchanges with Ningxia in January 2006. It is one of eight international friendship cities to receive medical assistance from the Ningxia Hui government.

project_name: Gov't donated 500,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In March 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 500,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Morocco.

project_name: Guizhou province provided anti-epidemic supplies to Morocco
description: On March 23, 2020, China’s Guizhou Province provided anti-epidemic supplies to Morocco. The supplies arrived on a Royal Air Maroc cargo plane in Casablanca, Morocco. The donation included 15,000 pairs of medical gloves, 20,000 N95 protective masks, 2,000 pieces of medical protective clothing, and other medical supplies. These supplies will be used to improve COVID-19 prevention efforts in Morocco.   The monetary value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: Eximbank provided loan for med. clinic construction project
description: On December 3, 1998, the Chinese Government and the Government of Morocco signed an RMB 150 million preferential loan framework agreement for the Comprehensive Medical Clinic Construction Project. Then, on November 30, 2001, the Export-Import Bank of China (China Eximbank) and the Government of Morocco signed an RMB 150 million government concessional loan (GCL) agreement for the Comprehensive Medical Clinic Construction Project. The estimated borrowing terms of the loan were as follows: a 16.666-year maturity, a 2.1666-year grace period, and a 3% interest rate. The loan proceeds were to be used by the borrower to fully finance the cost of an RMB 125,227,814.45 commercial contract, which Morocco’s Ministry of Health signed with China National Complete Plant Import & Export Corp., Ltd. (COMPLANT) on May 17, 2004.   Total disbursements under the loan agreement amounted to RMB 125,227,814.45.  The purpose of this project was to construct 6 comprehensive medical clinics: one in the town of Berrechid within Berrechid province, one in the city of Benslimane  (Ben Slimane) within Benslimane province, one in the town of Guercif within Guercif province, one in the town of Fnideq within the M'diq-Fnideq Prefecture, one in the town of Khemis Des Zemamra within El Jadida Province, and one in the city of Oulad Teima (Houara) in Taroudannt Province. Each clinic was to include 45 beds, 3 housing units for doctors, and a set of internal medicine, surgery, pediatric, obstetric, emergency and observation rooms.    Between March 2002 and April 2002, COMPLANT dispatched a team to conduct an on-site inspection of the project. It also signed a project work summary with the Ministry of Health of Morocco, which clarified the division of labor and work plans between the two parties. After three rounds of extensive and difficult negotiations in July 2002, July 2003, and April 2004, COMPLANT and Morocco’s Ministry of Health finally reached an agreement on the contract price and they signed a project construction contract on May 17, 2004.  Construction began on April 27, 2006 and ended on October 23, 2008. The project also passed final inspection on October 23, 2008.

project_name: Gov't provided funds to the Ministry of Health & social protection
description: In 2020, the Chinese government provided 7.15 million Moroccan dirhams in total grant funding to Morocco's Ministry of Health and Social Protection to broadly support the country's health system. More specifically, 2.65 million dirhams were provided via the value of in-kind donations of medical devices and medicines to hospitals in which Chinese medical teams were stationed. The remaining 4.5 million dirhams were used to strengthen human resources associated with the Ministry's health information systems.  The Moroccan Ministry of Health explicitly considered the projects supported by these funds to be non-COVID-19 related.

project_name: Province gov't donated supplies to Maputo Central Hospital
description: On September 3, 2020, a handover ceremony was held for the donation of medical supplies, which included 20,000 surgical masks, 5,000 N85 masks, 500 sets of overalls, and 300 sets of face shields, from Sichuan's Provincial Government to Maputo Central Hospital.

project_name: Gov't donated a batch of anti-Malarial drugs
description: In September of 2010, China agreed to donate medicine for malaria patients in Mozambique. This agreement was reached at the same time as the 18th Chinese medical group was also decided on (Project #1232). Information on the amount of medicine provided, dates the medicine reached the country, and the completion status are yet unknown.

project_name: Gov't donated anti-epidemic equipment to the gov't of Mozambique
description: Before June 3, 2020, an unspecified sector within the Chinese Government provided its first donation of anti-epidemic equipment to the Government of Mozambique. A specific first donation has not been identified, but as ProjectID#91935 records a "second donation" of COVID-19 supplies, this project functions as a placeholder for the "first donation".

project_name: Gov't donated Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: On August 6, 2021 the Chinese Government delivered an additional 200,000 donated Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Mozambique. A handover ceremony was attended by Chinese Ambassador to Mozambique Wang Hejun, Mozambican Health Minister Armindo Tiago and Deputy Health Minister Lidia Cardoso.  The vaccines were produced by the Beijing Institute of Biological Products Co. Ltd.   In 2021, the Chinese Government donated approximately 1.46 million doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Mozambique. A February donation of 200,000 doses is captured by project #95808. A People's Liberation Army donation of vaccines from June is captured in project #95811. An August donation of 200,000 doses is captured in project #95809. A final December donation of 1 million doses is captured in project #95810.

project_name: Gov't funds surgical center in Maputo, Mozambique
description: In February 2020, it was reported that the Chinese Government would assist in funding a $40 million surgical center at Maputo Central Hospital. The hospital is said to be eight stories with 600 beds. The financial support was announced through Rádio Moçambique by the Chinese Ambassador to Mozambique. According to media sources, the surgical center was completed before 04/24/2020.

project_name: China provided dental equipment to Maputo Central Hospital
description: In 2013, the government of China signed an agreement in Maputo for the provision of medical equipment for the Maputo Central Hospital. The equipment is worth US$1.6 million and is for the dental section of the hospital. In the previous year, the Chinese government donated medical equipment to the Maputo Military Hospital (#30375).

project_name: CNPC donated 100,000 surgical masks to Mozambique's Ministry of Health
description: On July 17, 2020, China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) provided a donation of 100,000 surgical masks to Mozambique's Ministry of Health.

project_name: Gov't donated 200,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: On February 25, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Mozambique. A handover ceremony was held for the vaccine at Maputo International Airport, and attended by Mozambique's Prime Minister, Carlos Agostinho do Rosário, Minister of Health, Armindo Tiago, and Chinese Ambassador Wang Hejun. The vaccines were produced by the Beijing Institute of Biological Products Co. Ltd. An August donation of 200,000 doses is captured in project #95809. A final December donation of 1 million doses is captured in project #95810.

project_name: Gov't donated Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: On December 13, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered an additional 1 million donated Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Mozambique. A handover ceremony was held in Maputo. The Chinese Ambassador to Mozambique, Wang Hejun, handed over the vaccines to Mozambican Health Minister, Armindo Tiago. At the ceremony, Ambassador Wang announced that the 1 million doses were part of the larger 1 billion pledged by Xi Jinping at the 8th Ministerial Conference of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation.   In 2021, the Chinese Government donated approximately 1.46 million doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Mozambique. A February donation of 200,000 doses is captured by project #95808. A People's Liberation Army donation of vaccines from June is captured in project #95811. An August donation of 200,000 doses is captured in project #95809. A final December donation of 1 million doses is captured in project #95810.

project_name: Ministry provided donation of med. equipment to Maputo hospital
description: On June 17, 2020, the Chinese Defense Ministry handed over 13 tons of medical protective equipment, including gloves, masks, thermometers, and 60 other boxes of unspecified equipment, to the Maputo Military Hospital to help fight COVID-19.

project_name: CNPC donated 15,000 masks to Mozambique INP
description: On August 28, 2020, China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) donated 15,000 surgical masks to Mozambique's Institute of National Petroleum. On the same day, CNPC donated a further 40,000 masks to Mozambique MIREME (see linked ProjectID#92130).

project_name: CNPC donated 15,000 masks to Mozambique's ENH
description: On or around December 27, 2020, a local subsidiary of China National Petroleum Company (CNPC) donated 15,000 masks to Mozambique's National Hydrocarbon Company, Empresa Nacional de Hidrocarbonetos (ENH).

project_name: PLA donated 60,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses to FADM
description: On June 3, 2021, the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) of China delivered 60,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Mozambique Defence Armed Forces (FADM).  A handover ceremony was held at Maputo International Airport. The National Director of Military Health in the Mozambican Defence Ministry, Agueda Duarte, and the military attaché at the Chinese embassy, Zhou Zhe, jointly signed a handover certificate. Also present were Mozambique's Defense and Health Ministers, Jaime Neto and Armindo Tiago, and the Chinese ambassador, Wang Hejun. The vaccines were to be passed on to the Mozambican Health Ministry for distribution to other groups because 60,000 doses was more than FADM required.  In 2021, the Chinese Government donated approximately 1.46 million doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Mozambique. A February donation of 200,000 doses is captured by project #95808. A People's Liberation Army donation of vaccines from June is captured in project #95811. An August donation of 200,000 doses is captured in project #95809. A final December donation of 1 million doses is captured in project #95810.

project_name: China donated maternity care equipment to Mozambique
description: On March 11, 2021, the Chinese government offered a donation of medical equipment to Mozambique to help treat mothers and their newborns and will be used to help Mozambicans who were displaced by Cyclone Idai two years prior.  The equipment is worth USD $1.7 million and is able to assist around 436,000 girls and women through 32 health units. This donation will be used to assist people in the Sofala and Manica Provinces which were affected by the cyclone. This donation is under the South-South Cooperation Program, which is an agreement between China and the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA).

project_name: Gov't donated funds via WHO for Covid pandemic relief in Mozambique
description: In March 2020, Chinese government provides USD 62,301 to support WHO response to COVID-19 outbreak in Mozambique.  This project is captured in UNOCHA Financial Tracking Service as Flow ID #218743.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for Beira Central Hospital ward construction
description:
During the 4th Ministerial Conference of the Forum for Economic and Trade Cooperation between China and Portuguese-speaking countries in 2013, the Chinese Government offered a $23 million grant for the Beira Central Hospital Pediatric Ward Construction Project. 
 
 This project involved the construction of a pediatric ward in 4000 square meter area that is adjacent to Beira Central Hospital. The four-story building includes 168 beds, and a children's emergency center, a clinical analysis laboratory, digital radiographs, and an intensive care and malnutrition unit. China State Construction Engineering Corporation Ltd. was the contractor responsible for implementation. A groundbreaking ceremony was held on July 8, 2016 and the project was completed on September 2, 2017.

project_name: CNPC donated 40,000 masks to Ministry of Mineral Resources & Energy
description: On August 28, 2020, after China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) donated 15,000 surgical masks to Mozambique's Institute of National Petroleum (see linked ProjectID#92129), CNPC donated a further 40,000 masks to Mozambique MIREME.

project_name: Gov't donated med. equipment for Maputo Central Hospital
description: On February 18, 2013, the Chinese Government and the Government Mozambique signed a $1.6 million grant agreement for the provision of medical equipment for the dental section of Maputo Central Hospital. The agreement was signed by Mozambican Health Minister Alexandre Manguele and Chinese Ambassador to Mozambique Li Chunhua.

project_name: China pledged to donate equipment to the Maputo military hospital
description: On February 27, 2012, the Chinese government pledged to donate equipment to the Maputo Military Hospital valued at a total of 20 million CNY (about 3.2 million USD). The equipment included both medical and office equipment (X-ray machines, scanners, and ultrasound machines), which should arrive between September and November of 2012. The agreement was signed by the Permanent Secretary of the Mozambican Defense Ministry, Maj-Gen Teofilo Joao, and the director of military cooperation in the Chinese Defense Ministry, Qian Li Hua. Reports from 2013 indicate that two donations were carried out in 2012 by the Chinese government to the Military Hospital.  Related to project #85219.

project_name: China renovates anti-Malaria center in Maputo
description:
In April 2008, the Chinese Government and the Government of Mozambique signed a grant agreement to establish a malaria control center in Maputo. This project involved the construction of laboratories and training rooms, the provision of equipment, and the dispatching of doctors to train staff. The center began operations on October 30, 2009, and it was officially handed over to the authorities on November 25, 2009. 
 
 4 malaria experts were dispatched on September 15, 2009 to Angola for 45 days and then to Mozambique for another 45 days to help with malaria control training. These expert visits are captured in Project ID #68603 and Project ID#68605, respectively.

project_name: Gov't provided anti-epidemic equipment to the gov't of Mozambique
description: On June 3, 2020, a handover ceremony was held for the "second batch" of anti-epidemic supplies, which included N95 masks, surgical masks, medical gowns, medical goggles, shoe protection, and gloves, from an unspecified organization within the Chinese Government to the Government of Mozambique.

project_name: Eximbank agreed to provide loan for Hospital renovation
description: On February 5, 2007 on an official tour across Africa, Chinese President Hu Jintao pledged to provide an RMB 1 billion concessional loan facility to be used at the discretion of the Government of Namibia (recorded in project #1314). The following borrowing terms would apply to subsidiary loans obtained through this facility: a 4.27% interest rate, a 15 year maturity, and a 5 year grace period. Then, in December 2007, China Eximbank and the Government of Namibia signed an RMB 1 billion concessional loan framework agreement, which identified several projects that would be funded according to a consistent set of terms and conditions. This project records the committed loan for the Oshakati State Hospital Renovation Project.  These projects reportedly included an RMB 300 million loan for the Modern Customs Scanning Equipment Acquisition Project (recorded in project #1241), an RMB 44 million loan for the Electronics Document and Record Management Systems (EDRMS) Project (recorded in project #1242), a $16.4 million loan for road construction in Eiseb Block Phase I (recorded in project #61037), and a $748,357 loan for Namibia Institute of Pathology (NIP) laboratories (recorded in project #61032). An additional RMB 645 million was reportedly set aside for three projects: Phase 2 of the Northern Railway Line Extension Project (recorded in project #1334), the Oshakati State Hospital Renovation Project (recorded in this project), and the Namibian Broadcasting Corporation Renovation Project (recorded in project #61036). As the breakdown of the financing between these three projects is unknown, the RMB 645 million committed for the three projects is recorded in project #1334. This framework agreement was signed by China’s Ambassador to Namibia Ren Xiaoping and Nambia’s Minister of Finance Saara Kuugongelwa-Amadhila.   However, in July 2009, Namibia’s Permanent Secretary of Finance Calle Schlettwein announced that he had notified the Chinese Government that the borrowing terms of the RMB 1 billion loan facility (recorded in project #1314) were too financially onerous for the Government of Namibia. He told a local newspaper that 'We did not suspend any agreements, we just told them that the terms were too burdensome for our financial situation.’

project_name: Gov't donated 250,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021, the Chinese Government donated approximately 350,000 doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Namibia. The Chinese Government delivered 100,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Zambia on March 16, 2021. The shipment arrived at Hosea Kutako International Airport and Namibian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of International Relations and Cooperation Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah attended the vaccine handover ceremony. Then, on July 16, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered another 250,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Namibia.

project_name: Embassy donated Covid supplies to Ministry of Health & social services
description: On April 8, 2021, the Chinese Embassy in Namibia donated COVID-19 supplies to the Ministry of Health and Social Services of Namibia. According to the Chinese Embassy in Namibia, the donation's purpose is to thank Namibia for caring for Chinese citizens in Namibia during the COVID-19 pandemic and assist Namibia against COVID-19. The donation included 20 oxygenators and 12,000 masks, among other unknown supplies. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't funds acupuncture treatment for Namibians
description: Since 1996, the Chinese government has funded the Chinese Acupuncture Department at the Katutura State Hospital in the Windohoek, Namibia. The department, which includes two doctors and two nurses, is entirely funded by the Chinese government. On average, 600 to 700 patients are treated every month for various ailments.

project_name: Gov't & Namibia oriental tobacco cc donate masks to the Khomas region
description: On September 24, 2020, the Chinese Ambassador in Namibia handed over a donation of 50,000 masks donated by the Chinese government and the Namibia Oriental Tobacco CC to the Khomas Region in Namibia. The value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: Embassy & Swakop Uranium donate funds to a foundation
description: On February 18, 2021, the Chinese Embassy and Swakop Uranium donated 1 million Namibian dollars to the One Economy Foundation. The donation was made with the aim of helping children, young people and women fight COVID-19, and was distributed to youth-led organizations, shelters for GBV survivors, HIV teen clubs, out-of-school youth, and young entrepreneurs.

project_name: Shanghai donated 20,000 masks to windhoek, Namibia
description: On May 22, 2020, the city of Shanghai donated 20,000 masks to its sister city of Windhoek, Namibia. The donation includes 3000 surgical and 17000 KN95 masks. The donation was handed over by the Chinese Embassy in Namibia.

project_name: Health Commission of China donated med. equipment to the Ministry
description: On January 12, 2021, the Chinese Embassy in Namibia held a ceremony to deliver a batch of medical equipment donated by the National Health Commission of China to the Ministry of Health and Social Services of Namibia. The equipment included an unknown quantity of oxygen concentrators and ventilators. The donation was meant to help in the fight against COVID-19.

project_name: China donated the fourth batch of Covid-19 equipment to Namibia
description: On October 1, 2020, the Chinese State Councilor and Foreign Minister Wang Yi donated COVID-19 supplies worth 5 million Namibian dollars (about USD $300,000) to Namibia on the occasion of China's 71st anniversary in Windhoek. The donation included 30,000 N95 masks, 10 oxygenators, 20 ventilators, and 100 thermometers, making this the fourth batch of COVID-19 supply donations from the Chinese government so far.

project_name: Eximbank agrees to provide loan for the institute of pathology project
description: On February 5, 2007 on an official tour across Africa, Chinese President Hu Jintao pledged to provide an RMB 1 billion concessional loan facility to be used at the discretion of the Government of Namibia (captured in the linked project #1314). The following borrowing terms would apply to subsidiary loans obtained through this facility: a 4.27% interest rate, a 15 year maturity, and a 5 year grace period.   Then, in December 2007, China Eximbank and the Government of Namibia signed an RMB 1 billion concessional loan framework agreement, which identified several projects that would be funded according to a consistent set of terms and conditions. These projects reportedly included an RMB 300 million loan for the Modern Customs Scanning Equipment Acquisition Project (recorded in project ID#1241), a RMB 44 million loan for the Electronics Document and Record Management Systems (EDRMS) Project (recorded in project ID#1242), a $16.4 million loan for road construction in Eiseb Block Phase I (recorded in project ID #61037), and a $748,357 loan for Namibia Institute of Pathology (NIP) laboratories (recorded in this project). An additional RMB 645 million was reportedly set aside for three projects: Phase 2 of the Northern Railway Line Extension Project (see Project ID#1334), the Oshakati State Hospital Renovation Project (recorded in project ID#61034), and the Namibian Broadcasting Corporation Renovation Project (recorded in project ID#61036).   This framework agreement was signed by China’s Ambassador to Namibia Ren Xiaoping and Nambia’s Minister of Finance Saara Kuugongelwa-Amadhila. However, in July 2009, Namibia’s Permanent Secretary of Finance Calle Schlettwein announced that he had notified the Chinese Government that the borrowing terms of the RMB 1 billion loan facility (captured in project ID#1314) were too financially onerous for the Government of Namibia. He told a local newspaper that 'We did not suspend any agreements, we just told them that the terms were too burdensome for our financial situation.’

project_name: Embassy donated money to a family in Katutura for med. expenses
description: On December 7th, 2018, a female Chinese Diplomat went to the house of Ester Abraham and her family in Katutura District. The Chinese Embassy donated money to the family for medical expenses for their five-year-old son with cerebral palsy. The Embassy learned about the family's situation through the media. The amount donated is unknown.

project_name: China donated 100,000 nad worth of hygienic supplies
description: On November 16, 2018, the Chinese Embassy to Namibia donated 100,000 NAD worth of hygienic supplies to combat spreading the ongoing hepatitis-E outbreak. The official donation ceremony took place at a clinic event co-organized by the Embassy, the Chinese-funded Chamber of Commerce, and the Red Cross Society in which the 12th medical team provided free consultations (#67797).

project_name: 1st lady donated sewing machines to the Namibian 1st lady's foundation
description: On July 10, 2020, the Chinese First Lady, Peng Liyuan, donated 30 sewing machines to Monica Geingob, First Lady of the Republic of Namibia, Monica Geingos' One Economy Foundation. The donation was made in support of women and children in Namibia. The Chinese Embassy in Namibia facilitated the donation, which was intended to support women's employment.   The donation was made alongside a donation of COVID-19 equipment from China's first lady (Project ID#93215).

project_name: 1st lady donated Covid equipment to the Namibian 1st lady's foundation
description: On July 10, 2020, the Chinese first lady donated 18000 Medical Masks and 120 infrared thermometers to the first lady of Namibia, Monica Geingos' One Economy Foundation. The donation was made specifically to help women and children.   The Chinese ambassador to Namibia facilitated the handover of the supplies, which were to be distributed to survivors of gender based violence and to youth organizations. The donation was made alongside a donation of 30 sewing machines by the Chinese Embassy (Project ID #93216).

project_name: Nanjing donated 30,000 face masks to the city of windhoek
description: On June 1, 2020, the Chinese city of Nanjing donated 30,000 face masks to the city of Windhoek in Namibia. The ambassador of the People’s Republic of China in Namibia, Zhang Yiming, and other senior Chinese embassy personnel officiated at the handover ceremony in Windhoek. This donation was expected to deepen the friendship between the two cities after they became sister cities in 2015.

project_name: China donated med. supplies as part of the Guangmingxing project
description: On May 18, 2018, the Chinese Government officially granted medical equipment and pharmaceutical consumables worth 1.825 million RMB (279,000 USD) to Namibia's Ministry of Health. The donation was part of a drive by the health ministry to assist the visually impaired and those suffering from cataracts. This donation is related to the Guangmingxing (光明行) project (#67811) to provide free cataract surgeries established in 2011.

project_name: China provided cataract surgeries under Guangmingxing project
description: In 2011, the Chinese Government launched the Guangmingxing (光明行) or "Bright Lines" project to provide free cataract surgeries for thousands of patients in Africa, Southeast Asia, and the Caribbean. On May 7, 2018, the first surgical team, consisting of 5 doctors and 3 nurses from Peking Union Medical College Hospital, arrived at the Windhoek Central Hospital to work with Namibian experts. By the time the Chinese doctors left on May 29, they had restored eyesight to 208 patients. The mission lasted for twenty days total. The lenses came from the Zhongguancun company Aibonod.  On May 18, 2018, China donated medical equipment and pharmaceutical consumables related to this project worth 1.825 million RMB to Namibia (see project #62633).

project_name: Gov't provided grant for Omuthiya dist. hospital  project
description: In early February 2009, during an economic and technical cooperation agreement (ETCA) signing ceremony, the Chinese ambassador to Namibia, H.E. Ren Xiaoping, announced that the Chinese Government would provide a grant worth RMB 70 million to the Government of Namibia for the Omuthiya District Hospital Construction Project. This project involved construction of a 60-bed hospital in the town of Omuthiya in the Oshikoto Region. It included a medical building, an emergency department, a pharmacy, a laboratory, an operating theater, a central sterile supply department, maternity, pediatric and tuberculosis wards. It also included kitchen, laundry facilities, administrative buildings, a mortuary, an incinerator and doctors' and nurses' living quarters.   China Jiangsu International Economic Technical Cooperation Corporation was the contractor responsible for implementation. Construction began on October 28, 2009. Then, a formal groundbreaking ceremony took place on November 15, 2009. A project design contract was signed on or around June 30, 2010 and the project was ultimately completed on May 1, 2011. However, upon completion, this project provoked significant domestic criticism and controversy. Namibian parliamentarians charged that the hospital suffered from poor workmanship. An estimated 13 million NAD was required to renovate it before it could be opened to the public.  The Chinese project title is 所70床位的综合医院 or 援纳综合医院项目 or 比亚奥姆西亚市援建的一所70床位的综合医院.

project_name: Chinese ambassador donated 1,000 Covid-19 testing kits
description: On March 18, 2020, Chinese Ambassador H.E Zhang Yiming donated 1,000 reagent testing kits to the Namibian government to be used in the fight against the COVID-19 pandemic. The handover ceremony was held in the capital of Windhoek.

project_name: Gov't donated 200,000 doses of Covid-19 vaccine to Namibia
description: On November 25, 2021, Ambassador Zhang Yiming announced that the Chinese Government will once again donate 200,000 doses of the Sinopharm vaccine to Namibia. According to the Chinese Embassy in Namibia, the ambassador made this announcement at the signing ceremony of the Economic and Technological Cooperation Agreement between China and Namibia. This donation follows an earlier donation of 100,000 Sinopharm vaccines from China made in March 2021. According to a media report, it is unclear when the donation will take place.

project_name: China's zhejiang province donated 3 ambulances & med. equipment
description: On October 14, 2014, Chinese Ambassador Xin Shunkang handed over three ambulances and medical equipment donated by Zhejiang Province to Namibian Health Minister Richard Kamwi. The fully-equipped ambulances were funded by Zhejiang Province after a delegation led by Vice Governor Huang Xuming visited Namibia in October 2013. The Ministry of Health and Social Services and the government of the Zhejiang Province of the People's Republic of China signed documents in April 2014, when it was agreed that the latter would donate ambulances to the ministry.  Each ambulance costs $636,724.82 Namibian dollars while the medical equipment is worth $200,000 Namibian dollars. The ambulances were purchased locally in Namibia and were face-lifted to be modern ambulances equipped with life-saving devices. Medical exchange between Namibia and Zhejiang started in 1996 when the province began to send doctors to work in Namibian hospitals. This project is completed.

project_name: China donated 3 ambulances worth 1.05 million RMB to Namibia
description: In October 2007, Sheng Changli, vice governor of Zhejiang Province, visited Namibia and donated 3 ambulances worth 1.05 million RMB.

project_name: Embassy donated Covid-19 equipment to 7 schools in Windhoek
description: On April 29, 2021, the Chinese Embassy in Namibia donated 45,000 surgical masks, 4,000 N95 masks, and 35 forehead thermometers to 7 primary and secondary schools in Windhoek, Namibia. According to the Chinese Embassy, the donation is worth 1 million Namibian dollars. The donation is intended to assist these schools during the COVID-19 pandemic.

project_name: China donated Covid-19 equipment to Namibia
description: On April 23, 2020 China donated medical equipment and protective gear to Namibia. The donation contains 20,000 N95 Medical Masks, 10,000 General Medical Masks, 2,000 Disposable Medical Protective Gowns, 2,000 Medical Goggles, 500 Portable Infrared Thermometers, and 10,000 Medical Shoe Covers.   The donation arrived at the Hosea Kutako International Airport in Windhoek. It was handed over along with another donation from the Jack Ma Foundation.

project_name: Gov't donated 100,000 Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021, the Chinese Government donated approximately 350,000 doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Namibia. The Chinese Government delivered 100,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Zambia on March 16, 2021. The shipment arrived at Hosea Kutako International Airport and Namibian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of International Relations and Cooperation Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah attended the vaccine handover ceremony. Then, on July 16, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered another 250,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Namibia.

project_name: Jiangsu provincial gov't donated 5,000 pcr test kits to Namibia
description: On November 11, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Namibia handed over 5,000 COVID-19 PCR testing kits donated by the Jiangsu Provincial Government to the Namibian Ministry of Health. The donation was announced by Zhang Yiming, the Chinese ambassador to Namibia.

project_name: China donated nad 4.3 million in Covid-19 equipment
description: On July 15, 2020, China donated PPE consignments worth N$4.3 million (260,000 U.S. dollars). The donation included 150 000 surgical masks, 5 000 medical disposable protective clothing, 15 000 protective face masks for medical use, 7 000 medical protective goggles, 7 000 pairs of disposable sterilized rubber surgical gloves, and 3 000 pairs of medical isolation shoe covers. Namibian Health Minister Kalumbi Shangula and Chinese Ambassador to Namibia Zhang Yiming attended the handover ceremony in Windhoek, Namibia.

project_name: Jiangsu donated 50,000 masks to Khomas region
description: On June 16, 2020, Chinese ambassador to Namibia Zhang Yiming handed over 50 000 masks to Khomas region that had been donated by Jiangsu province. The government in the Khomas region will distribute these masks among all districts.

project_name: China donated anti-Malarial medicines to Niger
description: On September 7, 2009, the Chinese government handed over 2 million CNY of anti-malarial medicines to the government of Niger.

project_name: Gov't donated drugs & med. equipment worth 500,000 RMB
description: On 31 October 2003, the Chinese Government officially donated drugs and medical supplies worth 500,000 RMB to Niger. The type and quantity of drugs and equipment are unknown.

project_name: China donated anti-Malarial medicine to Niger (june)
description: On June 27, 2011, Chinese Ambassador to Niger and the Nigerian Health Minister attended the handover ceremony for China's donation of a batch of anti-malaria medicine.  The amount of medicine is unspecified.  This cooperation works towards achieving the eight new initiatives under the framework of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation.

project_name: China donated anti-Malaria medicine to Niger
description: On December 15, 2006, the Assistant to the Chinese Minister of Commerce and the Nigerian Minister of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation and African Integration signed an exchange of letters involving the Chinese government's donation of 1 million CNY worth of anti-malaria medicine (MOU). The current status of this project and whether or not the drugs were actually delivered cannot be determined.

project_name: China donated unspecified supplies to Niger
description: On December 15, 2006, the Assistant to the Chinese Minister of Commerce and the Nigerian Minister of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation and African Integration signed an exchange of letters involving the Chinese government's donation of 2 million CNY worth of unspecified supplies (but they may be presumed to be medical supplies since this donation accompanied anti-malarial medications; MOU). The current status of this project and whether or not the supplies were actually delivered cannot be determined.

project_name: Communist party donated anti-epidemic materials to Niger party
description: On September 3, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Niger handed over the donation of anti-epidemic materials. These materials were donated from the Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party to the Niger Party for Democracy and Socialism. Ambassador Zhang Lijun and Yakuba, Deputy General Secretary of the Niger Party for Democracy and Socialism were both present at the ceremony.   Some or all of the supplies appear to be produced by China's Beijing Naton Technology Group Co Ltd ("Naton"). While the actual supplies were not specified, the boxes shown on the Embassy website during the handover ceremony correspond to boxes shown on https://www.natonmask.com/, Naton's website showing masks they produce. Thus, it can reasonably be assumed that masks were donated.

project_name: Gov't donated 1,200 mosquito nets to Niger
description: On October 14, 2003, the Chinese Government donated 1,200 mosquito nets to the Government of Niger as part of a national anti-malaria campaign. The donation value is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donated a batch of med. supplies to Niamey hospital
description: On June 28, 2018, the Chinese Government donated a batch of medical equipment to the Niamey General Referral Hospital. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  Immediately following the donation, the 20th Chinese medical team (see linked project ID#58561) carried out coronary and neurological operations as part of a Angiocardiographic Surgery Project effort.

project_name: Gov't donated medicine worth 500,000 RMB to Niger
description: On 11 December 2002, the Chinese Government officially donated medicine worth 500,000 RMB to Niger. The type and quantity of drugs are unknown.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for Niamey hospital construction project
description:
In 2013, China’s Ministry of Commerce reportedly committed RMB 317 million of grant funding for the Niamey General Referral Hospital Construction Project.  This project involved the construction of a general referral hospital with 500 beds on a 16 hectare plot of land in northern Niamey.  The hospital was designed to provided a wide array of in-patient and out-patient services, including emergency services, cardiology services, and laboratory services. It includes 16 operation rooms, a blood bank, and imaging facilities.  It will equally serve as a medical training center and will provide both in-patient and out-patient services.
 
 Beijing Urban Construction Group was the contractor responsible for implementation.  On 1 October, 2013, a project commencement ceremony took place.  An inauguration ceremony for the hospital was held on 2 August, 2016, and it was attended by China's Ambassador to Niger, Shi Hu, as well as the head of Niger's Parliament, Ousseini Tini, heads of public institutions, ministers, members of parliament and representatives of diplomatic corps in Niamey.  The hospital was put into use on 30 November, 2017.  The Niamey General Referral Hospital is reportedly the largest and most modern referral hospital in West Africa.

project_name: Gov't donated anti-epidemic materials to Guri Vie Meilleure foundation
description: On July 9, 2020, the Chinese Ambassador to Niger Zhang Lijun handed over the Chinese government's anti-epidemic materials to Niger. The materials went straight to the Guri Vie Meilleure Foundation, Niger's first lady's foundation. The donation was made in support of the foundation's campaign on AIDS prevention and control.   While the exact materials donated are unclear, the producer of the materials appears to be Yantai Show Long Medical Technology Co., Ltd, a company owned by Shandong Shulang Garment, that produces gloves, masks, and full-body PPE.

project_name: Donated funds in partnership with UNICEF for maternal & child services
description: On June 1, 2020, China donated CFA590 million (roughly 1 million USD) to Niger to improve its maternal and child health services. The project targeted more than 260,000 children and 96,000 women and mothers living far from health facilities.   The project partnered directly with UNICEF, the United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund, with the goal of supporting seven districts of the Tahoua region through a series of interventions. These interventions aimed at improving Tahoua's electricity, health communities, drug and treatment distribution, community engagement and coordination.   The funds are documented as being part of China's larger China South-South Cooperation Assistance Fund (SSCAF) (中国南南合作援助基金) (La cCoopération Sud-Sud de la Chine).

project_name: Gov't donated 400,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021, the Chinese Government donated approximately 800,000 doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Niger. The Chinese Government delivered 400,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Niger on March 21, 2021. The vaccine doses were were delivered by airplane to Niamey Air Base. The President of Niger, Mahamadou Issoufou, the Prime Minister of Niger, Brigi Rafini, Niger's acting Health Minister, Ahmed Boto, and the Chinese Ambassador to Niger, Zhang Lijun, attended the vaccine handover ceremony. Then, on December 14, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered another 400,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Niger.  Mr. JIANG Feng, the Chinese Ambassador to Niger, and Niger’s Minister of Public Health, Population and Social Affairs, Dr. Idi Illiassou Maïnassara, participated in the vaccine handover ceremony at the Diori Hamani International Airport.

project_name: Gov't donated drugs & med. equipment to Niger
description:
On 31 December 2008, the Chinese Government officially donated medicine and medical equipment to Niger. The type, quantities, and cost of the donation is unknown.  
 
 This project is linked to the 15th Chinese medical team serving at the same time as when this donation ceremony took place (project #35695).

project_name: China donated anti-epidemic materials worth 360 million fCFA
description: On June 10, 2020, Ambassador Zhang Lijun, Niger Minister of Humanitarian Aid and Disaster Management Magaggi (acting as Minister of Public Health), and Anya, WHO Representative in Niger, attended the handover ceremony of anti-epidemic materials, some or all produced by Cobes lndustries Co., Ltd.(CIC), worth 360 million FCFA at Diori Hamani International Airport in Niamey. The donation consisted of 10,000 test kits, 20,000 protective masks, 350,000 surgical bibs, 10,000 protective suits, 15,000 goggles, 15,000 pairs of disposable gloves, and 3,000 pairs of overshoes.   This donation is China's 2nd batch of anti-epidemic materials donated in 2020.

project_name: Gov't provided USD 113,824 for Covid-19 response via WHO
description: In March 2020, Chinese government provides USD 113,824 to support WHO response to COVID-19 outbreak in Niger.

project_name: Gov't donated 10 million RMB worth of med. supplies to Niger
description: On 7 July 2016, the China officially donated medical supplies to Niger's Ministry of Public Health valued at 10 million RMB. They will be distributed to 70 clinics across Niger.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for construction of center to combat Malaria
description: On 13 December, 2012, the unveiling ceremony of the Sino-Nigerien Center to Combat Malaria was held at National Hospital of Niamey (l'Hôpital National de Niamey).  This 860 million CFA franc donation included a fully-equipped research lab, rehabilitation of buildings, and anti-malarial drugs.

project_name: Gov't donated 400,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021, the Chinese Government donated approximately 800,000 doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Niger. The Chinese Government delivered 400,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Niger on March 21, 2021. The vaccine doses were were delivered by airplane to Niamey Air Base. The President of Niger, Mahamadou Issoufou, the Prime Minister of Niger, Brigi Rafini, Niger's acting Health Minister, Ahmed Boto, and the Chinese Ambassador to Niger, Zhang Lijun, attended the vaccine handover ceremony. Then, on December 14, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered another 400,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Niger.  Mr. JIANG Feng, the Chinese Ambassador to Niger, and Niger’s Minister of Public Health, Population and Social Affairs, Dr. Idi Illiassou Maïnassara, participated in the vaccine handover ceremony at the Diori Hamani International Airport.

project_name: China donated anti-Malarial medicine to Niger
description: On April 2, 2008, Chinese Ambassador Chen Gong and Nigerian Minister of Health attended the handover ceremony for China's donation of anti-malaria medicine, worth 1.5 million RMB.

project_name: China donated anti-Malarial medicine to Niger
description: On 21 December 2011, the Chinese Government officially donated anti-malarial drugs in pursuit of the Nigerien President's national campaign to reduce malaria-induced death rates. The value and quantity of medicine are unknown.

project_name: Gov't donated drugs & med. devices worth 5 million RMB to Niger
description: On 2 October 2002, the Chinese Embassy in Niger donated drugs and medical equipment worth 5 million RMB (434 million FCFA) for a rural clinic project. The specific details regarding types of medicine and equipment and their quantities are unknown.

project_name: Gov't donated medicine to Niger
description:
On 20 October 2005, the Chinese Government donated medicine to Niger. The type, quantity, and cost of the drugs is unknown.
 
 This project is potentially linked to the 13th medical team sent to Niger (#32814), as the team was in Niger at the time of the donation.

project_name: Gov't donated drugs & med. equipment
description:
On 19 January 2012, the Chinese Government officially donated medical equipment and medicine to Niger. The cost, quantity, and types of supplies are unknown.
 
 This is linked to the 17th Chinese medical team serving at the same time as this donation (#32673)

project_name: Gov't donated drugs & med. equipment
description:
On 8 January 2010, the Chinese Government officially donated drugs and medical equipment to Niger. The type, quantity, and cost of the donation is unknown.
 
 This is linked to the 16th Chinese medical mission, also a regular form of medical aid to Niger (project #35694).

project_name: China donated anti-Malaria drugs to Niger
description: In December, 2011 a handover ceremony for a Chinese donation of anti-malaria drugs took place at the Ministry of Health of Niger in Niamey. The financial details of this project are unknown.

project_name: China donated medicine & equipment worth 500,000 RMB
description: In November, 2004 a handover ceremony took place in Niamey, Niger in which China donated 500,000 RMB worth of drugs and medical equipment.

project_name: China donated 900,000 RMB of medicine to Niger
description: In March, 2013 a handover ceremony took place in Niamey for medicines worth 900,000 RMB donated by China to Niger.

project_name: China donated medicine & med. equipment to Niger
description: On December 10, 2010, the Chinese Ambassador to Niger and Nigerian Acting Minister of Health attended the handover ceremony of China's donation of a batch of unspecified medicines and medical equipment. The ceremony was held in Niamey.

project_name: Consulate in lagos donated med. equipment to Lagos uni. hospital
description: On August 1, 2018, Consul General Chao Xiaoliang visited Lagos State University Teaching Hospital (LASUTH) to donate an auto hematology analyzer and a semi-auto chemistry analyzer to the hospital's critical care unit. The equipment is worth 7 million Nigerian Naira. The purpose of the project was to support LASUTH in its delivery of quality healthcare to Nigerians.  The donation was part of the "China-Africa people-to-people friendship action" initiative that resulted from the 2012 conference of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation.

project_name: Gov't provided med. supplies to Nigeria
description: On April 23, 2020, the Chinese Government provided medical supplies to Nigeria. The donated medical supplies included protective equipment and ventilators. The monetary value of this medical donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony took place for this donation at the Office of the Secretary of the Federal Government of Nigeria. China’s Ambassador to Nigeria, Zhou Pingjian, and various Nigerian officials, including the National Coordinator of the Presidential Task Force on COVID-19, Sani Aliyu, attended the ceremony. At this ceremony, a separate donation was made from the China General Chamber of Commerce to Nigeria. The details of that donation are captured in Project ID#93775.

project_name: Gov't provided RMB 5 million for anti-Malarial activities
description: On April 26, 2006, China and Nigeria signed an agreement for a CNY 5 million grant for anti-malaria drugs, training for Nigerians to control malaria and bird flu, and co-operation in technology. According to Nigeria's Minister of State for Petroleum Edmund Daukoru, this grant was decided upon to reciprocate Nigeria and China's formalization of four oil block contracts, which include the maintenance and management of the Kaduna refinery and setting up a power generation station.The status of this grant is uncertain.   In November 2007, the handover ceremony of the Chinese government's assistance to the Nigerian Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources for the prevention and control of bird flue was held in Abuja, Nigeria. This was the second donation from the Chinese government: they had donated 429,000 boxes of anti-malarial drugs and 100,000 anti-malarial injections to the Nigerian Ministry of Health, which worth about RMB5 million.

project_name: Consulate provided 2nd batch of anti-epidemic materials & n10 million
description: On April 21, 2020, the Chinese Consulate-General provided its second batch of anti-epidemic materials and N10 million to Nigeria. These materials were provided to assist disadvantaged groups in Nigeria. The materials included food aid such as rice and instant noodles, medical equipment, and the monetary donation of N10 million.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation in Lagos, Nigeria. Tayu Aind, the Director of the General Office and other representatives of the overseas Chinese community attended the donation ceremony. This is the second batch of equipment provided by the Chinese Consulate General to Nigeria. The first batch took place on April 17, 2020, and the details of this donation are captured in Project ID#93092.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for establishment of anti-Malaria center
description: In 2009, the Chinese Government provided a grant to the Government of Nigeria for the establishment of a China-Nigeria Anti-Malaria Centre in Abuja. The monetary value of this grant commitment is unknown. The China-Nigeria Anti-Malaria Centre officially opened on October 30, 2009.

project_name: Gov't donated batch of anti-Malarial drugs worth RMB 5 million
description: On February 10, 2009, the Chinese Government donated a batch of anti-malarial drugs worth RMB 5 million to Nigeria’s Ministry of Health.

project_name: Gov't provided 2nd batch of med. supplies worth n170 million
description: On April 16, 2020, the Chinese government provided a second batch of medical supplies, worth N170 million, to Nigeria for COVID-19 response and prevention efforts. The donated supplies included 1,500 respiratory masks, 10,000 surgical masks, 1,750 disposable surgical gowns, 350 infrared thermometers, 1,750 medical goggles, 9,750 gloves, and 9,750 shoe covers.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation in the Cargo Wing of the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport (Abuja International Airport) in Abuja, the capital city of Nigeria. Li Yuan, the Economic and Commercial Counselor of the Chinese Embassy in Nigeria, and the Deputy Director of the International Cooperation Department of the Nigerian Federal Ministry of Finance, Budget and National Planning attended the ceremony.   This is reported as the second batch of medical supplies provided by the Chinese Government to Nigeria. The first batch of supplies arrived in Lagos, Nigeria on April 13, 2020, but no more information is available on this donation.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for friendship hospital construction project
description:
On August 23, 2007, the Chinese Government and the Government of Nigeria signed a $12.5 million grant agreement for the China-Nigeria Friendship Hospital Construction Project. This project involved the construction of the 150-bed Federal Staff Hospital in Abuja, Nigeria. The Government of Nigeria donated the 4.85 hectares of land where the hospital was built. It also provided the necessary infrastructural facilities, which included portable water, electricity and temporary access roads. 
 
 Anhui Construction Engineering Group Overseas Co., Ltd. was the contractor responsible for implementation. It signed a project implementation contract on August 7, 2009. Then, construction commenced on May 20, 2010 and was completed by April 2012. The China-Nigeria Friendship Hospital (or Nigerian-Chinese National Hospital) was officially commissioned and handed over to the Nigerian authorities on January 28, 2013. The Chinese Government also agreed to provide a supplementary grant of medical equipment and materials worth 250 million Naira (see Project ID #61184).

project_name: Gov't donated 470,000 Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: On July 23, 2021, the Chinese Government donated 470,000 COVID-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Nigeria. The Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria, Cui Jianchun, made the donation to the Nigerian Minister of Health, Dr. Osagie Ehanire, in Abuja, Nigeria. The donation came after the Government of Nigeria had to stop administering vaccines on July 8, 2021 due to a lack of vaccine supply

project_name: Gov't provided Covid-19 supplies to Nigeria
description: On March 23, 2020, the Chinese government provided medical supplies to the Nigerian Ministry of Health. These supplies included infection prevention and control materials that will be used to improve COVID-19 response efforts in Nigeria. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony took place for this donation. China’s Ambassador to Nigeria, Zhou Pingjian, the Nigerian Minister of Health, the Minister of State, and the Permanent Secretary attended the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for med. equipment & materials to hospital
description: According to 2015 report from Nigeria’s Ministry of Budget and National Planning, the Chinese Government agreed to provide a grant worth 10,000,000 naira for the provision of medical equipment and materials to the China-Nigeria Friendship Hospital (see Project ID#30629). The report characterizes the project as “on-going”. The China-Nigeria Friendship Hospital (or Federal Staff Hospital) is located on Jabi-Airport Road in the city of Abuja (within Gwarimpa Ward, Abuja Municipal Area Council and Federal Capitol Territory). Its locational coordinates are 9.116889 (longitude) and 7.421479 (latitude).

project_name: Construction corporation provided anti-epidemic materials
description: On May 12, 2020, China Civil Engineering Construction Company (CCECC) donated anti-epidemic materials to Nigeria. Alongside the construction of its new Covid-19 facility in Abuja, the CCECC provided Nigeria 2 ventilators, 1 oxygenator, and 10,000 face masks. These materials will be used at the new treatment facility for COVID-19 treatment and prevention. The monetary value of this donation is unknown. The details of the Covid-19 facility are captured in Project ID #93282.

project_name: Embassy provided Covid materials to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
description: On March 27, 2020, the Chinese Embassy provided anti-epidemic materials to the Nigerian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The materials included masks, infrared thermometers, disposable gloves, hand sanitizer, disinfectant, soap and other materials. These materials will be used to improve COVID-19 prevention and control efforts in Nigeria. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.   A handover ceremony was held for this donation. China’s Ambassador to Nigeria, Zhou Pingjian, the Director of the Policy Planning Department of the Nigerian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Director of the Regional Department, and the Director of the Training and Staff Welfare Department attended the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't donated medicines & med. equipment worth $5.5 million
description: From 2002 to 2007, China donated $5.5 million in drugs and medical equipment to Nigeria. The donation was disclosed by Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria, Xu Jianguo on November 5, 2007. Further project details were non-existent and targeted searching did not reveal any more information on the project.

project_name: Embassy provided anti-epidemic materials to federal territory schools
description: On May 15, 2020, the Chinese Embassy provided anti-epidemic materials, worth N5 million, to 100 Federal Capital Territory (FCT) schools in Nigeria. The materials included 100 forehead thermometers, 200 electro thermometers, 200 goggles, 4,000 PCS disposable medical face masks, 5,000 pairs of disposable medical gloves, eight packages of wet tissues, and 16 medicated soaps. These materials will be used to help students and staff at the schools proceed with education programming safely.   A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the FCT Minister's Office in Abuja, Nigeria. Li Xuda, the Cultural Counselor of the Chinese embassy in Nigeria, attended the ceremony as a representative of the Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria, Zhou Pingjian. The Permanent Secretary of the Federal Capital Territory Administration, Christian Ohaa, also attended the ceremony.

project_name: Construction corporation provided 2 Covid response facilities
description: On April 9, 2020, the China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation (CCECC) announced its provision of two COVID-19 response facilities in Abuja, Nigeria. This construction project was announced in a signed statement by the CCECC Managing Director, Micheal Jiang. The monetary value of these provisions is unknown. The first response facility that will be constructed is a 196-bed "This Day Dome Treatment Centre" in collaboration with Sahara Group and Arise News. The second facility is a 150-bed "Idu Depot Treatment Centre".   On May 12, 2020, CCECC confirmed that the "This Day Dome Treatment Centre" was delivered for operation to combat COVID-19. The facility was built in a local opera house in Abuja and equipped with 283 beds. It is unclear whether this temporary hospital includes both pledged facilities or just one. CCECC contributed to the facility by providing ground reconstruction, partitioning, and a water supply system. The new treatment center is expected to add to the 1,000-bed capacity in Nigeria's capital city of Abuja. The facility has the capacity to test, trace, and treat COVID-19 cases in Abuja, including a mobile laboratory with reagents for 200 to 1,000 daily molecular testing. It also has an intensive care unit for the treatment of the severe coronavirus cases.   This project is linked to Project ID#93020, which captures the anti-epidemic materials donated by the CCECC alongside the facilities.

project_name: Construction corporation provided anti-epidemic materials to Lagos
description: On March 30, 2020, China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation (CCECC) provided anti-epidemic materials to the Lagos State Government. The donated materials included face masks, sanitizers, bags of rice, and cash donations. This donation was confirmed by the Minister of Works and Infrastructure Olujimi Hotonu. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  During his acknowledgement, Minister Hotonu thanked CCECC for their donation and stated that the supplies will be used to complement the welfare packages that were previously announced by Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu. These packages, and the CCECC donation, will be distributed to low-income and unemployed individuals. Kevin Liu, a representative of CCECC, stated that the CCECC would provide more donations to Lagos to fight against COVID-19 in the future.

project_name: Embassy donated anti-epidemic materials to the University of Abuja
description: On November 10, 2021, the Chinese Embassy in Nigeria donated anti-epidemic materials to the University of Abuja. The donation includes an unknown quantity of medical masks, ventilators, and oxygen generators. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't provided grant to improve Malaria centre
description: The Chinese Government provided a 1.5 million yuan grant for provision of anti-malaria diagnostic equipment and consumptive materials to the China-Nigeria Anti-Malaria Centre (mentioned in Project ID#34916). The Chinese Government officially completed this project when it provided a handover certificate to the Government of Nigeria on or around May 8, 2014.

project_name: Embassy donated funds to remodel psychiatric ward of hospital
description: On November 20, 2019, the Chinese Embassy in Nigeria donated 11 million Naira to the Kebbi State Government. The purpose of the donation was to remodel the psychiatric ward of the general hospital in Zauro, Kebbi State.

project_name: Consulate provided 1st batch of anti-epidemic materials to Lagos
description: On April 17, 2020, the Chinese Consulate-General and the Overseas Chinese Association in Nigeria jointly provided the first batch of anti-epidemic materials worth N170 million to the Lagos State Government in Nigeria. The donated materials included 12,000 face masks, 100 protective clothing, 2,000 forehead thermometers, 2,000 surgical gloves, 1,550 hand sanitizers, one ventilator, and a check for N35.38 million.   A handover ceremony was held for this donation. Lagos State Communications Director, Frederick Olainde, attended the ceremony and received the donation from the Consul General of the People’s Republic of China in Lagos, Chu Maoming, on behalf of the Lagos government.  This is reported as the first batch provided by the Chinese Consulate-General to Nigeria. The details of the second batch, which took place on April 21,2020, are captured in Project ID #93093.

project_name: Gov't donated 12 ambulances for Ebola response activities
description: On May 15, 2015, the Chinese Government donated 12 ambulances to the Nigerian Center for Disease Control in Abuja. The ambulances were meant to support the Ebola response activities 12 hospitals in six major regions of the country. The Secretaries of the Nigerian Center for Disease Control and Ministry of Health spoke at the ambulance delivery ceremony. Only 11 of the 12 ambulances were ultimately handed over as one was damaged during the delivery process.

project_name: Gov't donated 2 million naira to the Nigerian Red Cross society
description: On December 12, 2013 the Chinese Embassy in Nigeria donated 2 million Nigerian naira to the Nigerian Red Cross Society. The donation was for the sensitization and mobilization of 12,600 people in Takar Local Government Area (LGA) and Katsina-Ala Local Government Area (LGA) within Benue State. Bello Diram, Secretary-General of the Nigerian Red Cross Society said at the time that 30 volunteers would reach 1800 households for HIV testing, awareness, and referrals to local health institutions.

project_name: Gov't donated equipment for combatting Avian flu worth ngn 70 million
description: In November 2007, China donated over NGN 70 million worth of equipment for controlling and fighting the avian flu to Nigeria's agriculture and water resource departments. The equipment was received by Dr. Abba Ruma, Minister of Agriculture and Water Resources. The equipment includes biological sitting cabinets, temperature freezers, an incinerator, and disinfectant equipment.  The gesture marked the second instance China has offered medical assistance to Nigeria this month. At the beginning of November, the Chinese government donated 529,000 doses of anti-malaria drugs in various forms to the Nigerian health administration.

project_name: China donated med. equipments to China-Nigeria friendship hospital
description: The Chinese government promise to provide a supplementary grant of medical equipments and materials worth 250 million Naira to the China-Nigeria Friendship Hospital on February 23, 2012. The current status of the donation is unclear.   The hospital is recorded in #30629.

project_name: Chamber of Commerce & corporation provide PPE to ministry of finance
description: On June 29, 2020, the China General Chamber of Commerce and China Great Wall Industry Corporation jointly provided anti-epidemic materials to the Nigerian Federal Ministry of Finance, Budget and National Planning. The materials included face masks, hand thermometers, thermal thermometers and other protective equipment. The announcement of this donation was communicated through a statement signed by the Special Advisor on Media and Communications, Yunusa Tanko Abdullahi. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. Nigeria’s Finance Minister, Zainab Ahmed and President of the China General Chamber of Commerce, Ye Shuijin, attended the ceremony.

project_name: China railway construction corporation provided anti-epidemic supplies
description: On April 8, 2020, China Railway Construction Corporation’s medical professional team provided anti-epidemic equipment, worth N1.5 million, to Nigeria. The supplies included face masks and personal protective equipment.   A handover ceremony took place for this donation at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport in Abuja, Nigeria. Zhou Pingjian, the Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria, representatives of the Nigerian Federal Government, and the Nigerian Minister of Health attended the ceremony.
