On behalf of the federal government, the Minister of Health welcomed the CRCC Epidemic Prevention Working Group and congratulated the Chinese government on their victory in the fight against COVID-19. The medical team provided alongside the donation is captured in Project ID#93020.

project_name: Gov't provided USD 1,075,000 to support Covid-19 via WHO
description: In March 2020, Chinese government provides USD 1,075,000 to support WHO response to COVID-19 outbreak in Nigeria.

project_name: Gov't commits to donate anti-Malaria medicine to Rwanda
description: On May 15, 2007 in Beijing, Rwandan President Paul Kagame and Chinese President Hu Jintao signed an agreement for China to provide Rwanda with anti-malaria medicine. The amount of medicine pledged as well as the project's current status are unknown.

project_name: China provided grant for kabuga hospital in Rwanda
description: On November 24, 2008, Rosemary Museminali, the Rwandan Minister for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, and Sun Shuzhong, the Chinese Ambassador to Rwanda, signed a grant agreement worth 10 million RMB for the construction of Kabuga hospital in Kigali, Rwanda. The construction, by Huashan International Engineering Company, started in August 2009 and finished in July 2011.

project_name: China Star donated nucleic acid tests to Ministry to test for Covid
description: On March 21, 2020, the Chinese construction company, China Star, donated 96 nucleic acid diagnostic kits to Rwanda’s Ministry of Health. A handover ceremony was held for this donation. The tests will be used to test for COVID-19 throughout Rwanda. This was the first pandemic donation from China Star to Rwanda. The second donation was delivered on April 1, 2020, and consisted of various types of protective supplies (see project ID#92431).

project_name: Gov't commits grant via WHO for Covid-19 pandemic relief in Rwanda
description: On March 10, 2020, the Chinese government committed a grant of USD 1,222,848 to support the WHO response to the COVID-19 outbreak in Rwanda.   This project is captured in UNOCHA Financial Tracking Service as Flow ID #218747.

project_name: Embassy hands over med. supplies to Ministry of Health to fight Covid
description: On September 22, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Rwanda handed over the second of medical supplies donated by the Chinese Government to the Ministry of Health of Rwanda. The first donation was received on April 26, 2020. In April, it was planned that this donation would consist of 5,000 medical preventive suits, 10,000 N95 face masks, 100,000 surgical masks, and 3000 medical eye shields. The handover ceremony took place at the Medical Purchasing and Production Department (MPCC) warehouse of the Rwanda Biomedical Center (RBC) in Kigali. Wang Jiaxin, the Commercial Counselor of the Embassy, and Zacharie Iyakaremye, the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Health of Rwanda, attended the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't grant for district hospital upgrading & expansion project
description: In 2017, the Chinese Government was reportedly agreed to help upgrade the hospital in Kibungo. The purpose of the Kibungo District Hospital Upgrading and Expansion Project is intended to increase the capacity of the facility from 242 to to over 1,200 beds. The facility in Kibungo is in Ngoma district and former Kibungo province. The Chinese Government grant contribution amount is unknown. The Chinese Government originally funded the construction of this hospital in 2002 (see Project ID#57434). Itis also funding a similar upgrade to the Masaka hospital (Project ID#53267).

project_name: China constructs anti-Malaria center in Rwanda
description: In 2009, the Chinese Government agreed to fund the construction of an anti-malaria center the Masaka Hospital, which was also being built with grant funding from the Chinese Government at the same time (see Project ID#56850). The center is located in the Masaka neighborhood in the capital city of Kigali. Its location lies approximately 17 kilometres, by road, east of the central business district of Kigali. The geographical coordinates of anti-malarial center at the Masaka Hospital are 01°59'30.0"S, 30°12'43.0"E (Latitude:-1.991667; Longitude:30.211944). The groundbreaking ceremony for the center took place on May 8, 2009.

project_name: Embassy donated anti-epidemic materials to the Imbuto Foundation
description: On May 7, 2021, the Chinese Embassy in Rwanda donated anti-epidemic materials to the Imbuto Foundation. The supplies include medical masks, hand sanitizers, forehead thermometers, and Mara smartphones, and were valued at RWF 53 million. The Imbuto foundation is a Rwandan NGO founded by First Lady of Rwanda Jeanette Kagame.

project_name: China donated med. equipment to masaka hospital in Rwanda
description: On May 5, 2013 the Chinese government donated 1,624,000 USD worth of laboratory kits, consultation machines, baby incubators, syringes, an ambulance, and other types of equipment to Masaka Hospital in Rwanda. The donation was made by Shu Zhan, Chinese Ambassador to Rwanda, on behalf of the Chinese government, and is intended to improve the quality of service at the hospital.

project_name: Consultative conference donated med. supplies to senate to fight Covid
description: On July 23, 2020 the Chinese Embassy in Rwanda handed over a batch of medical supplies to the Senate of the Republic of Rwanda. The medical supplies were donated by the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC). The donation consisted of 22,400 disposable medical masks. The handover ceremony took place at the parliament building in Kigali, the capital city of Rwanda. Wang Jiaxin, the Commercial Counselor of the Embassy, and Sosthene Cyitatire, the Clerk at the Senate, attended the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't donated 300,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: On November 7, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered another 300,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Rwanda. A handover ceremony was held at Kigali International Airport. Wang Jiaxin, Commercial Counselor of the Embassy, and Dr. Albert Tuyishime, Head of Department at Rwanda Biomedical Centre attended the ceremony.   This donation is one in a series of vaccine donations. On August 19, 2021, Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Rwanda (see project ID#95960). Then, on January 11, 2022,  Rao Hongwei, Ambassador of the People’s Republic of China to Rwanda, had a phone call with Hon. Vincent Biruta, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Rwanda, and officially notified him that the Chinese Government would donate a total of 4 million doses of COVID-19 vaccines to Rwanda in 2022. However, as of December 2022, there was no evidence of this pledge being fulfilled.

project_name: PLA donated med. supplies to defense force to fight against Covid
description: On June 3, 2020, medical supplies from China worth USD 290,000 arrived at Kigali International Airport. The supplies were donated to the Rwanda Defense Force (RDF) from the People's Liberation Army of China. Rao Hongwei, China’s Ambassador to Rwanda, and General Jean Bosco Kazura, the Chief of Defense Staff of Rwanda Defense Force, signed the handover certificate at the airport upon the arrival of the supplies.  The donated medical supplies were valued at USD 290,000 and included 50,000 units of disposable medical masks, 6,000 surgical masks, 6,000 medical N95 respirators, 4,200 medical safety goggles, 3,000 disposable medical protective face shields, 3,000 disposable one-piece protective gowns, 3,000 waterproof isolation gowns, 6,000 medical boots covers, 50 disposable nitrile gloves, 30 infusion pumps,  50 non-contact forehead infrared thermometers, 2 knapsack disinfection sprayers (16L) and 2 helmets for infrared temperature measurement.

project_name: China donated med. instruments & medicine to Rwanda
description: On August 28-30, 2006, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Chinese Communist Party, Wu Guanzheng , and Rwandan President Paul Kagame exchanged a letter according to which China will provide some 2 million CNY worth of medical instruments, general medicine, and anti-malaria medicine. The current status and start and end dates are unknown.

project_name: 1st lady of China donated supplies to 1st lady of Rwanda against Covid
description: On July 7, 2020, the Rwanda Biomedical Center (RBC) received 120,000 body temperature testers and 18,000 surgical face masks from the First Lady of China, Peng Liyuan. The supplies were a donation for the First Lady of Rwanda, Jeannette Kagame, and were delivered to Dr. Sabin Nsanzimana, the Director General of RBC. The First Lady of China donated the supplies to the Organization of African First Ladies, which then donated supplies to Rwanda.   The handover ceremony was held at the MPPC warehouse of Rwanda Biomedical Center (RBC) in Kigali. The Political Counselor of the Chinese Embassy in Rwanda, Xing Yuchun, the Advisor to the First Lady of Rwanda, Radegonde Ndejuru, and RBC’s Dr. Sabin Nsanzimana attended the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for Masaka hospital construction project
description: In 2006, the Chinese Government agreed to provide an RMB 60 million grant for the design and construction of the Masaka hospital in the Kicukiro District in Kigali. However, the grant did not initially disburse until August 20, 2008. Eventually, the Chinese Government provided an additional RMB 40 million of grant funding, bringing its total grant commitment for the project to RMB 100 million. The purpose of this project was to build a hospital with 100 beds and internal medicine, surgery, women and children departments, providing medical services to 320,000 local residents. China also provided medical equipment that the hospital might need to make it have better medical conditions. Construction began on May 7, 2009. The project was completed and the hospital was put into use on August 18, 2011. The hospital is located in the Masaka neighborhood, in the capital city of Kigali, the capital of Rwanda and the largest city in that country. Its location lies approximately 17 kilometres, by road, east of the central business district of Kigali. The geographical coordinates of Masaka Hospital are 01°59'30.0"S, 30°12'43.0"E (Latitude: -1.991667; Longitude: 30.211944).  The hospital offers services in general medicine, emergency medicine, traditional Chinese medicine, dentistry, orthopedic surgery, and psychiatry. As of July 2018, the hospital was operated by a team of six Chinese doctors assisted by a smaller number of Rwandan medical doctors and dentists.  Other disciplines offered at this hospital include maternity services, internal medicine, pediatrics, imaging services, general surgery, tuberculosis treatment, nutrition services, general anesthesia, HIV/AIDS treatment, and outpatient services. The hospital is intended to serve, primarily the residents of (a) Kicukiro District (b) Gasabo District and (c) Rwamagana District. The target population numbers between 380,000 and 400,000 people. The hospital is administered directly by the Rwanda Ministry of Health.

project_name: Embassy donated Covid protection kit & other supplies to association
description: On May 20, 2020, the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in the Republic of Rwanda, represented by Ambassador Rao Hongwei, facilitated the donation of COVID-19 protection materials to the Rwanda Wushu Association. Also included was corn flour, rice, beans, and cooking oil among other goods like masks. Receiving on behalf of Rwanda was Mr. Ma Boko, Permanent Secretary of Sports Ministry, and Mr. Richard, Vice President of Lu Wushu Association. The donation was valued at 24 million RWF.

project_name: Gov't donated med. supplies to Ministry of Health to fight Covid
description: On April 26, 2020, a handover ceremony took place for the donation of medical supplies from the Chinese Government to Rwanda.The ceremony was held at the MPPC warehouse of Rwanda Biomedical Center (RBC) in Kigali. The Chinese Ambassador to Rwanda,  Rao Hongwei, the Minister of Health of Rwanda, Dr. Daniel Ngamije, and officials from RBC attended the ceremony.  During the ceremony, the supplies were handed over to the Ministry of Health of Rwanda. The supplies included 2,000 N95 face masks, 10,000 surgical masks, 2,000 items of disposable protective clothing, 500 infrared thermometers, 2,000 medical protective goggles, 10,000 pairs of shoes covers, and disposable sterilized rubber surgical gloves.  This is the first official batch of emergency supplies that the Chinese Government has donated to Rwanda. A second batch arrived in September of 2020 (see project ID#92429).

project_name: China star donated med. equipment for the fight against Covid
description: On April 1, 2020, China Star, a Chinese construction company, donated medical equipment to Rwanda. The donated equipment included 60,000 surgical masks, 600 medical protective suits, 1,000 KN95 masks, 510 N95 masks and 908 disposable surgical suits. This is China Star's second donation of pandemic supplies to Rwanda. The first donation, on March 21, 2020, consisted of 96 nucleic acid testing kits (see project ID#92438). According to Wang Jiaxin, the Economic and Commercial Counselor at Chinese Embassy in Rwanda, the donation has been sent to a warehouse of RwandAir in Guangzhou, China. The transportation of the donation will be handled by the Rwandan Government.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for Masaka hospital expansion project
description: On June 1, 2016, Commercial Section Counselor Zhang Liyong at the Chinese Embassy to Rwanda and Rwandan Ministry of Health Permanent Secretary Jean-Pierre signed an agreement on the Masaka Hospital Expansion Project. The two sides reached a basic agreement on the scale of construction and the division of responsibilities between the two parties. The project will increase the number of beds from 140 to 1,356. The Chinese governments agreed to funded this project with a grant of about $42 million. The Masaka hospital was first constructed between 2009 and 2011 with an RMB 100 million grant from the Chinese Government (see Project ID#56850). The hospital is located in the Masaka neighborhood of the capital city of Kigali. Its location lies approximately 17 kilometres, by road, east of the central business district of Kigali. The geographical coordinates of Masaka Hospital are 01°59'30.0"S, 30°12'43.0"E (Latitude: -1.991667; Longitude: 30.211944).

project_name: Gov't donated 200,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: On August 19, 2021, Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Rwanda. A donation ceremony was held at Kigali International Airport. Rao Hongwei, the Chinese Ambassador to Rwanda, and Daniel Ngamije, Rwanda's Minister of Health signed the handover certificate. According to the Chinese ambassador, the commitment to donate the vaccines had been made about a month prior.   This donation is one in a series of vaccine donations. On November 7, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered another 300,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Rwanda (see project ID#95959). On January 11, 2022,  Rao Hongwei, Ambassador of the People’s Republic of China to Rwanda, had a phone call with Hon. Vincent Biruta, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Rwanda, and officially notified him that the Chinese Government would donate a total of 4 million doses of COVID-19 vaccines to Rwanda in 2022. However, as of December 2022, there was no evidence of this pledge being fulfilled.

project_name: Gov't donated anti-Malaria supplies
description: On June 10, 2019, the Chinese Government donated anti-malaria supplies to Sao Tome and Principle in a ceremony in the capital of STP. The handover certificate was signed by Ambassador Wang Wei of China and Minister of Health Neves of Sao Tome and Principe on behalf of the two governments. The materials contribute to Sao Tome and Principe's goal to eliminate malaria by 2025. Details of the supplies donated and their monetary value are unknown.

project_name: Gov't donated a batch of Covid-19 medicine & med. equipments
description: On March 26, 2020, at a ceremony held at the Ayres de Menezes Central Hospital in São Tomé and Príncipe, Ambassador Wang Wei, representing the Chinese government, delivered a batch of medicines and medical equipment to the Sao Tome Minister of Health, Mr. Edgar Neves. The equipment included antibiotics, vision monitor, cardiac defibrillator, and a ventilator to help the country be prepared for COVID-19.

project_name: Gov't pledges grant for construction of Dr. Ayres Menezes Hospital
description: The Chinese Government has agreed to a grant to be provided to the Sao Tome & Principe Government for construction of the Dr. Ayres Menezes Hospital. The financing package will have a grant element of at least 35%. The hospital is also being financed by a USD $17 million loan with a 34% grant element from Kuwait. Additional information on the grant and its implementation status is unknown.

project_name: Hospital established telemedicine PLAtform with hospital
description: On June 4, 2019, the West China Hospital at Sichuan University donated a telemedicine unit to the largest hospital in Sao Tome and Principe, also known as The Dr. Ayres de Menezes Hospital. This telemedicine unit allows the West China Hospital to provide technical assistance to Sao Tomean doctors, helping to train and assist physicians, and to provide remote consultations to Sao Tomean patients at the Dr. Ayres de Menezes Hospital. The unit was also expected to eventually allow Chinese doctors to perform surgery remotely using robots. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  Dr. Ayres de Menezes Hospital also has a telemedicine unit with the Portuguese Institute of Valle Flor.  In Portuguese, the project name is "Hospital oeste da China da Universidade de Sichuan Hospital Central de Sao Tome e Principe, unidos pela alianca internacionale hospitalar em rede."

project_name: Gov't donated 130,000 euros worth of med. supplies & equipment
description: On January 15, 2019, the Chinese Government donated 130,000 euros worth of medical equipment and medicine to hospitals in Sao Tome and Principe. The aid went to the largest hospital in Sao Tome, the Hospital Ayres de Menezes. This comes as the third medical donation from China to Sao Tome in the two years leading up to the 130,000 euro donation.

project_name: Gov't donated vehicles for the Malaria technical assistance project
description: On September 12, 2019, the Chinese Government donated vehicles as a part of the Anti-Malaria Technical Assistance Project (Phase II) to Sao Tome and Principe's Ministry of Health. The handover ceremony took place on this day, with speeches given by Chinese Ambassador to Sao Tome and Principe Wang Wei and Sao Tome and Principe Health Minister Edgar Neves. Wang and Neves also signed the handover agreement on behalf of the two governments. This is part of an overarching effort backed by China to eliminate malaria in Sao Tome and Principe by 2025.

project_name: Hospital donated remote consultation PLAtform equip to hospitals
description: On June 4, 2019, the West China Hospital of Sichuan Univerity donated remote consultation platform equipment to various Sao Tome and Principe hospitals. These hospitals include Aérez de Menezes Central Hospital, Sao Tome and Principe National Central Hospital, and International Network Alliance Hospital. This donation is part of China's "Eight Actions" from the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. Sao Tome and Principe's Minister of Health and the Chinese Ambassador to Sao Tome and Principe attended the ceremony.

project_name: cidca granted in agreement with UNFPA to provide healthcare assistance
description: On December 31, 2020, Zhang Maoyu, vice-chairman of the China International Development Cooperation Agency (CIDCA), signed a cooperation agreement with a representative of the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) that granted 1,000,000 USD to provide healthcare assistance to Sao Tome and Principe.  The CIDCA and the UNFPA agreed to cooperate on providing healthcare assistance to Sao Tome and Principe and Gambia in Central and West Africa that are affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. The project, supported by the South-South Cooperation Assistance Fund, aims to improve the capabilities in pandemic control and response in Sao Tome and Principe and Gambia and ensure their health systems can continuously provide basic public health services such as reproductive and maternal care during the pandemic. The 1,000,000 USD was used to provide PPE and medical supply to health workers to ensure the continuity of sexual and reproductive health services and the supply of essential reproductive health commodities.

project_name: Commission donated med. equipments for Covid to Ministry of Health
description: On December 15, 2020, the handover ceremony of the anti-epidemic medical equipment donated by the National Health Commission of China to the Ministry of Health of Sao Tome and Principe was held in the anti-epidemic material warehouse of Sao Tome. Gao Jinbao, Commercial Counselor of the embassy, ​​Viana, Director of International Cooperation of the Ministry of Health of Sao Tome and Principe, Almeida, Director of the National Center for Disease Control and Prevention of Sao Tome and Principe, and You Zhen, Captain of the 16th medical team in Sao Tome and Principe attended the ceremony. The medical equipment included ventilators, electrocardiogram machines, oxygen generators, and expectoration machines.

project_name: China donated a mobile cabin hospital
description: On May 26, 2020, Wang Wei, Chinese Ambassador to Sao Tome and Principe, and Sao Tome and Principe Minister of Health Neves jointly visited the spare makeshift hospital funded by the Chinese Embassy in Sao Tome and Principe. São Tomé and Príncipe’s spare mobile cabin hospital was renovated from the auditorium of São Tomé and Príncipe National Middle School. It has 40 beds and is designed to accommodate 70 beds maximum. The renovation of water and electricity pipelines, the purchase of mattresses and other supporting basic living materials were funded by the Chinese Embassy in São Tomé and Príncipe. The Chinese Medical Team in São Tomé and Príncipe is responsible for the hospital's nosocomial infection control zoning design.

project_name: Gov't donated mobile health unit
description: On March 4th, 2019, the Chinese Government donated a mobile healthcare unit to the Ministry of Health of Sao Tome and Principe. This mobile unit was delivered to Health Minister, Dr. Edgar Neves, and has adequate conditions for primary healthcare in the area of disease prevention and health promotion. The unit will aid the Dr. Ayres de Menezes Hospital and the National Health Service in providing healthcare services to Sao Tomeans. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  In Portuguese, the mobile healthcare unit is known as the "unidade móvel de saúde."

project_name: Gov't signed the contract on anti-Malaria technical assistance project
description: One June 1, 2020, the signing of contract between China and Sao Tome and Principe about Anti-Malaria Technical Assistance Project (Phase III) was held in the Ministry of Health of Sao Tome and Principe. Phase III of the project was implemented in two years. Among the projects undertaken during Phase III was the renovation of a malaria-tracking laboratory built with Chinese aid and a team of Chinese anti-malaria experts to carry out a mass drug administration (MDA) for 10 malaria-prone villages in Sao Tome and Principe. This project aims to eliminate Malaria in Sao Tome and Principe by 2025.   Phase II of the Anti-Malaria Technical Assistance Project is captured and detailed in Project ID#85767.

project_name: Gov't donated anti-Malaria supplies to support campaign in districts
description: On September 18, 2017, a ceremony attended by Wang Wei (the Chinese ambassador in Sao Tome) was held to hand over supplies — including anti-malaria drugs and sophisticated medial equipment like microscopes, intelligent mosquito detectors, automatic microplate readers, and medical cryogenic refrigerators — to the Government of São Tomé and Príncipe to support an anti-malarial campaign in Água Grande District and Mé-Zóchi District.

project_name: Gov't donated Covid supplies to the Red Cross society
description: On July 24, 2020, Wang Wei, Ambassador to Sao Tome and Principe, handed over to Lima, Director-General of the Red Cross Society of Sao Tome and Principe, the anti-epidemic materials donated to Sao Tome and Principe by Professor Peng Liyuan, wife of Chinese President Xi Jinping, on behalf of the Chinese government. The donation consisted of 10,000 masks and some infrared thermometers.

project_name: Gov't donated 100,000 Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: On September 13, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 100,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Sao Tome and Principe.

project_name: Ambassador provided 2nd batch of supplies to combat Covid
description: On June 12, 2020, the Chinese ambassador handed over the second batch of covid supplies to Sao Tome and Principe. It consisted of 5000 pcr test kits, N95 masks, gloves, and PPE. The supplies arrived in the country on June 11, 2020.

project_name: Gov't sent Covid-19 med. supplies
description: On April 17, 2020, the handover ceremony of Chinese government donation of COVID-19 medical supplies to the government of Sao Tome and Principe was held.  The supplies included N95 masks, ordinary medical masks, medical protective clothing, gloves, shoe covers, goggles, and forehead thermometers. The supplies arrived in Sao Tome on April 15 after arriving in Ghana for distribution on April 6.

project_name: China donated med. supplies to the serving Senegal foundation
description: On June 17th, 2019, the handover ceremony occurred for a batch of medical supplies donated from China to the "Serving Senegal" (Servir le Sénégal) Foundation. The Chinese government donated 1,260 walkers and 126 pierced chairs, the cost being equivalent to CFA $43 million, or around US $78,000.   The Foundation, headed by the first lady of Senegal Marieme Faye Salle, carries out projects to help youth and women and improve the state of health in Dakar. The Chinese government donated walking aids and toilet chairs to the Foundation in support of the "Elderly Assistance Program" promoted by the Senegalese government. The First Lady of Senegal, Marieme Faye Salle, the Minister of Health and Social Action Abdulaye Diouf Sal, the Vice Chairman of the Foundation, Alioune Sal and the main members of the foundation attended the ceremony as well as Chinese Ambassador Zhang Xun.

project_name: Zhejiang Guangsha donated funds & masks to city
description: On June 30, 2020, Zhejiang Guangsha Construction Vocational and Technical College donated 18,000 masks and $20,000 RMB to Guédiawaye, Senegal. Alongside the donation, students and teachers from Zhejiang Guangsha arranged a video conference where they also shared proper mask wearing techniques and aerobic exercise routines with Senegalese students in Guédiawaye.

project_name: Embassy grants drugs & med. supplies to the pikine hospital
description: On April 7, 2016 the Chinese Embassy in Senegal granted 46 million CFA Francs worth of drugs and medical supplies to the Pikine hospital in Dakar.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for children’s hospital construction project
description: In 2010, the Chinese Government agreed to provided an RMB 63.5 million grant to the Government of Senegal for the Diamniadio Children’s Hospital Construction Project. This project was funded with the grant proceeds from an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) that was signed on January 29, 2009. The Government of Senegal also provided 901 million FCFA of counterpart funding.   This project involved the construction of a children’s hospital with 136 beds in Diamniadio City, Rufisque Province, and Dakar Region (about 40 kilometers away from  Dakar) on a 2.8 hectare site and a construction area of 8,000 square meters. China Railway Seventh Group was responsible for project implementation. On March 26, 2010, a groundbreaking ceremony for the hospital was held. Then, on June 26, 2010, construction began. On January 18, 2014, the Diamniadio Children's Hospital (HED) was inaugurated by Senegal President Wade and officially handed over to the Senegalese authorities. The hospital had been operational since June 2012, but the construction project itself was not complete until January 2014.

project_name: Exchanged letters to support technical mission at national hospital
description: On February 8, 2018, Senegal and China signed the exchange of letters for the continuation of the support of the technical mission at the National Children’s Hospital Center in Diamniadio (Centre national hospitalier d’enfants de Diamniadio) ("继续为迪亚姆尼亚久儿童医院开展技术服务的换文"). The agreement was signed between the Chinese Ambassador to Senegal, Zhang Xun and Amadou Ba, the Minister of Economy, Finance and Planning of Senegal. The agreement stipulates that China will provide Senegal with technical assistance through a team of six members who will be responsible for training Senegalese technicians on how to use and maintain the facilities and equipment of the Diamniadio Children's Center.   In October 25, 2017, Senegal and China signed the implementing agreement for the expansion of the National Children’s Hospital Center in Diamniadio and provide the hospital with necessary medical facilities.  On November 15, 2018, the construction officially began and was certified as completed on December 19, 2019 (captured in #58274).

project_name: China donated supplies to hospital after 'brightness walk' operation
description: From November 9 to 23, 2018, the Fujian Provincial Health and Family Planning Commission coordinated and implemented the "Brightness Walk" (光明行) project. Cataract surgeries were performed on a total of 223 Senegalese patients with eye diseases (recorded in #86620).  Medical supplies were also donated to the hospital. Counselor Han Xiaofei and Pikine Hospital President Guye signed the handover certificate for the donation of ophthalmic equipment, consumables, medicines and other materials from China to Senegal.

project_name: Gov't organizes anti-Malarial training workshop in Senegal
description: In 2007, the Chinese Government sponsored a training workshop in Senegal to educate individuals on the fight against malaria.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for maternal & child hospital expansion project
description: On May 10, 2017, the Chinese Government and the Government of Senegal signed letters of exchange related to the Maternal and Child Hospital Expansion Project. China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) reportedly committed RMB 36,680,200 in grant funding for this project. The purpose of this project was to build a three-story obstetrics and gynecology complex with 84 hospital beds and 3 surgery rooms at the National Children's Hospital. China Electronics Engineering Design Institute (CEEDI) was responsible for project design. China Railway First Group was the contractor responsible for project implementation. Beijing Xida Engineering Consulting was also involved as a sub-contractor. On October 25, 2017, a project implementation agreement (援塞内加尔妇幼医院项目对外实施协议) was signed in Dakar. Then, on November 15, 2018, a groundbreaking ceremony for the project was held.  The project was originally scheduled for completion on November 17, 2019. However, it ultimately passed MOFCOM’s final inspection on December 22, 2019.

project_name: Gov't donated a batch of anti-Malarial drugs
description: On January 19, 2012, the Chinese Government donated a batch of anti-malarial drugs to the Government of Senegal. The monetary value of this donation is unknown. The Prime Minister of State, Souleymane Ndéné Ndiaye, and the Prime Minister of Health, Awa Marie Coll-Seck, were present at the donation ceremony.

project_name: China carries out the 'brightness walk' Ophthalmology activities
description: From November 9th to 23rd, 2018, the Fujian Provincial Health and Family Planning Commission coordinated and implemented the "Brightness Walk" (光明行) project. Cataract surgeries were performed on a total of 223 Senegalese patients with eye diseases. The team performing the surgeries was composed of members of the National Health and Family Planning Commission's "Bright Action" expert group, Professor Chen Weirong and his team from Zhongshan Eye Center of Sun Yat-Sen University, and Professor Xu Guoxing and his team from the First Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University. Along with Professor Weirong and Professor Guoxing, there were seven team members total. They also cooperated with the 17th Chinese medical team in Senegal.   In addition to the surgeries, they also carried out ophthalmic health education, academic exchanges and training of Chinese and foreign medical staff. On the 21st, a lecture was carried out by Professor Xu and Professor Chen on eye care and treatment of senile cataract. The event took place at Pikine National Hospital. The official surgery carried out is called "phacoemulsification". Medical supplies were also donated to the hospital (recorded in #88638). Counselor Han Xiaofei and Pikine Hospital President Guye signed the handover certificate for the donation of ophthalmic equipment, consumables, medicines and other materials from China to Senegal.

project_name: Gov't donated batch of anti-Malarial drugs worth $250,000
description: In 2006, the Chinese Government donated a batch of anti-malarial drugs to the Government of Senegal worth $250,000.   The French project title is don de médicaments antipaludique.

project_name: Embassy delivers municipal gov't's donation of covid med. supplies
description: On June 30, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Senegal and the Dakar Municipal Government held a handover ceremony to celebrate the arrival of anti-COVID-19 supplies donated by the municipal government of Guangzhou, China. The aid will go to support Dakar's "Million Masks" campaign.

project_name: Gov't donated batch of anti-Malarial supplies & equipment
description: On September 13, 2013, the Chinese Government donated a batch of anti-malarial supplies and equipment to the China-Senegal Malaria Prevention and Treatment Center (or Centre Chine-Sénégal de Prévention et de Traitement du Paludisme) worth CFA 120 million. The China-Senegal Malaria Prevention and Treatment Center is located at the Pikine National Hospital Center (Centre hospitalier National de Pikine) in Dakar.

project_name: Gov't donated batch of anti-Malarial drugs
description: On September 14, 2017, the Chinese Government donated a batch of anti-malarial drugs — specifically, 24,830 boxes of "Duo Cotecxin" with 9 tablets in each box —  to the Government of Senegal worth CFA 2 billion.   The French project title is don de médicaments antipaludique.

project_name: Gov't donated Covid-19 relief supplies to the Senegalese Ministry
description: On July 3, 2020, the Chinese Government donated Covid-19 relief supplies to the Senegalese Ministry of Health and Social Action. The donation included 10,032 testing reagents,10,000 sets of protective clothing, 15,000 pairs of goggles, and 20,000 N95 Masks, 15,000 pairs of gloves, 3,000 pairs of shoe covers and 350,000 surgical masks and other medical supplies. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.   This donation is comprised of two parts. The first, which contains the majority of the supplies donated, is the third batch of supplies donated by the Chinese government. The second comprises 20,000 surgical masks and is donated China Road and Bridge Senegal Corporation. After the handover ceremony was completed, representatives from the two sides signed the intergovernmental handover certificate for the third batch of anti-epidemic goods.

project_name: Gov't donated Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses & syringes
description: On May 14 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 300,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines and 308,000 syringes to the Government of Senegal. The vaccine doses and syringes are worth $5.4 million.  The donation was transported from Beijing to Darkar on an Air Senegal flight.

project_name: CIDCA & Mofcom donated 2nd batch of Covid-19 relief supplies
description: On April 20, 2020, the Chinese Ministry of Commerce and China International Development Cooperation Agency donated the second batch of COVID-19 relief supplies to Senegal and held a handover ceremony with the Senegalese Ministry of Health and Social Action on April 22. The shipment included 1,750 N95 masks, 10,000 surgical masks, 1,750 disposable coveralls, 350 infrared thermometers, 1,750 protection glasses, 9,750 pairs of disposable nitrile gloves, and 9,750 pairs of disposable shoe covers. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: China donated to UNICEF to help combat pediatric malnutrition
description: On March 11, 2020, the Government of China committed to donate USD 1,000,000 to the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) to fight pediatric malnutrition in Senegal during the Covid-19 Pandemic. The donation was completed by November 3, 2020 and intended to benefit 17,355 children under the age of five in north and east Senegal including the regions of Diourbel, Louga, Matam, Tambacounda and Saint Louis. The COVID-19 pandemic has increased the risk of malnutrition among children in Senegal due to the deterioration in the quality of their food, lack of access to nutrition and other health care services, and the shocks caused by the pandemic.

project_name: Gov't donated $304,870.91 USD of anti-Malarial drugs
description: On May 4, 2010, the Chinese Government donated a batch of anti-malarial medications to the Government of Senegal. The drugs donated by the Chinese government were supposed to facilitate the implementation of 'Free Malaria Treatment Program' advocated by President Abdoulaye Wade and further boost Senegal's anti-malaria capacity. The recorded grant disbursement amount in the Government of Senegal’s External Financing Management Platform (la Plateforme de Gestion des Financements Extérieurs du Sénégal, or PGFE) is $304,870.91 USD.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for establishment of Malaria center
description: In 2009, the Chinese Government provided a grant for the establishment of a China-Senegal Malaria Prevention and Treatment Center at the Pikine National Hospital Center (Centre hospitalier National de Pikine) in Dakar. The monetary value of this grant is unknown. This project was completed but the exact date of completion is unknown.   According to a 2011 Working Series report, in October 2009, the Jiangsu Anti-malaria Center sent experts to Senegal to provide anti-malaria training to more than 180 local health officials and medical specialists and complete the preparatory work of establishing the Senegal Malaria Control Center as part of the 12th group of malaria experts China has sent to Africa. Project #34838 covers the sending of experts. This project is for the grant for the center.   The French project title is Centre Chine-Sénégal de Prévention et de Traitement du Paludisme. The Chinese project title is 在比基纳医院援建了疟疾防治中心.

project_name: China donated vaccine doses & syringes to Ministry
description: On November 5, 2021, the Department of Prevention within Senegal's Ministry of Health and Social Action received 500,000 Sinopharm vaccine doses and 502,400 syringes from China.   This donation was given as a part of the #Covax Initiative.

project_name: JPC group donated pandemic materials to children's hospital
description: On June 19, 2020, Jiangsu Provincial Construction (JPC) Group donated anti-pandemic materials to Diamniadio Children's Hospital in Senegal. The donation included surgical masks, protective clothing, goggles, biological microscopes, three-channel electrocardiogram machines, bedside monitors, and syphgmomanometers, among other pieces of medical equipment. The exact amount and monetary value of the donation is unknown. During the handover ceremony, Gong Zhen, the leader of the third technical assistance project team of the Children's Hospital, and Mam Gay, the director of the Hospital were present.   The monetary value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for friendship fitness park project
description: In 2016, the Chinese Government funded the constrution of China-Senegal Friendship Fitness Park in Dakar. The park is located near the University of Dakar and is one of several such fitness parks that China is building throughout Senegal. According to Han Xiaofei, Economic and Commercial Counselor of Chinese Embassy in Senegal, multiple fitness parks have been built along the Corniche ouest Boulevard in Dakar by Chinese Embassy and Chinese enterprises in Senegal.   The project is apparently only in Phase I, with the first fitness park costing slightly less than RMB 3 million. According to Chinese Ambassador to Senegal Zhang Xun, five fitness parks have been built in five of the country’s provincial capitals, and two more will be added. As of March 28, 2018, the Thies-China-Senegal Friendship Fitness Park was also complete.

project_name: Gov't donated batch of anti-Malarial drugs to Senegal in 2011
description: On January 7, 2011, the Chinese Government donated a batch of anti-malarial drugs to the Government of Senegal.   The French project title is don de médicaments antipaludique.

project_name: China donated the 1st batch of Covid-19 supplies
description: On March 24, 2020, the government of China donated its first batch of Covid-19 supplies to Senegal. The donation included 3,000 pieces of protective clothing, 3,000 glasses, 3,000 masks and 500 infrared thermometers. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: China donated health equipment to the Seychelles hospital
description: On June 1, 2012, China presented assorted medical equipment to the Seychelles Ministry of Health at the Seychelles Hospital. The equipment included items for nerve surgery and cardiac treatment. The donation also included wheelchairs. Chinese ambassador Shi Zhongjun and Seychelles Health Minister Mitcy Larue had first signed a memorandum of understanding for the donation.

project_name: Dalian University donated med. masks to the University of Seychelles
description: On May 15, 2020, the Confucius Institute of the University of Seychelles, on behalf of Dalian University in China, donated 2,000 masks to the University of Seychelles. The purpose of this donation is to help students and professors at the University of Seychelles in fighting against the COVID-19 pandemic. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: Embassy donated med. supplies to the ministry of family affairs
description: On July 22, 2020, the Chinese Embassy donated anti-epidemic medical supplies to Seychelles' Ministry of Family Affairs women, children, and youth amidst the COVID-19 pandemic. This donation was handed over to the Seychellois Minister for Family Affairs, Mr Larue. The purpose of this donation is to help women and children in Seychelles better fight against the epidemic and enhance the welfare of women and children in Seychelles. The amount and value of this donation are not specified, but the purpose of this donation is to help Seychelles in fighting against the COVID-19 pandemic.

project_name: Embassy donated living supplies to Seychelles health care agency
description: On May 14, 2021, the Chinese Embassy in Seychelles donated living supplies to the Seychelles Health Care Agency. The donation includes milk, juice, biscuits, coffee, and shampoo. The estimated value of the donation is SCR 100,000.  The donation was received and will be dispersed by the Seychelles Health Care Agency to healthcare workers in Seychelles.

project_name: Health commission provided med. equipment to health care agency
description: On February 24, 2021, the National Health Commission of China donated medical equipment to the Health Care Agency of the Seychelles. The equipment included a ventilator and oxygen concentrator. The purpose of this donation is to support the Seychelles’ COVID-19 response efforts. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the Chinese Embassy in the Seychelles. The Chief of the Economic and Commercial office of the Chinese Embassy handed over the equipment to Kathleen Cecile, the Deputy Chief Executive of the Health Care Agency (HCA).

project_name: Gov't donated 5 ambulances to Seychelles
description: On May 16, 2013, the Chinese Government handed over a donation of 5 ambulances to the Seychelles Ministry of Health. The value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for Anse Royale Hospital rehabilitation project
description:
On June 26, 2008, the Chinese Government and the Government of Seychelles signed a grant agreement for the Anse Royale Hospital Rehabilitation Project. China’s Ministry of Commerce was the source of funding and it committed $3.5 million of grant funding in total.  
 
 This project involved the rehabilitation of the country’s second-largest (54-bed) hospital (Anse Royale Hospital), which is located on Baie Lazare Route in the Anse Royale administrative district. It has a rehabilitation and physiotherapy room, a labor room, an accident and emergency unit with a special treatment room and its own reception as well as an operating theatre and X-ray facilities. 
 
 China Qingdao Construction Group Corporation (now known as Qingjiang Group), which was a state-owned enterprise until 2015, was the contractor responsible for implementation. The foundation-laying ceremony was held on June 16, 2009, but construction did not start until July 9, 2009. Construction was completed on April 19, 2011 and an opening ceremony for the hospital was held on June 15, 2013. As of 2015, the hospital reportedly suffered from a lack of fans, air conditioners, and space.

project_name: Municipal gov't donated epidemic med. supplies to gov't of victoria
description: On July 16, 2020, Guangzhou Municipal Government donates medical supplies to the Government of Victoria, the capital of Seychelles. Victoria Mayor André received the donation on behalf of the city. The batch of supplies includes 50,000 disposable medical masks and 200 forehead thermometers. Because Guangzhou and Victoria are friendship cities, this donation fully demonstrates the high quality of friendship between the two cities and reflects the determination of the two cities to overcome the difficulties brought about by the COVID-19 pandemic.

project_name: Embassy donated computer to ASFF
description: In June 2005, the Chinese Embassy in Seychelles donated a computer to the Alliance of Solidarity for the Family (ASFF), a Seychelles non-government organization working under the direction of International Planned Parenthood Federation (IPPF) to address reproductive health and rights and domestic violence, abuse, and AIDS.

project_name: Embassy donated anti-epidemic med. supplies to the Ministry of Health
description: On May 8, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Seychelles donated anti-epidemic medical supplies to the Seychellois Ministry of Health. This donation includes N95 masks, protective clothing, goggles, etc. The purpose of this donation is to help Seychelles in fighting against the COVID-19 pandemic.

project_name: Gov't donated anti-epidemic med. supplies to the gov't of Seychelles
description: On May 26, 2020, an unspecified organization within the Chinese Government donated anti-epidemic medical supplies to the Government of Seychelles. This batch of medical supplies includes masks, forehead thermometer, protective clothing, goggles, etc. The purpose of this donation is to help Seychelles in fighting against the COVID-19 pandemic.

project_name: Embassy donated anti-epidemic med. supplies to MFA
description: On August 5, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Seychelles donated anti-epidemic medical supplies to the Seychellois Ministry of Foreign Affairs. This donation included 2,000 masks, 50 bottles of disinfectant hand sanitizer, and 3 forehead thermometers intended to support Seychelles in its fight against the COVID-19 pandemic. According to Ambassador to Seychelles, Guo Wei, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Seychelles has long supported the work of the Chinese Embassy in Seychelles, and the two sides have maintained close cooperation and cordial relations.

project_name: Gov't donated med. equipment to Seychelles
description:
On May 27, 2009, the Chinese Government handed over a donation of drugs and medical equipment to the Seychellois Ministry of Health.
 
 The value, types, and quantities of this donation are unknown.

project_name: Gov't donated anti-epidemic med. supplies to Ministry of Health
description: On August 11, 2020, the Chinese Government donated medical supplies to the Seychellois Ministry of Health. This donation includes 2,000 masks, 50 bottles of disinfectant hand sanitizer, and 3 forehead thermometers. This is the second batch of medical supplies from the Chinese Government. During the ceremony, the Ambassador in Seychelles, Guo Wei, and Secretary of State for Health Lloyd signed the certificate of handover of medical supplies. The amount and value of this donation are not specified, but the purpose of this donation is to help Seychelles in fighting against the COVID-19pandemic.

project_name: Embassy providedfunds towards Seychelles Covid relief fund
description: On September 23, 2021, the Chinese Embassy donated USD $20,000 to the Seychelles COVID-19 Relief Fund. The purpose of this donation is to support the Seychelles’ COVID-19 response efforts. This was the third of the Embassy's financial contributions to Seychelles' COVID-19 fund.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. The Chinese Ambassador to the Seychelles, Guo Wei, handed the check over to the Seychelles Minister for Finance, Economic Planning and Trade, Naadir Hassan.

project_name: Municipal gov't donated epidemic med. supplies to gov't of Victoria
description: On October 8, 2020, Shanghai Municipal Government donated anti-epidemic medical supplies to Seychelles' Government of Victoria. The mayor of Victoria, André, received this donation on behalf of the city and disbursed them to the Seychelles Ministry of Health and the Seychelles Red Cross. This donation includes 30,000 medical masks and 18,000 pairs of medical gloves. The purpose of this donation is to help Victoria, Shanghai’s friendship city, in its fight against the COVID-19 pandemic.

project_name: Embassy donated 'radiology cases' to Ministry of Health
description: On July 17, 2018, the Chinese Embassy in Seychelles donated 50 copies of "Radiology Cases – Image Interpretation and Diagnostic Essentials" (Chinese: 塞舌尔放射病例-影像解析及诊断要点) to the Ministry of Health of Seychelles. The book, written by Doctor Sun Zhanguo, a radiologist and member of the 16th Chinese medical aid team to Seychelles (see project ID#55684), offered interpretations of 403 radiological cases in Seychelles observed during consultations at the Radiology Unit in the Sheikh Khalifa Diagnostic Centre of the Seychelles Hospital (formerly the Victoria Hospital). The book was intended to simplify the interpretations of radiological cases, improve the implementation of CT scans, MRIs, ultrasounds, X-rays, and mammograms by Seychellois clinicians, and enable short training at the Radiology Unit by local doctors. The book was submitted to Seychelles' Ministry of Health Ethics Committee and to additional peer-reviewers prior to its donation. The book was set to be distributed to the Radiology Unit and library of Seychelles Hospital. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: Embassy grants funds for child's med. treatment in Seychelles
description: On 9 April 2013, the Chinese Embassy in Seychelles donated $3,000 to Dylan Albest, a sick 3-year-old child, for his medical treatment.

project_name: Ambassador donated funds to the Seychelles Ministry of Health
description: On August 24, 2021, the Chinese Ambassador to Seychelles, Guo Wei, donated $10,000 dollars to the Ministry of Health in Seychelles.  At the same ceremony, the Chinese Ambassador to Seychelles, Guo Wei, also donated anti-epidemic aid in the form of masks to the Seychelles Ministry of Health on behalf of the Seychelles-China Culture and Tourism Association (see project ID#97091)

project_name: Ambassador donated masks to the Seychelles Ministry of Health
description: On August 24, 2021, the Chinese Ambassador to Seychelles, Guo Wei, donated anti-epidemic aid in the form of masks to the Seychelles Ministry of Health on behalf of the Seychelles-China Culture and Tourism Association.   There is also a donation of $10,000 dollars to the Ministry of Health (see project ID#97567)

project_name: Chinese hospital ship visits Seychelles
description:
On 27 October 2010, the Chinese Navy’s hospital ship, Peace Ark, anchored at Victoria's port for a five-day visit to Seychelles. During the visit, Chinese medical workers treated 139 Seychellois people including 19 operations. The crew also visited Anse Etoile Primary School to examine students. 
 
 Since its commission in 2008, Peace Ark has conducted multiple humanitarian missions and maritime exercises around the world. It serves in China's East Sea Fleet and goes by two names: Daishan Dao (岱山岛) and Heping Fangzhou (和平方舟 = Peace Ark).

project_name: Gov't donated 25,000 Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In June 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 25,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Seychelles.

project_name: Gov't donated med. equipment to Seychelles
description: On April 29, 2010, the Chinese government handed over a donation of drugs and medical equipment worth $21,000 USD to the Seychellois Ministry of Health. The donated equipment is for Victoria Hospital (now Seychelles Hospital) and includes acupuncture needles, sterilization, and other equipment and accessories to be used in the X-ray department, operating theatre, and wheelchairs for the Rehabilitation Centre.

project_name: Embassy donated funds to the Seychelles anti-epidemic relief fund
description: On January 14, 2021, the Chinese Embassy in Seychelles donated S77,000 to the Seychelles Anti-epidemic Relief Fund, which is a special fund under the Seychelles Ministry of Finance, National Planning and Trade.    The fund was set up by the president earlier in 2021 to finance the vaccination program of the island nation’s population that started on January 10.

project_name: Gov't provided trop. infectious disease prevention & control training
description: On May 11, 2019, the Chinese Military Medical Expert Group held the opening ceremony of the CNMEG's Training Workshop on Infectious Disease Surveillance and Biosafety in Republic of Sierra Leone Armed Forces (RSLAF). This project entailed an infectious disease prevention and control technology training class for the Sierra Leone Armed Forces that was held at the Sierra Leone Joint Ministry of Health Tropical Infectious Diseases Prevention and Control Center. Nearly 40 medical workers from the Sierra Leonean Army's frontline health outposts and the Sierra Leonean Joint Ministry of Health participated in the training. Hu Zhangliang, Chinese Ambassador to Sierra Leone, Savali, Commander of the Sierra Leonean Joint Ministry of Health, and Xu Zhe, leader of the China Military Medical Experts' Group and director of the Tropical Infectious Diseases Prevention and Control Center, attended the opening ceremony. The duration of this training is unknown, but the project is believed to be completed.  This project is linked to the December 2016 ETCA between Sierra Leone and China, through which the Chinese Government was to fund 300 million Yuan to build the West Africa Center for Tropical Infectious Disease Prevention and Control (recorded in the umbrella project ID#62554).

project_name: Gov't donated medicine & med. equipment to friendship hospital
description: On January 31, 2018 , a handover ceremony for a donation of medicines and medical equipment from the Chinese Government to the government of Sierra Leone was held at the China-Sierra Leone Friendship Hospital (中塞友好医院). Zhang Xueqian, Economic and Commercial Counselor of the Chinese Embassy in Sierra Leone, and Brima Kargbo, Chief Medical Officer of the Ministry of Health of Sierra Leone, attended the ceremony.

project_name: China donated medicines & med. apparatus to Sierra Leone
description:
In May 2011, the Chinese Ambassador to Sierra Leone, Kuang Weilin, and Sierra Leonean Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Joseph Bandabla Dauda exchanged notes for China to provide medical equipment, anti-malaria medicine as well as malaria treatment devices to Sierra Leone, according to the Chinese Embassy in May 2011. These notes were exchanged next to an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement on the same occasion (project #62697).
 
 In October 2011, the Chinese Ambassador to Sierra Leone, Kuang Weilin handed over medicines and medical apparatus donated by the Chinese government to Sierra Leone, according to the Chinese Embassy in October 2011. Deputy Minister of Health and Sanitation, Borbor Sawyer, received the aid on behalf of the Sierra Leonean government.

project_name: China donated anti-Malarial medicine to Sierra Leone
description: In November 2009, Chinese Ambassador to Sierra Leone, Qui Shao Fang donated anti-malaria drugs to the Ministry of Health and Sanitation in Freetown. The ceremony was held at the Central Medical Stores in Freetown. The donation came as a result of the certificate signed between the Sierra Leone Government and the PRC to strengthen bilateral relations.

project_name: Embassy provided funding for parliament health centre project
description: On April 12, 2016, Zhao Yanbo, Ambassador of Sierra Leone, was invited to attend the opening ceremony of the Chinese Government-funded Parliament Health Centre. More than one hundred people attended the ceremony, including the President of the Parliament, the majority leader, the minority leader, the secretary-general, and the health minister. The monetary value of this financial commitment is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donated 200,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021 and 2022, the Chinese Government donated approximately 900,000 doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Sierra Leone. The Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Sierra Leone on February 25, 2021. The shipment arrived at the Lungi International Airport in Freetown, Sierra Leone. Its reception was acknowledged with a handover ceremony led by Sierra Leone's Acting Minister of Health, the Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs, and Chinese Ambassador Hu Zhanglang. Then, on March 1, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered another 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines and 201,600 disposable needles and syringes to the Government of Sierra Leone.  Then, on August 18, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered another 200,000 donated Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses, 201,600 syringes, 40,000 Novel Coronavirus Nucleic Acid Diagnostic Kits, and 50,000 Novel Coronavirus Antigen Detection Kits to the Government of Sierra Leone. The Chinese Government delivered an additional 300,000 donated Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Sierra Leone on July 22, 2022. The Ministry of Health and Sanitation (MOHS) of Sierra Leone held a handover and acceptance ceremony for the donation on August 9, 2022.

project_name: China provided training course to 5 med. staff from Sierra Leone
description: On July 14, 2017, the Sierra Leone-China Friendship Hospital held a farewell ceremony for five of its medical staff who will go to study in China. The Chinese Ministry of Commerce provided funding for the training and Hunan Children's Hospital will be responsible for the course. This team included 3 nursing staff, 1 imaging staff and 1 laboratory technician. The training will improve their ability in medical practice.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for establishment of Malaria center
description: A malaria prevention and treatment center was held an opening ceremony in Freetown on October 30, 2009. The center, which is called the China-Sierra Leone Malaria Prevention and Treatment Center, is located at King Harman Road Hospital. This Center is part of a larger promise from President Hu Jintao in building 30 such centers in Africa made at the African Cooperation Forum Beijing Summit in November of 2006. The Chinese Government provided a grant for the establishment of the China-Sierra Leone Malaria Prevention and Treatment Center, but the monetary value of this grant commitment is unknown  After the establishment of the center, Chinese experts were able set up and test the facilities, exchange ideas with local specialists, and provide technical training to medical staff. For the three years following the establishment of the center, the Chinese government provided the center’ facilities and drugs free of charge.   It is important that the center should serve as national bases not only for laboratory and clinical departments, but also, and more importantly, for research into anti-malaria strategies (including malaria prevention), for exchanges of advanced technology and for training medical staff.

project_name: [Ebola] China pledges to build hospital
description: On June 21, 2016, China has agreed to build a disease control center and a new office for Sierra Leone's health ministry to improve the country's health care system.

project_name: China donated anti-Malarial drugs
description: In September 2013, the Chinese Ambassador Kuang Weilin and Foday Sawi Lahai, Deputy Minister of Health and Sanitation, signed a hand-over certificate of a batch of anti-malaria drugs worth 2 million Yuan (approx. $320,000), according to the Chinese Embassy in Sierra Leone. The Economic and Commercial Counsellor of the Chinese embassy, Zou Xiaoming, and some officials from Ministry of Health and Sanitation attended the signing ceremony.

project_name: China implements free cataract surgeries in Sierra Leone
description: On November 6, 2018, the Chinese Government launched the 6th "Guangmingxing" (Brightness Trip) free cataract surgery project in the City Hospital of Kenema, Sierra Leone. The project was funded by the National Health Commission of China and was organized by the provincial Health Commission of Hunan Province. The team was made up of six senior ophthalmologists and nurses from Xiangya Hospital of Hunan Province.   The project lasted for about a month, during which the medical team carried out over 100 free cataract operations for local residents of Freetown and Kenema. The team also donated ophthalmological equipment worth 1.6 million Yuan to the local hospitals. This project is completed.

project_name: China donated anti-Malarial drugs to Sierra Leone
description: On February 22, 2012, the Chinese Ambassador to Sierra Leone, Kuang Weilin handed over to Sierra Leonean Minister of Health and Sanitation Zainab Hawa Bangura a batch of anti-malaria drugs donated by the Chinese Government, according to the Chinese Embassy in Sierra Leone. Officials from the Ministry and Economic and Commercial Counsellor Liu Yulin were present at the ceremony at the Central Medicine Store in New England.

project_name: China provided funds for cataract surgeries under project
description: On February 9, 2006, the 'Bright Journey' Project ('光明'项目) officially began in Sierra Leone. The Chinese Embassy in Sierra Leone provided $4,000 USD for 150 cataract surgeries for Sierra Leone patients (p. 492).

project_name: China provided Malaria control training to 30 med. staff
description:
On August 14, 2017, the Chinese Embassy funded 30 medical staff from Sierra Leone's Ministry of Health and Sanitation to receive training on malaria control in China, according to Awareness News. The group included medical Doctors, nurses, and health care workers who will attended a training course at the Jiangsu Institute of Parasitic Diseases, Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province, China between August 16 and September 4, 2017. 
 
 The Economic and Commercial Counselor of the Chinese embassy, Shen Xiaokai, gave 30 flight tickets to Sarah Kamara, the Deputy Chief Medical Officer to be distributed to the participants.

project_name: China donated artemisinin anti-Malarial drugs to Sierra Leone
description: On October 21, 2008, the Chinese embassy in Sierra Leone handed artemisinin-based anti-malarial drugs to the government of Sierra Leone.These anti-malarial drugs can effectively cure malaria and relieve the patient's pain. The Ministry of Health and Sanitation distributed the medicines to various hospitals to benefit the public. Qiu Shaofang, Ambassador to Cyprus, Business Counselor Zhao Zhongqiu and other officials of the Embassy, ​​Cypriot Minister of Health Kabia, Deputy Minister, officials of the Ministry of Health and the media and about 20 people attended the handover ceremony.

project_name: Donation to maternal health & cerv cancer prevention project
description: On October 29, 2018, Deng Boquing, Vice-Chairman of the China International Development Cooperation Agency (CIDCA), signed an agreement on the Sierra Leone Maternal Health and Cervical Cancer Prevention Project in cooperation with the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) and the Sierra Leone Ministry of Health. The Chinese Government committed USD $2 million to support this project. Dereje Wordofa, Deputy Executive Director of the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), was present at the signing of the agreement.   The project, implemented over two years in the Western Province of Sierra Leone, would improve obstetric care services and cervical cancer screening and treatment in Sierra Leone. The project will also support the provision of strong medical services for the prevention, screening and treatment of cervical cancer. As part of the implementation of the project, UNFPA and the Sierra Leone Ministry of Health and Sanitation will partner with Hunan Maternal and Child Health Hospital to improve the quality of emergency obstetric care services for women with high-risk pregnancies. The United Nations Population Fund and Hunan Maternal and Child Health Hospital will provide technical support for the implementation of the project and promote the exchange of experts in related fields within the framework of the Sierra Leone National Health Strategy and the current national cooperation mechanism.   From January 26 to February 2, 2019, a Chinese delegation led by UNFPA met with the UNFPA Office in Sierra Leone, senior government officials, NGO representatives, journalists, the Chinese embassy and medical team from Hunan province of China to assess the maternal and child health situations there for the implementation of the Sierra Leone Maternal Health and Cervical Cancer Prevention Project. On January 28, 2019, the China South-South Cooperation Assistance Fund's tripartite cooperation meeting on the Sierra Leone Maternal Health and Cervical Cancer Prevention Project was held at the Ministry of Health of Sierra Leone. At this time, the parties involved (including representatives from UNFPA, the Ministry of Health of Sierra Leone, National Health Commission of China, the Hunan Provincial Maternity and Child Health Hospital, and the Chinese Medical Team for Sierra Leone) discussed the planned implementation stages of the project.  In March 2021, UNFPA reaffirmed its commitment to carry out the project. The funding of USD $2 million from the Chinese Government is dedicated towards UNFPA training on cervical cancer screening. The training has targeted fifty health providers drawn from the Directorate of Reproductive Health of the MOHS, five major hospitals and four community health centers. The first training slated from 19-28 April 2020 is a Training of Trainers (TOT) so as to get a core cadre of trainers to cascade trainings down to more providers to improve access to cervical cancer screening and treatment services.  The Sierra Leone Maternal Health and Cervical Cancer Prevention Project is funded under the China South-South Cooperation Assistance Fund. The fund was established after the 2015 Sustainable Development Summit, with the goal of strengthening exchanges and cooperation between developing countries and promoting the realization of sustainable development goals.

project_name: China provided anti-Ebola training program in Sierra Leone
description:
On January 6, 2015, China launched the Anti-Ebola Training Program in Sierra Leone. Chinese Ambassador Zhao Yanbo, Ambassador of Sierra Leone attended the launching ceremony. Since the Ebola outbreak, China has provided all-round support. Up to the launch of this project, Chinese public health experts have trained more than 2,300 people in Sierra Leone. 
 
 This intensive training project will further penetrate the grassroots level, and in the three administrative villages of Zhuyi, Corso, and Grafton, systematically help the grassroots to enhance their current anti-epidemic capabilities and their ability to respond to other infectious diseases in the future.
 
 The current status of the project is unknown.

project_name: Hunan provincial gov't donated med. equipment to Sierra Leone
description:
In November 2006, the government in Hunan Province, China, committed to donate a set of medical equipments to Sierra Leone when Sierra Leone's President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah visited Hunan Province during the Beijing Summit of the China-Africa Cooperation Forum. In mid-August 2007, the equipments were delivered to Freetown, including 6 devices including X-ray machines, electrocardiographs, and digital ultrasonic diagnostic instruments. The medical equipments worth RMB 550,000. 
 
 On September 5, 2007, the Chinese embassy held a handover ceremony for the donation of medical equipment from the Government of Hunan Province to the Government of Sierra Leone. Chinese Ambassador to Serbia Cheng Wenju, Political Counselor Wang Haitao, Business Counsellor Zhao Zhongqiu, Serbian President Kaba, Minister of Health Thomas, and local news media attended the handover ceremony.

project_name: Gov't donated 200,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021 and 2022, the Chinese Government donated approximately 900,000 doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Sierra Leone. The Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Sierra Leone on February 25, 2021. The shipment arrived at the Lungi International Airport in Freetown, Sierra Leone. Its reception was acknowledged with a handover ceremony led by Sierra Leone's Acting Minister of Health, the Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs, and Chinese Ambassador Hu Zhanglang. Then, on March 1, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered another 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines and 201,600 disposable needles and syringes to the Government of Sierra Leone.  Then, on August 18, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered another 200,000 donated Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses, 201,600 syringes, 40,000 Novel Coronavirus Nucleic Acid Diagnostic Kits, and 50,000 Novel Coronavirus Antigen Detection Kits to the Government of Sierra Leone. The Chinese Government delivered an additional 300,000 donated Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Sierra Leone on July 22, 2022. The Ministry of Health and Sanitation (MOHS) of Sierra Leone held a handover and acceptance ceremony for the donation on August 9, 2022.

project_name: China donated anti-Malarial drugs to Sierra Leone
description: In June 2014, the Chinese Ambassador to Sierra Leone, Zhao Yanbo, signed an agreement with Samura Kamara, Sierra Leone's Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation to donate a batch of anti-malarial drugs, according to the Chinese Embassy.

project_name: Hunan Province provided pathology training for 2 Sierra Leone doctors
description: In early 2019, the Health Commission of Hunan Province (湖南省卫生健康委员会) invited medical doctors Donald Samuel Bangura and Wuyah Novella Sheriff of the Sierra Leone-China Friendship Hospital (中塞友好医院) to undertake a three month pathology training course at the Hunan Cancer Hospital (湖南省肿瘤医院) in China. The training of the two Sierra Leoneans would enable the Sierra Leone-China Friendship Hospital to establish a pathology department. The three month training course focused on knowledge and technology of pathology, and it enabled them to complete the whole process of pathological specimen section, which they were able to experiment with at the end of the learning stage. The two doctors were also supported by members of the 21st China Medical Team who actively assisted them to keep in touch with the Health Commission of Hunan Province.  It is unclear when the doctors began or completed training. As of late December 2019, the two doctors were still working together with the 21st China Medical Team, and they were directly responsible for specimen preparation, management of pathological data, and getting diagnostic advice from telepathological consultation.  The training initiative follows the establishment of a remote pathology platform at the hospital which connected local medical staff with specialists at the Hunan Cancer Hospital (recorded in project ID#62600).

project_name: Grant for construction of hospitals & health units to Ministry
description: On February 4, 2019, President Julius Maada Bio announced that the Chinese government had provided grant funding to Sierra Leone's Ministry of Health and Sanitation for the construction and equipping of two government hospitals and five peripheral health units in the Western Area Rural and Urban. The new structures would be dedicated to cervical cancer screening and treatment.  This project is linked to project ID#86080, which records China's USD $2 million grant to the Sierra Leone Maternal Health and Cervical Cancer Prevention Project.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for friendship hospital construction project
description: In April 2008, the Chinese Government and the Government of Sierra Leone signed letters of exchange for the Sierra Leone-China Friendship Hospital Construction Project. China’s Ministry of Commerce committed grant funding for this project, but the monetary value of this grant commitment is unknown. This project involved the construction of a modern hospital in Jui — a town located just outside the east end of the Freetown city limits — with 100 beds, a hostel for the Chinese medical team, an equipment room, a laboratory, theaters, dialysis and intensive care units, surgical and medical departments, a mortuary, a funeral parlor, andX-Ray department, and other facilities. Anhui Construction Engineering Group (安徽建工集团有限) was the contractor responsible for implementation.   In April 2009, the groundbreaking ceremony for the hospital was held. Construction began on July 16, 2009 and ended in March 2011. On May 13, 2011, the Chinese government officially handed over the new hospital to the government of Sierra Leone. Then, on March 26, 2012, Linqu Qushan Hospital of Shandong Province signed an agreement with Sierra Leone’s Ministry of Health and Sanitation, which allows the Chinese staff from Linqu Qushan Hospital to operate the Sierra Leone-China Friendship Hospital. (塞拉利昂政府与山东临朐朐山医院就经营我援塞新医院签订合作协议). In November 2012, President of Sierra Leone, Ernest Bai Koroma, opened and commissioned the hospital.

project_name: China provided pediatrics training course to 19 med. staff
description: On July 31, 2017, the Ministry of Health and Sanitation of Sierra Leone and the Chinese Embassy in Sierra Leone jointly organized a meeting for the 19 medical staff who will receive training for the critical care of pediatrics in China. The Chief Medical Officer of the Ministry of Health, Brima Kargbo, and Shen Xiaokai, Commercial Counselor of the Chinese Embassy in Sierra Leone, attended the ceremony and delivered a speech.   This came as part of the " 2017 Pediatric critical care treatment technology training in developing countries" program funded by the Chinese Ministry of Commerce. On September 2, the "2017 Pediatric Critical Care Technology Training Course in Developing Countries", "2017 Developing Countries Newborn and Premature Infant Treatment Technology Training Course" and "2017 Egyptian Hospital Training Course" were held in Hunan Children's Hospital.  The participants will be trained by Hunan Children's Hospital for eight weeks in children hospital system learning. During the study period, the students will also go to the Second Xiangya Hospital of Central South University to participate in relevant professional training.

project_name: China launches phase two of maternal & child health innovation project
description: On June 5, 2018, the Chinese Embassy in Sierra Leone hosted a launch ceremony for the second phase of the "China and Sierra Leone Maternal and Child Health Innovation Project". A Chinese medical team from Hunan province in China offered free medical care to children, pregnant and lactating mothers for 12 days. The team took up temporary residency at the China-Sierra Leone Friendship Hospital for the implementation of the project. The project falls under an MOU signed in August 2016 by the National Health and Family Planning Commission of the People's Republic of China and the Sierra Leone Ministry of Health and Sanitation.  Wu Peng, Chinese Ambassador to Sierra Leone, attended the launch ceremony and delivered a speech. Sierra Leone's Health and Sanitation Minister Alpha Wurie, Chinese Economic and Commercial Counsellor Zhang Xueqian, and Vice President of the Hunan Provincial People's Hospital Li Quanqing were also in attendance.  The first phase of the project was implemented in 2016 (recorded in the linked project ID#53016).

project_name: China donated anti-Ebola materials to Sierra Leone
description:
On March 13, 2015, China donated a batch of anti-Ebola materials to Sierra Leone. Zhao Yanbo, Ambassador of Sierra Leone, and Koroma, President of Serbia, attended the handover ceremony. 
 Ambassador Zhao and Deputy Minister of the Ministry of Health Savi signed anti-epidemic materials handover certificates on behalf of the two governments.

project_name: China implements the 5th Guangmingxing cataract surgery project
description: In August 2016, the Chinese Ambassador to Sierra Leone, Zhao Yanbo, and Sierra Leone's Health and Sanitation Minister signed an agreement for the fifth "Guangmingxing" project which will provide free cataract surgeries to Sierra Leone. Ambassador Zhao emphasized that the past four similar project have successfully helped thousands of cataract patients to regain their bright future and the forthcoming fifth “Guangmingxing” event will continue the previous successful experience and benefit more people in Sierra Leone.  The Chinese National Health and Family Planning Commission supported the project.
