In November 2016, the project was officially launched in the Sierra Leone-China Friendship Hospital in Jui, Freetown. According to the agreement, the Chinese medical team will perform hundreds of free cataract surgeries, and donate a batch of ophthalmological instrument and materials. China will also hold some lectures on ophthalmological health and boost technical cooperation between the medical staff from China and Sierra Leone about cataract surgery. On December 5, 2016, the "Brightness Trip to Sierra Leone" officially ended.

project_name: China donated Covid aid to Sierra Leone
description: On November 24, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Sierra Leone held a handover ceremony for a batch of COVID aid donated to Sierra Leone. The content of the aid was included testing kits, respirators, surgical masks, personal protective equipment and other related accessories. (See: The cost of the equipment was unspecified. The handover ceremony was attended by Ambassador Hu Zhangliang and senior officials from Sierra Leone, including the Minister of Defense, General Coordinator of the National New Crown Epidemic Emergency Command Center, Deputy Minister of Defense, Vice Minister of Health, and the General Staff of the Armed Forces Cisse.

project_name: Embassy donated Covid aid to Sierra Leone Ministry
description: On March 19, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Sierra Leone held a handover ceremony for a batch of COVID aid for the Ministry of Health and Sanitation of Sierra Leone. The donation includes 500 sets of protective gowns and N95 masks, 1,000 pairs of medical gloves and surgical masks, 200 medical goggles, and one 50 kw generator. According to the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs, part of the materials were donated by Chinese-funded institutions in Sierra Leone, though which groups and the exact amounts are unspecified. The specific monetary value of the donations is also unspecified. The Chinese Embassy additionally equipped CDC experts and Chinese military groups working in Sierra Leone with testing kits.  Ambassador Hu Zhangliang and senior officials from Sierra Leone attended the handover ceremony.

project_name: CDC holds international training on Malaria diagnostic techniques'
description: On October 28, 2019, the "China-Sierra Leone International Training on Malaria Diagnostic Techniques," jointly organized by the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention, USAID/PMI and the Ministry of Health of Sierra Leone, was launched in the Bintumani Hotel in Freetown. The course lasted for six days, consisted of two three-day sessions, and trained a total of 75 Sierra Leonean hospital technicians responsible for malaria diagnosis. Experts from the Chinese Center for Disease Control Team and the Chinese Military Medical Expert Team conducted the trainings. Dr. Amara Jambai was chairman of the program.  In attendance at the opening ceremony for the course were Chargé d’affaires of the Chinese Embassy, Sierra Leone's Vice Minister of Health, Sierra Leone’s Chief Medical Officer and Deputy Chief Officer of the Ministry of Health, and the Head of the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention Expert Team.

project_name: Chinese Navy provided humanitarian med. services to Sierra Leone
description:
On September 19, 2017, per Xinhua News, the Chinese naval hospital ship 866 (known as "Peace Ark") arrived at Freetown Port, Sierra Leone tasked with a mission to deliver free medical services. A welcoming ceremony was held on the ship. The goal of this mission was to enhance the cooperation between the two countries.
 
 During the visit, the staff carried out free medical services for both Sierra Leonean and Chinese people. In total, they received 8,177 patients, and performed  CT, DR, B-ultrasound, electrocardiogram checks for 3,909 people. 34 people were hospitalized, and 51 had operations. The hospital ship sent a medical teams to the Joint HQ of health of the Sierra Leonean armed forces, Sierra Leone-China Friendship Hospital, resettlement sites for the mudslide victims, and homes for the disabled to carry out health and disease prevention and education, medical visits, environmental killings, cultural associations, etc.
 
 On September 26, 2017, the ship left Sierra Leone.

project_name: Gov't donated Sinopharm Covid vaccine doses & other supplies
description: In 2021 and 2022, the Chinese Government donated approximately 900,000 doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Sierra Leone. The Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Sierra Leone on February 25, 2021. The shipment arrived at the Lungi International Airport in Freetown, Sierra Leone. Its reception was acknowledged with a handover ceremony led by Sierra Leone's Acting Minister of Health, the Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs, and Chinese Ambassador Hu Zhanglang. Then, on August 18, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered another 200,000 donated Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses, 201,600 syringes, 40,000 Novel Coronavirus Nucleic Acid Diagnostic Kits, and 50,000 Novel Coronavirus Antigen Detection Kits to the Government of Sierra Leone. The Chinese Government delivered an additional 300,000 donated Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Sierra Leone on July 22, 2022. The Ministry of Health and Sanitation (MOHS) of Sierra Leone held a handover and acceptance ceremony for the donation on August 9, 2022.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for disease prevention & center construction
description: In December 2016, during his visit to China, Sierra Leone's President Ernest Bai Koroma signed an RMB 300 million grant agreement with the Chinese Government for the Tropical Infectious Disease Prevention and Control Center Construction Project. This project involved the construction of a West Africa center for tropical infectious disease prevention and control at the 34 Military Hospital in the Wilberforce Barracks in Freetown.   The facility houses equipment for the diagnosis of HIV and AIDS, malaria, typhoid, lung infections, TB and Hepatitis A, B & C. Malaria and TB tests, as well as some medications, are provided to patients free of charge. It has the capacity to treat 60-100 patients per day and contains a teleconference center so that doctors may consult with Chinese medical experts.  This grant commitment was part of Chinese President Xi Jinping's commitment made during the Johannesburg Summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC) in 2015 to improve the country's capability to respond to epidemics like Ebola. Beijing Urban Construction Group Co. Ltd., Sierra Leone Armed Forces (RSLAF), and the People's Liberation Army of China (PLA) were jointly responsible for project implementation. The project started around January 2018 and took about 6 months to complete. The project handover ceremony was held on July 5, 2018. The Chinese Army aided in the construction but the start date is unclear.

project_name: China donated anti-Malarial drugs to Sierra Leone
description: On May 13, 2015, the Chinese Ambassador to Sierra Leone, Zhao Yanbo, signed a handover certificate with Sierra Leone's Deputy Minister of the Ministry of Health and Sanitation to for anti-malarial drugs in Freetown, according to the Chinese Embassy in Sierra Leone and Chinese Ministry of Commerce.

project_name: China launches 2nd phase of the safety laboratory technical project
description: On June 6, 2018, the launching ceremony of the Second Phase of the Fixed Biological Safety Laboratory Technical Cooperation Project was held in Freetown. As part of the project, China will continue to provide technical assistance to Sierra Leone for a period of 3 years in the areas of monitoring, inspection, research and control of epidemics. The Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention operates the laboratory, and is responsible for the implementation of this project.  On December 14, 2018, Wang Gang and He Xiaozhou of the Viral Disease Institute left China to implement the second phase of technical assistance project for the fixed biosafety laboratory in Sierra Leone. On December 14, 2019, members of China's CDC left China to aid the second phase of the technical assistance project in Sierra Leone. Since the outbreak of COVID-19, the 11-member team has shifted its focus to fighting against the coronavirus for the people of Sierra Leone.. On September 3, 2020, Dr. Liu Tiezhu from the Institute of Viral Diseases, as a member of the expert group, went to Sierra Leone to implement the second and third phases of technical assistance projects for the fixed biosafety laboratory in Sierra Leone.  On October 21, 2021, the second batch of experts for the third phase of the technical assistance project left China for Sierra Leone, so it is thought that the second phase of the project had been completed by this time, in alignment with its expected three-year completion period.   China established a fixed bio-safety level III laboratory in Sierra Leone in 2015 following the break-out of Ebola epidemics in 2014. The lab cost $4.35 million and is recorded in project ID#44339.

project_name: [Ebola] China pledges equipment & personnel for Jui hospital
description: On August 16, 2016, China and Sierra Leone have signed an agreement on medical aid in maternal health care as well as eye surgery, so that the problem of shortage of doctors that is still existing in the country can be solved.

project_name: Embassy donated $80,000 worth of Ribavirin to Sierra Leone
description:
On February 22, 2011, the Chinese Ambassador to Sierra Leone, Kuang Weilin and Sierra Leone's Minister of Health and Sanitation, Zainab Hawa Bangura signed the certificate of handing-over of Ribavirin worth $80,000. The medicine will be used for curing Lasha Fever, one of the epidemics prevalent in the Eastern province.
 
 Sierra Leone's Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Mrs Ebun Jusu and Commercial Counsellor Liu Yulin from the Chinese Embassy were also present at the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't donated med. supplies & remote pathology platform to hospital
description: In December 2018, a Chinese grant of equipment for a new remote pathology platform at the China-Sierra Leone Friendship Hospital (中塞友好医院) was shipped to Sierra Leone. On January 15, 2019, an opening ceremony was held for the platform at the China-Sierra Leone Friendship Hospital in Freetown.   The project connects medical professionals based in Freetown with Chinese experts at the Hunan Cancer Hospital (湖南省肿瘤医院) for remote consultations. It aims to promote early tumor screening and the collection of medical data such as tumor incidence in Sierra Leone. The opening ceremony was attended by Chinese Ambassador Wu Peng, Sierra Leone Minister of Health Alpha Wurie, Economic and Commercial Counselor of the Embassy in Sierra Leone Zhang Xueqian, and Vice President of the Hunan Cancer Hospital Hu Jun.  In February 2019, 5 medical experts from Hunan Cancer Hospital travelled to Sierra Leone to install and debug related equipment donated by the Chinese government and provide professional guidance to medical staff. The project is related to the implementation of the initiatives of the 2018 Beijing Summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation.

project_name: China donated cholera medication to Sierra Leone
description:
In August 2012, the Chinese Ambassador to Sierra Leone, Kuang Weilin, on behalf of the Chinese government, signed an exchange of letters with the Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of Sierra Leone to donate a batch of cholera drugs to Sierra Leone. The Head of Political Section and Spokesperson of the Chinese Embassy , Xu Zhou, said the embassy was closely following the cholera situation in the country and was deeply concerned about the development. All Africa, a media outlet, reported that the drugs are worth 1 million Yuan. 
 
 In December 2012, the hand-over ceremony of the drugs took place at the Central Medical Store in Freetown. Fan Xiaodong, the Political Counsellor of the Chinese embassy signed the certificate with the First Deputy Minister of Health and Sanitation.

project_name: China donated anti-Malarial drugs to Somalia
description: On October 31, 2007, Somali President Abdullahi Yusuf and Chinese Ambassador in Kenya, Zhang Ming signed an agreement to provide 1.5 million USD aid to Somalia (ID #28496). The agreement includes 500,000 USD in humanitarian aid, 1 million USD for reconstruction , and anti-malaria drugs worth about 132,000 dollars.

project_name: China grants $500,000 to Somalia for Malaria-control
description: In October 2009, according to the Chinese Embassy in Kenya, the Chinese Ambassador, Deng Hongbo, donated $500,000 in cash to Mohamed Osman Aden, the Somali Temporary Chargé d'affaires to Kenya, Mohamed Osman Aden, as the Chinese government's aid for malaria control projects. China also donated a batch of anti-malaria medicine worth 1 million Yuan (project #35217).

project_name: China donated goods to Banadir hospital in Mogadishu
description:
In November 2014, according to the Chinese Embassy in Somalia, the embassy donated a batch of goods including food, drugs, medical supplies and fuel to Banadir Maternity & Children Hospital in Mogadishu through the Ministry of Health of Somalia.
 
 This project is linked to #31067, the planned rehabilitation project of the Banadir Hospital.

project_name: Gov't donated 500,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021, the Chinese Government donated approximately 700,000 doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Somalia. The Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Somalia on April 11, 2021. The vaccines arrived in Mogadishu, the capital of Somalia, and a handover ceremony was held at the Aden Adde International Airport in Mogadishu. Somalian Health Minister, Fawziya Abikar Nur, Information Minister, Mohamed Abdi Hayr, and the Chinese Ambassador to Somalia, Qin Jian, attended the handover ceremony.  Health Minister Fawziya Abikar Nur stated that 100,000 people would benefit from the donation. Minister Nur also stated that the vaccines would be distributed to all federal member states of the Somali government, with priority given to frontline health workers, essential service providers and the elderly. Then, on December 5, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 500,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Somalia. The vaccines arrived at the Aden Adde International Airport in Mogadishu, Somalia, and a handover ceremony was held. Somalia’s Minister of Health and Human Services, Fawziya Abikar Nur, and China’s Ambassador to Somalia, Qin Jian, attended the ceremony.

project_name: China pledges to rebuild Banadir Maternity & Children Hospital
description: In September 2013, China and Somalia signed a cooperation agreement in Mogadishu to rebuild Banadir Maternity & Children Hospital (贝纳迪尔医院扩建项目), a teaching hospital in Wadajir District of Mogadishu. The Somali Prime Minister and the Foreign Minister Fawsiya Yusuf Haji Aden and the Chinese ambassador to Kenya, Liu Guangyuan, signed the agreement which outlines a five year recovery plan, including rebuilding the National Theater (project #31069), the Mogadishu Stadium (project #31068) and a road between Galkayo and Burao (project #31070) in addition to the hospital. In November 2014, China furthered its aid to this hospital by providing it materials.

project_name: China donated anti-Malaria medicine to Somalia
description: In October 2009, as the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs reports, the Chinese Ambassador to Kenya, Deng Hongbo donated a batch of anti-malaria medicines worth 1 million Yuan to the Somali government. Mohamed Osman Aden, the temporary Temporary Chargé d'affaires to Kenya of Somalia, signed the hand-over certificate in the Chinese embassy in Nairobi. project_name: BOC donated med. supplies to South Africa DOH
description: On May 07, 2020, Bank of China Johannesburg Branch donated 100,000 disposable medical masks, 600 sets of protective clothing, and five respirators to South Africa's Department of Health to relieve the shortage of medical supplies in South Africa. These supplies were worth ZAR 2 million. South African Secretary of Health Zweli Mkhize and BOC Johannesburg Branch's chairman Li Tao attended the handover ceremony.  Bank of China donated five batches of pandemic materials to South Africa in spring of 2020. In aggregate, the donation consisted of 170,000 masks, 600 protective suits, and 5 ventilators. The first donation consisted of 30,000 masks to Gauteng province on April 14, 2020 (see project ID#93779). The next was 100,000 masks, 600 protective suits, and 5 ventilators to South Africa Ministry of Health on May 7, 2020, as captured by this project.  The final donation was 20,000 masks to KwaZulu-Natal on May 9, 2020 (see project ID#93792). The other two donations were for 10,000 masks and were delivered at an unknown date before May 9, 2020. These donations are captured in project ID#93780 and 93791 respectively.

project_name: Consulate donated anti-epidemic materials & food to national assembly
description: On October 29, 2020, the Chinese Consulate General in Cape Town donated ZAR 100,000 in anti-epidemic materials and food relief to the National Assembly of South Africa. The materials included 100 relief food packages, 6,000 medical masks, 120 goggles, and 120 pieces of protective clothing.  The supplies were provided in a donation ceremony attended by South African National Assembly Deputy Speaker Cinori and Chinese Consul General Lin Jin. The supplies will ultimately be delivered to the Redhill Community on the outskirts of Cape Town. This project is the second donation from the Chinese Consulate in Cape Town to the South African National Assembly. The first donation occurred in May 2020 and is captured by project ID#93815.

project_name: PLA donated med. protective gear to the SANDF
description: On March 26, 2020, the People's Liberation Army donated medical protective gear to the South African National Defence Force (SANDF). The supplies included 30,000 face masks and 2000 eye goggles. The monetary value of the protective gear is unknown.  Chinese Defence Attache Major General Shang Hong delivered the equipment to Chief of the SANDF General Solly Shoke in a handover ceremony at the South African Military Health Services (SAMHS) medical depot in Pretoria. Other members in attendance included SANDF Chief of Staff Lieutenant General Lindile Yam, Lieutenant General Jabulani Mbuli (Chief Logistics Division), Major General Noel Nhdlovu (Deputy Surgeon General), and representatives from Hennox Supplies Company.  The donation of medical supplies to SANDF was the beginning of a series of medical supply donations on behalf of the People's Liberation Army; subsequent donations occurred in August (project ID#93502) and November 2020 (project ID#93501).

project_name: PLA donated med. protective gear to the national defense force
description: On November 27, 2020, the People's Liberation Army donated medical protective gear to the South African National Defense Force (SANDF). The supplies included 30,000 masks, 400 suits, and 500 thermometers. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.   The supplies were donated in a handover ceremony where Rear Admiral Bravo Mhlana received the donation on behalf of SANDF.  The donation of medical supplies to SANDF was a part of a series of medical supply donations on behalf of the People's Liberation Army of China; previous donations occurred in March 2020 (project ID#93500) and August 2020 (project ID#93502).

The project was completed on November 13, 2019.   Juba Teaching Hospital is the only national referral hospital in the whole country of South Sudan and it is located in Juba City, Central Equatoria State. With an estimated population of 9.86 million based on annual population growth of 3% from a population census conducted in 2008 and lack of proper functioning primary health care facilities upcountry, many South Sudanese have nowhere to go but to this national referral hospital.The Chinese Government-financed renovations of the hospital included an emergency department building, department of gynecology and obstetrics building, and a dormitory for Chinese medical teams. The project also included the provision of medical equipment such as CT machines and EEG machines as well as one year of technical cooperation following the completion of construction.

project_name: Embassy donated epidemic materials to ministry of national defense
description: On April 30, 2020, the Chinese Embassy donated anti-epidemic materials to the Ministry of National Defense of South Sudan. The specific type, amount and monetary value of this donation are unknown.  These supplies were handed over to South Sudan during the meeting between Hua Ning, the Chinese Ambassador to South Sudan, and South Sudan’s new Defense Minister, Angelina Jany Teny. The Ambassador and Defense Minister also discussed COVID-19 prevention efforts and cooperation between China and South Sudan.

project_name: Gov't donated anti-epidemic med. supplies
description: On August 19, 2020, the Chinese government donated anti-epidemic supplies to South Sudan. A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the Juba International Airport when the medical team arrived (Project ID#93193). These supplies will be used for COVID-19 prevention efforts. The type, quantity, and monetary value of these supplies are unknown.

project_name: China granted $300,000 in anti-cholera assistance to South Sudan
description:
On October 21, 2015, Chinese Ambassador to South Sudan, Ma Qiang, signed an agreement of $300,000 in anti-cholera assistance with South Sudanese Foreign Minister Benjamin. Other details are unspecified.
 
 This agreement is one of the six agreements signed at the same event. This series of agreements is captured in #53328, #53329, #53330, and #53331.

project_name: Gov't provided grant via ETCA for 500-bed hospital in South Sudan
description: On 22 November 2011, the Chinese Government signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement granting a total of 200 million RMB to the newly established Government of South Sudan. This ETCA reportedly financed four different projects: (1) a 500-bed hospital (Project #35423), (2) construction of two secondary schools (see Project #32586), (3) a friendship hall (see Project #35424), and (4) a national theater (see Project #35425). The financial breakdown is unknown.

project_name: 1st lady of China donated med. supplies to Ministry of Health
description: On July 1, 2020, the First Lady of China, Peng Liyuan, donated medical supplies to the South Sudanese Ministry of Health. The supplies were handed over to the First Lady of South Sudan, Mary Ayen Mayardit. The supplies consisted of 18,000 face masks and 120 thermometers. These will be distributed to healthcare workers across South Sudan. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: China signs mou with South Sudan for med. training
description: On September 25th, 2013, the Chinese Ambassador to South Sudan and the South Sudanese Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation signed a bilateral agreement on the training of medical personnel to run Rumbek hospital. This is linked to project ID #31197, an agreement to donates anti-malarial drugs signed at the same time.

project_name: Gov't funds of women's hospital technical cooperation project
description: On December 10, 2015, the Chinese Government and the Government of South Sudan signed a financing agreement for Phase 1 of Rumbek Kiir Mayardit Women's Hospital Technical Cooperation Project (captured via Project ID#53336). The purpose of this project was to maintain and support the ongoing operations of the Kiir Mayardit Women's Hospital in Rumbek. Phase 1 commenced in May 2017 and officially reached completion on July 5, 2019. Phase 2 of the Rumbek Kiir Mayardit Women's Hospital Technical Cooperation Project (captured via ProjectID#92076) also sought to maintain and support the ongoing operations of the Kiir Mayardit Women's Hospital in Rumbek. It commenced on May 23, 2019 and reached completion on May 22, 2022. Salva Kiir Mayardit Hospital — also known as Rumbek/Rumbik Hospital and Rumbek Kiir Mayardit Women's Hospital — was built with financial support from the Chinese Government (as captured via Project #47301 and Project ID#53331). It has 50 beds and a total construction area of ​​about 3,700 square meters. The hospital began operations in 2014 and it is reportedly one of the most modern hospitals in South Sudan.

project_name: China donated medicines & med. supplies to Juba teaching hospital
description: On February 10, 2017, China handed over medical equipments and medicines to the Ministry of Health of South Sudan at Juba Teaching Hospital. The exact value of the donation is not known. This project is completed.

project_name: Gov't donated anti-epidemic supplies
description: On June 11, 2020, the Chinese government donated anti-epidemic supplies to South Sudan. The supplies arrived at the Juba International Airport in Juba, the capital of South Sudan. The anti-epidemic supplies will be used to improve COVID-19 prevention efforts in South Sudan. These supplies included 5,000 protective suits, 15,000 facemasks, 100,000 surgical masks, 5,000 protective goggles, 5,000 gloves, 20,016 nucleic acid detection reagents, and 834 packets of diagnostic kits. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the Juba International Airport. Hua Ning, the Chinese Ambassador to South Sudan, Hon. Mayen Dut Wol, the Undersecretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Hon. Moua Moti Mouna, the Acting Undersecretary of the Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, and John Andruga Duku, the South Sudanese Ambassador to China, received the medical supplies at the airport. Chinese Ambassador Hua Ning and South Sudanese Undersecretary Mayen Dut Wol signed the handover certificate for their respective governments. Dominic Panther Mading, the Director General of the China Affairs Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Senior Colonel Feng Bo, the Defence Attaché, and Cai Senming, the Economic Counselor of the Embassy, also attended the ceremony.

project_name: China donated ambulance to Juba teaching hospital
description: On July 29, 2017, the Chinese government donated an ambulance with medical equipment to the Juba Teaching Hospital in South Sudan. China North Industries Corporation will provide the ambulance free maintenance service for a period of 3 years. The value of this donation is unknown. During this donation, the Chinese government also donated 1 million USD to South Sudan for cholera eradication (recorded in project #60787), and donated medicine and equipment to the Juba Teaching Hospital (recorded in project #58668). This project is completed.

project_name: Province donation of gastroenterology equip to Juba teaching hospital
description: On April 20, 2014, the inauguration ceremony of the gastroenterology unit of Juba Teaching Hospital was held. Anhui Province donated gastroenterology equipment to the Juba Teaching Hospital. Also, Huawei company donated auxiliary equipment facilities, including room decoration and air conditioning (captured in #58597).

project_name: China grants USD 1.5 million & anti-Malarial drugs
description: On July 5, 2018, Chinese and South Sudanese officials signed exchanged letters for China to provide USD 1.5 million in funds and RMB 5 million (USD 0.8 million) worth of anti-malaria drugs to South Sudan for anti-malaria medicine and improving public health service. The cash assistance was handed over to South Sudan's Minister of Health on October 25, 2018. The anti-malarial drugs were handed over to the government of South Sudan on February 21, 2019.

project_name: China donated USD 1 million to South Sudan to fight cholera
description: On April 13, 2017, Chinese Ambassador to South Sudan He Xiangdong signed an exchange of notes pledging to donate USD 1 million to South Sudan to help eradicate cholera. The funds were handed over to South Sudan on July 29, 2017. China has provided aid to help improve public health in South Sudan, also working to eliminate malaria. During this donation, the Chinese government also donated an ambulance to the Juba Teaching hospital (recorded in project #60788), and donated medicine and equipment to the Juba Teaching Hospital (recorded in project #58668). This project is completed.

project_name: Gov't donated anti-Malaria drugs to South Sudan
description: On November 26, 2012, Chinese and South Sudanese officials held a ceremony for China's donation of anti-malarial drugs to South Sudan. China donated 1,960 cartons of artemether injections, which contained 3.14 million doses, enough to treat 500,000 patients. The total value of the medication donated is unknown.

project_name: Embassy held hiv/aids advocacy campaign in South Sudan
description: On November 5, 2019, the 2019-2020 South Sudan National AIDS Prevention and Control Campaign, supported by the Chinese Embassy in South Sudan and organized by the "Concern South Sudan" organization, was launched in Juba. Aimed at increasing prevention and treatment for people living with the disease, the effort will be channeled through the First Lady's charity, Concern South Sudan, with the support of the Chinese Embassy in South Sudan. The specific value of the support undertaken by the Embassy is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donated 100,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In August 2021, the Government of South Sudan announced that the Chinese Government was in the process of transporting 100,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to Juba. The date on which this batch of vaccines was delivered is unknown.

project_name: PetroChina donated anti-epidemic materials to ministry
description: On June 23, 2020, PetroChina Company Limited, a Chinese oil and gas company, donated a batch of anti-epidemic materials to the Ministry of Petroleum and Mining of South Sudan. The total donation amounted to 112 boxes of medical supplies. The materials included 100,00 surgical masks, 5,000 N95 masks, and 100 thermometers. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation in Juba, the capital of South Sudan. China’s Ambassador to Sudan, Hua Ning, South Sudan's Deputy Minister of Petroleum and Mining, the Economic and Commercial Counselor of the Embassy, and the Deputy General Manager of PetroChina International attended the ceremony.

project_name: China donated medicines & med. supplies to friendship hospital
description: On January 25, 2017, the Chinese ambassador visited Upper Nile Region in South Sudan and donated medical supplies and medicine to the Faruzi Friendship Hospital. The amount and value of the donation is unknown.

project_name: China donated anti-Malaria drugs
description: On October 22, 2016, Chinese Ambassador to South Sudan He Xiangdong signed an agreement with South Sudanese Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Deng Alor Kuol to donate CNY 5 million of anti-malaria drugs to South Sudan.  China has donated several batches of anti-malaria drugs and equipment to South Sudan as a part of an initiative to eradicate the disease.

project_name: Gov't commits grant via WHO for Covid-19 pandemic relief
description: On March 10, 2020, the Chinese government committed a grant of USD 100,000 to support WHO response to the COVID-19 outbreak in South Sudan.  This project is captured in UNOCHA Financial Tracking Service as Flow ID #218751.

project_name: China promises to provide 3 million RMB worth of medicine to Sudan
description:
In July 2007, the Chinese government pledged to provide anti-malaria medicine worth 3 million RMB to southern Sudan along with gratuitous aid of 20 million yuan. On November 4 and December 3, 2007, the Chinese government and Sudanese government signed letters of exchange to provide 3 million RMB worth of medicine.
 
 The medicine was provided by Kunming Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd. and Shanghai Fosun Pharma Co., Ltd., and was delivered to the city of Juba (currently part of South Sudan) in March and May 2008. On June 1, 2008, Chinese Ambassador to Sudan Li Chengwen and Sudanese Minister of Presidential Affairs Joseph Loire signed a certificate formally handing over the medicine.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for Juba teaching hospital renovation & expansion
description: On April 10, 2019, Chinese Ambassador to South Sudan Hua Ning and Undersecretary of South Sudan's Foreign Ministry Baak Valentino Wol signed an exchange of letters to conduct a feasibility study the second phase of the expansion and modernization of South Sudan's biggest public health facility, the Juba Teaching Hospital. The feasibility study was carried out on August 14, 2019. Then, on March 20, 2021, the Chinese Government and the Government of South Sudan signed a grant agreement for Phase 2 of the Juba Teaching Hospital Renovation and Expansion Project. The Phase 2 project, with a total site area of about 2.28 hectares and a total floor area of about 16,000 square meters, includes six functional divisions: specialist outpatient division, medical technology division, inpatient division, infectious disease division, administration division and logistics support division. On August 25, 2020, the Chinese Government and the Government of South Sudan officially inaugurated a cancer screening facility Juba Teaching Hospital.  Then, between March 2022 and April 2022, MOFCOM (the project financier) dispatched a group of experts to South Sudan to inspect the progress begin made through Phase 2 of the Juba Teaching Hospital Renovation and Expansion Project. Then, on July 6, 2022, the Chinese Government and the Government of South Sudan signed a project implementation agreement for Phase 2 of the Juba Teaching Hospital Renovation and Expansion Project.

project_name: China donated anti-Malarial drugs to South Sudan
description: On September 25th, 2013, the Chinese Ambassador to South Sudan and the South Sudanese Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation signed a bilateral agreement on provision of anti-malarial medicine. On December 10, 2013, the Chinese Ambassador to South Sudan and the South Sudanese Minister of Health held a ceremony officially handing over the medicine. The cost of the medicine was estimated to be USD 500,000. This project is linked to #31198, another agreement signed at the same time for the training of medical personnel to run Rumbek hospital.

project_name: China provided 2nd phase of technical assistance for women's hospital
description: On August 23, 2019, Chinese and South Sudanese officials signed an exchange of letters for China to provide a second phase of technical assistance for the Kiir Mayardit Women's Hospital. Through this project, China would send experts to South Sudan to give technical guidance on equipment in the hospital, train local technical staff, and provide on-site guidance and assistance on the daily maintenance of the buildings and equipment in the hospital. China would also supply some equipment, materials and spare parts. The project would last for three years following the arrival of the Chinese technical experts. The first phase of technical assistance began in May 2017 and was completed in July 2019 (project #53336). The exact value of China's contributions for this project and date that the Chinese experts arrived in South Sudan are unknown.

project_name: Hi-speed group donated anti-epidemic equipment to ministry
description: On September 24, 2020, Shandong Hi-Speed Group Corporation (SDHS) donated anti-epidemic materials to the Ministry of Roads and Bridges in South Sudan. The materials included 40,000 face masks, 10 ventilators, 10 oxygen concentrators, and 500 personal Protective Equipment (PPE). The monetary value of this donation is unknown.   A ceremony was held for this donation at the South Road and Bridge Department in Juba, South Sudan. Ambassador Hua Ning, the South Road and Bridge Minister, Simon Mijok Mijak, the Deputy Foreign Minister, and the Deputy Finance Minister attended the ceremony and delivered speeches.

project_name: Gov't donated anti-epidemic supplies to Juba teaching hospital
description: On December 4, 2020, the Chinese Government donated anti-epidemic equipment to Juba Teaching Hospital in South Sudan. This equipment consisted of five ventilator machines and their accessories. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.   A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the South Sudanese Ministry of Health. China’s Ambassador to South Sudan, Hua Ning, and South Sudan's Undersecretary of Health attended the ceremony and signed the protocol and donation certificate on behalf of their respective governments. The Director of the Department of International Cooperation of the Ministry of Health of South Africa, representatives of the eighth Chinese medical team in South Africa, officials of the Ministry of Health of South Africa, and representatives of the Juba Teaching Hospital attended the ceremony.  This donation follows a signing ceremony for a Memorandum of Understanding between China and South Sudan which outlines the details of China’s continued dispatch of medical teams to South Sudan for another five years.

project_name: Gov't donated anti-epidemic materials to the Care Association
description: On July 1, 2020, the Chinese government donated a batch of anti-epidemic materials to the South Sudan Care Association. This donation was made by Chinese First Lady Peng Liyuan in response to the African First Lady Development Association's request for China’s support. The specific type, amount, and monetary value of this donation are unknown.  A handover ceremony took place for this donation. Mrs. Aion, the wife of President Kirr of South Sudan, Hua NIng, the Chinese Ambassador to South Sudan, Dr. Artem, the Executive Director of the South Sudan Caring Association, and the Deputy Minister of Health of South Sudan attended the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't provided med. equipment to juba teaching hospital
description: In March of 2021, the Chinese government donated medical supplies and medicine to the Juba Teaching Hospital in South Sudan. The donated supplies included drugs that are commonly used in various medical departments, a mobile high-frequency X-ray machine, a surgical lifting platform, vehicles, and other medical equipment. These drugs and equipment were jointly purchased by the Chinese National Health Commission and the Health Commission of the Anhui Province. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the Juba Teaching Hospital. China’s Ambassador to China, Hua Ning, and the Director of the Juba Teaching Hospital attended the ceremony. This donation is part of China’s larger initiative to support the reconstruction and improvement of the Juba Teaching Hospital.

project_name: Gov't grants funds to support women's hospital construction project
description: In 2012, the Chinese government funded 6 million USD through a grant to support the First Phase of Rumbek Kiir Mayardit Women's Hospital Project (南苏丹拜克基尔•马亚尔迪特妇女医院项目). The purpose of this hospital construction project was to provide medical services to women, particularly those with pregnancy related complications such as fistula. The Rumbek Kiir Mayardit Women’s Hospital is located in the town of Rumbek in Lakes State. The hospital covers an area of 32000 m^2 and has a total construction area of ​​approximately 3,700 m^2. It has a 60 bed capacity, delivery rooms, theatres, a waiting home, laboratories, diagnostic equipment, offices and a mortuary. China Jiangxi International Economic and Technical Cooperation Co., Ltd. was the contractor responsible for project implementation. The project was initiated on March 31, 2012 and completed on November 2013. It was officially handed over to South Sudan on December 10, 2013. On July 12, 2014, the official opening ceremony for this hospital was held.

project_name: China donated $1.5 million to South Sudan for Ebola prevention
description: On October 25, 2018, the Chinese government donated $1.5 million to the government of South Sudan to help prevent the spread of the Ebola virus, which at the time was ravaging the neighboring Democratic Republic of the Congo. The Chinese donation would be used to purchase ambulances and other emergency response tools to help strengthen the country's vigilance against the deadly virus.

project_name: Gov't donated funds via UN for refugees for Covid relief
description: In November 2020, Chinese government provides USD 691,115 to provide Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) to support COVID-19 Response for Refugees and Host Communities in Kenya, Tanzania and South Sudan.  This project is captured in UNOCHA Financial Tracking Service as Flow ID #250455.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for women's hospital construction project
description: On October 21, 2015, Chinese Ambassador to South Sudan Ma Qiang signed an agreement for the second phase construction on the Rumbek Kiir Mayardit Women's Hospital with South Sudanese Foreign Minister Benjamin.   The project involved the construction of a dormitory for medical personnel at the Rumbek Kiir Mayardit Women's Hospital, which is located in the town of Rumbek in Lakes State.  Construction of the dormitory began in December 2017. Then, on July 5, 2019, Chinese and South Sudanese officials signed a certificate officially handing over the newly renovated hospital.

project_name: Embassy donated anti-epidemic supplies to the Ministry of Health
description: On July 17, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in South Sudan donated anti-epidemic supplies to the Ministry of Health in South Sudan. The supplies included 58 oxygen concentrators and 2,000 ventilator consumables. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the Juba Teaching Hospital in South Sudan. Chinese Ambassador to South Sudan, Hua Ning, and South Sudan's Deputy Minister of Health attended the ceremony and delivered speeches. The Economic and Commercial Counselor of the Embassy, Cai Senming, the Director of Juba Teaching Hospital, the captain of the 7th South Sudan medical team, Tang Youbin, and the South Sudanese Medical Team Leader of the Technical Cooperation Group also attended the ceremony.

project_name: China provided anti-Malaria medicine to South Sudan
description: On November 22, 2011, the Chinese Vice Minister of Commerce Jiang Yaoping signed a bilateral framework on trade and technical cooperation with South Sudanese officials, with which they delivered a gift of 400 boxes of anti-malarial medicines. 400 boxes of anti-malaria medicines contains about 640,000 doses and can be used to cure about 200,000 people. The cost of this donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't funds phase 2 of women's hospital technical cooperation project
description: On December 10, 2015, the Chinese Government and the Government of South Sudan signed a financing agreement for Phase 1 of Rumbek Kiir Mayardit Women's Hospital Technical Cooperation Project (captured via Project ID#53336). The purpose of this project was to maintain and support the ongoing operations of the Kiir Mayardit Women's Hospital in Rumbek. Phase 1 commenced in May 2017 and officially reached completion on July 5, 2019. project_name: Embassy donated medicine & equip to Al-Sabah children’s hospital
description: On March 8, 2017, the Chinese Embassy in South Sudan donated a set of medicine and medical equipment to the Al-Sabah Children’s Hospital in Juba. The medications donated included ampilcllin, diclofenac, amoxillin, and others, and the equipment donated included microscopes, blood pressure machines and diabetes testing machines. The donation was made through the Office of H.E. Mary Ayen Mayardit, the First Lady of South Sudan. It was a gift to children and women of South Sudan on the occasion of the International Women’s Day. The total value of the donation is unknown. This project is completed.

project_name: China granted med. supplies to support the Boma health initiative
description: On January 11, 2018, China granted 24 containers of transport and communication devices, medicine, and medical supplies worth USD 3 million to South Sudan to support the Boma Health Initiative. The medical supplies donated included surgical clothes, medical equipment and instruments, and communication devices.

project_name: China provided $760,000 to South Sudan for construction of hospital
description: On April 5, 2011, China opened a hospital in Bentiu through a $760,000 grant to South Sudan. The hospital combines traditional Chinese and Western medicines; it is equipped with  advanced equipment including X-ray apparatus, type-B ultrasonic imager, Holter, electrocardiogram monitor, anesthesia apparatus, automatic testing apparatus, shadow less lamp, and a high frequency electrotome treatment machine. It has 30 sickbeds and eight senior wards; each ward of department is equipped with air conditioners and electric fans. It is staffed by 15 physicians, technician and nurses. The commitment date for this project is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donated USD 100,000 via WHO for Covid pandemic relief
description: In April 2020, Chinese government provides USD 100,000 for South Sudan National COVID-19 Preparedness Plan.  This project is captured in UNOCHA Financial Tracking Service as Flow ID #208095.

project_name: Gov't donated funds via UN children's fund for Covid pandemic relief
description: On March 11, 2020, the Chinese government provided a USD 1,000,000 grant for COVID-19 response in South Sudan (SM200732) via the United Nations Children's Fund.  This project is captured in UNOCHA Financial Tracking Service as Flow ID #223687.

project_name: Chinese donation of mobile clinics to Sudan
description: On June 2, 2010, an agreement was signed by China's Ambassador to Sudan, Li Chengwen, and Sudan's Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs on handing over about ten mobile clinics and medical equipment for Darfur at the cost of 10 million Chinese yuan. The ceremony was attended by Ambassador Charles Menyang, Sudan's Undersecretary of the Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs. The exact commitment date is unknown.

project_name: Palogue friendship hospital
description:
In April 2006, the China National Petroleum Corporation aided 1.3 million USD for the construction of the Palogue Friendship hospital in Palogue, Sudan, near the Melut Basin. The project has been completed.
 
 The start and end dates are unknown.

project_name: KRC friendship hospital
description:
In September 2004, CNPC donated 1.2 million USD to build the 3,000 m2 KRC Friendship Hospital near Khartoum. The hospital consists of eight departments including Surgery, Internal Medicine, Gynecology, and Pediatrics. With 60 beds and 4 attending physicians, the hospital has the capacity to treat 2,000 patients each month. The project has been completed.
 
 The start and end dates are unknown.

project_name: China donated funds with UNICEF to reduce child mortality
description: According to a media report on August 24, 2018, the Sudan Ambassador to China, Ahmed Shawir, announced during an interview that China will contribute US$1 million for child mortality reduction project to Sudan. The project will be conducted in partnership with the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF).

project_name: CNPC provided funds for friendship hospital reconstruction & expansion
description: In 2009, the Chinese Foundation for Poverty Alleviation (CFPA) sent its first assessment team to Sudan for the purpose of investigationg the first Abu Ushar Friendship Hospital Reconstruction and Expansion Project. In May 2010, China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) granted $600,000 USD to CFPA for the construction of Abu Ushar Hospital.   The final cost of the project overran this fund, ending with a total cost of $1.105 million USD (6.93 million RMB). CFPA took on 73 percent of the $505,000 in cost overruns equal to $368,650 USD (see Project #71822); Sudanese Al-Birr and Tawasul Charity Organization (BTO) took 20 percent equal to $101,000 USD; and the remaining $35,350 USD was covered by the Chinese Embassy in Sudan (see Project #71824).   Chinese Foundation for Poverty Alleviation (CFPA) was the implementing contractor. Construction began in June 2010. The increased costs and other difficulties led to the project being completed three months behind schedule. According to the Asian Development source, construction was completed in May 2011 and the hospital was inaugurated on 16 July 2011.   The hospital was originally a horse farm built during the British colonial period in 1929. In 1974, Abu Ushar Friendship Hospital became the headquarters for the Chinese medical mission. The hospital receives 5,000 cases monthly. China Foundation for Poverty Alleviation (CFPA) carried out a maternal and infant healthcare network project at this facility (see Project ID#30435). Abu Ushar Hospital was renovated again in 2016 (see Project ID #53314).

project_name: med. facilities for melovue hospital
description:
From 2004 to 2007, the China National Petroleum Corporation donated 400,000 USD worth of medical facilities, including ambulances and surgical operation rooms, to Melovue (also spelled Malwal or Malawi) Hospital.
 
 The commitment, start, and end dates are unknown.

project_name: National petroleum corporation donated friendship hospital to Sudan
description: China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) granted the Farojie Friendship Hospital in Sudan (法鲁杰友谊医院项目). On January 4, 2011, Chinese Ambassador to Sudan Li Chengwen attended a ceremony celebrating the opening of the hospital.

project_name: Gov't donated Malaria prevention & treatment center equipment
description: In June 2014, the Economic and Commercial Counselor's Office of the Chinese Embassy in Sudan reported that Chinese officials donated equipment for Sudan's malaria prevention and treatment center equipment project (援苏疟疾防治中心设备项目), as well as their anti-malarial drug project (described in #56796). The handover certificate for the equipment was signed before June 2014.

description: In 2009, the Chinese Foundation for Poverty Alleviation (CFPA) sent its first assessment team to Sudan for the purpose of investigationg the first Abu Ushar Friendship Hospital Reconstruction and Expansion Project. The Chinese Embassy in Sudan granted $35,350 USD for this project. Abu Ushar Hospital was renovated again in 2016 (see Project ID#53314).

project_name: CNPC donated anti-epidemic materials to the Sudanese gov't
description: On May 26, 2020, the CNPC donated anti-epidemic materials to the Sudanese Government. The materials were received by the Sudanese Minister of Energy and Minerals. The contents of the donation are unknown.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for friendship hospital construction project
description: Around 2008, the Chinese Ministry of Commerce provided an RMB 70 million grant to the Government of Sudan for the Ad-Damazin Friendship Hospital Construction Project.   The Ad-Damazin Friendship Hospital Construction Project involved the construction of a 88-bed hospital in the city of Ad-Damazin (الدمازين), which is the capital city of Blue Nile State. On 14 April 2008, the China Urban Construction Design and Research Institute's Overseas Project Department and the Sudan Federal Ministry of Health signed a design contract for this hospital.  were the main contractors responsible for implementation. Qingjian Group and China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation (CCECC) built the hospital. China National Pharmaceutical Foreign Trade Corporation also provided and installed medical equipment for the hospital.   A groundbreaking ceremony was held on 30 August 2009, and the hospital was handed over to the Sudanese government on 29 September 2011.  Then, on 12 July 2012 Sudan's Vice President, Ali Osman Mohammed Taha, officially inaugurated the Sudanese Chinese Friendship Hospital in Blue Nile State.  This hospital was one of 30 general hospitals built across Africa as part of an initiative launched at the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC).

project_name: Gov't provided grant for women hospital construction project
description: In 2008, the Chinese Ministry of Commerce provided a $2.9 million USD grant to the Government of Sudan for the construction of the Kiir Maryardit Women Hospital. On 5 July 2019, China added dormitories to the same hospital (see Project ID#53331).  China Jiangxi International Economic and Technical Cooperation Company (CJIC) was the implementing contract. Works began on 31 March 2012. The project passed acceptance on 10 October 2013. This 3,700 square meter hospital is located in Rumbek. Rumbek was originally located in Sudan but it became part of South Sudan after gaining independence in 2011. Therefore, on 10 December 2013, the Kiir Maryardit Women Hospital was handed over to the South Sudanese Ministry of Health. It was officially opened and operational in July 2014.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for dorm construction at friendship hospital
description: On 20 March 2011 and 6 April 2011, the Chinese and Sudanese government officials signed an exchange of letters for a project to build housing units for doctors at Ad-Damazin Friendship Hospital in Blue Nile State. The Chinese Government provided a grant of an unknown value to finance this project.  On 15 May 2012, Qingjian Group Co. Ltd. and the Sudan Ministry of Health signed the implementation contract. The project at Ad-Damazin Friendship Hospital includes 44 housing units for doctors, with simple furniture and equipment. On 20 November 2013, the Chinese Ambassador to Sudan signed a certificate officially handing the housing facilities over to the Sudanese Ministry of Health.

project_name: Fula friendship hospital
description:
In October 2004, the China National Petroleum Corporation aided 1.5 million USD for the construction of the Fula Friendship hospital in Al Fula, Sudan. The project has been completed.
 
 The start and end dates are unknown.

project_name: China initiates project offering free cataract surgeries
description:
On August 15, 2016, the launching ceremony of the “Guangmingxing” project was held at the Eye Hospital of Nile College ("双尼罗河大学" translation uncertain) in Khartoum. Chinese Ambassador to Sudan Li Lianhe and Assistant President of Sudan, Vice Chairman of the Development Relations Committee, Health Minister, Dean of the Nile College Eye Hospital, China’s aid medical team and local people attended the event. The value of the technical assistance is unknown.
 
 The "Guangmingxing" project is a measure launched by the Chinese government to actualize the agreements reached at the Sino-African Cooperation Forum in Johannesburg. Ophthalmologists from the First Hospital of Xi'an, Shaanxi Province, China, worked in Sudan for 90 days. The closing ceremony for the project was held on October 24, 2016 at the University of Nile. In November 2016, it was reported that the collaboration between the Chinese Embassy and the Sudanese Health Ministry had resulted in 1,041 cataract surgeries, where all patients had regained their eyesight. It appears that these surgeries were also in collaboration with the Sanad Charity Foundation, a Sudanese NGO. 
 
 This indicates that the operation surpassed its goal of 1,000 total surgeries (which would have averaged 30 operations a day). The visiting team included 50 ophthalmologists, surgeons, surgery assistants and medical technicians. 
 
 With the help of this program, Sudan plans to reduce its rate of blindness by 0.3% by 2020, an initiative launched in 2005.

project_name: Gov't provided friendship hospital reconstruction & expansion
description: In 2016, China’s Ministry of Commerce provided an RMB 20.31 million grant to the Government of Sudan for the Second Abu Ushar Friendship Hospital Reconstruction and Expansion Project. The purpose of this grant was to cover 100% of the commercial contract with China Geo-Engineering Corporation.   The Abu Ushar Friendship Hospital (苏中阿布欧舍友谊医院) covers an area of ​​4.05 hectares, has 143 beds, and has a daily outpatient capacity of about 200 people. It is located in the town of Abu Ushar (or Abu `Ushar, أبو عشر) within Gezira State, 110 km southeast of Khartoum. China Geo-Engineering Corporation was the contractor responsible for implementation. The groundbreaking ceremony was on 7 November 2016 and works ended on 31 August 2017. Then, on 12 November 2017, a formal project handover ceremony took place.  The hospital was originally a horse farm built during the British colonial period in 1929. In 1974, Abu Ushar Friendship Hospital became the headquarters for the Chinese medical mission. The hospital receives 5,000 cases monthly. China Foundation for Poverty Alleviation (CFPA) carried out a maternal and infant healthcare network project at this facility (see Project ID#30435). China also financed the first renovation to the hospital in 2010 (see Project ID#53415).

project_name: China pledges to finance a hospital ICU reconstruction in Zanzibar

project_name: Gov't provided grant for establishment of an institute
description: During the Forum on China-Africa Coorperation in 2006, China agreed to fund and build a cardiac surgery treatment and training center (also known as Jakaya Kikwete Cardiac Institute or 援坦桑尼亚心脏外科诊疗培训中心项目) in Tanzania's Muhimbili National Hospital. The total cost of the project was 26.6 billion TZS ($15.8 million USD). The construction was shared between the governments of China and Tanzania. China's contribution to the project was 63.5 million RMB.   In 2008, the Chinese government sent a team to Dar es Saleem for initial design and technical study for the center. On May 25, 2009, China Shandong International Economic and Technical Cooperation Corporation (SIETC) won the bid to build the hospital. On July 18, 2009, the contract signing ceremony was held at the Tanzania Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, and SIETC undertook the task of constructing the facility. On March 31, 2010, the project was officially launched. On February 6, 2012, it was completed and handed over to Tanzanian government. On April 27, 2014, the facility was officially put into operation. In April 2015, the cardiac surgery treatment and training center was separated from the Muhimbili National Hospital and renamed the Jakaya Kikwete Cardiac Institute.   Built upon the request of the Tanzanian Ministry of Health and Welfare, the cardiac surgery treatment and training center in Muhimbili National Hospital is one of 30 aid projects involving the construction of hospitals. At present, the Jakaya Kikwete Cardiac Institute is the only specialist hospital for cardiac diseases in the whole territory of Tanzania and has become the largest and best specialist hospital for cardiac diseases in East Africa. As well as many Tanzanian citizens, patients also attend this hospital from other countries in East Africa.

project_name: Gov't donated 500,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021 and 2022, the Chinese Government donated approximately 5.565 million doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Tanzania. The Chinese Government delivered 3 million donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Tanzania on July 14, 2021. Two weeks later, on July 31, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered a batch of Sinovac COVID-19 vaccine doses and syringes to Tanzania’s Zanzibar Revolutionary Government.  The number of vaccine doses and syringes that were donated is unknown. Zanzibar Trade and Industrial Development Minister Omar Shaban and Chinese Consul General in Zanzibar Zhang Zhisheng went to the airport to greet and attend the handover ceremony. The Chinese Government delivered an additional 1,065,500 donated Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Tanzania on October 8, 2021. The package arrived at the Julius Nyerere International Airport in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. The Tanzanian government held a grand welcoming ceremony at Julius Nyerere International Airport on the same day. Minister Counselor Xu Chen of the Chinese Embassy in Tanzania, Minister of Health Guajima of Tanzania, Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Sokoyne of Tanzania and other government officials, UN Resident Coordinator Milisik, heads of diplomatic missions in Tanzania and diplomatic envoys from many countries in Tanzania attended the event. Then, on November 1, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 500,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Tanzania. A handover ceremony took place in Dar es Salaam at the Julius Nyerere Airport. Chinese Ambassador Chen Mingjian, Minister of Health Dr. Guajima, Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Health of Tanzania Macubi, Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Tanzania Sokoin attended the ceremony. activities and speeches. Several month later, on January 26, 2022, the Chinese Government delivered 800,000 donated Sinopharm vaccine doses to the Government of Tanzania. Two days later, on January 28, 2022, the Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated Sinovac COVID-19 doses to Tanzania’s Zanzibar Revolutionary Government. The vaccines were handed over to a Representative of the Zanzibar Revolutionary Government, Minister for Education and Vocational Training Simai Mohammed Said, by the Chinese Consul General in Zanzibar Zhang Zhisheng at the Abeid Amani Karume International Airport.

project_name: Gov't donated masks to Tanzania for Covid-19 relief
description: On June 29th, 2021, the Chinese Consulate General in Zanzibar donated masks to Zanzibar at the Zanzibar Ministry of Health. Consul General Zhang Zhisheng signed a handover certificate with Omar Shajak, Permanent Secretary of the San Francisco Ministry of Health. This batch of supplies includes 30,000 disposable medical surgical masks and 5,000 N95 masks. The purpose of this donation is to help Tanzania fight against the pandemic.

project_name: China donated anti-Malarial drugs to Zanzibar in 2013
description: On January 15, 2013, members of the Chinese Consulate in Zanzibar met with officials from Zanzibar's Ministry of Health to sign a handover certificate for the donation of anti-malarial drugs.

project_name: China donated masks & disposable gloves to Tanzania for Covid relief
description: In March 2021, Chinese Consulate General in Zanzibar donated 12,000 disposable medical masks and some medical surgical gloves to Zanzibar (Tanzania) Mnazi Mmoja Hospital and Abdulla Mzee Hospital to help alleviate the emerging threat of COVID-19 in Tanzania.

project_name: China donated anti-ngiri disease medicial supplies to Tanzania
description: On September 2, 2021, the Ministry of Health, Social Welfare, Elderly, Gender, and Children received the equipment for surgical equipment for gonorrhea surgery from China, which will be used for gonorrhea surgery in Unguja and Cahkechake Hospitals on the Pemba. According to Zhang Zhisheng, the Chinese Ambassador to Zanzibar, the purpose of this batch of medical equipment is to treat citizens with small boxes. He explained that at least 100 patients will benefit from the help to improve their health.

project_name: Ministry sponsors hospital management training for med professionals
description: On August 12, 2018 the Chinese Embassy in Tanzania hosted a farewell party for 30 Tanzanian medical professionals from national and provincial hospitals who were sponsored by the Chinese Ministry of Commerce to attend a one month training seminar in Hunan on hospital management practices. The medical professionals were sent off alongside 20 Tanzanian students who received medical scholarships (captured in project #88100). The farewell ceremony was attended by dignitaries and officials from both China and Tanzania including: Chinese Ambassador Wang Ke and Tanzanian Minister of Education Ndali Chako. The training course was provided in response to a November 2017 request from Tanzanian President John Magufuli for Chinese assistance in developing Tanzania's human resources in the field of medicine of which Chinese President Xi Jinping responded and approved.

project_name: Embassy, International Corporation lmt, & CCECC donate supplies
description: On April 9, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Tanzania handed over the first batch of medical supplies to the Government of Tanzania to help enhance the capacity of Tanzania to fight the COVID-19 pandemic. The first batch of medical supplies includes 100,000 face masks, 1,000 protective clothes, and 150 forehead thermometers. Among these supplies, some are donated by the Chinese Embassy (Project ID#92878), and some are donated by two Chinese companies, Hunan Dongfang Jinxi International Corporation Limited (Project ID#94315), and China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation (CCECC) (Project ID#94316). The monetary value of the donation is unclear.

project_name: China donated med. supplies for Covid-19 relief
description: On January 21, 2021, the ceremony of China's donation of anti-epidemic medical equipment to Zanzibar was held at the Zanzibar Ministry of Health. Consul General Zhang Zhisheng signed the handover certificate and delivered a speech with Simai Mohamed, Minister of Education and Vocational Affairs and Acting Minister of Health, Community Development, Gender, and Children. The donation was worth 348 million Tanzania shillings. The purpose of this donation is to help Tanzania fight against the COVID-19 pandemic.

project_name: Gov't provided funds for construction of a children's facility at JKCI
description: In October 2018, the Chinese Government committed TSh16.6 billion TZS to supporting the construction of a children's cardiac facility. The Government of Tanzania is providing another TSh10 billion TZS towards the completion of the project. This facility will be treated as an extension of the Jakaya Kikwete Cardiac Institute (JKCI) to provide more space for heart patients of all ages. The new facility will have a capacity of between 280 and 350 beds, compared to the prior capacity of 128 beds. The facility will also provide medical assistance to countries such as Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, Zambia, Malawi, Comoros, and others.   As of June 29, 2019, a feasibility study had been completed on the expansion of the cardiac institute, and the project has moved into the implementation stage.

project_name: Gov't provided med. scholarships to Tanzanian healthcare professionals
description: China granted medical scholarships to 20 Tanzanian students to study in China. A farewell ceremony was held for this as well as a medical training course (project #89268) on August 12, 2018. The 20 students receiving scholarships were doctors, teachers, and researchers from Muhibili Medical University who will go to Qilu Medical College of Shandong University to study bone marrow transplantation, liver transplantation, interventional radiology, cardiothoracic surgery, critical care supervision, and other topics.

project_name: China donated anti-Malarial drugs to Tanzania
description: On July 25, 2017, representatives from China's embassy in Tanzania met with Vice Minister of Health Ke Guangzula in Nzega Regional Hospital in Tabora Province to handover the donation of anti-malarial drugs.

project_name: China donated of med. equipment to Zanzibar
description:
On March 11, 2010, the Chinese government donated medical equipment worth 64 million TZS to the Zanzibar government. The equipments were handed over by Zhu Xiangjun, head of the Chinese medical team in Zanzibar, and were received by the Zanzibar Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Sultan Mohd Mughery. Some of the equipments would go to serve in the theater at Mnazi mmoja general hospital.
 
 According to a 2011 Working Series report, China has been sending medical teams to Zanzibar since August 1964.

project_name: Embassy donated hand-washing devices to schools to fight Covid
description: On June 25, 2020, the Chinese Embassy donated hand-washing devices to 100 primary and secondary schools in Tanzania to aid in the fight against COVID-19. The donation included: 100 hand-washing devices and 550 liters of hand sanitizer. The donation is worth 22,000,000 Tanzanian Shillings. The handover ceremony took place at the embassy and was jointly organized by the Chinese Embassy in Tanzania and the Tanzanian NGO Kawa Foundation. Wang Ke, Chinese Ambassador to Tanzania, Malangwa, Acting Administrative Secretary of the Province of Tajikistan, Mfuma, Chief Medical Officer, Kowa, Executive Director-General of the Kaowa Foundation, and representatives of the donated schools attended the ceremony.

project_name: Chinese peace ark 2017 visit in Tanzania
description: On November 19, 2017, the Peace Ark Hospital Ship docked in Dar es Salaam and provided assistance to more than 6400 patients. It left after 8 days, on November 26. The last visit by the Peace Ark Hospital ship was 7 years ago, in 2010 (#65378)

project_name: China donated anti-Malarial drugs to Tanzania
description: On December 2, 2005, the government of China donated 139 million TZS worth of anti-malaria drugs to Tanzania. Both Ambassador Yu Qingtai and Tanzanian Health Minister Anna Abdallah commended the donation.

project_name: China donated drugs & med. equipment to Lome & Kara regional hospitals
description: On July 6, 2004 the Chinese ambassador to Togo, Zhang Shixian, donated drugs and medical equipment worth about 35 million FCFA to the Togolese Minister of Health, Suzanne Aho Assouma. The donation was made at the office of the Economic and Commercial Council at the Embassy and is meant for the Lome Regional Hospital and the Kara Regional Hospital.

project_name: China donated anti-Malaria equipment
description: On March 26, 2013, the Chinese Economic and Commercial Counselor and Togolese Minister of Health signed the certificate of delivery for the donation of malaria diagnosis and treatment equipment in Lomé from China.  According to "中多两国签署援多疟疾诊疗设备交接证书," the donation was worth 1.5 million RMB.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for Lomé hospital center construction project
description:
In September 2005, it was announced that the Chinese Government would construct a hospital in Togo's capitol city of Lomé. China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) reported provided CFA 4 billion of grant funding for the Lomé Regional Hospital Center Construction Project. 
 
 This project involved the construction of a 100-bed hospital in the northern part of the the city of Lomé that occupies an area of 5,462.66 square meters. The hospital, which is known as the Centre Hospitalier Régional de Lomé commune (CHR), was also equipped with modern medical equipment. Fujian Construction Engineering Group (福建建工集团总公司) was the contractor responsible for implementation. Construction began on December 18, 2007 and ended on May 26, 2009. The project was officially handed over to the Togolese authorities on June 17, 2009. The Togolese Health Minister Comlan Mally (L) and Chinese Ambassador to Togo Yang Min signed the project handover certificate. The hospital was officially inaugurated on April 26, 2010.

project_name: China donated med. supplies to prevent Ebola
description: On September 30, 2014, Chinese Ambassador to Togo Liu Yuxi and Togolese Prime Minister Ahumé Zunu signed a medical assistance agreement on behalf of the two governments. Through the agreement, the Chinese government provided Togo with a batch of Ebola prevention and control materials, totaling 420 000 000 West African CFA Franc (5 million RMB). On November 1, 2014, the donation batch of Ebola prevention and control materials arrived in Lime via a charter freight flight.  On November 20, 2014, the handover ceremony for the aid was held. The donation included medical clothing, protective goggles, knapsack sprayers, emergency kits, and ultraviolet ray germicidal lamps.

project_name: China donated anti-Malaria drugs
description: On June 24, 2008 the Chinese Ambassador to Togo, Yang Min presented anti-malaria drugs to the Togolese Minister of Health, Charles Kondi Agba. The donation was made up of oral and injectable drugs valued at over 33 million West African CFA francs. This was the second donation of drugs that China offered to Togo, according to the measures proclaimed by the Chinese government during the Beijing summit, during the forum on the Sino-African cooperation in November 2006.

project_name: China donated 150,000 insecticidal mosquito nets
description: On September 11, 2019, a handover ceremony for 50,000 insecticidal mosquito nets provided by China to Togo was held in the city of Lomé. The donation is valued at 900 million CFA. More than 40 people including the Ambassador to Togo, Chao Weidong, and the Togolese Minister of Health and Public Health, Mustafa Mijiava, attended the event. Ambassador Chao Weidong and Minister Mijiava delivered speeches and signed the project handover certificate. The mosquito nets will be used to help protect the people of Togo against malaria and promote anti-malarial work. In particular, the nets will be provided to pregnant women and children.

project_name: Embassy provided anti-epidemic materials & food
description: On September 17 and 18, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Togo provided a batch of medical protective equipment and food to the Togo Disabled Persons' Federation and the Togo-China Friendship Association.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. China’s Ambassador to Togo, Chao Weidong, the Secretary-General of the Ministry of Social Action, Women's Promotion and Literacy, the Director of the National Relief Agency, the Chairman of the Togo Disabled Federation Council and Chairman of the Togo-China Friendship Association, and the former Togolese Ambassador to China attended the ceremony.  The monetary value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donated 702,000 Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: On April 23, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Togo. Chinese Ambassador to Togo Chao Weidong and the Togolese Minister of Health Mustafa Mijiyawa received the vaccine doses at Gnassingbe Eyadema International Airport. Then, on August 20, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Togo. On the same day, the Chinese Government donated 702,000 additional doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Togo via COVID-19 Vaccines Global Access (COVAX) — a worldwide initiative aimed at equitable access to COVID-19 vaccines directed by the GAVI vaccine alliance, the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations, the World Health Organization, and UNICEF. Then, between October 18 and 26, 2021, the Chinese Government donated 702,000 additional doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Togo via COVAX.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for Malaria prevention & treatment center
description:
In February 2008, the Chinese Government pledged to build a malaria prevention and treatment center in Togo. It reportedly committed CFA 210 million of grant funding for this project. On January 8, 2009, the center was officially inaugurated. Togolese Health Minister Komlan Mally and Chinese Ambassador to Togo Yang Min attended the inauguration ceremony. Yang Min indicated at the ceremony that the construction of this center was one of the measured announced by the Chinese Government at the Beijing Summit of the Forum on Sino-African Cooperation in November 2006.
 
 The center was temporarily located in the compound of the Lomé polyclinic (polyclinique de Lomé) while the Chinese Government-financed Lomé Regional Hospital Center [Centre Hospitalier Régional de Lomé commune (CHR)] was still being constructed (see Project ID#2174). project_name: Embassy donated daily necessities
description: On June 18, 2020, the Chinese Embassy provided charitable materials to the Togo National Basic Development Assistance Agency. The materials included grain, oil, and other daily necessities. These materials will be distributed to families that have been severely impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation on June 18, 2020. project_name: China donated med. equipment to Togo

The Management Committee of New Crown Virus Epidemic Prevention Materials and Sanitary Equipment of the Presidential Palace of Togo received the batch of materials on behalf of the Togolese government.

project_name: China donated equipment to Kara regional hospital
description: In January 2014, the new Chinese Ambassador to Togo, Liu Yuxi, visited the Kara Regional Hospital Center, commonly known as the Chinese hospital of Tomde. During his visit, the Ambassador announced the renewal of a donation of medical equipment worth 296,000,000 FCFA to the hospital.

project_name: Provided emergency cash to help control the spread of Cholera

However, the producer of the materials appears to be Yantai Show Long Medical Technology Co., Ltd, a company owned by Shandong Shulang Garment, that produces gloves, masks, and full-body PPE.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. project_name: China merchants group provided anti-epidemic materials to lct terminal

project_name: Embassy provided anti-epidemic materials to ministry
description: On May 20, 2020, the Chinese Embassy provided anti-epidemic materials to the Ministry of Development, Planning and Cooperation of Togo. project_name: China donated med. supplies to Togolese minister of health
description: On March 24, 2005 China delivered medicine worth US$100,000 to Togo to help the country fight malaria, cholera and meningitis. The medicine was officially received by Togo's Health Minister Suzanne Aho Assouma. The donation is a part of cooperation between China and Togo in the field of public health.

project_name: Gov't provided a $1.3 million USD grant for health care centers
description: On February 27, 2012, the Chinese Government agreed to give Tunisia $1.3 million USD to upgrade local hospitals and health care centers in areas affected by flooding in northwestern Tunisia.

project_name: Gov't of China donated the 2nd batch of Covid-19 vaccines
description: On August 2nd, 2021, Ambassador Zhang Jianguo, Tunisian Minister of Foreign Affairs Jerendi, and Major General Vergani were present for the handover ceremony of the second batch of COVID-19 vaccines from China to Tunisia. In combination with the first batch, China has exported a total of 500,000 doses of Covid-19 vaccines to Tunisia.

project_name: Gov't donated med. supplies
description: On April 16, 2020, the Chinese Government donated medical supplies to the Tunisian Ministry of Health. The supplies included N95 masks, nucleic acid testing kits, and medical goggles. The shipment of supplies was sent on April 15, 2020, arriving at an airport in Tunisia. Wang Wenbin, the Chinese Ambassador to Tunisia, Zhang Gengling, the Economic and Commercial Counselor at the Chinese Embassy, and the General Directorate of the Tunisian Ministry of Health received the supplies at the airport.   The purpose of this donation is to help Tunisia fight against the Covid-19 pandemic. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.
