A handover ceremony was held for this donation on April 16, 2020. Wang Wenbin, the Chinese Ambassador to Tunisia, handed over the supplies to Tunisian Defense Minister Imed Hazgui. Following the ceremony, the two officials signed the handover certificate.

project_name: Gov't provided grant to exp& the university hospital in SFAX
description: On October 8, 2019, China signed an exchange of letters with Tunisia for a feasibility study for the expansion of the University Hospital in Sfax. The prime minister of Tunisia, Youssef Chahed, stated that China would provide a second donation for the expansion of the hospital; the first donation referring to the grant provided by China to Tunisia to build the hospital, captured in linked project ID#30323. The value of the grant for the expansion project is unclear. Chinese Ambassador to Tunisia Wang Wenbin and Tunisian Acting Minister of Health Sonia Ben Sheikh signed on behalf of the two governments at the Prime Minister's Office of Tunisia.   According to the Tunisian prime minister, the hospital's extension would include a large-scale surgical center, and construction was to start during the first half of 2020. The inauguration ceremony for the original hospital building (#30323), however, did not occur until December 2020 due to COVID-19-related complications, so it is unclear if this timeline was honored.

project_name: China donated anti-epidemic materials to the Ministry of Health
description: On December 30th, 2020, Ambassador to Tunisia Zhang Jianguo provided anti-epidemic materials from the Government of China to the Tunisian Minister of Health Fauz Mehdi. The purpose of this donation is to help Tunisia fight against the Covid-19 pandemic.

project_name: Gov't of China donated 2nd batch of anti-epidemic materials
description: On June 10, 2020, the second batch of anti-epidemic materials assisted by the Chinese government arrived in Tunisia for a handover ceremony. Chargé d’affaires Yuan Lijie and Brigadier General Firgani, the military security chief of the Ministry of Defense, were present to meet the materials, and signed handover certificates on behalf of the two governments. This batch consisted of N95 masks, new coronavirus nucleic acid test kits, medical eye masks, medical protective clothing, and surgical gloves. The purpose of this donation is to help Tunisia fight against the Covid-19 pandemic.

project_name: Gov't provided a grant for the SFAXhospital construction project
description: In 2012, the Chinese Government and Government of Tunisia began negotiations on a possible $30 million USD grant for the construction of a university hospital center in the city of Sfax. In June 2013, the Chinese Government publicly announced its intention to construct the hospital. Then, on November 17, 2014 and November 18, 2014, the Chinese Government and Government of Tunisia signed an exchange of letters, which officially committed grant funding for the Sfax Hospital Construction Project. The Chinese Government provided RMB 330 million of grant funding for the project. On March 13, 2017, the Tunisian Government ratified the exchange of letters via Decree n° 2017-360. Tunisia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs was responsible for the execution of this degree.  The purpose of the project was to build a 246-bed general hospital — with a total construction area of about 26,000 square meters — in the city of Thyna (طينة) outside of Sfax. The hospital included outpatient and emergency facilities, a logistic supports building, an administrative office building, an inpatient department, and a facilities management building. The 14-block hospital also included an 80-bed psychiatry unit, a morgue, guard rooms, and other facilities. This was China's largest aid project in the Tunisian health sector. China State Construction Engineering Corporation was the contractor responsible for implementation. Its subsidiary, China Construction Eighth Engineering Division Corp., Ltd., was also responsible for implementation. Zhengzhou Zhongxing Engineering Supervision Co., Ltd. and SIPPR Engineering Group Co., Ltd. (SIPPR) provided project management and supervision services.  A project implementation agreement was signed on April 29, 2016. Construction commenced on December 1, 2016. It passed an inspection on November 30, 2019 and was completed on the same day. After the completion of construction, work continued on the handover process. However, the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic threw the process into disarray. It was only in August 2020 that China State Construction Engineering Corporation that sent 5 of its employees to work on the handover process, which entailed consultations with Tunisia's Tunisian Ministry of Health on issues in the project. Ultimately, the project was externally accepted by Tunisia.  Chinese Ambassador to Tunisia Zhang Jianguo and Tunisian Minister of Health Faouzi Mehdi signed the project handover certificate on December 9, 2020. The hospital's inauguration ceremony, which was attended by President of Tunisia Kais Saied, was held on December 10, 2020. The hospital opened its doors — under the name ‘Hôpital Militaire Slim Chaker Sfax’ — on January 4, 2021 and began receiving patients.. After completion, the Tunisian Government placed the hospital under the supervision of Tunisia’s Ministry of Defense in order to transform the hospital into a national center for the treatment of patients infected with COVID-19 during the ongoing pandemic.  On October 8, 2019, the Chinese Government and the Government of Tunisia signed an agreement to conduct a feasibility study for the Sfax Hospital Expansion Project (captured by linked project ID#66243).

project_name: MoD donated anti-pandemic med. materials to the MoD
description: On June 3, 2020, The Chinese Ministry of Defense provided the Tunisian Ministry of National Defense with new coronary pneumonia epidemic prevention and control medical supplies. At this handover ceremony, Ambassador Wang Wenbin, Defense Military Office Wang Zhenyu, and Brigadier General Vergani went to the airport to attend the handover ceremony. The purpose of this donation is to help Tunisia fight against the Covid-19 pandemic.

project_name: Gov't donated 200,000 Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021 and 2022, the Chinese Government donated approximately 1.7 million doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Tunisia. The Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Tunisia on March 25, 2021. At the vaccine handover ceremony, the Chinese Ambassador to Tunisia Zhang Jianguo was present to the donation to the Tunisian Minister of Health Sudu Mehdi. Then, on February 22, 2022, the Chinese Government delivered another 1.5 million donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Tunisia.

project_name: Gov't grants $439,560.40 to Uganda for health sector activities
description: On January 4, 2010, the Chinese Government committed a grant worth $439,560.40 to the Government of Uganda. This grant is provided for general health sector activities. According to the Aid Management Platform (AMP) of the Government of Uganda's Ministry of Finance, Planning, and Economic Development, this grant has been fully disbursed.

project_name: Chinese donation of reproductive health med. equipment
description: On June 1, 2009, the Chinese Government committed $294,000 in grant funding for the provision of reproductive health equipment to the Government of Uganda. Then, on June 30, 2009,  Wang Zeshan, Charge d'affaires at the Chinese Embassy, handed over the equipment to Uganda's Health Minister Stephen Malinga. The equipment included an ultrasound, a urine analysis equipment, an ECG machine, a mammogram machine, and some lamps and tables. The donated equipment will be provided to the Mulago and Jinja hospitals.

project_name: Embassy donated anti-covid supplies to Uganda civil aviation authority
description: On December 10, 2021, the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in Uganda delivered a shipment of COVID-19 equipment to the Uganda Civil Aviation Authority (UCAA) at Entebbe International Airport in Kampala. The shipment was worth approximately UGX 160,000,000 and consisted of face masks, protective overalls, eye shields, disposable gloves, infrared thermometers, face shields, and flat-screen TVs.

project_name: Donation of medicine & equipment to friendship hospital
description: On November 13, 2014, the 16th Chinese medical team donated medicine and medical equipment worth 10 million RMB to the China-Uganda Friendship Hospital.  According to the exchange agreement signed on December 13 and December 27, 2010, the Chinese Government committed to providing a batch of medical equipment and supplies to the China-Uganda Friendship Hospital, including purifying air conditioners, pulse oximeters, ventilators, and manufacturing facilities. Oxygen machine, desk and other materials.

project_name: China donated anti-Malaria drugs
description: On April 20, 2009, at the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs offices in Kampala, Chong Quan, the Chinese Assistant Minister of Commerce, handed over anti-malaria drugs, ARCO and Duo-Cotexin, worth approximately 400,000 USD to Richard Nduhura, Uganda's Health Minister.   This is a subproject of #63793, an anti-malaria program from 2006 to 2014.

project_name: Embassy provided grant for the Bugolobi house project for the UWESO
description: On March 13, 2019, the Chinese Embassy in Uganda donated USD 58,500 to the Uganda Women’s Relief for Orphans (UWESO), an organization that helps orphaned children who lost their parents due to civil unrest or the HIV/AIDS epidemic) for the purchase of building materials for the Bugolobi House. The donation ceremony was held at the Ugandan Presidential Palace and attended by the President of Uganda, the Minister of Education and Sports, Janet Museveni, and Chinese ambassador, Zheng Zhujiang.

project_name: China donated 8 computers to Mulago hospital
description: On June 23, 2006, Chinese Prime Minister Wen Jiabao visited the Institute of Infectious Diseases at Mulago Hospital and donated 8 computers to the hospital. The amount is unknown.During the same visit, Wen Jiabao gave the hospital a donation of 100,000 USD (See Project ID#23426).

project_name: China donated med. supplies to friendship hospital in Naguru
description: On August 9th of 2018, China donated medical supplies worth US$70,000 to the China-Uganda Friendship Hospital in Naguru, Kampala, Uganda. The batch included a wide range of items for all departments, including supplies and those used for acupuncture and Chinese doctrine.  The handover ceremony was attended by Chinese Ambassador Zheng Zhuqiang, Ugandan Minister of Health Jane Ayi, and the Chinese medical team. The China-Uganda Friendship Hospital was built with Chinese aid in 2008 (project #23467, #12177).

project_name: Embassy donated anti-epidemic materials to ministry & hospital
description: On May 15, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Uganda donated a shipment of anti-epidemic supplies to the Ugandan Ministry of Internal Affairs and Mulago National Referral (Specialized) Hospital. The donation included medical masks, KN95 masks, and medical-grade protective clothing intended to help the recipients fight the COVID-19 pandemic.

project_name: Gov't donated 4 shipments of anti-epidemic med. supplies to the gov't
description: On April 28, 2020, the Government of China, represented by Ambassador Zheng Zhuqiang, handed over a shipment of anti-epidemic supplies to the Government of Uganda, represented by Uganda's Minister of Health, Jane Aceng. At the handover ceremony, the two sides signed the intergovernmental handover certificate of the anti-epidemic materials, and Ambassador Zhuqiang stated that this shipment was the first batch of anti-epidemic supplies to fight COVID-19, and that more would be arriving in the following months.  The first shipment consisted of 10,000 surgical masks; 2,000 N95 masks; 2,000 sets of disposable protective clothing; 500 infrared thermometers; 2,000 pairs of medical protective goggles; 10,000 pairs of medical gloves; and 10,000 pairs of medical isolation shoe covers.   The second shipment arrived in Uganda on July 15, 2020. Details about the exact contents of the donation are unknown, but the supplies were donated to be used by clinicians at the China-Uganda Friendship Hospital in Kampala. The value of the second shipment was 60 million shillings (approximately USD $16,440).  The third shipment arrived on September 23, 2020. This shipment included COVID-19 testing kits and ventilators. At the handover ceremony, the two sides also signed an agreement for joint hospital cooperation in the fight against the pandemic.   The fourth shipment arrived on April 14, 2021. It primarily contained new coronavirus nucleic acid detection reagents.

project_name: China provided aid to Uganda to fight Ebola virus
description: On January 18, 2001, China's Vice President, Hu Jintao, and Uganda's Vice President, Wandira Specioza Kazibwe, signed an agreement for China to give Uganda a grant of 80,000 USD to help fight against the Ebola virus.

project_name: China donated of med. supplies to Uganda
description: On August 6, 2015, the Chinese Red Cross and Uganda Red Cross held a medical material handover ceremony in the Manafwa area in Uganda. The medical supplies are provided by the Chinese government. The Chinese Red Cross is responsible for the implementation. The donation includes 26 types of medical equipment such as ambulances, operating beds, solar mobile power supplies, gasoline engine pumps, desktop computers, wheelchairs, and medical masks. The total value is about 1.7 million Chinese yuan.

project_name: Gov't grants $427,837.99 for health sector activities
description: On April 21, 2008, the Chinese Government committed a grant worth $427,837.99 to the Government of Uganda. This grant is provided for general health sector activities. According to the Aid Management Platform (AMP) of the Government of Uganda's Ministry of Finance, Planning, and Economic Development, this grant has been fully disbursed.

project_name: Sinohydro funds the Masindi Barracks centre IV renovation & expansion
description: On October 11, 2019, a groundbreaking ceremony was held for the Masindi Barracks Hospital project donated by China Electric Power Uganda Karuma 812 Joint Venture, which is effectively controlled by Sinohydro (China Water Resources and Hydropower Construction Corporation). The purpose of the project is to expand and transform the existing hospital, including a new operating room, laboratory, doctor's dormitory, nurse's dormitory, canteen, and the renovation and repair of some original buildings. Originally, the project was expected to finish in 8 months, but it was delayed because of the COVID-19 Pandemic. It was originally expected to cost $1.5 million, but eventually it cost $1.7 million.  The project was constructed by local company Excel Construction ltd. and was finished on April 16, 2021 under the witness of officials from the Chinese companies and Uganda People's Defense Force (UPDF).

project_name: Gov't provided grant for the construction of friendship hospital
description: On October 3, 2008, China's ambassador to Uganda, Sun Heping, announced that the Chinese Government would build a hospital and malaria treatment/prevention center called the China-Uganda Friendship Hospital in Naguru (CUFH-N) with a grant of $6 million. The purpose of the project was to (a) provide health services to the residents of Nakawa Division, Kampala Metropolitan Area; and (b) decongest Mulago National Referral Hospital, the only general public hospital serving an estimated 3 million inhabitants of the Kampala Metropolitan Area. It involved the construction of a two-storey hospital with a bed capacity of 100, the construction of staff houses, and the supply and installation of medical equipment including a CT-scan. China National Complete Plant Import and Export Corporation (COMPLANT) was the contractor responsible for project implementation. Kampala Capital City Authority (KCCA) donated the 5 acre site where the hospital was built. The Government of Uganda also contributed an estimated $2 million in tax waivers on construction materials used to build the hospital, landscaping, road access and licensing fees.   The 5772.8-square-meter hospital was slated to begin construction in August 2009. The groundbreaking ceremony was held on September 23, 2009. Construction was completed in November 2011. The handover ceremony was held on January 6, 2012  In June 2012, Jing Yanhui, an official from the Chinese embassy in Uganda, announced that a malaria treatment and prevention center would be added on to the hospital in the near future.

project_name: Chinese donations of medication & equipment for Malaria treatment
description: From November 2006 to 2014, the Chinese government has been helping Uganda in fighting Malaria in the form of carrying out training programs for treating Malaria and donations of anti-Malaria medication and equipment. The donations are made through multiple projects throughout the 8 years, which are listed as below:  2006 China committed donation of anti-malarial drugs (completed in 2007) (#85127) 2006 China funded the three-day anti-malarial program in Uganda (#34837) 2006 Donation of anti-malarial drugs (#60078) 2007 China committed donation of anti-malarial drugs (completed in 2008) (#60074) 2009 Donation of anti-malarial drugs (#12360) 2010 Donation of anti-malarial drugs batch 1 (#14359) 2010 Donation of anti-malarial drugs batch 2 (#14612) 2012 Donation of anti-malarial drugs (#60758) 2013 Donation of anti-malarial drugs, equipment, and supplies (#37927)

project_name: Provincial gov't donated with anti-epidemic med. supplies to MoH
description: On June 19, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Uganda held a handover ceremony for supplies donated by the Provincial Government of Hunan to the Ugandan Ministry of Health. Based on photos of the event published by the Embassy, the shipment consisted of at least eight boxes of anti-COVID materials, with at least half of those boxes containing surgical masks.

project_name: Gov't donated anti-epidemic med. supplies to the friendship hospital
description: On July 15, 2020, an unspecified organization from within the Chinese Government donated 60 million shillings (about 16,440 U.S. dollars) worth of medical supplies to the China-Uganda Friendship Hospital to boost the hospital's efforts in treating COVID-19 patients. Details about the exact contents of the donation are unknown, but the supplies were donated to be used by clinicians at the China-Uganda Friendship Hospital in Kampala. The value of the second shipment was 60 million shillings (approximately USD $16,440). Chinese Ambassador to Uganda Zheng Zhuqiang handed over the assortment of medical supplies to  Emmanuel Batibwe, director of the China-Uganda Friendship Hospital in Kampala, Uganda. This was the Chinese Government's second medical supplies donation to the Government of Uganda.

project_name: China grants to Mulago hospital
description: On June 23, 2006, Chinese Prime Minister Wen Jiabao visited the Institute of Infectious Diseases at Mulago Hospital and provided a grant to the hospital to train health workers to handle HIV/Aids patients. The grant amount is unclear.  During the same visit, Wen Jiabao gave the hospital a donation of 8 computers (See Project ID#16519)

project_name: Infectious disease hospital provided training for staff at hospital
description: On April 22, 2020, medical staff from China's Yunnan Provincial Infectious Disease Hospital shared their insights and experiences fighting the spread of COVID-19 with their counterparts at the China-Uganda Friendship Hospital in Kampala, Uganda via videoconference. According to Xinhua, the staffs "discussed clinical manifestations, diagnosis, and treatment experience," as well as personal protection equipment (PPE) protocol for staffers, and nursing for COVID-19 patients. The China-Uganda Friendship Hospital was one of those in Uganda designated to combat the pandemic.

project_name: China funds anti-Malaria training program
description: In November 2006, soon after the China-Africa Summit, a three-day anti-malaria training program was held in Kampala and funded by the Chinese government as part of China’s efforts to join forces with Uganda to fight the disease. The program started on November 27th and ended on November 29th, during which 5 experts from China provided training on treating and controlling Malaria to 48 primary doctors and officers from Uganda.   This project is linked to #63793, which details all of the malaria-related projects in Uganda funded by China.

project_name: Donation of anti-Malaria drugs batch 2
description: On October 8, 2010, the Chinese government donated anti-malarial drugs worth 4,000,000 RMB to Uganda. China's ambassador to Uganda, Sun Heping, handed over the donation to Richard Nduhuura, State Minister for General Duties in the Health Ministry.

project_name: China commits grant for hr support to Jinja hospital
description: On January 2, 2000, China and Uganda signed a grant agreement for human resource support for Jinja Hospital worth $966,174.24. China sent multiple medical teams to Jinja Hospital after this grant commitment was made. However, according to the Aid Management Platform (AMP) of the Government of Uganda's Ministry of Finance, Planning, and Economic Development, only $292,911.54 (34%) of the grant commitment was actually disbursed as of June 14, 2009. Jinja Regional Referral Hospital, commonly known as Jinja Hospital, is a hospital in the city of Jinja, eastern Uganda.

project_name: Gov't donated via WHO for Covid-19 pandemic relief
description: In March 2020, Chinese government provides USD 116,600 to support WHO response to COVID-19 outbreak in Uganda.  This project is captured in UNOCHA Financial Tracking Service as Flow ID #218753.

project_name: Gov't donated 300,000 Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: On July 31, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 300,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Uganda’s Ministry of Health. The shipment had originally been promised by Yang Jiechi, Member of the Political Bureau of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) and Director of the Office of the Foreign Affairs Commission of the CPC Central Committee, on February 21, 2021, during a meeting he had with Ugandan President Museveni. The 300,000 doses arrived initially at National Medical Stores in Entebbe, about 40 km south of the capital of Kampala. From there, they were to be distributed to the population by the Ministry of Health.  Then, on October 19, 2021, the Government of Uganda received a second shipment of 700,000 Sinovac vaccine doses from the Chinese Government. These doses also arrived at the National Medical Store in Entebbe. First, 300,000 doses were to be released to administer to teachers who were due to receive their second dose. The remaining 400,000 doses were to be split into two groups, with half being used as first doses and the other half as second doses. Then, on December 20, 2021, 600,000 more doses of the Sinovac vaccine, donated by the Chinese government, arrived at the National Medical Store. This brought the grand total of Sinovac doses of donated by the Chinese Government to 1,600,000.

project_name: Company donated anti-epidemic med. supplies to Ministry of Health
description: On April 26, 2020, Hunan Constructing Engineering Group Co., Ltd. committed to donate 10,000 sets of medical protective clothing and 200,000 medical-grade masks to the Uganda's Ministry of Health. On June 30, 2020 the donation was handed over by Preparatory Office of the Uganda-Hunan Industrial Park (on behalf of the Hunan Constructing Engineering Group Co., Ltd.) and received by Dr. Diana Atwiinw of Uganda's Ministry of Health. The total value of the donated goods was $150,000 (RMB 1.23 = SHS 558 million).

project_name: Gov't donated 700,000 Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: On July 31, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 300,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Uganda’s Ministry of Health. The shipment had originally been promised by Yang Jiechi, Member of the Political Bureau of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) and Director of the Office of the Foreign Affairs Commission of the CPC Central Committee, on February 21, 2021, during a meeting he had with Ugandan President Museveni. The 300,000 doses arrived initially at National Medical Stores in Entebbe, about 40 km south of the capital of Kampala. From there, they were to be distributed to the population by the Ministry of Health.  Then, on October 19, 2021, the Government of Uganda received a second shipment of 700,000 Sinovac vaccine doses from the Chinese Government. These doses also arrived at the National Medical Store in Entebbe. First, 300,000 doses were to be released to administer to teachers who were due to receive their second dose. The remaining 400,000 doses were to be split into two groups, with half being used as first doses and the other half as second doses. Then, on December 20, 2021, 600,000 more doses of the Sinovac vaccine, donated by the Chinese government, arrived at the National Medical Store. This brought the grand total of Sinovac doses of donated by the Chinese Government to 1,600,000.

project_name: Company donated med. equipment to  friendship hospital
description: On August 21 , Jiangxi International Company donated a batch of medical equipment to Sino-Uganda Friendship Hospital.   According to the relevant agreement between the Chinese and Uganda governments, Jiangxi International Company is implementing the joint technical cooperation project of the government office of the Uganda government, the office building of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Sino-Uganda Friendship Hospital.

project_name: China donated anti-Malaria medicine to Uganda
description: On March 21, 2012, the Chinese Embassy signed a Letters of Exchange agreement on behalf of the Chinese government to donate anti-malaria drugs to Uganda.  The capacity and total cost of the donation are not known. As of 2010, China had made 4 similar donations, but it is not clear how many have been given since.

project_name: China donated 6,000 mosquito nets to Karamoja, Uganda
description: On September 6, 2016, Ambassador Zhao Yali, on behalf of the Chinese Embassy, ​​donated 6,000 mosquito nets to Karamoja Affairs Department. The Chinese side hoped that the donation would contribute to fight against malaria.

project_name: Gov't donated Covid testing kits & ventilators to the gov't
description: On September 23, 2020, an unspecified organization from within the Chinese Government handed over its third shipment of anti-epidemic supplies to the Government of Uganda to include COVID-19 testing kits and ventilators. At the handover ceremony, the two sides also signed an agreement for joint hospital cooperation in the fight against the pandemic.

project_name: ILD of the central committee donated Covid-19 supplies to NRM
description: On June 17, 2020, on behalf of the International Liaison Department of the CPC Central Committee, China's Ambassador to Uganda, Zheng Zhuqiang, handed over a shipment of anti-epidemic materials to the ruling party of Uganda, the National Resistance Movement (NRM). The NRM was represented at the hand-off ceremony by its Secretary-General, Justine Lumumba Kasule. The amount and exact contents of the donation are unknown.

project_name: China committed the donation of anti-Malaria drugs
description: On April 19, 2007, in accordance with an agreement signed on June 23, 2006, China handed over anti-malaria drugs worth 2 million RMB to the Uganda Ministry of Health. The anti-malaria drugs were provided by Beijing Holley-Cotec Pharmaceuticals Co., Ltd. Between 2007 and 2009, the Chinese government donated anti-malaria medicine worth US$500,000 per annum through the ministry of health.

project_name: Gov't donated anti-Malarial medicine, equipment, & supplies
description: In 2013, the Chinese Government signed agreements to deliver anti-malaria supplies to Uganda. On June 20, 2014, the handover ceremony of medical equipment and antimalarial medicines aided by the Chinese government to the Uganda government was held at the Kampala Naguru China-Ukraine Friendship Hospital.  The Chinese Ambassador to Uganda, Zhao Yali, attended the event and signed the "China Aid Uganda Anti-malarial Center Medical Equipment" and Material Handover Certificate" and "China’s 2013 Aid to Uganda Antimalarial Drug Handover Certificate".  The Minister of Health of the Uzbek Government and other officials from the Ministry of Health also attended the ceremony.

project_name: Embassy donated covid supplies to friendship school in Kanungu
description: In November 2021, the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in Uganda donated to the China-Uganda Friendship School a shipment of materials including hand sanitizers, hand sprayers, disinfectants, soaps, thermometers, and masks.   The monetary value of this donation is unclear.

project_name: Gov't grants $435,476.85 for health sector activities
description: On April 28, 2009, the Chinese Government committed a grant worth $435,476.85 to the Government of Uganda. This grant is provided for general health sector activities. According to the Aid Management Platform (AMP) of the Government of Uganda's Ministry of Finance, Planning, and Economic Development, this grant has been fully disbursed.

project_name: China donated anti-Malaria drugs
description: During the Forum of China-Africa Co-operation Summit (FOCAC) held in November 2006, the Chinese government committed to providing a first batch of anti-malarial drugs worth approximately US $250,000 to the Uganda Ministry of Health. The actual commitment was made on June 23, 2006. The Ugandan government records the actual disbursement as US $253,285.74, a total of two disbursements made in 2006 and 2007, respectively. This donation was also part of the three-day anti-malarial program held in Kampala (#34837). The batch was delivered in 2 segments: one on August 11, 2006 and the other on April 24, 2007.   This project is linked to #63793, which details all of the malaria-related projects in Uganda funded by China.

project_name: Donation of us $400,000-worth anti-Malaria drugs batch 1
description: On January 18, 2010, the Chinese government donated over 244,000 doses of anti-malarial drugs worth 400,000 USD to Uganda. China's ambassador to Uganda, Sun Heping, handed over the donation of 144,000 doses of Arco and 100,000 doses of Duo-Cotexin to Richard Nduhuura, State Minister for General Duties in the Health Ministry.

project_name: China committed the donation of anti-Malaria drugs
description: On July 25, 2007, the Chinese government agreed to donate anti-malaria drugs worth 3,000,000 RMB to the Uganda Ministry of Health. On April 29, 2008, China handed over the anti-malaria drugs to Richard Nduhura, Uganda's Health Minister. The anti-malaria drugs were provided by Beijing Holley-Cotec Pharmaceuticals Co., Ltd. and Kunming Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd. Between 2007 and 2009, the Chinese government donated anti-malaria medicine worth US $500,000 per annum through the ministry of health. This donation comes as a part of a Chinese initiative meant to help reduce the number of cases of malaria in Uganda.

project_name: China donated med. supplies to friendship hospital
description: On April 17, 2019, the Chinese Embassy donated medical supplies worth USD 100,000 to the Ugandan government. The handover ceremony took place at the China-Uganda Friendship Hospital in Naguru, which is located within Kampala, Uganda. This hospital was built with Chinese aid in 2008 (project #12177)  China's agreement to send medical teams to Uganda every year also comes with donations of medical equipment.

project_name: Gov't grants $598,175.56 for health sector activities
description: On October 25, 2010, the Chinese Government committed a grant worth $598,175.56 to the Government of Uganda. This grant is provided for general health sector activities. According to the Aid Management Platform (AMP) of the Government of Uganda's Ministry of Finance, Planning, and Economic Development, this grant has been fully disbursed.

project_name: Gov't provided the 4th batch of Covid testing kits to the gov't
description: On April 14, 2021, China handed over the fourth batch of anti-epidemic supplies to the Government of Uganda. Chinese Ambassador to Uganda Zheng Zhuqiang and Ugandan Minister of Health Azeng attended the handover ceremony at the Ministry of Health of Uganda. This donation includes new coronavirus nucleic acid detection reagents (COVID-19 testing kits).   China's first donation of anti-epidemic medical supplies to Uganda arrived on April 28, 2020, and was captured via Project #92846. The Government of China's second donation of anti-epidemic medical supplies to Uganda arrived on July 15, 2020, and was captured via Project #94681. The Government of China's third donation of anti-epidemic medical supplies to Uganda arrived on September 23, 2020, and was captured via Project #94682.

project_name: Corporation donated mosquito nets to UPDF & 2 schools
description: On April 8, 2016, the ribbon-cutting ceremony of the mosquito repellent net factory jointly established by China-Africa Medical Materials Co., Ltd (中非医用材料有限公司) and Tianjin Yongkuo International Trade Co., Ltd.(天津永阔国际贸易有限公司) was held in Kampala. At the ceremony, the mosquito net factory also donated 1200 long-lasting mosquito repellent nets to the UPDF and the two schools.

project_name: Embassy donated 2 ambulances to the gov't of Uganda
description: In early April 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Uganda donated a pair of ambulances to the Ugandan Government in order to support its fight against the COVID-19 pandemic.

project_name: Gov't donated 600,000 Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: On July 31, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 300,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Uganda’s Ministry of Health. The shipment had originally been promised by Yang Jiechi, Member of the Political Bureau of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) and Director of the Office of the Foreign Affairs Commission of the CPC Central Committee, on February 21, 2021, during a meeting he had with Ugandan President Museveni. The 300,000 doses arrived initially at National Medical Stores in Entebbe, about 40 km south of the capital of Kampala. From there, they were to be distributed to the population by the Ministry of Health.  Then, on October 19, 2021, the Government of Uganda received a second shipment of 700,000 Sinovac vaccine doses from the Chinese Government. These doses also arrived at the National Medical Store in Entebbe. First, 300,000 doses were to be released to administer to teachers who were due to receive their second dose. The remaining 400,000 doses were to be split into two groups, with half being used as first doses and the other half as second doses. Then, on December 20, 2021, 600,000 more doses of the Sinovac vaccine, donated by the Chinese government, arrived at the National Medical Store. This brought the grand total of Sinovac doses of donated by the Chinese Government to 1,600,000.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for construction of Malaria center at hospital
description: In January 2008, Dr. James Tibenderana, director of the Uganda Malaria Research Center, announced that China would build a malaria treatment and prevention center attached to the Mulago Referral Hospital worth 700 million UGX. Then, on May 1, 2008, the Chinese Government committed $429,000 for the construction of the center. The official handover ceremony was held on May 15, 2008.

project_name: China donated over 7,000 med. beds & mattresses
description: January 2016, China donated to Uganda Ministry of Health over 7,000 medical beds and mattresses worth about 6 million U.S. dollars. The donations have been distributed to health facilities across Uganda. According to the Ugandan Ministry of Health, each major hospital will receive about 100 mattresses while a county-level health center will receive 24 mattresses. The donations will enable the government to meet all the needs for beds and mattresses in general hospitals and county-level health centers around the country. Specific funding Chinese organization is unknown.

project_name: China donated hospital supplies to a church hospital in Ibanda, Uganda
description: On May 31 2015, Chinese Ambassador Zhao Yali went to Ibanda Regional Church hospital in the Ibanda area, and donated some hospital equipment in partnership with the Ugandan Golf Club. The equipment included a blood testing machine, 50 mattresses, and contributed 16m shs/UGX towards the construction of a laboratory.

project_name: Jiangxi international donated covid aid
description: On April 22nd, 2020, China Jiangxi International Economic and Technical Cooperation Co. Ltd., a Chinese contractor, donated 50,000 pieces of surgical masks, 1,000 sets of medical protective suits and 50 pieces of infrared thermometers to Zambia. Olipa Phiri, Minister in the Office of the Vice-President expressed thanks to the Chinese firm. The purpose of this donation is to help Zambia fight against the pandemic.

project_name: Embassy provide 20,000 masks to university of Zambia
description: On June 4, 2021, the Jilin Province of China and the Chinese Embassy jointly donated medical masks to the University of Zambia. The total number of masks provided was 50,000. The Jilin Province provided 30,000 masks while the Chinese Embassy provided 20,000 masks. These masks will be used to improve COVID-19 response efforts by the University of Zambia, the largest public university in the country. Masks will be distributed among students and faculty in the university. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation in Lusaka, Zambia. Li Jie, China’s Ambassador to Zambia, and Professor Luke Mumba, the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Zambia, attended the ceremony. Chinese and Zambian directors of the Confucius Institute at the University of Zambia also attended the ceremony.   Jilin Province's contribution to this donation is captured in Project ID#98594.

project_name: Avic donated thermal scanner to Ndola to prevent the spread of Ebola
description: On 18 September 2014, AVIC International donated an infrared fever-sensing thermal scanner to Zambia, which was installed at Simon Mwansa Kapwepwe International Airport in Ndola. The purpose of this donation was to prevent the Ebola virus from spreading to Zambia.  A similar donation was made to the Kenneth Kaunda International Airport in Lusaka ( see project ID#40923).

project_name: Avic international donated thermal scanner to Zambia to prevent Ebola
description: On September 18, 2014, Health Minister Joseph Kasonde declared the launch of the US$30,000 worth Thermal Scanner donated by AVIC International at Kenneth Kaunda International Airport in Lusaka. The minister said Zambia had no reason not to succeed in the fight against Ebola as the country had put the necessary preventive measures in place. Dr Kasonde said Zambia was benefiting from China in strengthening the health system against the deadly virus, among other conditions. Chinese Ambassador to Zambia Yang Youming said the donation was worth celebrating as the Thermal Scanner would come in handy in the fight against Ebola and that AVIC International's gesture was a demonstration of the friendship from the Chinese community in Zambia. AVIC International civilian representative Xu Fei said the Kenneth Kaunda International Airport donation had brought the total Thermal Scanners donation cost to $60,000 following a similar donation at Simon Mwansa Kapwepwe International Airport in Ndola.  This project is linked to #40924.

project_name: Gov't agrees to donate med. equipment to Kitwe central hospital
description: In 2005, the Chinese Government agreed to donate medical equipment to Kitwe Central Hospital. It is unclear if the Chinese Government followed through on this commitment. The value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: ICBC provided loan for hospital construction & associated works
description: On December 21, 2015, the Government of Zambia and ICBC signed a $135,806,251.37 commercial loan agreement for the Hospital Construction and Associated Works Project. The proceeds of the loan were to be used by the borrower to finance 85% of the cost of a $159 million commercial contract between the Government of Zambia and China National Complete Engineering Corporation (CNCEC), which was signed in November 2014 and amended in February 2015. The Government of Zambia agreed to cover the remaining 15% of the commercial contract cost. The borrowing terms of the loan are unknown. However, Sinosure apparently provided a credit insurance policy.   The project involved the construction of Lusaka Specialised Hospital, the Chinsali General Hospital, and the Petuake General Hospital.  The Chinsali General Hospital Construction Project involved the construction of a provincial general hospital in the town of Chinsali with 102 doctors’ residences, 4 dormitories for nurses, a nurse training school; and the procurement and installation of medical equipment, furnitures, appliances, teaching facilities and office equipment. Petuake General Hospital is located in the town of Petauke. Lusaka Specialised Hospital is located in Chongwe district near Kenneth Kaunda International Airport (on Kenneth Kaunda International Airport Road).  On August 23, 2016, Zambia’s Ministry of Construction handed over the project site to CNCEC for preparatory work. Then, on October 26, 2016, Zambia’s Ministry of Finance made a 15% advance payment (worth approximately $24 million dollars) to CNCEC.   Construction began in June 2017. However, a formal groundbreaking ceremony (for the construction of the Lusaka Specialised Hospital) did not take place until October 17, 2017.  By May 2018, the project had achieved a 40% completion rate. Then, on October 10, 2019, a medical equipment delivery ceremony was held.  The project was originally scheduled to reach completion by May 2020. As of May 19, 2020, the Chinsali General Hospital and Petuake General Hospital were already in use; however, the specialized hospital in Lusaka was still being constructed at that time. The Lusaka Specialised Hospital was put into use on June 5, 2021.

project_name: Gov't donated 100,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021 and 2022, the Chinese Government donated approximately 600,000 doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Zambia. The Chinese Government delivered 100,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Zambia on May 31, 2021. Then, on August 9, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 100,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines as well as 102,400 syringes to the Government of Zambia. Li Jie, the Chinese Ambassador to Zambia, attended the vaccine handover ceremony and delivered a speech. The aid package was meant to help the Government of Zambia combat its third wave of COVID-19. The Chinese Government delivered an additional 400,000 donated Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Zambia on January 24, 2022.

project_name: Gov't grants funds for provision of military & med. equipment
description: On September 25th, 2013, the Chinese government signed a grant agreement providing $8 million USD (42.2 million ZK) to the Government of Zambia in the form of medical and military equipment to be used to upgrade military hospitals countrywide. Chinese Ambassador to Zambia Zhou Yuxiao explained that the delivery of the equipment would occur in three phases over the course of three years. It is unclear whether these goods were ever delivered.

project_name: China donated equipment to endoscopy center at hospital
description: In May 2017, at the 70th World Health Assembly, the Chinese Government and the Government of Zambia signed a hospital cooperation agreement (Chinese name: 建立对口医院合作关系的协议), which granted 6.99 million RMB for constructing the China-Zambia Endoscopy Unit at Levy Mwanawasa Hospital (#57325). First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University was responsible for training 5 Zambian hospital staff (#85187), installing endoscopic equipment worth 3 million ZMK, and other related related operations. The equipment was delivered on August 8, 2018, when Chinese and Zambian officials held a launching ceremony to mark the beginning of the the operations of the center.

project_name: Eximbank provided gov't concessional loan for mobile hospital project
description: In 2010, China Eximbank and the Zambia Ministry of Finance signed an RMB 361 million (USD $53 million) government concessional loan (GCL) agreement for the Mobile Hospital Project. The GCL carried the following terms: 15 year maturity, 5 year grace period, 2% interest rate, 0.075% commitment fee, and 1% management fee.   This project supported the acquisition of 9 sets of mobile hospitals and 150 emergency ambulances. One mobile hospital was assigned to each of country’s 9 provinces. Each mobile hospital included a fleet of seven vehicles, including an operating theater, a laboratory, an X-ray unit, and a pharmacy vehicle. Each mobile hospital had at least 35 health workers, including a surgeon, physician, anesthetist, pharmacist, dentist, eye specialist, nurses, and laboratory technologists. Once the mobile hospitals arrived in a given location, they provided curative healthcare services for 7 days.   The purpose of Mobile Hospital Project was to facilitate the purchase of medical facilities, spare parts, and medical consumables, and provide relevant trainings and services. Its ultimate objective was to provide equitable access to quality healthcare to the people in remote and hard-to-reach areas. China National Aero-Technology Import and Export Corporation (CATIC), which was later renamed AVIC International, was the contractor responsible for project implementation. This project was completed when all mobile hospitals became operational in 2011. Then, between 2011 and 2013, AVIC International provided free support and maintenance for the mobile hospitals as part of its sale contract. By 2014, the mobile medical service had reached 9 provinces, 76 regions, and 491,120 patients. It had also performed 25,611 surgeries.

project_name: Gov't signs economic & tech coop agreement granting for Malaria drugs
description: In November 2006, the Chinese Government signed an economic and technical cooperation agreement (ETCA) granting RMB 1.5 million to the Government of Zambia in order to purchase anti-malaria drugs. This batch of drugs was successfully delivered sometime in 2006 but the exact date of delivery is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donated batch of anti-Malarial supplies
description: On December 29, 2011, the Chinese Government and the Government Zambia signed three letters of exchange, one of which was for the donation of a batch of anti-malarial supplies worth 1.5 billion kwacha to Chainama Hills College Hospital. This batch of anti-malarial supplies was officially delivered and handed over to the authorities on September 17, 2013.   The two other letters of exchange that were signed are captured in projects #2337 and #15518.

project_name: Gov't donated for improvements to Kabwe Central hospital
description: In December 2018, the Chinese Government granted $80,000 USD for improvements, new equipment, and other infrastructure in order to upgrade Kabwe Central Hospital's status to a Central Hospital. The funds were said to be mobilized from Zambia-based Chinese companies as part of their corporate social responsibility. Upgrading and expanding the hospital will prepare it to better address the population's needs. (CHINA DONATES $80,000 TO KABWE HOSPITAL FACE LIFT)  The exact handover date is unknown.

project_name: Gov't donated 100,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021 and 2022, the Chinese Government donated approximately 600,000 doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Zambia. The Chinese Government delivered 100,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Zambia on May 31, 2021. Then, on August 9, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 100,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines as well as 102,400 syringes to the Government of Zambia. Li Jie, the Chinese Ambassador to Zambia, attended the vaccine handover ceremony and delivered a speech. The aid package was meant to help the Government of Zambia combat its third wave of COVID-19. The Chinese Government delivered an additional 400,000 donated Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Zambia on January 24, 2022.

project_name: China trains Zambian personnel for endoscopy center at hospital
description: In May 2017, at the 70th World Health Assembly, the Chinese Government and the Government of Zambia signed a hospital cooperation agreement (Chinese name: 建立对口医院合作关系的协议), which granted 6.99 million RMB for constructing the China-Zambia Endoscopy Unit at Levy Mwanawasa Hospital (#57325). First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University was responsible for training 5 Zambian hospital staff, installing endoscopic equipment (#85188), and other related related operations. It is unclear exactly when this training took place. On August 8, 2018, Chinese and Zambian officials held a launching ceremony to mark the beginning of the the operations of the center.

project_name: Jilin province provided 30,000 masks to University of Zambia
description: On June 4, 2021, the Jilin Province of China and the Chinese Embassy jointly donated medical masks to the University of Zambia. The total number of masks provided was 50,000. The Jilin Province provided 30,000 masks while the Chinese Embassy provided 20,000 masks. These masks will be used to improve COVID-19 response efforts by the University of Zambia, the largest public university in the country. Masks will be distributed among students and faculty in the university. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation in Lusaka, Zambia. Li Jie, China’s Ambassador to Zambia, and Professor Luke Mumba, the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Zambia, attended the ceremony. Chinese and Zambian directors of the Confucius Institute at the University of Zambia also attended the ceremony.  The Chinese Embassy's contribution to this donation is captured in Project ID#92881.

project_name: Gov't grants for construction of endoscopy center at hospital
description: In May 2017, at the 70th World Health Assembly, the Chinese Government and the Government of Zambia signed a hospital cooperation agreement (Chinese name: 建立对口医院合作关系的协议), which granted 6.99 million RMB for constructing the China-Zambia Endoscopy Unit (Chinese project name: 中赞腔镜中心) at Levy Mwanawasa Hospital. First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University was responsible for project implementation including personnel training (#85187) and donating equipment (#85188). On August 8, 2018, Chinese and Zambian officials held a launching ceremony to mark the beginning of the the operations of the center.

project_name: Gov't grants for levy Mwanawasa hospital expansion project
description: In 2016, at the Summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation in Johannesburg, the Chinese Government agreed to finance the Levy Mwanawasa Hospital Expansion Project (Chinese project name: 赞比亚利维·姆瓦纳瓦萨综合医院扩建). Then, during State Councilor Wang Yong's visit to Zambia in June 2017, government officials signed Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) granting 200 million RMB for this project. The Chinese govenment reportedly contributed a total of 400 million RMB to the Levy Mwanawasa Hospital Expansion Project so it is unclear when they provided the remaining 200 million RMB.   The purpose of this project was to increase the number of beds at Levy Mwanawasa Hospital (previously called Lusaka General Hospital the China-Zambia Friendship Hospital) from 150 to 850 and equip the hospital with modern technology. The total construction area was approximately 50,000 square meters, and the project included the construction of a  including out-patient department, emergency department, medical technology service, inpatient department, administrative and scientific research area and logistics service area.   China IPPR International Engineering Co., Ltd. — a subsidiary of CAMCE — was the contractor responsible for project design.  Shanxi Construction Engineering Group was the contractor responsible for project implementation. Construction began on  May 12, 2017. Then, a groundbreaking ceremony was held on June 6, 2017. The originally anticipated project completion date was November 12, 2020 but the project was not handed over to Zambia’s Ministry of Health until March 25, 2020.   The Chinese Government also provided a grant in 2009 for construction work at Levy Mwanawasa Hospital (when it was still called Lusaka General Hospital), which is captured in project #32627.

project_name: Gov't grants for provision of med. equipment & supplies to hospital
description: On December 29, 2011, the Chinese Government and Government Zambia signed 3 letters of exchange, one of which was for the provision of extra medical equipment and supplies to the Levy Mwanawasa General Hospital worth RMB 10 million. This donation was officially handed over to Zambian authorities on September 17, 2013.  The two other letters of exchange that were signed are captured in projects #15507 and #15518.

project_name: Gov't provided USD 487,917 to support Covid-19 via WHO
description: In March 2020, Chinese government provides USD 487,917 to support WHO response to COVID-19 outbreak in Zambia.

project_name: Gov't donated eye surgery equip to University Teaching Hospital
description: On December 23, 2019, Counsellor Ouyang Daobing handed over modern eye surgery equipment to Prof. Elwyn Chomba and Dr. Kennedy Malama for use at Levy Mwanawasa University Teaching Hospital (LMUTH) in Lusaka, Zambia. The donation was held at the Chinese Embassy in Zambia. LMUTH's website records the value of the donation as equivalent to 3 million Zambian Kwacha. The equipment was donated as a part of the 2019 "Bright Journey" (which is also sometimes translated as "Bright Action") program, under which Chinese doctors had been conducting eye surgery operations at LMUTH for the previous two weeks.

project_name: Party donated med. materials to patriotic front party to combat Covid
description: On June 30, 2020, the Communist Party of China (CPC) donated various medical supplies to Zambia's governing party, the Patriotic Front (PF), as part of efforts to help the country tackle the COVID-19 pandemic. The donated items included 30,000 surgical face masks, 500 protective clothing and 240 thermometers. The PF then passed many of the materials onto churches, which operate schools and hospitals.   The materials were donated to the Patriotic Front on behalf of the CPC International Department by the Chinese Embassy in Zambia. The purpose of this donation is to help Zambia fight against the pandemic. The PF was Zambia's ruling party from 2016-2021.

project_name: Gov't grants for Lusaka general hospital construction project
description: According to the 2009 and 2010 editions of the Government of Zambia’s Development Cooperation Reports, in 2009, the Chinese government disbursed $4.5 million USD of grant funding for the Lusaka General Hospital Construction Project. The hospital is also known as the China-Zambia Friendship Hospital or Levy Mwanawasa University Teaching Hospital.   China Jiangsu International Economic and Technical Cooperation was the contractor responsible for project implementation. Construction started on October 29, 2009 and ended on July 30, 2011. A project completion ceremony was held in Lusaka on August 8, 2011.   This project involved the construction of a hospital with 159 beds and CT, X-ray, and surgery units. Lusaka General Hospital rests on 1.84 hectare of land along Great East road in Lusaka. It has floor space of approximately 7,472 square meters. By 2013, the hospital was reportedly treating 2,600 patients and delivering 260 babies each month, on average. Of its 455 staff, eleven were Chinese and all were from Henan province. They included five surgeons, two radiologists, a gynecologist, anesthetist, a nurse, and interpreter.  In 2016, the Chinese Government provided an additional grant worth RMB 400 million for expanding the same hospital (project #40727).

project_name: Co., ltd  grants funds for the nachitete hospital construction project
description: In 2016, Mpande Limestone Ltd. — a subsidiary of Chinese state-owned Sinoma Cement Co., Ltd. and project company that was created to design, finance, and implement China Development Bank-financed Sinoma Zambia Building Materials Industrial Park Project in Zambia (#72642) — spent a total of $1.21 million USD for the Nachitete Primary School and Hospital Construction Project. The school cost $410,000 USD (#85243) and the hospital cost $800,000 USD .  The hospital can hold 3,000 patients. Mpande Limestone Ltd. was responsible for project implementation. Construction started on September 1, 2016, and ended on February 1, 2017.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for Malaria prevention & treatment center project
description: In November 2006, the Chinese Government agreed to provide a grant to the Government of Zambia for the construction of a China-Zambia Malaria Prevention and Treatment Centre at the Chainama Hills College Hospital. The value of this project is unknown.   The contractor responsible for project implementation was Jiangxi Construction Engineering Co. (江西建工公司). Construction ended in January 2009 and the official handover ceremony took place on June 26, 2009.  Four Chinese experts subsequently helped set up and test the facilities, exchange ideas with local specialists and provide technical training to 20 medical staff.

project_name: Sichuan times tech donated med. supplies to the angel of hope fund
description: On April 21, 2020, Counselor Wang Wei, the wife of China’s Ambassador to Zimbabwe, attended the handover ceremony for materials donated by Sichuan Times Technology Co., Ltd., and Huawei to the "Angel of Hope Fund" in Zimbabwe. The donated materials included 50,000 masks, 510 protective suits & 1,000 goggles. Huawei reportedly contributed 30,000 masks. The First Lady of Zimbabwe, Auxillia Mnangagwa, and representatives of Sichuan PD Times Technology, Huawei, and Zimbabwe National also attended the event.

project_name: Embassy donated masks to union of journalists in Mashonaland West
description: During the last week of January in 2021, the Chinese Embassy donated 10 boxes of surgical masks to media houses and at least 35 practicing journalists in Mashonaland West province, Zimbabwe. The Zimbabwe Union of Journalists (ZUJ) Mashonaland West chapter sourced the masks. The donation is expected to protect journalists working on the frontline to help disseminate COVID-19 information.

project_name: Gov't donated cataract surgery equipment to central hospital
description: On March 30, 2011, Chinese Ambassador, Xin Shunkang, handed over to President Mugabe cataract equipment that was used by Chinese eye doctors to carry out cataract surgeries. Hainan Airlines and Anhui Foreign Economic Construction Group (FECC) funded the cataract surgeries recorded in linked project #22026. This linked project also records the financial flows associated with the cost of the surgeries themselves. The exact value of this donation is unknown.

project_name: Sinohydro donated masks to Matabeleland North Province
description: On May 19, 2020, Sinohydro donated ZWL 1.5 million and 15,000 face masks to Matabeleland North province. The Matabeleland North provincial affairs minister Richard Moyo received the donation from Sino Hydro site manager for Hwange, Tang Zhaolai at the Hwange Five Miles Hospital. Sino Hydro's contract work in Hwange includes the Hwange power station Unit 7 and 8 expansion project in partnership with the Zimbabwe Power Company (ZPC).

project_name: Gov't provided medicines & med. equipment to friendship hospital
description: On 7 July, 2010, the Chinese Government signed an agreement to provide $1.5 million USD worth of medical equipment and drugs to the China-Zimbabwe Friendship Hospital in Mahusekwa, Mashonland East.  The Government of China was represented by Vice Minister, Jiang Zengwei, and the Government of Zimbabwe was represented by Minister of Health and Child Welfare, Henry Madzorera.  It should be noted that the very same hospital receiving the medial equipment and drugs was constructed using Chinese funds: further details are captured in linked projects #20443 (Phase I) and #72842 (Phase II). The linked project #26668 captures how the Chinese Government announced plans to donate $10 million USD worth of additional medical equipment to the China-Zimbabwe Friendship Hospital in October 2010.

project_name: Donated monitoring equip, water purification drugs, & supplies
description: On 18 November, 2013, a group of medical experts to Zimbabwe donated a batch of medical supplies through the local NGO Women Unlimited to the community of Epworth.  The supplies include blood pressure monitoring equipment, blood sugar monitor, water purification drugs, and disinfection supplies. The value of this donation is unknown. The linked project #35655 captures the dispatch of China's 13th medical team.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for pharmaceutical warehouse construction project
description: On December 1, 2015, the Chinese Government and the Government of Zimbabwe signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA), which committed RMB 400 million for several projects (captured via Project ID#72821). RMB 90 million was earmarked from the ETCA for the initial preparatory works associated with the National Pharmaceutical Warehouse Construction Project. However, China's Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) ultimately provided $24 million of grant funding for the project, which involved the construction of a warehouse that can accommodate 22,000 pallets of medicines. At the time, the country's existing warehouse of the National Pharmaceutical Company (NatPharm) — Zimbabwe's national drug procurer — could accommodate 9 pallets of medicines.  This project encountered various delays, one of which was disagreement over the  location of the warehouse.  This disagreement was solved by determining that the warehouse would be built in the originally planned location of Harare. Project implementation began in August 2019, and it was expected to end within two years (August 2021). The construction of the warehouse -- at the Sally Mugabe Central Hospital in Harare -- was ultimately completed in June 2022. An official handover ceremony took place in October 2022.

project_name: Chinese-Zimbabwean hospitals to be twinned
description: In 2010, China agreed to 'twin' Chitungwiza Central Hospital with a hospital in China. Health professionals from the two institutions will participate in exchange programs. The development comes from the success of the Brightness Journey, a program where three Chinese eye specialists conducted free cataract removing surgeries at the Chitungwiza Hospital. Further details were not found. This is related to projects ID#823 and ID#22026.

project_name: Gov't donated Ureteroscope equipment to Parirenyatwa Hospital
description: On 10 October, 2012, the 12th Chinese medical team handed over ureteroscope equipment worth $50,000 USD to Parirenyatwa Hospital and the University of Zimbabwe School of Medicine. The dispatch of the 12th Chinese medical team to Zimbabwe is captured in the linked project #22506. This project is completed.

project_name: Gov't provided USD 1,069,750 for wash project via UN children's fund
description: In December 2020, Chinese government provides USD 1,069,750 for WASH project via United Nations Children's Fund in Zimbabwe.

project_name: Gov't donated 200,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021 and 2022, the Chinese Government donated approximately 7 million doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Zimbabwe. The Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Zimbabwe on February 15, 2021 (Project ID#95670). Then, on March 16, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered another 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Zimbabwe (Project ID#95671). The People’s Liberation Army (PLA) of China delivered an additional 100,000 donated Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses to the Zimbabwe Defence Forces on May 17, 2021 (Project ID#95672). Then, on September 26, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered another 500,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Zimbabwe (Project ID#95673). Several months later, on December 20, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 1 million donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Zimbabwe (Project ID#95674). Then, on November 25, 2022, the Government of Zimbabwe received another shipment of 3 million donated Sinopharm vaccine doses from the Chinese Government (Project ID#95675). At a formal handover ceremony, Chinese Ambassador to Zimbabwe Guo Shaochun delivered the donation on behalf of Peng Liyuan, the wife of Chinese President Xi Jinping, for the women, children and teenagers of Zimbabwe to Auxillia Mnangagwa, the wife of Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa.

project_name: China donated med. equipment to the maternal & child health project
description: On May 7, 2019, the China Hunan Maternity and Child Care Centers held a ceremony for the launch of Phase 3 of the Maternal and Child Health Innovation Project for the Parirenyatwa Hospital in Harare, Zimbabwe (中国援津“妇幼健康”创新工程宫颈疾病预防和设备捐赠第三期). In Phase 3, Hunan Maternity and Child Care Centers sent 8 experts, provided treatment of cervical cancer for 1,000 women for free, and donated 500,000 RMB of medical equipment to Zimbabwe. Chinese Ambassador to Zimbabwe Guo Shaochun, First Lady of Zimbabwe Oxelia Mnangagwa, Minister of Health and Child Care Moyo, Chinese Economic and Commercial Counsellor in Zimbabwe Chen Ning, and the project implementation unit attended the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't provided funds for the nutrition project via UN children's fund
description: In December 2020, Chinese government provides USD 135,000 for the nutrition project via United Nations Children's Fund in Zimbabwe.

project_name: Gov't donated diagnostic tools to chitungwiza central hospital
description: On March 28, 2011, the Sally Mugabe Renal Training Institute at Chitungwiza Central Hospital opened. China had donated state-of-the-art chemistry analyzers to carry out diagnostic tests at this Renal Training Institute. Contacts for this project include President Mugabe and Chitungwiza Central Hospital's Chief Executive Officer, Dr. Obadiah Moyo. The amount of tests donated and their value are uncertain. This project is completed.

project_name: Eximbank provided buyer credit loan for med. equip & supplies project
description: On March 21, 2011, China Eximbank and the Government of Zimbabwe signed a $89,955,000 buyer’s credit loan (BCL) agreement for the Medical Equipment and Supplies Project. This loan carries the following borrowing terms: an 11 year maturity (final maturity date: 2022), a 4 year grace period, an interest rate of 6-month LIBOR plus a 3% margin, a 0.375% management fee, and a 0.375% commitment fee. It is backed by a Sinosure credit insurance policy.   This project involved the acquisition of NMR, CT, digital X-ray machines, ultrasound machines, anesthesia machines, incubators, medical carts, ambulances, and mobile clinic buses. China Machinery Engineering Corporation (CMEC) was the contractor responsible for implementation of the project. The equipment was officially commissioned and handed over to the authorities at the Harare Central Hospital on March 5, 2015.    However, there are signs that the China Eximbank loan contracted by the Government of Zimbabwe for the Medical Equipment and Supplies Project has underperformed financially. As of 2018, the borrower had accumulated principal and interest arrears and penalties worth $31,729,633.19. According to a report released by the Debt Management Office of Zimbabwe’s Ministry of Finance in mid-2022, the loan was still in arrears at the end of 2021. By the end of 2021, total external debt arrears to China Eximbank included $13 million for the NetOne Expansion Phase 1 Project, $47 million for the NetOne Expansion Phase 2 Project, $67 million for the Rehabilitation of Municipal Water and Sewage Treatment Works Project (City of Harare Project), $7 million for the National Defence College Project, $54 million for the Victoria Falls Airport Renovation and Expansion Project, $3 million for the Robert G. Mugabe International Airport Expansion Project, $0.5 million for Phase 2 of the TelOne Broadband Expansion Project, and $73 million for the Medical Equipment and Supplies Project. The loan’s amount outstanding (including principal, interest, and arrears) was $87,383,270.54 as of September 2021.

project_name: Gov't provided grant for the friendship hospital construction project
description: During the 2006 Forum on China-Africa Co-operation in Beijing, the Chinese Government agreed in principle to construct a China-Zimbabwe Friendship Hospital in Mahusekwa District and Mashonaland East Province (approximately 70 km east of Harare). Then, in 2009, the Chinese Government and the Government of Zimbabwe signed an RMB 70 million grant agreement for Phase 1 of the China-Zimbabwe Friendship Hospital Construction Project.   Phase 1 involved the construction and furnishing of a 17,000 square meter hospital with 129 beds. It also involved the construction of one block of 2-story outpatient and emergency treatment facilities, two blocks of 2-story buildings for inpatient treatment, the installation of a hospital canteen, a substation and generator room. Nantong Construction Group Co., Ltd. was the contractor responsible for implementation of Phase 1. A groundbreaking ceremony took place October 30, 2010, and the hospital was opened and handed over to the Zimbabwean authorities on September 21, 2012. The hospital was officially commissioned in 2013. Project ID#20443 captures Phase 1.   In 2017, the Chinese Government and the Government of Zimbabwe signed a grant agreement for Phase 2 of the China-Zimbabwe Friendship Hospital Construction Project. Phase 2 involved the installation of a mortuary and incinerator room, concrete water tower, borehole, access roads, and a parking lot. The monetary value of the grant provided for Phase 2 is unknown.   China Railway Sixth Group was the contractor responsible for the project's implementation.   The hospital was intended to be handed over to Zimbabwe's Ministry of Health and Child Welfare. This phase of the project began on January 17, 2018 and ended on February 28, 2019. An official project handover ceremony for Phase 2 took place on November 16, 2019.

project_name: Gansu province donated med. supplies to West Mashonaland Province
description: On May 6, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Zimbabwe held a handover ceremony for the donation of epidemic prevention and control materials from the Gansu Province to the West Mashonaland Province of Zimbabwe. The Gansu provincial government thanked Gansu Construction Investment, China Gansu International and Hualong Group for their cooperation and support in putting together the donation. The donation included 12,000 face masks, and 1,000 protective suits. China’s Ambassador to Zimbabwe, Guo Shaochun, the Governor of West Mashonaland, the Chairman of Hualong Group, and various other Zimbabwean government officials attended the ceremony.

project_name: Gov't donated 1st batch of anti-epidemic supplies
description: On April 23, 2020, the Chinese Embassy donated a first batch of COVID-19 supplies which included 166,000 masks, 7,600 protective suits, 20,000 test kits, 12,000 pairs of gloves, and five ventilators to Zimbabwe. The donation ceremony was held in Harare with the Chinese ambassador to Zimbabwe and the President of Zimbabwe present.

project_name: Hongyu enterprises provided grant for establishment of med. center
description: On July 23, 2020, the Health Point Upper East Medical Center (HPUEMC) officially opened. Hongyu Enterprises, Jin'an Corporation, and China Mingchang Engineering Corporation partnered with Health Point, a private medical institution to establish the COVID-19 treatment and isolation facility. The three companies together donated 3,000,000 USD for the facility and equipment. The center is a private hospital and has the capacity to accommodate up to 50 COVID-19 patients.  In addition to providing quality health care to COVID-19 patients, the new facility will also provide training to other medical institutions in the country.

project_name: Gov't donated 2nd batch of anti-epidemic materials
description: On June 11, 2020, a handover ceremony was held for the donation of a second batch of anti-epidemic materials from the Chinese government to Zimbabwe. The ceremony was held at the Presidential Palace in Zimbabwe where the two sides signed the handover certificate of donated materials and received the materials on site. The second batch of assistance included 165,000 surgical masks and more than 25,000 pieces of personal protective equipment.  China’s Ambassador to Zimbabwe, Guo Shaochun, President Mnangagwa of Zimbabwe, Head of Zimbabwe's Anti-Epidemic Working Group, National Chairman of Zimbabwe’s Democratic League, Minister of Foreign Affairs, Minister of Local Government, and the Minister of Health attended the ceremony.

project_name: Jin'an corporation provided grant for establishment of med. center
description: On July 23, 2020, the Health Point Upper East Medical Center (HPUEMC) officially opened. Hongyu Enterprises, Jin'an Corporation, and China Mingchang Engineering Corporation partnered with Health Point, a private medical institution to establish the COVID-19 treatment and isolation facility. The three companies together donated 3,000,000 USD for the facility and equipment. The center is a private hospital and has the capacity to accommodate up to 50 COVID-19 patients. In addition to providing quality health care to COVID-19 patients, the new facility will also provide training to other medical institutions in the country.

project_name: Gov't pledges donation of med. equipment to friendship hospital
description: On 26 October, 2010, the Chinese Government announced plans to donate $10 million USD worth of medical equipment to the China-Zimbabwe Friendship Hospital in Zimbabwe as part of a three-year infrastructure package that includes a number of other unrelated projects.  The plan was signed into agreement in by the Chinese Deputy Minister of Commerce, Jiang Zengweni, in July 2010 and was announced by the Chinese Ambassador to Zimbabwe, Xin Shunkang.  It should be noted that the China-Zimbabwe Friendship Hospital, located in Mahusekwa, was constructed in Zimbabwe using Chinese funds. This donation is a supplement to the construction of the hospital (see linked projects #20443 and #72842) and is separate from the original cost of the building. In July 2010, the Chinese Government signed an agreement for a separate donation to provide $1.5 million USD worth of medical equipment and drugs to the China-Zimbabwe Friendship Hospital, which is recorded in the linked project #21460.

project_name: Gov't donated 1 million Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine doses
description: In 2021 and 2022, the Chinese Government donated approximately 7 million doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Zimbabwe. The Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Zimbabwe on February 15, 2021 (Project ID#95670). Then, on March 16, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered another 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Zimbabwe (Project ID#95671). The People’s Liberation Army (PLA) of China delivered an additional 100,000 donated Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses to the Zimbabwe Defence Forces on May 17, 2021 (Project ID#95672). Then, on September 26, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered another 500,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Zimbabwe (Project ID#95673). Several months later, on December 20, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 1 million donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Zimbabwe (Project ID#95674). Then, on November 25, 2022, the Government of Zimbabwe received another shipment of 3 million donated Sinopharm vaccine doses from the Chinese Government (Project ID#95675). At a formal handover ceremony, Chinese Ambassador to Zimbabwe Guo Shaochun delivered the donation on behalf of Peng Liyuan, the wife of Chinese President Xi Jinping, for the women, children and teenagers of Zimbabwe to Auxillia Mnangagwa, the wife of Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa.

project_name: Nanning City donated anti-epidemic materials to the city of Harare
description: On May 29, 2020, a handover ceremony was held for the donation of anti-epidemic materials from Nanning City, the capital of the Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, to the government of Harare, the capital city of Zimbabwe. The materials included 10,000 masks and 1600 units of personal protection equipment. China’s Ambassador to Zimbabwe, Guo Shaochun, delivered the materials on behalf of Nanning City. The mayor of Harare and other government officials also attended the event.   From the materials provided by Nanning City, Mayor of Harare Cllr Herbert Gomba donated masks and surgical gowns to 3 cities including Bulawayo, Gweru, and Mutare.

project_name: Gov't provided USD 1,240,000 via UN population fund
description: In January 2020, Chinese government provides USD 1,240,000 responding to the health needs of women and girls affected by Tropical Cyclone Idai in Zimbabwe.
